title: Judea & Samaria Desk
subtitle: The Palestinian Authority, security, settlement and land in Judea and Samaria

items.headline: Czech lawmaker tours Samaria with Yossi Dagan and calls Judea and Samaria "the historic land of the State of Israel"
items.summary: Miroslav Janulik, described by Israeli outlets as a senior lawmaker from the Czech ruling party, toured Samaria on Tuesday as a guest of Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan. The two recorded a joint video from the lookout known as "the country's balcony," which looks west toward the coastal plain. Janulik said it was his first visit to Samaria, that from the lookout one can see Tel Aviv, Haifa and Ben Gurion Airport, and that Judea and Samaria are "the historic land of the State of Israel." He said it matters for Europe as well as for Israelis "to stay here," and that "we will remain with you" (Channel 14; Kipa; Olam Katan). Dagan thanked him and said Judea and Samaria are a security belt not only for Tel Aviv and Israel but for Europe and Western culture, calling the ridge "our forward defense line." The visit followed Dagan's meetings in Prague about two weeks earlier, part of his effort to enlist European support against sanctions on Judea and Samaria; after those meetings, Andrej Knutek, the head of the Czech ruling party's group in the European Parliament, separately backed applying Israeli sovereignty there (same outlets). Spelling of the Czech lawmaker's surname varies in the Hebrew reports (Yanulik / Yanulink).
items.source: Channel 14 / Kipa / Olam Katan / Yossi Dagan

items.headline: Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva opens a branch at Geva Shomron; Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira recites the blessing "who sets a border for the widow"
items.summary: A branch of the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva has been set up in the new community of Geva Shomron, next to Sa-Nur in northern Samaria, Olam Katan reported on Monday. Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira, one of the yeshiva's heads, recited on the site, with the divine name, the blessing "who sets a border for the widow," said on seeing Jewish homes settled in their place; Rabbi Ben Zion Algazi, also a head of the yeshiva, took part (Olam Katan). The community itself went up in late October, when ten families of yeshiva graduates moved onto the former Paratroopers training base (see the 29 Oct edition). The council and the yeshiva had planned a Torah branch beside the families as part of building the community. The Samaria council says Geva Shomron is the tenth community it has established in the area in less than a year, under a plan for 19 new communities in northern Samaria. Shapira had said at the founding ceremony, "The people of Israel chooses to cut an eternal covenant with this land."

places.name: Geva Shomron (next to Sa-Nur)
places.note: Approximate: OpenStreetMap / Nominatim point for Sa-Nur; the new community is on the former Paratroopers base beside it, as in earlier desk items

items.headline: Yesha Council and the Farms Association launch "Eshet Chayil": shooting days for licensed farm women, including a gunman-in-the-home drill
items.summary: The Yesha Council and the Farms Association, working with the regional councils' security departments, have begun a project they call "Eshet Chayil" ("woman of valor"): professional shooting days, each about five hours, for farm women in Judea and Samaria who already hold a gun license (Arutz 7; Olam Katan). The drills are meant for the first minutes of an attack on an isolated farm, and include a short-range gunman entering the house and safe use of a handgun where children are present. Hagai Tam, the Yesha Council's acting director-general, said farm women are often the first to face a security incident, and that holding a license is not the same as being ready to use the weapon with skill. In the same Arutz 7 report, the council cited the Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR): 634 terror attacks in the area in the past two months, including 90 attacks on shepherds (see also the JSR tally below).

items.headline: Reporter: the Qalandiya road is due to open in about a month, cutting the drive from Judea and Samaria to Route 443 to about five minutes
items.summary: Journalist Eliya Aviv reported, and Olam Katan carried on Monday, that the Qalandiya road is due to open in about a month and will link Judea and Samaria to Route 443 and the center of the country in a drive of about five minutes, without going through Jerusalem (Olam Katan). The report says drivers now often lose time in heavy traffic around the Hizma checkpoint at the entrance to Jerusalem, and that the new road is meant to bypass that bottleneck. The timing is Aviv's account as reported by Olam Katan; it was not confirmed in an official statement opened for this edition. This is a different road from the Funduq bypass ("Mevo Shomron"), whose first section the Samaria council said would open this week (see the 23 Nov edition).

items.headline: JSR: 634 terror and harassment events against Jews from 20 Sep to 22 Nov, the olive-harvest period; five cows die in a poisoning at Har Bazak farm
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Judea and Samaria Situation Room said on Monday that from 20 September to 22 November, the olive-harvest season, it recorded no fewer than 634 terror and harassment events against Jews in Judea and Samaria (JSR, 23 Nov). Arutz 7, quoting the same room in a 25 November report, gave the figure as 634 attacks in the past two months, including 90 attacks on shepherds (Arutz 7). On Monday JSR also said five cows had died, and others were dying, in what it called an Arab poisoning at Har Bazak farm in Samaria, and it later posted video of that incident; on Tuesday it said Arabs had poisoned a dog from Man Farm in the Hebron Hills, and that the dog was taken to a clinic in serious condition (JSR, 24 Nov; JSR, 25 Nov; JSR English). No second outlet opened for this edition had independently confirmed the farm poisonings; they are reported here as JSR's account. In its 24-hour wrap on Tuesday afternoon, JSR listed one attack on shepherds, three stone-throwing attacks on vehicles, and two poisonings of animals owned by Israelis (JSR).

places.note: approximate: the Har Bazak peak, as in earlier desk items; the farm itself is not mapped

items.headline: JSR: the tomb of Eleazar son of Aaron in Awarta is vandalized for the second time in a month; Jewish burial estates at Hurvat Korkosh, near Barkan, are defaced the next day
items.summary: JSR reported on Monday that Arabs from Awarta in Samaria had vandalized the tomb of Eleazar son of Aaron, which tradition places in the village. It said this was the second time in about a month the compound had been damaged, after residents of the village set fire to the tomb on the night of 20-21 October; the photographs it circulated were credited to Elisha Yered (JSR). The next day, JSR said, Arabs vandalized Jewish burial estates from the Second Temple period at Hurvat Korkosh, near Barkan: Arabic graffiti was sprayed and trash was thrown there. The photographs were credited to Ayelet Lash, a must-check settler-side source who lives in Rachelim (JSR). Both incidents are JSR's account, with the photographs it published; they were not confirmed in a second outlet opened for this edition.

items.headline: JSR: firebomb and stones at an Israeli bus north of the Burqa bends start a fire; no one is hurt
items.summary: JSR reported on Tuesday morning that Arabs had thrown a firebomb and stones at an Israeli bus north of the Burqa bends, and that the attack started a fire at the site. It said there were no casualties (JSR). The report does not name which Burqa, and it was not confirmed in a second outlet opened for this edition.

places.note: Nominatim, village point, used in earlier desk items; JSR said only "north of the Burqa bends," without naming the village (approximate)

items.headline: JSR: two Hamas operatives held in Salim; an M16 found in Kafr Qallil; stones at Ma'ale Tidhar and near Qaryut; an incident with a 13-year-old shepherd near Gitit
items.summary: JSR reported a series of incidents on Monday and Tuesday. Security forces, it said, arrested two wanted Hamas operatives overnight in the village of Salim in Samaria, suspected of advancing the group's terror activity (JSR, 24 Nov). In a separate counterterror operation in Kafr Qallil, reservists of Battalion 8208 found an M16 rifle and full magazines and confiscated them (JSR). JSR also reported stone-throwing at Israelis in the Ma'ale Tidhar area of Gush Etzion, with no damage and no casualties (JSR), and stones at a Jewish shepherd near the village of Qaryut in Binyamin, with no known casualties (JSR). A 24 November post said an incident had taken place the day before near Gitit in the Jordan Valley while a 13-year-old Jewish shepherd was grazing his flock, and pointed to video on the Telegram channel "Kacha Ze Ovdim"; the post as published did not describe the attack itself (JSR). These items are JSR's account and were not confirmed in a second outlet opened for this edition.

places.name: Ma'ale Tidhar
places.note: Nominatim, as in earlier desk items

items.headline: Channel 18, the pro-settlement video channel, posts a local breakdown of the arson near Ramallah that was widely reported as "settler violence"
items.summary: Channel 18 Israel, the pro-settlement video channel founded by David Friedman (X @channel18israel), posted on Tuesday a "local breakdown of the bigger picture" of recent arson near Ramallah that, it said, was being widely reported as "settler violence" (Channel 18). The channel wrote that the attackers were "probably local Jewish guys," that exact perpetrators are often hard to confirm, and that some past cases were later shown to have been misattributed. Those are the channel's claims. The underlying incidents in four Palestinian villages were already on the 23 Nov edition, including the Diaspora Ministry's finding that a separate viral video of a raid on a banana plantation was made with AI.

items.headline: JSR: a French member of the European Parliament recirculates an old video as settlers poisoning Palestinian sheep; the room says the Israeli on camera was trying to save the flock
items.summary: JSR said on Monday that Rima Hassan, a French member of the European Parliament, had posted on X an old blood-libel clip, with the Al Jazeera logo, in which, she said, Israeli settlers were seen poisoning sheep belonging to Palestinian herders north of Ramallah. The post had about 28,000 views when JSR wrote. The room said the clip is old and that the truth about it had already been shown: the Israeli in the footage was not poisoning the flock but giving it charcoal water to try to save it after, JSR says, Arabs had poisoned the animals (JSR). The account of what the video shows is JSR's; Hassan's post was not opened independently for this edition.

items.headline: JSR: pro-Palestinian accounts keep circulating AI videos of Jews supposedly destroying Arab olive trees
items.summary: JSR said on Monday that pro-Palestinian accounts were still publishing AI-generated videos of Jews supposedly destroying Arabs' olive trees. It named, among those spreading the clips, an anti-Zionist group called Voice of Rabbis, with more than 300,000 followers, and a Turkish activist, Abdurrazak Yildiz (JSR). This follows the Diaspora Ministry's finding, already on the 23 Nov edition, that a viral video of "hilltop youth" raiding a banana plantation near Nablus was made with AI. JSR's identifications of the accounts were not checked on a second outlet.

items.headline: JSR: a video circulating on Arab social media tells viewers how to carry out attacks, including training in homes and orchards
items.summary: JSR English reported on Tuesday evening that a video instructing viewers on how to carry out attacks against Jews was circulating on Arab social media. According to the room, the video tells viewers that even without dedicated training sites they can use civilian spaces such as homes and orchards (JSR English, 25 Nov). This is JSR's account of the clip; the video itself was not opened from an original page for this edition.

items.headline: JSR: PA foreign minister meets lawmakers from Brazil, Argentina and Colombia, with the released Fatah operative Zakaria Zubeidi in the room
items.summary: JSR reported that on 23 November the Palestinian Authority foreign minister, Varsen Aghabekian Shahin, met a delegation of lawmakers from Brazil, Argentina and Colombia. Also at the meeting, it said, was Zakaria Zubeidi, a released prisoner who sits on Fatah's Central Committee, formerly the commander of the Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades in Jenin and the man responsible for the 2002 attack on the Likud branch in Beit She'an, in which six Israelis were murdered, as well as many other attacks in the second intifada (JSR). The meeting and Zubeidi's presence are reported here as JSR's account; they were not confirmed in a second outlet opened for this edition.

items.headline: Channel 18 announces a debate between David Friedman and hilltop activist Saadia Hershkop on Arabs under full Israeli sovereignty
items.summary: On 25 November, Channel 18 Israel, the pro-settlement video channel founded by former U.S. ambassador David Friedman, and its interviewer Sam Schubert (X @samschub) announced a debate that night between Friedman and Saadia Hershkop, a Brooklyn-born hilltop youth activist, on "what happens to the Arabs under full Israeli sovereignty" (Channel 18; Sam Schubert). The channel called it "not a mainstream debate" and said the two men "want the same end." The announcement posts were read; a finished recording was not opened for this edition, so the substance of the exchange is not summarized here.

items.headline: Samaria Regional Council holds a week of events for wounded soldiers, security forces and terror victims: Dagan calls them "the defensive wall of the people of Israel"
items.summary: For the national day of honor, the Samaria Regional Council is holding a week of events, talks and performances for families of Israelis wounded in the army, in the security forces and in attacks. The program includes a morning of honor for wives of the wounded, cultural shows and a large gathering. Council head Yossi Dagan said, "All of Samaria embraces you, you are the source of our strength — we salute your courage," and the council's materials used the phrase "the defensive wall of the people of Israel" (Srugim).

items.headline: Ayelet Lash: three lambs are born overnight at Meir La'aretz farm
items.summary: Ayelet Lash, a right-wing activist and special-needs teacher from Rachelim in Samaria, and a must-check source for the desk, posted on Wednesday that three lambs had been born overnight at Meir La'aretz farm, and she sent good wishes to the ewe (Ayelet Lash). The post is her own farm-side report and was not confirmed in a second outlet.

items.headline: Higher Planning Council set to advance 1,515 homes in Karnei Shomron, Harsha and Etz Efraim, including the area's first assisted-living complex
items.summary: The Civil Administration's Higher Planning Council is set to advance plans for 1,515 homes in three communities, a move led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is also a minister in the Defense Ministry: a plan for 436 homes in a new neighborhood of Karnei Shomron goes forward for public deposit, alongside an assisted-living complex of 250 units for older residents; a plan for 637 homes in Harsha in the Binyamin Regional Council goes for final approval and, with a second plan already approved there, brings the building advanced in Harsha to more than 900 homes; and a plan for 192 homes in Etz Efraim goes for final approval, where, the planners say, demand for homes is higher than the supply (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Simcha Raz, Olam Katan). Smotrich said the plans are "very big news for settlement," and that the special part for him is the assisted living in Karnei Shomron; Channel 14 also quotes him: "Against those who cooperate with supporters of terror and want to set up a Palestinian state, we are fortifying and strengthening settlement." Peace Now, which opposes the settlements, says the council will meet on Wednesday and gives the date as 24 November, which is a Tuesday, so the exact day is unconfirmed. By its count these plans bring the homes advanced in 2026 to 13,479, second only to 2025, when 27,939 were advanced, and to 47,132 since January 2023; it objects to the council meeting and approving plans under a caretaker government (Peace Now).
items.source: Arutz 7 / Channel 14 / Simcha Raz (Olam Katan) / Peace Now

items.headline: "Mevo Shomron" road, the Funduq bypass, opens its first section this week after about eight years and more than a quarter billion shekels
items.summary: The first section of the Funduq bypass road, which the Samaria Regional Council calls "Mevo Shomron," is due to open to traffic this week, and the whole road within about a month, the council said on Sunday. The first stage runs from the Jinsafut junction toward Yakir, Emanuel, the Kedumim bloc, the Barkan industrial zone and Kiryat Netafim; the eastern section, toward Havat Gilad, Kedumim and the rebuilt communities of northern Samaria, follows about a month later. Council head Yossi Dagan said the work took about eight years and more than a quarter billion shekels, and that in coming years drivers will be able to go from Kfar Saba to the hill-ridge communities and northern Samaria on a divided road at 100 km per hour, on the way to "a million residents in Samaria." Karnei Shomron council head Yehonatan Koznitz also took part (Arutz 7; Walla; Olam Katan; Simcha Raz).
items.source: Samaria Regional Council (via Arutz 7, Walla, Olam Katan) / Simcha Raz

items.headline: Reporter: retired Border Police officer Yaron Palumbo to head the Judea and Samaria police headquarters for nationalist crime and outpost evictions; Elisha Yered warns of a return to the demolition campaigns of a decade ago
items.summary: Reporter Ayana Ben Aderet reported on Sunday, as a first report, that retired Chief Superintendent Yaron Palumbo, formerly deputy commander of the Border Police's Judea and Samaria sector, will come out of retirement to head the inter-agency headquarters in the Judea and Samaria Police District, the main body that enforces against nationalist crime, disturbances and the removal of outposts (Ayana Ben Aderet). No second source had confirmed the appointment by publication. Elisha Yered, a hilltop activist, wrote that the security system seems to be preparing for a left-wing government: the appointment, he said, means a return to "the demolition campaigns of a decade ago," when the state fought every settlement outside the community fences; everyone he knows from that time remembers Palumbo commanding those evictions (Elisha Yered). Separately, the move of Maj. Gen. Dado Bar Kalifa to head Central Command remains set for early 2027 (see the 20 Nov edition).

items.headline: Diaspora Ministry: viral video of "hilltop youth" raiding a Palestinian banana plantation near Nablus was made with AI; JSR flags a second AI clip of Israelis "stealing" an Arab flock
items.summary: Israel's Ministry of Diaspora Affairs and Combating Antisemitism told JNS that a video said to show Jewish "hilltop youth" stealing bananas and damaging equipment at a Palestinian plantation near Nablus was generated with artificial intelligence. It drew more than 1.5 million views, first appeared on X on 16 November and was spread by accounts in the United States, Brazil, Turkey, Qatar and Pakistan, some suspected to be bots. The ministry says the clip seems to have been made in response to Palestinian media reports, not independently verified, of damage to banana plantations in the Nablus area. Minister Amichai Chikli: "We will not allow lies to become truth" (JNS). The same day the Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) said another AI-made video, showing Israeli residents supposedly stealing an Arab-owned flock, was circulating online (JSR; JSR Hebrew).

items.headline: Overnight arson and "revenge" graffiti in four Palestinian villages; no arrests. Minister Dichter calls the perpetrators terrorists and backs administrative detention; Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe warns against blaming all settlers
items.summary: Overnight Saturday to Sunday, vandals burned cars and property and sprayed Hebrew graffiti, including "revenge," in Deir as-Sudan, Kafr Malik and Deir Abu Mash'al near Ramallah and in at-Tuwani in the South Hebron Hills. The army and Border Police went to all four villages; Judea and Samaria police opened an investigation, and no one had been arrested. The IDF condemned the attacks, saying they "undermine stability" and hurt its counterterror work (IDF Spokesperson; Ynet; N12). In Deir as-Sudan the village council head told Raya that two cars were burned at about 11:15 p.m. (Raya). Minister Avi Dichter (Likud) called those responsible "lawbreakers at best and terrorists at worst" and said administrative detention should be used (Arutz 7; Ynet). Yotam Deshe, Israel Hayom's settlements reporter, wrote that the arsonists must be caught and jailed, but that while their identity and home are unknown they should not be labeled "extremist settlers" by default, since people from inside the Green Line also take part, and tying the crimes to everyone who lives in Judea and Samaria risks sanctions on people never involved (Yotam Deshe).
items.source: IDF Spokesperson / Ynet / N12 / Raya / Arutz 7 / Yotam Deshe (Israel Hayom)

items.headline: U.S. House Democratic leader Jeffries backs early action on the "settler violence" sanctions bill; Moran Tal says the EU funds Palestinian building in Area C
items.summary: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, his party's nominee for speaker, said he supports advancing the West Bank Settler Violence Protection and Prevention Act within the new Congress's first 100 days and expects "strong support" in his caucus; he declined to take a position on the Block the Bombs and Stop the Settlements bills, JNS reported from his interview with The New York Times (JNS; Raya). Responding to the push for sanctions, Moran Tal wrote that the European Union not only does not sanction Palestinian terrorists but funds them "in the billions" and helps them create facts on the ground in Area C (Moran Tal).

items.headline: From the farms: Smotrich hands out ATVs to western Binyamin farms and says 20 approved farms "is not enough"; new farm near Jericho; Yishai Fleisher brings a Montana rancher to the hilltop shepherds
items.summary: Video posted by Settlers From Within, an anti-settlement account, shows Smotrich giving ATVs to farm founders in western Binyamin and describing farms as a way to "hold on to the land"; the account says he noted that only 20 farms have been approved so far and called for more (Settlers From Within). The same account posted a farmer celebrating a new farm near Jericho as "a return to the ancestral inheritance" and pointing to open land around it (Settlers From Within); the farm's name and location are not given (unconfirmed). Yishai Fleisher, the Hebron community's international spokesman, posted a video of a visit with an experienced Jewish rancher from Montana who came to advise hilltop youth raising livestock in Judea (Yishai Fleisher). Farmer Eliav Libi wrote about the Einot Yehuda springs below the Shuval farm, dedicated to Yehuda Dimentman, who was killed in the shooting attack at Homesh and was among the founders of the Homesh core group (Eliav Libi). Olam Katan, reposted by Amishav Melet, said Torat HaMedina and the Melet family would hold a launch on Monday for the second edition of the book "Meshiv HaRuach LeTzahal," which it calls a Jewish alternative to the IDF Spirit document (Amishav Melet repost).
items.source: Settlers From Within / Yishai Fleisher / Eliav Libi / Olam Katan (via Amishav Melet)

items.headline: Activist and PA-side claims: 50 structures razed at Khirbet al-Malih in the northern Jordan Valley; PA Civil Affairs counts 30 "settler attacks" in a day; workers held near the Hizma checkpoint
items.summary: Raya, a Ramallah radio station and news site, quoted the head of the al-Malih council, Mahdi Daraghmeh, as saying army and Civil Administration crews with four bulldozers demolished 50 homes, animal pens and farm buildings at Khirbet al-Malih in the northern Jordan Valley on Sunday without prior notice; no Israeli statement was found, and the structures' legal status is not given (Raya). The PA's Civil Affairs Commission said it recorded 30 settler attacks across Judea and Samaria in 24 hours, without details (Raya). Raya also reported workers hurt by gunfire and about 18 detained near the Hizma checkpoint, a common crossing point for Palestinians entering Israel without permits (Raya; headline only, unconfirmed). Ultra Palestine says the road to Marj Sia is surrounded by seven outposts, three within 500 meters of it (Ultra Palestine). The Times of Israel carried a Physicians for Human Rights report in which medics say checkpoints and settlers delay ambulances, and a report that Israel is deporting more foreign activists from the area (from the paper's feed; the article pages were blocked).
items.source: Raya / PA Civil Affairs Commission / Ultra Palestine / Times of Israel

items.headline: JSR: 311 attacks and friction incidents against Israelis in one month; over the weekend four Israelis hurt; about 40 Arabs stone residents near Uri Ad, north of Kedumim; a driver hurt by stones on the Ein Samia road
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) said it documented 311 incidents of assault and friction against Israelis across Judea and Samaria between 21 October and 21 November 2026, about 10 a day; its headline calls them "310 Palestinian terror attacks" (JSR; JSR Hebrew). Over the weekend of 20 to 22 November, JSR counted two attacks on Jewish shepherds, six stone attacks and one attempted ramming, with four Israelis hurt; details of the attempted ramming were not given (JSR). On Sunday morning about 40 Arabs threw stones north of Kedumim, at Israeli residents near the community of Uri Ad; JSR says the group had been "harvesting" olives at a spot not approved by the army. No one was hurt (JSR; JSR; Simcha Raz). On Sunday evening, Elisha Yered reported, Arabs from al-Mughayyir stoned a Jewish car on the road between Ein Samia and the Shiloh hills, damaging it and hurting a resident's finger (Elisha Yered). Raya, quoting al-Mughayyir council head Amin Abu Aliya, gave the opposite account of the same evening: that settlers attacked Palestinian cars at the village entrances and passengers were cut by glass (Raya). The two accounts could not be reconciled.
items.source: JSR / Simcha Raz (Olam Katan) / Elisha Yered / Raya

places.name: Uri Ad, north of Kedumim
places.note: Approximate: Uri Ad not mapped; marker at Kedumim (Nominatim), as in earlier desk items

places.name: Ein Samia road (toward the Shiloh hills)
places.note: Ein Samia point used in earlier desk items (approximate)

items.headline: Talia farm's flock stolen in daylight near the security fence in the Hebron Hills, then found after wide searches; owner says he was afraid to respond after police took his gun
items.summary: On Saturday the sheep of the Talia farm, near Yatir in the Hebron Hills, were stolen and were returned after wide searches, Elisha Yered reported. Yered quotes the owner, reserve Maj. Betzalel Talia, whose mother was killed in the 7 October massacre, as saying Israeli Arabs together with Palestinians broke a gate in the separation fence and took the flock from the farm's grazing land, and that he was afraid to respond because the police had taken his pistol and the same clan had threatened and attacked him several times, each time ending in his own arrest. He says the thieves are Palestinians with special permits and a key to the fence. These claims are his; no police statement was found (Elisha Yered).

places.name: Talia farm, near Yatir
places.note: Approximate: farm not mapped; Nominatim point for Yatir (Meitar area)

items.headline: Bethlehem man in his 20s held over a bag of ready-to-use pipe bombs and firebombs hidden near Umm Safa to attack Israelis
items.summary: Police say a Bethlehem resident in his 20s was arrested over the weekend on suspicion of planting a bag of ready-to-use pipe bombs and firebombs near the village of Umm Safa, meant for attacks on Israeli civilians. Police found the bag in October after a tip to the Judea and Samaria District's anti-crime unit; Border Police sappers destroyed the devices, and weeks of investigation led to the suspect. The arrest was made by the Prison Service's Masada unit, district police and troops of the Etzion Brigade (Walla; Channel 14; Srugim). Ayelet Lash, a right-wing activist from Rachelim, urged Israelis to get gun licenses: "The enemy is raising its head" (Ayelet Lash). Lash also posted video from Friday night in which, she says, a man in PA forces uniform on a motorbike blocks an IDF force operating in Bethlehem (Ayelet Lash), and wrote that on Sunday morning a guard at a Gush Etzion community caught an Arab driver wearing a kippah who tried to get through the gate (Ayelet Lash); both are unconfirmed.
items.source: Israel Police (via Walla, Channel 14, Srugim) / Ayelet Lash

places.name: Bethlehem
places.note: Bethlehem city point (Nominatim); Umm Safa is not mapped because reports do not say which village of that name

items.headline: Beit El shooting follow-up: HaKol HaYehudi says the man killed by the security coordinator had been jailed by the PA for arms dealing and appears in Hamas records as one of its own
items.summary: After Beit El's security coordinator killed one of two Arabs who approached the community on Friday (see the 21 Nov edition), HaKol HaYehudi and its writer Elchanan Groner said their check found that the dead man had been held in a PA prison for arms dealing and opposition to the PA, and is listed in Hamas's "black book" of complaints about PA treatment, apparently as one of its men. Groner: someone who comes near Beit El at night "probably did not go to pick flowers." The IDF statement says the coordinator fired in the air and then at one suspect, the second was detained, and the incident is under review (HaKol HaYehudi; Elchanan Groner). Elisha Yered called it an attempt to infiltrate the community and described the dead man as an arms dealer and apparently a Hamas operative (Elisha Yered). The dead man's name was not published, and the records were not independently checked (unconfirmed).
items.source: HaKol HaYehudi / Elchanan Groner / Elisha Yered / IDF Spokesperson

items.headline: Border Police seize 28 firebombs and hidden ammunition in Anata; a woman who boasted on TikTok of smuggling Palestinians is caught at the Ofer crossing with three in her car
items.summary: Undercover Border Police officers in Anata seized 28 firebombs ready to throw, about 6 liters of flammable liquid and about 50 pistol rounds hidden in a scooter; four suspects were held over the overnight burning of a building in the Shuafat camp, part of a feud between two families after a boy was killed there on Saturday (reported as 10 or 13 years old) (Israel Hayom; Walla). Yotam Deshe reported that police waiting at the Ofer crossing arrested a 22-year-old woman from the south, who had said on a TikTok live stream that she smuggles Palestinians into Israel for money, and a 17-year-old with her; three Palestinians without permits were in the car, one in the trunk. The district fraud unit had investigated for a month (Yotam Deshe).
items.source: Israel Police / Israel Hayom / Walla / Yotam Deshe (Israel Hayom)

items.headline: Southern Syria: Druze man in IDF uniform with lieutenant colonel rank visits his family in Hader after decades; the 210th Division opens an inquiry. Turkey's foreign minister claims Israel flies weapons to a Druze group
items.summary: Video spread on social media showed a man in IDF uniform with lieutenant colonel insignia getting out of a military vehicle and embracing his family in the Druze village of Hader in southern Syria. Kan found he is not an IDF officer in regular or reserve service but an Israeli civilian who works in a security organization; reports name him as Atef Hasson of Mas'ade, who left the village decades ago. The 210th Division, which holds the Syrian border, learned of the visit from the video and opened an inquiry into how he entered Syria and wore the uniform (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Itay Blumental, Kan; IDF reply via Blumental). The video was first published by Arab media outlets. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan claimed in a TV interview that Israel sends weapons and ammunition by helicopter every week to one of three Druze groups in southern Syria to create a pretext for an operation against Syria; Israel had not responded (Walla). The claim is his and unconfirmed. Halutzei HaBashan, which campaigns for Israeli settlement in the Bashan, hosted Susie Dym at a Knesset conference initiated by MK Limor Son Har-Melech, where she spoke for wide settlement along natural borders (Halutzei HaBashan).
items.source: Kan (via Arutz 7) / Channel 14 / Itay Blumental (Kan) / Walla / Halutzei HaBashan

items.headline: Ramla crime clans Jaroushi and Shamali sign a sulha in Lod after a seven-year feud with about 40 dead; Raed Salah of the outlawed Northern Branch attends, and critics say killers will go free
items.summary: The Jaroushi and Shamali families of Ramla signed a reconciliation (sulha) at the home of the Azbarga family in Lod on Saturday, ending a feud of about seven years in which about 40 people were killed, including bystanders; before the ceremony family representatives held an unusual meeting at the Ramla police station (Israel Hayom; Ynet). HaKol HaYehudi says Raed Salah and Safwat Freij, heads of the two branches of the Islamic Movement, took part; that Haaretz's police reporter said the event was held under police sponsorship against the position of Minister Itamar Ben Gvir; and that the host was Jum'a Azbarga, a Likud activist (HaKol HaYehudi). Maureen Amitai of the Homa institute (Arei Israel) said that "dozens of murderers go free and no one intends to indict them" (Homa). Meir Ettinger wrote that such a sulha gives "cruel murder cells" immunity and leaves the weapons with the crime groups (Meir Ettinger); Ayelet Lash called it "a state within a state" (Ayelet Lash).
items.source: Israel Hayom / Ynet / HaKol HaYehudi / Homa / Meir Ettinger / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: Police find an IDF LAW rocket launcher, a Kalashnikov and a pipe bomb in a Jaljulia home compound; a masked rider with a loaded pistol caught in Taibe; 71 illegal residents arrested in Kafr Qasim
items.summary: Police uncovered a weapons cache in a residential compound in Jaljulia overnight Saturday to Sunday holding an IDF-issue LAW launcher, a Kalashnikov rifle, explosive bricks, a pipe bomb and ammunition, and arrested a suspect. In Taibe a motorcyclist who tried to flee was caught with a loaded pistol, a face mask and gloves; police suspect he was on his way to commit a serious crime (Maariv; Walla). Police, Yasam officers and Border Police arrested 71 Palestinians staying illegally in a residential compound in Kafr Qasim (Walla; Israel Hayom). Ayelet Lash: "The left is busy whitewashing supporters of the massacre, the supporters of the massacre are busy preparing another massacre" (Ayelet Lash).
items.source: Israel Police (via Maariv, Walla, Israel Hayom) / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: Elchanan Groner relays a border security man's warning of "crazy" weapons smuggling by Bedouin gangs from Egypt with four drones at a time; Ayelet Lash says the security system has no idea what is coming in
items.summary: Elchanan Groner posted a message he said he received from a security man on the Egyptian border about arms smuggling by Bedouin militias: "Insane amounts keep coming through... buggies, drones, freely. Every time they now lift four drones together," and "I don't have the right equipment to deal with it." He also pointed to a new method, GPS-guided smuggling balloons (Elchanan Groner; Groner). Ayelet Lash posted a video of what she called one of dozens of nightly smuggling runs, by drone, off-road buggy and large balloons, and said most are never caught and no one knows whether only pistols and rifles come in or heavier weapons (Ayelet Lash). She also wrote that on Saturday there was gunfire from the Jordanian side opposite the Jordan Valley at midday, which the army said was a Jordanian exercise, and arms smuggling in the evening (Ayelet Lash). These are their reports and were not confirmed by the army or police.

items.headline: Regavim asks the attorney general to reject the Joint List's demand to halt enforcement against illegal building in the Negev; Arab media report about 400 demolition orders around Wadi al-Na'am
items.summary: Regavim, a pro-settlement land-use group, sent an urgent letter to Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara asking her to reject outright last week's request by Joint List MKs to stop enforcement against illegal building in the Negev. It says the request tries to get around a High Court ruling last month, by Justice Kanfi-Steinitz, that dismissed a similar petition by Ra'am, and that a caretaker government must enforce the law like any other. "The basic duty of a caretaker government, like any other government, is to enforce the law fully," the letter says (Olam Katan; Regavim). Raya reported that the authorities handed out about 400 demolition orders on Sunday around Wadi al-Na'am, an unrecognized Bedouin village southwest of Shaqib al-Salam that it says has more than 15,000 residents (Raya); no Israeli statement was found. Background on the planning contest: the Khamaisi Plan backgrounder.

places.note: Approximate: Wadi al-Na'am not mapped; marker at Shaqib al-Salam (Nominatim)

items.headline: From the right: Tibi hosted in Amman by an ex-Jordanian MP who praised 7 October; Moran Tal on Hamas eulogies for the Islamic Movement founder who mentored Mansour Abbas; Omri Haim on "Mawtini" sung in Haifa
items.summary: HaKol HaYehudi and Meir Ettinger report that MK Ahmad Tibi, just after becoming a Knesset deputy speaker, visited Jordan and was hosted in Amman by former Jordanian MP Khalil Atiyeh, who held a reception for the Joint List's election result; they say Atiyeh once burned an Israeli flag in parliament, praised the 2014 Har Nof synagogue attackers and praised the 7 October massacre (HaKol HaYehudi; Meir Ettinger; Elchanan Groner). Moran Tal wrote that when Sheikh Abdullah Nimr Darwish, founder of the Islamic Movement and Mansour Abbas's teacher, died in May 2017, Ismail Haniyeh and Khaled Mashal eulogized him by phone at the funeral, and the Muslim Brotherhood, Hamas and the sons of Hamas founder Ahmed Yassin sent condolences; she quotes Hamas praising his "long path of struggle" (Moran Tal; Moran Tal). Omri Haim, head of Channel 14's Arab-affairs desk, said about 2,000 people at Haifa's congress center sang "Mawtini," the unofficial Palestinian anthem, at the end of a Trio Joubran concert on Saturday night (Omri Haim). These are their claims, with the evidence they post.
items.source: HaKol HaYehudi / Meir Ettinger / Elchanan Groner / Moran Tal / Omri Haim (Channel 14)

items.headline: PA Nablus governor Ghassan Daghlas hosts two men freed after 22 years for the 2004 Carmel Market suicide bombing and praises their "sacrifice"
items.summary: Ghassan Daghlas, the PA's governor of Nablus, met on Saturday with Yahya Zahran and Hassan Ahmad, released after 22 years in Israeli prison for their part in the November 2004 suicide bombing at Tel Aviv's Carmel Market, which killed three Israelis and wounded about 30 (JNS says more than 30); the attack was claimed by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. In a post on the governorate's official Facebook page Daghlas called their release a moment honoring their "patience, sacrifice and steadfastness," and added that "the joy of freedom is not complete" until all prisoners are freed (JSR; JSR Hebrew; JNS). JSR has reported a string of similar visits by PA governors with released prisoners this month, including Ramallah governor Laila Ghannam (see the 20 Nov edition).

items.headline: About 50 Arabs stone Israeli residents near the Tzafnat farm by Tapuah Junction and hurt three; a Metzudat David shepherd is hurt by stones near al-Mughayyir
items.summary: About 50 Arabs threw stones at Israeli residents near the Tzafnat farm in Samaria on Friday, 20 November, and three Israelis were hurt, JSR said; the severity of the injuries was not given, and no second source had reported the attack by publication (JSR; JSR English). The farm sits near Tapuah Junction; it was founded about a year before June 2026 by two families from Yitzhar and Tapuah to hold state land between the villages of Huwara and Jamma'in and the main road from Tapuah Junction to Ariel (HaKol HaYehudi, June 2026). The same afternoon about 20 Arabs threw stones at a shepherd of the Metzudat David farm near al-Mughayyir; JSR first reported no injuries and later said the shepherd was hurt (JSR; JSR update). Stones were also thrown at an Israeli car on Route 450 near Beitillu in Binyamin, with no injuries or damage (JSR; Simcha Raz). JSR's tally for Thursday, 19 November: two attacks on Jewish shepherds and two stone attacks (JSR). The poisoning of Metzudat David's herds has reached U.S. television: Fox News quoted farm founder Evyatar Karo as saying the farm has lost 25 animals, which he said choke and cry as they die, and Yesha Council head Israel Ganz warned that a child could be next to eat laced dates and that water sources could be poisoned (Fox News, 19 Nov; Simcha Raz).
items.source: JSR / Simcha Raz (Olam Katan) / HaKol HaYehudi / Fox News

items.headline: Elchanan Groner: a Fatah prisoner freed in the hostage deal now runs activist events from Khirbet al-Marajim, an illegal compound between Duma and the Allon Road farms
items.summary: Elchanan Groner of HaKol HaYehudi reported on Friday that Kutaiba Muslim, a Fatah member of a shooting cell in the second intifada who was sentenced to 33 years, served 26 and was freed in the hostage deal about a year and a half ago, has in recent months been staging what Groner calls provocations with Israeli and foreign left-wing activists against the Michtam LeDavid farm and other farms near the Allon Road. Groner says Muslim works from Khirbet al-Marajim, an illegal compound between the village of Duma and the farms that the Civil Administration has not demolished, and that the PA delivered fencing there on Friday. He also says Muslim received a certificate of honor from Fatah and PA figures including Jibril Rajoub and Nablus governor Ghassan Daghlas, launched a prison memoir at Balata camp on 27 June 2026, joined a Fatah delegation to al-Mughayyir on 10 September, and on 12 November received a doctorate from An-Najah University on education as a tool of "resistance" among prisoners. He asks the army and police why they let him keep operating next to Jewish communities and the Allon Road (Elchanan Groner; reposted by Elisha Yered). These details are Groner's and were not checked independently. The PA news agency WAFA confirms that Muslim lives there: it reported the same evening that settlers "surrounded the house of the prisoner Kutaiba Muslim Abu Hamda" at Khirbet al-Marajim and tried to break in, a claim no Israeli source confirmed (WAFA Hebrew).

items.headline: Ahmad Yaqoub, the Menashe Brigade's most wanted man and head of the cell behind the July 2024 Gilboa seam bombing, gives himself up at the Salem crossing; 15 more drones seized in Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Ahmad Yaqoub turned himself in to troops at the Salem crossing on Friday morning, 20 November, after Menashe Brigade forces, guided by the Shin Bet, ran dozens of operations to catch him, the IDF said. The army says he headed the cell that set off bombs on the security barrier near Gilboa on 23 July 2024, wounding two Defense Ministry workers, tried over the years to carry out shooting and bombing attacks, and was in touch with terror groups outside Judea and Samaria; he was handed to the Shin Bet for questioning (IDF Spokesperson; Times of Israel). Army Radio, quoted by an Arabic outlet, called him Ahmad Yaqoub (Turkman) and "wanted number one" in the brigade's area, which includes Jenin (quoted in the Times of Israel report). The OSINT account Aleph noted that he had been reported killed: on 28 August 2026 it relayed a Jenin Battalion of Islamic Jihad notice naming an "Ahmed Yaqoub Turkman" among men killed in an air strike in Jenin (Aleph); that they are the same man is not confirmed. Separately, the IDF said a focused effort seized about 15 drones in Judea and Samaria in the past week, and more than 500 since the start of the year (IDF Spokesperson; Simcha Raz).
items.source: IDF Spokesperson / Times of Israel / Aleph / Simcha Raz

places.name: Salem crossing
places.note: Approximate: Zububa village point (Nominatim), next to the crossing; the crossing itself was not found

items.headline: Givat Beit Anot residents spot bird trappers with a security drone; the army detains them and the songbirds are freed
items.summary: Residents of Givat Beit Anot in the Hebron Hills, flying a security drone over their grazing land on Friday morning, spotted several young Arabs laying nets to catch protected songbirds, with two cages of already-trapped birds as bait. Troops called to the site detained the suspects and the birds were released (JSR; Netanel Frankel). Resident Yedidya Amsalem said the trappers sent teenagers in because the site is close to the Trans-Judea Highway while adults watched from a distance, and that since the hilltop was founded its residents have stopped dozens of trapping attempts (Elisha Yered). Elisha Yered, whose group hands out drones to hilltop communities, called the catch "another achievement in the field thanks to the drones we gave" (Elisha Yered).
items.source: JSR / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew) / Elisha Yered

places.name: Givat Beit Anot (near Beit Einun)
places.note: Approximate: hilltop not mapped; same marker as earlier desk items

items.headline: Wadi Zarqa: a "solidarity harvest" of about 150 activists, mostly Israelis and foreigners, near the Or Binyamin hilltop; JSR says an Or Binyamin shepherd was attacked
items.summary: Peace Now said about 150 peace and human-rights activists joined a solidarity olive harvest in the West Bank on Friday morning, 20 November, and that people from "wildcat outposts" could only shout insults at them (Peace Now). Israelis at the site described it as an olive harvest with almost no Arab pickers: Netanel Frankel of JNS Hebrew reported that dozens took part, most of them Israelis and foreigners, in Wadi Zarqa in western Binyamin, and that a shepherd was attacked during the event (Netanel Frankel). JSR said dozens of far-left activists and a few Arab "pickers" attacked a Jewish shepherd of the Or Binyamin farm, with no injuries or damage (JSR). Peace Now did not name the site, so it is not confirmed that its event and the Wadi Zarqa event were the same. Elisha Yered also shared an Arutz 7 interview with Efrat Quinn, 23, a mother of two who lives at Or Binyamin without running water or regular power (Elisha Yered).
items.source: Peace Now / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew) / JSR / Elisha Yered

places.name: Or Binyamin (Wadi Zarqa)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Wadi a-Zarqa, as in earlier desk items

items.headline: Elisha Yered in Olam Katan: the army still warns PA forces before raids despite Central Command's announced change, and he saw a raid route posted on Arab Telegram an hour ahead
items.summary: In his weekly Olam Katan column, Elisha Yered writes about the army procedure known as "kipul shotrim" ("folding up the police"), under which a brigade operations room tells the PA security forces, through the liaison office, about a planned operation so PA police can leave the area, and troops wait for confirmation before going in. He says Central Command announced a change to the rule after his earlier reports, but that new testimony from soldiers shows advance notice went on and raids ended empty-handed, and that even a force chasing stone-throwers after an attack was asked why it had not waited for PA approval. He describes seeing troops waiting at the turn from Route 60 to Deir Dibwan about six weeks ago while a local Arab Telegram channel posted their full route, through Rammun, Taybeh, Deir Jarir, al-Mazra'a al-Sharqiya and Kafr Malik to Khirbet Abu Falah, about an hour before forces entered Kafr Malik (Olam Katan; Elisha Yered). These are Yered's claims; the army has not responded to them in the reports that were opened. The desk reported on 16 November two raids that came up empty after PA forces were told in advance.

items.headline: Beit El's security coordinator kills one of two Palestinians who approached the community, after first firing in the air; neither was armed, and the army is reviewing the incident
items.summary: Soldiers and Beit El's security squad were called out on Friday evening, 20 November, after a report that two suspects were approaching the community. The community security coordinator reached the spot, fired in the air and then at one of them, who was killed; the second was detained and handed over for questioning, the IDF said. The army is investigating, and its findings will go to the authorities who decide whether to examine the incident further (IDF Spokesperson; Ynet). Neither man was armed, Ynet and the Times of Israel reported. The PA named the dead man as Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, 42, of al-Bireh, and the detained man as Firas Fares Samad, 36 (Times of Israel). Raya placed the shooting near the village of Dura al-Qar', which borders Beit El (Raya). Why the two men were approaching the community has not been reported.
items.source: IDF Spokesperson / Ynet / Times of Israel / Raya

items.headline: Police: masked Israelis ambush a patrol car in the South Hebron Hills with a stone barricade and rocks, and an officer fires in the air; one suspect held. Masked men also smash cars in al-Halqum near Tekoa
items.summary: Police on an operation against Jewish extremist violence in the South Hebron Hills on Friday saw a group of masked suspects dressed in black, chased them, and were then ambushed: the group set up a stone barricade, threw rocks and tried to keep the officers inside their car, which was damaged. An officer who felt his life was in danger fired in the air and the group fled. One suspect, who police say first tried to give a false identity, was arrested; police will ask to extend his detention (Times of Israel, citing police). Earlier on Friday, security cameras showed at least three masked men with clubs and stones smash the windows of three cars at a Palestinian compound in al-Halqum, near Arab Tekoa; no one was arrested, and the army is checking whether they came from two nearby outposts, Maariv reported. Maariv also reported that right-wing activists took over a Palestinian fruit stand in the Jenin area and are suspected of taking most of the produce (Maariv).
items.source: Israel Police (via Times of Israel) / Maariv

places.name: South Hebron Hills (area)
places.note: Approximate: police did not name the site; same area marker as earlier desk items

items.headline: PA claims: two new outposts, north of al-Nuwei'ma and near Nabi Musa; a man shot in the back during a harvest at Nabi Salih; Israeli flags at a girls' school in Lubban al-Sharqiya
items.summary: The PA Civil Affairs Commission listed 20 settler "violations" on Thursday, 19 November, including a new outpost north of al-Nuwei'ma near Jericho and another in the Nabi Musa desert at a site where an outpost had been removed before, plus Israeli flags and Hebrew signs near Deir Razih and Hamsa west of Dura (Raya). WAFA said settlers fired live rounds at olive pickers on the edge of Nabi Salih on Friday and a young man was hit in the back, and that settlers put Israeli flags at the entrance to the girls' high school in Lubban al-Sharqiya (WAFA; WAFA). Raya reported a house demolished in al-Mazra'a al-Gharbiya, northwest of Ramallah (Raya). The Arab League welcomed the British and Australian sanctions over settlement and urged other states to follow (Raya). None of these claims was confirmed by an Israeli source by publication.
items.source: PA Civil Affairs Commission (via Raya) / WAFA / Raya

items.headline: Southern Syria: Al Jazeera reports three tanks west of Saida al-Hanout, mines set off by the "Sofa 53" patrol road, and a five-vehicle incursion into Jamla and Abidin
items.summary: Al Jazeera's "Syria Now" reporter said three Israeli tanks entered the area west of Saida al-Hanout in southern Quneitra on Friday, 20 November, maneuvered and fired at farmland, then pulled back through the Abu al-Ghaythar gate. On Thursday, it said, troops set off a group of anti-personnel mines near the route of "Sofa 53", the fortified IDF patrol road along the buffer zone, at al-Mu'akkar west of Mazraat al-Hanout, and five vehicles entered Jamla and Abidin in western Daraa before returning to a post near Ma'ariya, with no contact with residents. The Sijil monitoring center counted 395 Israeli actions in Syria in October, including 126 incursions, 36 raids and 44 checkpoints, the highest monthly numbers this year (Al Jazeera). These are the Syrian side's accounts; the IDF did not comment. Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new since 19 November.

items.headline: Police and Border Police dig up a buried army crate in Zarzir holding eight IDF artillery-shell fuzes and an M16 magazine; a woman dies after a car blows up in Tira
items.summary: Northern District police and Border Police, acting on information about weapons in an open area of Zarzir, in the Jezreel Valley, dug where the ground looked recently disturbed and found an IDF crate with eight fuzes for artillery shells and an M16 magazine. The items went to the police forensic labs to identify who held them; no arrest was reported (Maariv). Activist Ayelet Lash wrote that the find shows Israel's enemies "are preparing a massacre" while politicians court Arab parties; that is her view (Ayelet Lash). In the Triangle, a woman of about 40 died on Friday night after a car exploded in Tira (Maariv).

items.headline: From the right: Moran Tal on a video of Ra'am's founder that the party keeps sharing; Meir Ettinger on Jabareen's "we won't back bombing our people"; Kalman Liebskind asks Yashar's religious MKs about counting on Balad
items.summary: OSINT researcher Moran Tal wrote that Mansour Abbas told President Herzog last week that he and Ra'am follow the path of Islamic Movement founder Abdullah Nimr Darwish, and pointed to a video from a southern-branch conference Darwish attended before his death, which she says Ra'am and southern-branch people share again and again around the anniversary of his death (Moran Tal). Writer Meir Ettinger reposted an interview in which Joint List chairman Jabareen told the Panet site, "We are an Arab party; will we be for bombing our own people?" and called Gaza part of a Palestinian state with the West Bank (Meir Ettinger). Makor Rishon editor Kalman Liebskind wrote an open letter to Yashar's religious and right-wing candidates, including Matan Kahana and Yoram Cohen, asking whether they are comfortable being counted in a 67-seat bloc against Netanyahu together with Balad (Kalman Liebskind). These are their views and claims as posted.
items.source: Moran Tal / Meir Ettinger / Kalman Liebskind (Makor Rishon)

items.headline: Samaria council unveils the plan for "Shira," a new city east of Rosh HaAyin beside Route 5: about 60,000 homes for more than 200,000 residents
items.summary: Israel Hayom on Thursday evening, 19 November, published for the first time the Samaria Regional Council's plan for Shira, the new city formerly called "Rosh HaAyin East." According to the plan, the city would have about 60,000 housing units and more than 200,000 residents on about 16,000 dunams, built as dense apartment housing like the cities of the Tel Aviv area and open to the general public. The name is a Hebrew acronym for "Gate of Jerusalem" and was given by council head Yossi Dagan. The project is being advanced with the Israel Land Authority and the Finance Ministry, and Dagan credited Rosh HaAyin mayor Raz Sagi with helping on the planning (Israel Hayom). The security cabinet approved the city as a new community in December 2025, and the Interior Ministry gave it an official community code on 3 September 2026; Channel 14's report at the time gave its area as about 9,500 dunams, smaller than the figure in the new plan (Channel 14, 3 Sep). Dagan presents the city as a security step: it would sit between Rosh HaAyin and three Palestinian villages to its east, stop Palestinian building from spreading west toward Rosh HaAyin and Petah Tikva, and serve as "a defensive belt" for the Tel Aviv area against an October 7-style attack from PA territory. He said the council has worked on it for more than four years, as a central part of its "A Million in Samaria" plan for cities, rail lines, hospitals and industrial zones. No building timetable was given in the report.
items.source: Israel Hayom / Channel 14 / Samaria Regional Council

items.headline: Further Channel 18 clips: Elisha Yered calls for canceling the Oslo Accords and closing the Palestinian Authority; he says most incidents labeled settler violence are self-defense
items.summary: Channel 18 Israel, a pro-settlement video channel founded by former U.S. ambassador David Friedman, posted further English-subtitled clips on 16 to 18 November from its interview of Elisha Yered, a hilltop youth leader, by Sam Schubert. The interview itself was already reported here on 12 and 15 November. In the later clips, Yered said that if he met Prime Minister Netanyahu he would call for the Oslo Accords to be canceled and for the Palestinian Authority to be closed, arguing that the accords "cost us blood" and that there are already "almost thirty" Jewish settlement points in Areas A and B (Channel 18, 16 Nov). He said Israeli military control should let citizens travel "even in the heart of Arab cities," because "if we don't control that area, the enemy will" (Channel 18, 16 Nov). Those demands are his. A Haaretz report already on this edition also counts more than 30 sites set up in PA-controlled areas, without government or army approval; it does not confirm his policy argument. On sovereignty, Yered said, "Anyone who supports terror — and I say this with sadness — that ninety-nine percent of the Arabs here shouldn't be here." He pointed to a post he said the Qusra municipality published on 8 October 2023 praising "the martyrs of Gaza and the Hamas terrorists" (Channel 18, 16 Nov); that municipal post was not independently confirmed for this item. In other clips he said 95 to 98 percent of incidents labeled "settler violence" are self-defense, mid-event filming, or sometimes "a blatant lie," and described trying to film a field fire and a stone ambush with one hand already "neutralized," for 15 seconds (Channel 18, 18 Nov; Channel 18, 18 Nov). Those percentages are his and are unconfirmed. He also said, "If the state will not worry about me, then we will take care of our own security," and that he is not willing to take the risk that his wife will be "the next victim" (Channel 18, 18 Nov). Friedman reposted the 18 November filming clip. Schubert's own account has not posted a new interview since 13 November, only comments on this series.
items.source: Channel 18 Israel / Elisha Yered / David Friedman

places.name: Qusra
places.note: Village point (approximate), as in earlier desk items; cited in Yered's claim about a municipal post

items.headline: Paving begins on the doubled Route 60 between the Michmash crossing and Givat Asaf, part of a project of about 1 billion shekels
items.summary: Workers began laying asphalt on Thursday, 19 November, on the section of Route 60 between the Michmash crossing and Givat Asaf in Binyamin, after months of preparing the route. The project, estimated at about 1 billion shekels, widens the road to two lanes in each direction from Sha'ar Binyamin to the British Police junction. A plan to double the northern section as well, from the British Police junction past Shilo and Eli to Tapuah Junction, has also been approved, and a traffic light at the Hizma junction is nearly finished (Haredim10). Binyamin council head Israel Ganz said that "to bring a million residents to Binyamin, Judea and Samaria, it is not enough to build homes; we need a revolution in roads" (Netanel Frankel, JNS Hebrew; also reported by Simcha Raz, Olam Katan, with photos from the Binyamin council).
items.source: Binyamin Regional Council / Haredim10 / JNS Hebrew / Olam Katan

items.headline: Allon Road farms: attacks on the road fell as farms went up, but the herds now face poisonings, stones and arson, Binyamin council figures show
items.summary: Israel Hayom on 19 November followed the shepherds of the Metzudat David farm, which graze daily above the Allon Road near al-Mughayyir. Figures from the Binyamin council and the Farms Association, partly reported here on 17 November, tie the farms to a drop in terror incidents on the road: 459 in 2022 with three farms, 314 in 2023 with six, 126 in 2024 with 11, and 52 in the first half of 2025 with 13. The council says large-scale army activity also played a part. The new figures are about the price the farms pay: the Binyamin security center logged at least 34 stone-throwing incidents against shepherds, residents and troops around Metzudat David from January to October 2026, seven arsons and six shootings or reports of gunfire, and the farms near the road reported 16 poisonings or suspected poisonings between June 2025 and October 2026, including dates and sweets laced with a substance suspected to be poison and tainted water pits and troughs. Farm founder Evyatar Karo said, "Even the army knows we are the front line." Council head and Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz said terrorists from al-Mughayyir are trying to drive the farms out "to return the dangerous situation" on the road (Israel Hayom). The figures are the council's own and were not checked independently.

items.headline: Jordan Valley council starts preparing 700 dunams for farming near Na'ama; Elisha Yered's group finishes a road from Yitzhar to the Tzon Aviezer farm
items.summary: The Jordan Valley Regional Council has begun preparing 700 dunams for farming near the community of Na'ama, as part of a five-year plan that also calls for 13 new communities in the next three years, Simcha Raz of Olam Katan reported on 19 November with the council's photos (Simcha Raz). The figures come from that single report and are unconfirmed elsewhere. In Samaria, Elisha Yered said on 18 November that the "Redeeming Gush Kaneh" project finished its first stage, a paved road with a water crossing linking Yitzhar and the Tzon Aviezer farm, paid for by a crowdfunding campaign, and invited families to visit (Elisha Yered).

items.headline: Homesh yeshiva opens a branch in Area A on land of the village of Yasid; the army says it removed the site once and it went back up
items.summary: Haaretz reported on 18 November that a new site set up a few weeks ago serves as a branch of the Homesh yeshiva, whose main campus is at Homesh in northern Samaria. The branch is on land of the Palestinian village of Yasid, in Area A, which Israelis are barred from entering, in an area where infrastructure had been laid for a new Palestinian neighborhood. The army told Haaretz it removed the site once and that it was rebuilt. Haaretz quotes a Palestinian landowner who says owners cannot approach their land, and counts more than 30 sites set up in PA-controlled areas without approval from the government or the army (Haaretz). The yeshiva has not commented in reports that were opened.

places.name: Yasid (Area A)
places.note: Nominatim village point; the branch itself is not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: Civil Administration enforcement in six sectors clears nearly 100 dunams of land taken illegally in Area C; equipment seized at the Nahal Arugot nature reserve
items.summary: Civil Administration officers and its inspection unit, with IDF forces, finished a broad enforcement operation in six sectors on Thursday, 19 November, Israel Hayom reported. Dozens of illegal Palestinian structures were taken down and close to 100 dunams of illegally seized land in Area C were cleared. The largest clearance was at Deir Ibzi' in Binyamin, where two structures were removed and nearly 90 dunams cleared, including seven dunams planted with olive trees. At Bidya in the Ephraim sector, illegal drilling and pumping of water was stopped and the equipment seized; near Jericho a four-dunam compound with two structures and a water pool was removed; three homes and farm buildings were razed in the seam zone at Beit Awwa and Deir Samit; work was stopped on an industrial hangar near Tene Omarim; land seizures with about 100 trees were cleared at Wadi Artas and Battir; and a scrapyard beside the security fence at Hizma was removed (Israel Hayom; Kan also reported the operation). Separately, the inspection unit seized several engineering vehicles that were doing illegal work in the agreed nature reserve in the Judean Desert near Nahal Arugot, in an air and ground operation; Minister Bezalel Smotrich said "we will not allow anyone to take over its land" (Arutz 7). The Palestinian side's account, from Raya radio, says forces took two excavators belonging to the al-Tarwa and Abu Nur families "while they were extracting stone" in the Sa'ir desert area east of Hebron, and that settlers burned a third (Raya). The two reports appear to describe the same operation, but this is not confirmed, and the arson claim has no Israeli confirmation.
items.source: Civil Administration / Israel Hayom / Arutz 7 / Raya

places.name: Nahal Arugot (Judean Desert reserve)
places.note: Nominatim stream point; the exact work site is not published (approximate)

items.headline: Stones smash a window of an Israeli bus at the lower Hizma roundabout on Route 437 overnight; masked men stone a ranger of the Ma'ale Tidhar farm
items.summary: Stones thrown during the night of 18 to 19 November smashed a window of an Israeli passenger bus at the lower Hizma roundabout on Route 437 in Binyamin; no one was hurt (JSR; Simcha Raz). On Thursday morning masked Arabs threw stones at a ranger vehicle of the Ma'ale Tidhar farm, which JSR places in the Gush Etzion region; there were no injuries or damage (JSR; Simcha Raz; Netanel Frankel). JSR's tally for Wednesday, 18 November: three attacks on Jewish shepherds and two stone attacks on vehicles across Judea and Samaria, with one Israeli hurt (JSR). Ayelet Lash also wrote of stones thrown on Thursday at a car at Funduq and at cars at the Dhahiriya junction, with windows broken; those two reports are unconfirmed (Ayelet Lash).
items.source: JSR / Simcha Raz (Olam Katan) / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew) / Ayelet Lash

places.note: Hizma village point (Nominatim); the roundabout is nearby (approximate)

places.note: Nominatim, as in earlier desk items

items.headline: Border Police undercover unit seizes a Fatah man suspected of promoting attacks in Tubas; Hebron man held for threatening to kill Jerusalem deputy mayor Aryeh King
items.summary: Undercover Border Police officers in Judea and Samaria, acting on Shin Bet intelligence, arrested a Fatah activist suspected of promoting terror activity and attacks on Thursday, 19 November, in a covert raid on a building in Tubas, in the Menashe Brigade sector; the operation ended without incident (Channel 14; also reported by Srugim and Israel Hayom). It came a day after the same unit arrested two Fatah men in Aqqaba (reported here on 19 November). Separately, police said a Hebron resident in his 20s was arrested on the night of Tuesday, 17 November, on suspicion of sending death threats to Jerusalem deputy mayor Aryeh King and threatening a terror act. A covert inquiry by the Jerusalem central unit's fraud and cyber department traced him, and police, Hebron station officers and Judea Brigade troops raided his home in the city and seized his phone. He was to be brought before the Ofer military court on Thursday, and a gag order covers other details until 26 November (Maariv; Kan and Ynet also reported the arrest).
items.source: Border Police / Israel Police / Channel 14 / Maariv / Kan

items.headline: Police break up a ring selling forged Israeli ID cards to Palestinians for about 500 shekels; a car stolen in Kfar Saba stopped on its way to Judea and Samaria; two Emmanuel factories closed over illegal workers
items.summary: Detectives of the Judea and Samaria police district's minorities unit arrested a Palestinian from the Hebron area on Wednesday night, 18 November, in the act of selling forged Israeli ID cards, after an undercover agent bought cards from him; three forged cards were found on him. Police say the ring supplied cards for about 500 shekels in cash so Palestinians could enter Israel without a permit posing as other people. A second Hebron-area man, suspected of entering Israel with a card he bought, was arrested near Beit Yehoshua (Behadrei Haredim, citing police; Israel Hayom also reported it). On the same night, Border Police and Central District police stopped an attempt to move a car stolen in Kfar Saba into Judea and Samaria and arrested two suspects after they tried to escape a roadblock on Route 444 (Channel 14). HaKol HaYehudi reported that Ariel police found four Palestinians staying illegally, from Nablus, Deir Istiya and Jamma'in, working without permits in the Emmanuel industrial zone on 18 November, and that two factories there were closed after the inquiry (HaKol HaYehudi; the closures are unconfirmed in other outlets).
items.source: Israel Police / Behadrei Haredim / Channel 14 / HaKol HaYehudi

places.name: Emmanuel (industrial zone nearby)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Emmanuel; the industrial zone is not mapped

items.headline: Channel 14: the chief of staff is holding up Maj. Gen. Dado Bar Kalifa's entry as head of Central Command, which runs Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Channel 14 military correspondent Hallel Bitton Rosen reported on 19 November that although Defense Minister Israel Katz and Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir agreed months ago that Maj. Gen. Dado Bar Kalifa would take over Central Command from Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, Zamir has refused to set a date for the handover. Senior defense officials quoted by the channel say he is waiting to see whether a left-wing government forms or new elections are called, and that a new government might cancel the appointment. The IDF Spokesperson replied that Bar Kalifa, "as recommended by the chief of staff and approved by the defense minister," was agreed for the post; the copy that was opened breaks off before the reply gives an entry date (Channel 14). Channel 04 ran a similar report on 18 November. Central Command is in charge of the army in Judea and Samaria.

items.headline: JSR: PA Ramallah governor Laila Ghannam attends a Chinese Embassy aid signing; JSR also posts a PA-area poster calling to "set the land ablaze" under settlers; mother of the 2017 Armon Hanatziv attacker deported
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) reported on 19 November that Laila Ghannam, the PA's governor of Ramallah and al-Bireh, attended the signing of a cooperation agreement between the Chinese Embassy to the PA and the Al-Zaytouna Association, under which China will fund aid for university students. JSR says Ghannam meets with terrorists weekly and last week attended a funeral where Hamas flags were flown (JSR). The same day JSR posted an Arabic poster, which it describes as incitement in the PA, showing a masked gunman and burning figures of Jews over a map, with the text "From Jenin to Hebron, from Nablus to Ramallah, let us set the land ablaze under the feet of the renegade settlers"; JSR did not say where it was published (JSR Telegram). In Jerusalem, Channel 14 Arab-affairs reporter Omri Haim reported that police found and arrested the mother of the terrorist who carried out the 2017 truck attack on the Armon Hanatziv promenade, which killed four soldiers, after she had lived in Jabel Mukaber for years without a permit, and deported her to PA territory. Police acted about three days after the channel's report. Merav and Herzl Hajaj, parents of Lt. Shir Hajaj, who was killed in the attack, called it "a first step" and asked that a law revoking the residency of terrorists' relatives be allowed to take effect (Channel 14).

places.name: Ramallah and al-Bireh
