items.headline: Hebron Hills council head: two banks have halted foreign-currency trade accounts after the British sanctions; he asks the government to protect the companies hit
items.summary: Eliram Azoulay, head of the Hebron Hills (Har Hebron) Regional Council, said two banks told him they were instructed to stop foreign-currency trade accounts, HaKol HaYehudi reported on 19 November, citing his interview with Roi Katz on the Knesset Channel. The Har Hebron development company is one of the eight building, development and architecture firms Britain sanctioned on Tuesday. Azoulay also said other companies in Judea and Samaria report being cut off from Gmail, Microsoft and cloud services; those companies were not named (HaKol HaYehudi). The Times of Israel, in a headline and summary opened for this edition, reported that the council's foreign-currency accounts were frozen and that Azoulay fears insurance companies will refuse to work with the council for fear of secondary sanctions. Eliav Libi, a farmer on the Australian sanctions list, said he spoke about the sanctions and about settlement in Areas A and B in an interview with Ofer Hadad on Channel 12 on 19 November (Eliav Libi).
items.source: HaKol HaYehudi / Times of Israel / Eliav Libi

places.name: Hebron Hills (area)
places.note: approximate, as in earlier desk items

items.headline: Court orders activist Arik Ascherman to pay 60,000 shekels to a Kochav HaShahar family he filmed and accused of invading land
items.summary: The Jerusalem Magistrate's Court ordered Arik Ascherman, head of the left-wing group Torat Tzedek, to pay damages and costs totaling 60,000 shekels to a family from Kochav HaShahar for libel and invasion of privacy. In 2024 Ascherman filmed six members of the family, parents and children, on a walk in open country near Nahal Yitav, accused them of "invading lands" and "trampling the law," and broadcast it live on Facebook with the children's faces visible. Judge Tali Lahav found the invasion claim was not proved, noted that the family was walking in open land that was neither fenced nor farmed, and said Ascherman admitted he published before checking the facts. The family was represented by attorney Menashe Yado of the Honenu legal aid group (Arutz 7; Elchanan Groner).

places.name: Kochav HaShahar
places.note: Nominatim; the Nahal Yitav walk site is not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: Five Kafr Kana men charged over a home garage that repaired guns for criminals; Negev police seize mosque loudspeakers in Tel Sheva; state asks a year's delay on Bedouin buildings on Jewish land near Nevatim
items.summary: The Northern District prosecution on Thursday, 19 November, indicted five Kafr Kana residents aged 32 to 43 over a weapons workshop that police say ran in a home garage, repairing guns for criminal groups, and asked that they be held until the end of proceedings. After weeks of surveillance, police raided the garage about two weeks ago with a drone and found two disassembled M16 rifles, many gun parts and tools. Police say about 800 weapons have been seized in the Northern District since the start of the year (Channel 14; also posted by Elchanan Groner). In the Negev, police with Border Police and city patrol officers disconnected and seized the sound system of a building used as a mosque in Tel Sheva after repeated noise complaints, earlier fines and warnings (Arutz 7). Regavim said that at a hearing this week the state asked for another year to carry out a court ruling given more than three years ago against hundreds of illegal structures on private Jewish land in the Negev, citing a complex mapping process (Regavim); Olam Katan reported the request and identified the site as near Nevatim (Olam Katan). In the Triangle, Faris Abu Ghazaleh, 74, was shot dead in his shop in Ar'ara months after his son and grandson were killed, and Raya counts 185 killings in Arab society since the start of the year (Raya); the count is unconfirmed by police.
items.source: Israel Police / Channel 14 / Arutz 7 / Regavim / Olam Katan / Raya

places.name: Nevatim (area of the illegal structures)
places.note: Nominatim community point; the structures are not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian outlets report IDF incursions into al-Rafid and near Jubata al-Khashab, and a blast where troops were clearing ground near Saida al-Jawlan
items.summary: Syrian outlets reported several IDF moves in Quneitra province on Thursday, 19 November. Syria TV said Merkava tanks entered the edge of Jubata al-Khashab in the northern countryside in the morning (Syria TV). The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported a new incursion into the town of al-Rafid in the southern countryside (SOHR), and local sources quoted by Sham TV in the evening put the force there at nine military vehicles (Sham TV). Daraa 24 reported an explosion west of Mazraat Saida al-Jawlan, at a site where Israeli forces were bulldozing, probably the detonation of mines (Daraa 24). Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemned the incursions in Quneitra and Daraa (Sijil News). The IDF did not comment in the reports that were opened, and these are the Syrian side's accounts. Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new about the area.
items.source: Syria TV / SOHR / Sham TV / Daraa 24

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: settlers cut the water line to al-Masoudiya near Burqa; a house in Deir ad-Dik razed despite a High Court freeze, which the state calls "human error"
items.summary: Raya radio quoted a local land committee official who said settlers cut the water line to the al-Masoudiya area on Burqa land, northwest of Nablus, on 19 November, and that power there has been cut for two months (Raya). Raya also reported an army raid in Tuqu' with tear gas and journalists and council members held in Kharas (Raya). Ultra Palestine, citing Haaretz, said a house of a 68-year-old widow and 31 relatives in Deir ad-Dik, west of Salfit, was demolished last Tuesday although the High Court had frozen the demolition on 11 September; the state prosecution called it "human error" (Ultra Palestine). Breaking the Silence protested the administrative detention of Mehdi Tunsi, a 26-year-old Hebrew University student from East Jerusalem (Breaking the Silence), and Haaretz and Times of Israel headlines say a court extended his detention; the security grounds have not been published. +972 Magazine reported renewed army drills in the Masafer Yatta firing zone (headline only; the page was blocked).
items.source: Raya / Ultra Palestine / Haaretz / Breaking the Silence / +972

items.headline: Army and Civil Administration finish a three-sector enforcement drive in Area C: 21 dunams cleared in Ephraim, greenhouses and tents removed in the Jordan Valley, and two occupied two-story buildings taken down in the Hebron Hills
items.summary: The Civil Administration and the IDF completed a coordinated enforcement operation against what they call illegal Palestinian building and land seizure in Area C, officials said on Wednesday, 18 November, describing work carried out over the previous day. In the Ephraim Brigade area, forces cleared about 21 dunams in the villages of Ras Atiya and Burqin, including about 200 olive saplings and 60 mature olive trees that the administration says were planted on land taken unlawfully (Srugim; Walla; Jerusalem Post, citing the army and COGAT). In the Jordan Valley, forces took down a greenhouse compound of about two dunams, a cluster of residential tents, storerooms and concrete shade structures in Bardala and Ein al-Beida. In the Judea Brigade area, they acted against two occupied two-story buildings at Khirbat Adirat in the south Hebron Hills, the same vicinity that Tuesday's edition already recorded from activist accounts as al-Dirat, east of Yatta. The army and the Civil Administration said they will keep enforcing the law against illegal building and land grabs in Judea and Samaria. The official account did not name any Jewish outposts in this operation.
items.source: Civil Administration / IDF / Srugim / Walla / Jerusalem Post

places.name: Khirbat Adirat, east of Yatta
places.note: Yatta town point (Nominatim); Adirat itself is not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: Explosive device with a PLO flag found near the Gilad farm is neutralized by an army bomb technician; the Yesha Council says Palestinians put it there
items.summary: An explosive device with a PLO flag attached to it was found on Wednesday morning, 18 November, near the Gilad farm in Samaria, the Yesha Council said. The council said Palestinians had placed the charge. Army forces called a bomb technician, who neutralized it, and no one was hurt (Walla, quoting the council; JSR Hebrew). JNS Hebrew reporter Netanel Frankel included the same incident in his end-of-day list, citing the Situation Room (Netanel Frankel). The army did not issue a separate public statement that was opened for this edition.
items.source: Yesha Council / Walla / JSR / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew)

places.name: Havat Gilad
places.note: Nominatim; exact find spot not published (approximate)

items.headline: Hundreds of Vizhnitz Hasidim, led by the rebbe's three sons, pray at Joseph's Tomb in Nablus for his recovery; Samaria council head Yossi Dagan joins them
items.summary: Hundreds of Vizhnitz Hasidim entered Joseph's Tomb in Nablus on Wednesday night, 18 November, for a special prayer for the recovery of the Vizhnitz rebbe, Rabbi Yisrael Hager, 14 years after the rebbe himself visited the site and fixed a mezuzah there. The gathering was led by his three sons, Rabbi Chaim Meir Hager, Rabbi Yaakov Mordechai Hager and Rabbi Yitzchak Yeshayahu Hager. They were joined by the rabbi of Samaria, Rabbi Eliyakim Levanon, and by the head of the Samaria Regional Council, Yossi Dagan, who greeted the rabbis and spoke a blessing for the rebbe's recovery, tying the visit to building and holding the land (Srugim). The same son's earlier visit with Dagan a few months ago was also recalled in the report.

items.headline: Undercover Border Police and Shin Bet arrest two Fatah men suspected of planning an attack, after a chase in Aqaba; forces also operate in Zababida
items.summary: Undercover Border Police from the Judea and Samaria unit, directed by Shin Bet, arrested two Fatah operatives overnight into Wednesday, 18 November, on suspicion of advancing terrorist activity and planning an attack, in a joint statement from the police and Shin Bet. The wanted men were sought in the village of Aqaba, in the Menashe Brigade area; they tried to flee as the force closed in, and both were caught after a pursuit. At the same time the force also operated in nearby Zababida. No members of the force were hurt (Maariv; Ynet; Jerusalem Post; JDN). Israel Hayom's settlements reporter Yotam Deshe noted that Fatah is the movement of PA chairman Mahmoud Abbas, and set the arrests against Britain's sanctions on Israeli firms in Judea and Samaria the same week (Yotam Deshe).
items.source: Israel Police / Shin Bet / Maariv / Ynet / Jerusalem Post / Yotam Deshe (Israel Hayom)

items.headline: Owner of the Halomot Yosef farm in the Dotan Valley is hurt in a stick attack; the army holds two Palestinian suspects and says the details are under review
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria Situation Room reported on Wednesday, 18 November, that Arabs attacked the owner of the Halomot Yosef farm (also called Emek Dotan) in northern Samaria with sticks, and that the farmer was hurt (JSR Hebrew). The army later told JNS that troops had detained two Palestinian suspects after a report of an attack on an Israeli civilian in Samaria, and that "the details are under review" (JNS). Netanel Frankel carried the Situation Room's account in his daily list (Netanel Frankel). The army's statement to JNS did not itself name the farm or describe the injuries in more detail.
items.source: JSR / JNS / IDF / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew)

places.name: Halomot Yosef / Emek Dotan farm, northern Samaria
places.note: Nominatim 'Emek Dotan' village point in Area C; the farm itself is not separately mapped (approximate)

items.headline: Stones thrown at a shepherd, and later at a flock, at the Malachei Avraham farm in the Hebron Hills; no one is hurt, JSR and Simcha Raz say
items.summary: The Situation Room reported two incidents on Wednesday, 18 November, at the Malachei Avraham farm in the Hebron Hills: Arabs threw stones at a Jewish shepherd, and later threw stones at a flock and prevented it from returning to the farm. It said no one was hurt (JSR Hebrew, first incident; JSR Hebrew, second incident). Olam Katan's settlements reporter Simcha Raz, quoting the Situation Room, wrote that this was again "terror against the Malachei Avraham farm" (Simcha Raz). The farm itself is not in the public map sources checked for this edition, so it is not plotted here.

items.headline: Paratroopers seize a sewage tanker between Beit El and Ofra after residents of the new Kfar Ana site track it with a drone; the driver says the truck broke down
items.summary: Residents of the new Kfar Ana site in Binyamin spotted a sewage tanker in a stream bed near Beit El on Tuesday, 17 November, followed it with a drone and called the authorities. Fighters from Paratroop Battalion 202 seized the truck; the driver said it had a mechanical fault, and the soldiers had it towed to a confiscation lot, Arutz 7 reported on Wednesday (Arutz 7; JDN). The area is between Beit El and Ofra. Residents said pirate dumps and sewage dumping had gone on for years in the wadis, and that since the site was founded a few months ago they have been trying to shut that activity down. The Situation Room said an Arab was filmed dumping sewage into a stream near Beit El and that the army caught the tanker while the dumping was still going on (JSR Hebrew); Arutz 7 and JDN describe the tanker as having been stopped and seized on suspicion of dumping, not as a confirmed completed dump. Netanel Frankel also listed the incident, citing JSR (Netanel Frankel).
items.source: Arutz 7 / JDN / JSR / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew)

places.name: Kfar Ana / Khirbet Kfar Ana, between Beit El and Ofra
places.note: Nominatim archaeological site 'Khirbet Kfar Ana' near Ein Yabrud; the new community itself is not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: JSR: Brazil's ambassador to the PA attended a funeral in Silwad last week where Hamas flags were flown beside Fatah flags
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria Situation Room reported on Wednesday, 18 November, that Brazil's ambassador to the Palestinian Authority, Joao Marcelo Queiroz Soares, attended a funeral last week in Silwad, in the heart of Judea and Samaria, and that Hamas flags were flown there alongside Fatah flags (JSR English; JSR Hebrew). This is the Situation Room's account; a second, independent confirmation of the ambassador's attendance was not found in the sources opened for this edition.

items.headline: Police and Border Police arrest a father and son from al-Eizariya after footage showed a dog thrown from a hilltop and killed
items.summary: Samaria and Judea District police, acting on information received during the past week, said they identified two residents of al-Eizariya, a father and son in their 20s and 60s, in security-camera footage showing a dog thrown from a hilltop in the village with a rope around its neck; the dog was killed. Overnight into Wednesday, 18 November, the Gilad serious-crime unit and Border Police fighters in Judea and Samaria arrested the two men. They were questioned at the Ma'ale Adumim station and held, and the police said they would ask a court to extend the detention. The police said they treat violence and cruelty to animals severely and will use all investigative means to bring those involved to court (Srugim, quoting the police; JSR English, also using police footage).

places.name: al-Eizariya
places.note: Nominatim town point; exact hilltop not published (approximate)

items.headline: Fire in a mosque in Kfar Daha, near Afula, before dawn; police and fire investigators are on the scene, and Shin Bet is checking a possible nationalist motive. Ynet says Hebrew graffiti was sprayed on the building
items.summary: A fire broke out before dawn on Thursday, 19 November, in a mosque in the village of Daha (Dahi), near Afula. Firefighters and police put out the flames and kept them from spreading through the building. Police opened an investigation with fire-service investigators. Kikar Hashabbat, citing the circumstances, said Shin Bet has joined the inquiry and is checking a possible nationalist motive (Arutz 7; Kikar Hashabbat, quoting a police statement). Ynet, in a headline and summary opened for this edition, reported a suspicion of arson as a hate crime and said Hebrew graffiti was sprayed on the building (Ynet). Israel Hayom's headline treated it as a suspected reprisal attack and noted that about two weeks earlier a 15-year-old Arab was charged with trying to burn Torah scrolls; the police statement itself did not name a motive (Israel Hayom). No suspects had been named in the reports that were opened.
items.source: Israel Police / Arutz 7 / Kikar Hashabbat / Ynet / Israel Hayom

items.headline: Jewish driver held after eight people are hurt in a ramming at several spots in Kafr Qasim; police say the main suspicion is driving under the influence of drugs, and they are also checking a nationalist motive. Residents call it an attack
items.summary: Eight people were hurt on Wednesday evening, 18 November, when a Jewish Israeli driver hit pedestrians at several points inside Kafr Qasim, in the Triangle. Three were in moderate condition and five were lightly hurt, and the driver was arrested (Srugim; Ynet). Police said the leading suspicion at this stage was driving under the influence of drugs, and that they were also examining a possible nationalist motive; the motive had not been determined. Residents of Kafr Qasim called the ramming an attack. Ultra Palestine described the driver as a settler and said three of those hurt were women leaving a wedding hall, which is its account (Ultra Palestine). The investigation is continuing.

items.headline: President Herzog criticizes the police for arresting Ra'am activists in the Negev on election day without search or arrest warrants
items.summary: President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, 18 November, criticized the police over the arrest of Ra'am activists in the Negev on election day, after they were suspected of a scheme to interfere with the vote. Herzog said it is not permitted to enter a citizen's home, including the home of a Bedouin doctor in the Negev, without a court warrant, and that citizens' rights must be protected "no matter where they come from" (Srugim). Srugim described the remarks as unusual for the president and noted that he had been relatively quiet on the election-interference investigation until now. This item reports his criticism; it does not settle the underlying police case.

items.headline: Activist and PA-side claims: Ultra Palestine says forces arrested Jerusalem journalist Seif al-Qawasmi after an assault and the smashing of his vehicle at the Jaba checkpoint, north of Jerusalem
items.summary: Ultra Palestine reported on Wednesday evening, 18 November, that Israeli forces arrested Jerusalem journalist Seif al-Qawasmi after he was assaulted and his vehicle was smashed at the Jaba checkpoint, north of Jerusalem (Ultra Palestine). This is Ultra Palestine's account; an Israeli official statement on the incident was not found in the sources opened for this edition.

items.headline: Britain sanctions eight settlement builders and the Tzav 9 movement, and Australia lists Daniella Weiss, Eliav Libi, Nachala, Amana and Hashomer Yosh; Sa'ar promises countermeasures, and council heads say the building will go on
items.summary: On Tuesday, 17 November, Britain's Foreign Office put asset freezes and bans on serving as company directors on eight Israeli construction, development and architecture firms that it says plan, build, supply or market housing and public infrastructure in Judea and Samaria, and on Tzav 9, the Israeli protest movement that blocked aid convoys to Gaza. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband tied the step to the E1 tender, which he said was near its final deadlines: "do not bid, do not build, and do not profit" (UK government). The firms, as listed by Olam Katan's settlements reporter Simcha Raz: the Har Hevron Development Company, Hemdat Shomron, S.A.G., Lev HaHar Initiatives, Harei Zahav, Ariel Megurim Yehuda VeShomron, Ami Gvirtzman Architects 2021 and Z.F. Building Company (Simcha Raz). Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar called it "a hostile act against private, law-abiding companies," said "Israel will not surrender and will not change its policy under outside pressure," and said the government will look for new ways to strengthen settlement in Judea and Samaria and to protect everyone building there; he promised countermeasures (Srugim). Samaria council head Yossi Dagan: "We will build our homeland even more. Before them we built, and after them we will build" (Srugim). Yesha Council chairman Yisrael Gantz said Britain had "declared economic war on Israel" (quoted by Simcha Raz), and Beit Aryeh-Ofarim council head Sharon Alfasi said "the future of Israeli settlement will not be decided in London" (quoted by Simcha Raz). Peace Now said Netanyahu and Smotrich had dragged Israel into "a heavy diplomatic and economic price" (Arutz 7). That evening (18 November in Australia) Australia listed three people, Daniella Weiss, Itamar Yehuda Levi and Eliav Libi, and four bodies, Amana, the Nachala movement, Hashomer Yosh and the Eyal Hari Yehuda construction company, for financial sanctions, with travel bans on the three people (Australian foreign ministry). Foreign Minister Penny Wong said it is the first time Australia has targeted a construction company, told Australian businesses not to bid on settlement tenders, and cited E1 (Penny Wong). Haaretz reporter Liza Rozovsky wrote that all of those named are already under British or European sanctions (Liza Rozovsky). Eliav Libi, a farmer and Farms Association board member whom this desk follows, had not commented on the listing by the time of this edition (see the separate item on his post about Susya).
items.source: UK government / Australian government / Srugim / Arutz 7 / Simcha Raz (Olam Katan)

items.headline: Attorney general orders the E1 bid envelopes kept shut until a new government is formed; Ma'ale Adumim's mayor says the city will petition the High Court
items.summary: Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara told the Israel Land Authority not to open the bids in the tender for building in E1 until a new government is formed, after the opening had already been put off until after the elections, Channel 14's Yinon Magal first reported on Tuesday (Srugim; Arutz 7). The tender is for 1,234 housing units; Israel Hayom's settlements reporter Yotam Deshe, who reported earlier that the attorney general had pushed the bid deadline (first set for 19 October, eight days before the elections) past the vote, wrote: "It is happening again" (Yotam Deshe). Ma'ale Adumim mayor Guy Yifrach said the city will petition the High Court to have the envelopes opened without delay, and said the attorney general told the court only a month ago that she would allow them to be opened on 19 November: "We will not let the future of Ma'ale Adumim and the advancement of Mevaseret Adumim be made hostages" (Arutz 7). Minister Itamar Ben Gvir: "The attorney general is not the government and not the housing minister" (Arutz 7). Simcha Raz called the delay "a scandal" (Simcha Raz). Earlier on Tuesday, Peace Now, Bimkom and Ir Amim, through attorney Michael Sfard, had written to the attorney general asking for exactly this step, citing the risk of sanctions (Peace Now). The British sanctions announcement the same day referred to "the final deadlines for the E1 tender" (see the item above).
items.source: Srugim / Arutz 7 / Yotam Deshe (Israel Hayom) / Peace Now

places.name: Ma'ale Adumim (E1 lies between it and Jerusalem)
places.note: Nominatim city point; the E1 area itself is not plotted (approximate)

items.headline: Army's first probe of the Jericho attack: a head-on ramming and an assault with clubs, hoes and stones, checked as a planned ambush; two suspects held; the Palestinian woman who died was probably hit by an Israeli civilian firing at stone throwers
items.summary: The IDF Spokesperson released first findings on Tuesday evening, as reported by Ynet. The attack took place on the outskirts of Jericho in Area A, next to Area C, "in an area that Israelis are barred by law from entering." During "a violent friction," attackers drove head-on into an Israeli car and assaulted the Israelis with clubs, hoes and stones, and the army is checking whether it was a planned ambush. More Palestinians then threw stones from behind a wall, more Israeli civilians arrived, and several of them fired toward where the stones came from. The army says the Palestinian woman who was killed was "probably" hit by an Israeli civilian's fire aimed at the stone throwers and that the circumstances are still under review; three Israeli civilians and four Palestinians were hurt, Judea and Samaria District police opened an investigation, and the two suspects in the ramming and assault were arrested (Ynet). Channel 14's military correspondent Hallel Bitton Rosen reported the security establishment's assessment that the cell planned the attack in advance and lay in wait for the Israeli car (Channel 14). Ynet gives the woman's age as 72; the PA side (Raya, citing local sources) names her as Fidda Muhammad Fheidat, 60, says 10 others were wounded by settler fire, and says the army closed Jericho's southern and two northern entrances (Raya). The age difference is not resolved. A Haaretz headline says a witness described 15 settlers entering Area A and one firing in all directions; the article is behind a paywall and was not read. The first reports of the attack are in the 17 November edition.

places.name: Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta, Jericho (near the new Jewish homes)
places.note: Nominatim neighborhood point; exact attack spot not published (approximate)

items.headline: Smotrich at the Herbst farm hours after the attack: the farm, the bought homes and "Dia" are "renewing Jewish settlement in Jericho"; Karhi orders faster cell antennas for 11 new northern Samaria communities
items.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Binyamin council head and Yesha Council chairman Yisrael Gantz came on Tuesday morning, with the Settlement Administration, to the Herbst family farm on the edge of Jericho and met Hanan and Leah Herbst and the heads of the Nachala movement, Channel 14 reports. Smotrich called Monday night's attack "a very serious lynch attempt" by "rioting terrorists from the outskirts of Jericho" and said: "The farm here, the homes that were bought and 'Dia', a community we are establishing in the area, are renewing Jewish settlement in Jericho for the first time since the founding of the State of Israel. Jericho is the lock of the Land of Israel... we are coming back here" (Channel 14). The families moved last week into a compound bought jointly by Nachala, the Binyamin council and the Armonot farm (Netanel Frankel, JNS Hebrew); an earlier cabinet decision listed Armonot as the new name of the Dia site (see earlier desk items). In northern Samaria, Communications Minister Shlomo Karhi toured Hinanit with Samaria council head Yossi Dagan and said he has ordered faster installation of cellular antennas in the 11 communities set up in the area in recent months, and that six older communities will be connected to fiber optics. Karhi: "While some in the Knesset choose to cooperate with terror supporters and challenge our historic right to the land of our fathers, we give them a decisive answer, strengthen Jewish settlement in Judea and Samaria and set facts on the ground" (Arutz 7; Netanel Frankel). In the Hebron Hills, Elisha Yered posted that at the Ozri farm near Adora, plowing and sowing go on through the night to cover all the land, which he says was worked for decades by "Arab invaders" from the village of Idhna (Elisha Yered; his claim about the land's past use was not checked).
items.source: Channel 14 / Arutz 7 / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew) / Elisha Yered

items.headline: Three masked men attack four Hanina farm shepherds near Ramun with stones and clubs while two others steal the farm's vehicle; about 20 stone three shepherds near Duma; an Israeli lightly hurt by a Palestinian car at the Havat Gilad junction
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) reported on Tuesday afternoon that three masked Arabs attacked four Jewish shepherds from Hanina's farm with stones and clubs near the American academy at Ramun in Binyamin, while two others stole the farm's vehicle; apparently no one was hurt (JSR; also Netanel Frankel; Simcha Raz). Later, about 20 Arabs threw stones at three Jewish shepherds near Duma; no injuries, but the shepherds' Ranger was damaged (JSR). On Tuesday night a Palestinian car hit an Israeli at the Havat Gilad junction; he was lightly hurt and treated by Hatzalah Yosh medics (Arutz 7). Hallel Bitton Rosen reported that the car struck one of a group of Jews gathered near the junction and fled (Hallel Bitton Rosen); Yotam Deshe, after posting video of the incident, wrote that it "does not look to me like an attack" (Yotam Deshe). Whether it was deliberate is not established. Simcha Raz reported that an Arab driver rammed the Ranger of a Givat Or Yehuda resident near Itamar and fled toward Awarta, disabling the vehicle, with no injuries (Simcha Raz); an earlier version of his post placed it near Kiryat Arba, and no second source was found. JSR's tally for Monday, 16 November: six incidents, three attacks on shepherds and three stone attacks on Israelis, with one Israeli hurt (JSR). No new JSR report or weekly survey appeared on its website since the last edition.
items.source: JSR / Arutz 7 / Hallel Bitton Rosen (Channel 14) / Yotam Deshe (Israel Hayom) / Simcha Raz (Olam Katan)

items.headline: 17 bombs found and destroyed in Nur a-Shams; eight wanted men arrested in Sa'ir and a-Shuyukh; Border Police undercover unit catches two Hamas men; Beit Hanina man, 19, charged with planning a bomb and gun attack at the Lions' Gate
items.summary: Security forces found and destroyed 17 explosive devices in the Nur a-Shams camp in western Samaria: 11 pipe bombs, four fire-extinguisher bombs and two bombs built to blow up under vehicles, according to a police photo release passed on by JSR (JSR; Simcha Raz). The Etzion Brigade and Border Police, guided by the Shin Bet, finished an operation on Monday in Sa'ir and a-Shuyukh near Hebron: eight wanted men arrested, more than 80 places searched and more than 30 illegal vehicles confiscated (IDF Spokesperson; Arutz 7). The Border Police undercover unit for Judea and Samaria, guided by the Shin Bet, arrested two wanted Hamas men suspected of activity in the group's military wing; Channel 14 puts the arrests in the Ephraim Brigade area (Arutz 7). An indictment was filed against Muhammad al-Azza, 19, of Beit Hanina, who prosecutors say planned to set off a bomb by remote control at the Lions' Gate and then open fire on Jews and police near the Temple Mount, and spent about two years gathering information, looking up bomb-making instructions and training (Arutz 7; HaKol HaYehudi). Separately, Hallel Bitton Rosen reported on Channel 14 that a plan agreed on Monday at a meeting led by Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir would, in the coming months, take one division out of Gaza and a division headquarters out of Lebanon and cut nine battalions, two in the north, three in the south and four in the Central Command, with no replacement forces; she presents it as preparing for the policy of a left-wing government. No IDF response was found (Hallel Bitton Rosen).
items.source: JSR / IDF Spokesperson / Arutz 7 / HaKol HaYehudi / Hallel Bitton Rosen (Channel 14)

items.headline: Kalashnikovs flown in by balloon near Nitzana and pistols stopped at the Jordan border; Rosh HaAyin, 600 meters from the fence, prepares for a raid; Ben Gvir: the Negev demolitions will go on
items.summary: The army and police stopped an attempt on Monday night to bring Kalashnikov rifles into Israel by balloon over the Egyptian border in the Nitzana area; the weapons were handed to police (IDF Spokesperson; Emanuel Fabian, Times of Israel). Hallel Bitton Rosen put the haul at seven Kalashnikovs and reported that on Tuesday morning the Northern District police border unit and reservists of Battalion 1861 stopped the smuggling of five pistols across the Jordan border near a community her post spells "Lirdena" (probably Yardena in the Beit She'an Valley; not confirmed) (Hallel Bitton Rosen). Rosh HaAyin mayor Raz Sagi told Arutz 7 that the city, whose homes are 600 meters from the security fence, is setting up firing positions, ordering sniper rifles and enlarging its standby squads to prepare for a raid like that of 7 October, while stressing there is no concrete warning (Arutz 7). Regavim described the PA's "daily race" of building and road paving along the seam line, together with the training of PA security forces, as "a ring of strangulation" around central cities (Regavim). Minister Itamar Ben Gvir answered a Joint List letter asking the attorney general to freeze demolitions in unrecognized Bedouin villages in the Negev: "We will continue to demolish illegal construction, enforce the law and restore governance. We will not give up on the Negev!" (Channel 14; for the planning background see the Khamaisi Plan backgrounder). Two Rahat residents wearing kippot drove into Kibbutz Gvulot without being checked at the gate; police found and questioned them, and the Eshkol council said no criminal or nationalist motive was found (Arutz 7). In Jerusalem, the Honenu legal group appealed to the State Attorney after a case was closed against four Arab bus inspectors suspected of beating a Haredi 17-year-old on line 39A; the appeal says they threatened passengers, deleted recordings and switched off their body cameras (Elchanan Groner; also posted by Ayelet Lash).
items.source: IDF Spokesperson / Emanuel Fabian / Hallel Bitton Rosen / Arutz 7 / Regavim / Channel 14 / Elchanan Groner

places.name: Yardena (Jordan border, probable site)
places.note: Nominatim; the post's place name is unclear (approximate)

items.headline: From the right: Gadi Taub says Netanyahu's Mansour Abbas quote came from a Moran Tal exposé; Ra'am's Ibrahim Hijazi says MK Segalovitz would deal with prisoners and Al-Aqsa
items.summary: Matan Kahana was elected Knesset speaker on Tuesday night with the votes of the Arab parties; Olam Katan called it "a black day" (Netanel Frankel; Olam Katan). Historian Gadi Taub wrote that the quote the prime minister used from Mansour Abbas on a single state came from an exposé by Moran Tal on the Shomer Saf channel (Gadi Taub). A thread by @imshin quoted Moran Tal: "I have heard Mansour Abbas explain dozens of times to an Arab audience that their continued presence on their land within Israel is at risk" (Imshin). Moran Tal also noted that Islamic Movement northern branch networks had described her as being from the "settler" Regavim movement (Moran Tal). Channel 14 reports that Ibrahim Hijazi, a senior Ra'am figure, said in an interview that Ra'am cannot itself handle the issues of Palestinian security prisoners and Al-Aqsa, and named MK Yoav Segalovitz as the answer; Channel 14 describes the host, Ismat Mansour, as a Palestinian terrorist who murdered a Jew. Ra'am said it wants Segalovitz to be in charge of fighting crime in Arab society (Channel 14; also Omri Haim). Writer Meir Ettinger says lawyer Yahya Dahamsheh was presented until August 2026 as head of the Islamic Movement's political bureau and since then as head of Ra'am's political bureau, which he says shows the claimed separation is a spin (Meir Ettinger). These are the writers' claims and views.
items.source: Netanel Frankel / Olam Katan / Gadi Taub / Moran Tal / Channel 14 / Meir Ettinger

items.headline: Elchanan Groner: Palestinian olive harvest right next to the Samaria Brigade headquarters; Telem graffiti protests employing Arab workers; HaKol HaYehudi: forces must guard Eli while the army publicizes 150 secured harvest events
items.summary: Elchanan Groner posted a photo on Tuesday morning of a Palestinian olive harvest beside the Samaria Brigade headquarters and wrote that Palestinians also work inside the base: "Didn't they learn anything from 7 October?" (posted by Hadashot HaGvaot, credited to Groner). HaKol HaYehudi reports that as the harvest season ends, the army's Arabic-language spokesman and the Civil Administration published a video and figures saying more than 150 coordinated harvest events were secured, while soldiers and Border Police were needed to guard communities such as Eli because harvesters came close to homes (HaKol HaYehudi). Groner reported graffiti sprayed at a building site in Telem, in the Hebron Hills, in protest against employing "enemies," an issue he says is stirring the community (Elchanan Groner), and posted video from the Barkai neighborhood of Carmel of what he called a convoy of smugglers' cars driving wildly tens of meters from homes (Elchanan Groner). Ayelet Lash passed on an anonymous message saying contractors working for the Mateh Binyamin council use Arab drivers to transport special-education girls and that the council's hotline said it could not stop this (Ayelet Lash; the writer's claim, not checked), and posted video she says shows Arabs throwing live, bound dogs into a large pool near Ma'ale Efrayim, with residents of a nearby farm rescuing the last one (Ayelet Lash; unconfirmed).
items.source: Elchanan Groner / HaKol HaYehudi / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: Eliav Libi, sanctioned by Australia the same evening, says a house burned with tefillin and holy books inside during an enforcement action at Susya and tells the army and police: "Stop these acts"
items.summary: Farmer and Farms Association board member Eliav Libi wrote on Tuesday night that "the event today in Susya, in which a house was burned with tefillin and holy books inside, and not for the first time," along with house burnings at Nahalat HaNavi, the forceful dispersal of girls at the Malachei HaShalom junction protest and an evacuation in which a bulldozer entered a house while teenagers were on its roof, are "a wake-up call to the entire security system." "Even an enforcement action cannot look like a pogrom," he wrote, and called on the IDF, the police and all law enforcement to make a deep reckoning: "We are brothers" (Eliav Libi). No army or police account of a Tuesday enforcement action at Susya was found, so the details are his. The Malachei HaShalom arrests are in the 17 November edition.

places.note: Nominatim; the site of the burned house is not given (approximate)

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian outlets report artillery and machine-gun fire on Kuwaya during the Yarmouk Basin incursion, a house burned and families leaving; Egypt condemns; Halutzei HaBashan shows its video at a Knesset event
items.summary: The Lebanese outlet Almodon reports that a large Israeli column moved from the Golan to the al-Jazira base late Monday night and on toward Ma'ariya and Abidin; troops beat a driver returning from an olive press and smashed his minibus, heavy fire toward homes in Kuwaya burned one house down, and six artillery shells fell on farmland between the villages, prompting some residents to leave for nearby villages. Kuwaya's mayor, Amjad Suleiman, said mortar fire came from the al-Jazira base (Almodon). Syria's state agency SANA reported that Egypt condemned the incursions in rural Quneitra and Daraa (SANA). No IDF statement on these moves was found; this continues the incursion in the 17 November edition. Halutzei HaBashan, the group pushing for Israeli settlement in the Bashan, posted the video it screened at the Knesset event marking two years since "the liberation of the Hermon crown and parts of the Bashan": "We are back to the Bashan!" (Halutzei HaBashan). Its Telegram channel has posted nothing since July.

items.headline: PA finance minister: a salary date should be set by the end of the week and a World Bank grant of about $300 million is near; Jericho's schools shut after the attack; "Stab the Jews" video circulates in Telegram groups
items.summary: PA Finance Minister Stephan Salameh said on official radio that the government hopes to announce when public employees will be paid within days, likely before the end of the week, while it works "day and night" to secure a minimum salary; he said there are positive signs on a new World Bank grant of about $300 million, part of it for the budget and salaries, and that the previous Israeli government "closed all doors" on releasing the withheld clearance revenues (Raya; the PA side's account). After Monday night's attack, Jericho's education directorate shut all public and private schools in the city on Tuesday, a closure was placed on the city for several hours, and security officials told Ynet that tension among residents has risen sharply and that economic activity and visitor traffic have been hurt (Ynet). JSR reported that a video calling "Stab the Jews!" was being spread on Tuesday morning in Telegram groups in Judea and Samaria (JSR). In Tulkarm, the camp's popular committee says the army issued a military order taking for military use the roads it cut through the Tulkarm and Nur a-Shams camps over destroyed homes, which the committee says will block rebuilding (Raya; the PA side's account, no Israeli confirmation found).

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: demolitions in Kafr ad-Dik and al-Dirat, a new outpost reported at Khashem al-Daraj, olive trees burned in Burqa; Joe Truzman identifies a "numbered" Balata detainee as a former PFLP plotter
items.summary: Ultra Palestine says the army demolished the home of Hamad Marwan Naji in Kafr ad-Dik, west of Salfit, despite a court order to halt (Ultra Palestine), and a family home in al-Dirat, east of Yatta (Ultra Palestine); Simcha Raz described the same day's work as the Civil Administration demolishing illegal Palestinian homes in Masafer Yatta and Kafr ad-Dik (Simcha Raz). The al-Baidar group, quoted by Ultra Palestine, says settlers began a new outpost at Khashem al-Daraj, southeast of Hebron (Ultra Palestine). Raya says settlers set fire to olive trees in Burqa, east of Ramallah, on Tuesday evening (Raya). None of these were confirmed by an Israeli source. Against Palestinian posts comparing Balata detainees marked with numbers to the Nazis, Joe Truzman of FDD's Long War Journal wrote that one of them "sure looks like" Morad Kaabi, arrested years ago by the Shin Bet over a PFLP plot for a shooting attack (Joe Truzman).
items.source: Ultra Palestine / Raya / Simcha Raz / Joe Truzman

places.name: al-Dirat, east of Yatta
places.note: Yatta town point (Nominatim); al-Dirat not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: Attackers ram a car taking Israelis to the new Jericho community, then go at them with axes and clubs; two 18-year-olds lightly hurt, and the Israelis opened fire
items.summary: Shortly after midnight on Tuesday (Israel time), a car carrying Palestinians sped into an Israeli car on the outskirts of Jericho, the IDF says. The attackers got out with weapons and attacked the people in the Israeli car, and after that stones were thrown at the Israelis, who "responded with fire to remove the threat." The army says there are Israeli and Palestinian wounded and that forces are chasing suspects and have set up roadblocks; it calls the details still under review (IDF Spokesperson; Arutz 7). Ynet reports that the two Israelis hurt are 18-year-olds, lightly wounded near the new "HaTmarim" neighborhood and taken to Shaare Zedek hospital, and that they were attacked with clubs and axes; the Binyamin council put the number of Israelis hurt at three (Arutz 7 headline), and Arutz 7 says they were on their way to the new community it calls "Ir HaTmarim" (Ynet; Arutz 7). Channel 14's military correspondent Hallel Bitton Rosen reported four attackers, a well-known farm owner and his son in the Israeli car, and that "accurate fire" killed one female attacker; the IDF statement does not say anyone was killed, so that detail is unconfirmed (Hallel Bitton Rosen). Binyamin council head and Yesha Council chairman Yisrael Gantz: "Terrorists tried to murder Israelis tonight, and thanks to the quick action of the security forces their attempt failed" (quoted by Ynet). The Palestinian side's account: the PA news agency WAFA, citing PA security sources, says a woman, Fidda Muhammad Fheidat, 60, was killed and 10 people were wounded by settler gunfire in Duyuk al-Tahta west of Jericho, and ties the shooting to the eight homes Jews moved into on 4 November (WAFA). The two accounts have not been reconciled. Background: about 20 Jewish families moved into eight homes in Area C near the Hasmonean palaces site early this month (4 November, according to WAFA), in a move led by the Nachala movement with Binyamin council backing; the organizers say the homes were bought in full with ownership papers, and since then movement to and from the homes has been in escorted convoys (Ynet). See the desk items of 14 and 16 November on the Jericho homes.
items.source: IDF Spokesperson / Ynet / Arutz 7 / Hallel Bitton Rosen (Channel 14) / WAFA

places.name: Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta, Jericho (the new Jewish homes are nearby)
places.note: Nominatim neighborhood point; exact attack spot not published (approximate)

items.headline: Palestinian car hits two young Israelis on the access road to Anton farm near Kfar Tapuach and flees to Yasuf; army closes the village, then calls it "friction" rather than a terror attack
items.summary: On Monday at about 5:30 p.m., a Palestinian Hyundai reached the access road to Anton farm next to Kfar Tapuach and hit two Israelis, who were lightly hurt; the driver fled to the village of Yasuf, and troops closed it, Olam Katan's Simcha Raz and Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe reported (Simcha Raz; Yotam Deshe). Raz added that stones were thrown at the troops in Yasuf and a soldier was lightly hurt in the leg (unconfirmed by the army) (Simcha Raz). Later that evening the IDF said that "this was friction between Israeli civilians and Palestinians in the area of the village of Yasuf" (IDF Spokesperson). Samaria council head Yossi Dagan asked the government to treat the event "with the same seriousness" as if it had ended worse, and added that "only the IDF and the security system are authorized to use force" (Srugim). The Palestinian side's account, citing Army Radio, is that settlers from a nearby outpost had gone to the edge of the village before the clash (Raya); the full sequence has not been published.
items.source: Simcha Raz (Olam Katan) / Yotam Deshe (Israel Hayom) / IDF Spokesperson / Srugim / Raya

places.name: Kfar Tapuach (Anton farm nearby)
places.note: Nominatim; the farm is not mapped (approximate)

items.headline: First demolition of a rocket maker's home in Judea and Samaria: army razes the Kafr Ni'ma house of Abdullah Khatib, whose cell built rockets and carried out a launch test
items.summary: IDF troops, Judea and Samaria Border Police and engineering units under the Binyamin Brigade demolished on Monday the home of Abdullah Khatib, who the army says pushed rocket production in Judea and Samaria and was responsible for a rocket launch test. His cell, which also worked on "game-changing" weapons, was arrested by the IDF, Shin Bet and the police counterterror unit in Ramallah in September 2025; rockets and explosives were destroyed and a lathe for making rockets was found. The army calls the demolition "unprecedented," justified by the rocket threat (IDF Spokesperson; Emanuel Fabian, Times of Israel). Raya, a Ramallah outlet close to the PA, says the army blew up two homes in Kafr Ni'ma west of Ramallah, those of prisoners Abdullah al-Khatib and Ibrahim Abu Adi (the second home is not in the IDF statement) (Raya). On Channel 14, its military correspondent Hallel Bitton Rosen argued that home demolitions do not deter and that "you need to take land" (retweeted by Bitton Rosen).
items.source: IDF Spokesperson / Emanuel Fabian / Raya / Channel 14

items.headline: "Reversing the barrels" plan: if PA forces turn their guns on Israel, the PA would be declared an enemy and "war" announced, the cabinet was told; army and Shin Bet see no sign of it now
items.summary: Right-wing reporter Amiel Yarchi reports that the IDF showed ministers a plan, drawn up at their request, for the scenario in which PA security forces turn their weapons on IDF troops and Israeli communities: in response the PA would be defined as an enemy and "war" declared, as the Central Command chief and the defense minister told Sunday night's cabinet meeting. The IDF and Shin Bet told the cabinet there is currently no indication of such a scenario (Amiel Yarchi). Single-source detail, unconfirmed. Israel Hayom and Kan reported on 16 November that the cabinet discussed the scenario (see that day's lead).

items.headline: Elisha Yered: a unit that rushed after stone throwers on a Samaria road was investigated for not waiting while PA police were told and pulled back; HaKol HaYehudi says the warnings go on
items.summary: Settlement activist Elisha Yered reports that an IDF force that got a report overnight of stones thrown at Jewish cars on a Samaria road raced out to cut off and catch the attackers, and that commanders then opened a "serious inquiry" because the force did not wait for the Palestinian security services to be updated and to withdraw first. He says waiting half an hour would have made the response pointless (Elisha Yered). His account is unconfirmed; the road and unit are not named. HaKol HaYehudi writes that about a week after Central Command chief Avi Bluth was reported to have ordered an end to the procedure of updating the PA before arrests, it continues in the field; the IDF told it that "no information is passed to any party that endangers our forces or the success of operations" (HaKol HaYehudi). Activist Ayelet Lash, of Rachelim, posted without giving a source that an army sapper's survey in the Nur Shams camp found a site the army had not known about, with 11 pipe bombs, 4 fire-extinguisher bombs and at least 2 underbelly bombs (unconfirmed) (Ayelet Lash). See the desk items of 7 to 9 and 16 November on the order to stop warning PA forces.
items.source: Elisha Yered / HaKol HaYehudi / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: Binyamin council figures: terror incidents on the Allon Road fell from 459 in 2022 to 52 so far in 2026 as farms along it grew from 3 to 13
items.summary: Data from the Binyamin council's operations center, reported by Channel 14: 459 terror incidents on the Allon Road in 2022, 314 in 2023, 126 in 2024, 131 in 2025 and 52 from January to early November 2026. Over the same years the number of farms along the road rose from three (2022) to six, 11 and 13 (2025). Council head Yisrael Gantz: "the strategic farms protect the road and save lives." Farms Association director Amichai Shahuat (transliteration of the Hebrew) says shepherds going out with their flocks create a buffer between threat sources and the road (Channel 14). The figures are the council's own. Elisha Yered posted on the same day that the Sde Yonatan field-crop farm has finished its first plowing before sowing, below Mitzpe Idit at the back entrance to Ma'ale Mikhmas, a hill from which, he says, hundreds of stone and firebomb attacks on the Allon Road were launched before it was settled (Elisha Yered).

places.name: Allon Road, Binyamin
places.note: Approximate: a point on the Allon Road (Nominatim), as in earlier desk items

places.name: Ma'ale Mikhmas (Mitzpe Idit and Sde Yonatan nearby)
