items.headline: Civil Administration gives notice of at least 28,105 dunams of state land for grazing and 584 dunams for water reservoirs near Fasayil; objections open for 30 days
items.summary: Since the election, the Custodian of Government Property in the Civil Administration has given notice of at least nine grazing allocations totaling 28,105 dunams across Judea and Samaria, plus 584 dunams for water reservoirs near Fasayil in the Jordan Valley, according to the anti-settlement group Peace Now. The notices announce an intention to allocate and give 30 days for objections; they do not name the recipients, and Peace Now says the land is divided among only nine settlers. Counting earlier notices (16,151 dunams in February 2025 and about 533 dunams in January 2026), grazing allocations by the custodian now total 44,182 dunams. Peace Now says the next government should cancel them (Peace Now; Peace Now on X). The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission counts six notices from 12 October to 13 November covering 13,120 dunams, including 12,356 for grazing east of Ramallah and in the northern Jordan Valley, 584 for "engineering works" in the Far'a valley and 180 for farm-produce processing at Qalandiya; it notes these are use permits on land already declared state land, not new declarations (Raya). The two groups' figures differ and have not been checked against the notices.

items.headline: Ambassadors of Panama, Honduras and Guatemala tour Samaria with Yossi Dagan; Panama's envoy calls residents "the buffer of the state"
items.summary: In what Channel 14 calls a first delegation of its kind, the ambassadors of Panama, Honduras and Guatemala toured Samaria on Monday with council head Yossi Dagan, with help from the Israel Allies group, and looked out over the Dan region from the "state's balcony" lookout at Peduel. Honduras's defense attaché also came. Panama's ambassador Ezra Cohen: "We bless the residents of Judea and Samaria; may they continue to be the buffer of the state. You are heroes." Honduras's ambassador José Luis Núñez Bennett: "It is an honor for us to be here" (Channel 14; Simcha Raz).

items.headline: Regavim petitions the Jerusalem District Court to remove a building-materials yard, an unlicensed horse farm and a truck lot built along Begin Road at the city's northern entrance
items.summary: Between the Ben Zion Netanyahu interchange and the Atarot junction, next to Begin Road, a building-materials yard, an unlicensed horse farm and a car and truck parking lot were set up without permits and against a military order banning construction, the land-enforcement group Regavim says in a petition to the Jerusalem District Court demanding immediate enforcement. It cites aerial photos from 2021, 2025 and 2026 and says that in April 2023 the authorities told it the matter was "known and being handled" (Elchanan Groner; Olam Katan; HaKol HaYehudi). Makor Rishon and Channel 14 also ran the story (headlines only seen). The petition text itself was not seen.
items.source: Regavim, via Elchanan Groner / Olam Katan / HaKol HaYehudi

places.name: Begin Road near Atarot, northern Jerusalem
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for the Atarot area; the compounds are not mapped

items.headline: JSR: about 10 "harvesters" stone residents in Or Yedidya farm's grazing land; Hanina farm shepherd stoned; a man reported hurt by stones at Jit junction near Kedumim
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) reported on Monday that about 10 Arab "olive harvesters" threw stones at Israeli residents in the grazing areas of Or Yedidya farm in Samaria, and later three more did so; no one was hurt (JSR Telegram; JSR on X). Stones were also thrown at a shepherd from Hanina farm in Binyamin, with no injuries (JSR). Olam Katan's Simcha Raz reported a man hurt by stones at the Jit junction near Kedumim (no official confirmation found) (Simcha Raz). JSR's tally for Sunday, 15 November: seven incidents, including an attack on a shepherd, three stone attacks on Israeli vehicles, a road blocked with stones, damage to a spring and a suspected arson (JSR). JSR also reported that the official Telegram channel of Saraya al-Quds, Islamic Jihad's military wing in Judea and Samaria, posted praise for the 2002 Worshippers' Way attack in Hebron on its 24th anniversary, calling the three attackers "heroes"; 12 soldiers, Border Police officers and Kiryat Arba response-team members were killed, including Hebron Brigade commander Col. Dror Weinberg (JSR; also Yotam Deshe, Israel Hayom). No new JSR report or weekly survey appeared on its website since 15 November.
items.source: JSR (Yesha Council) / Simcha Raz / Yotam Deshe

places.name: Hanina farm (near Rammun)
places.note: Approximate: point is Rammun village (Nominatim), as in earlier desk items

items.headline: Six arrested, including teenage girls, at a protest against a Palestinian olive harvest at the entrance to Malachei HaShalom; Eli residents object to a harvest beside a neighborhood
items.summary: After a High Court petition filed by al-Mughayyir, large IDF and Border Police forces on Monday allowed Palestinian olive harvesters near Malachei HaShalom and the nearby Gal Yosef farm, Elisha Yered reports; dozens of residents protested and Border Police arrested six, including a girl he says was beaten and pulled by her hair (Elisha Yered). The legal aid group Honenu says about six were held, some of them minors; the girls say they sat quietly by the road and that police called the area a closed military zone without showing an order or map and kept pushing and hitting them after they moved away (Elchanan Groner; Simcha Raz, with Honenu video). No police account was found. Separately, Eli residents were angered by a notice that a harvest would be held Tuesday around the Palgei Mayim neighborhood, with troops and Border Police inside the community; Simcha Raz later clarified that the harvest is next to the community and the forces will be inside it (Simcha Raz).
items.source: Elisha Yered / Honenu via Elchanan Groner and Simcha Raz

places.name: Eli
places.note: Nominatim; Palgei Mayim neighborhood not mapped

items.headline: Weapons seizures: nine guns in Rahat and Negev Bedouin towns, a rifle hidden under stairs in Ar'ara, an M16 and Kalashnikov cache with grenades near Musmus, an M16 at a Nazareth investigator's home
items.summary: Southern District police, the National Guard and Border Police seized two assault rifles, a long gun and six pistols in Rahat and Bedouin towns in the Negev, in Rahat a gun was found in a car fleeing a shooting, and some of those arrested are suspected of shootings tied to a feud between families; in Ar'ara a rifle was found hidden in the floor under a staircase in a house under construction (Channel 14). Near Musmus in Wadi Ara, a police dog led Border Police and Umm al-Fahm detectives to a hidden cache of three M16 rifles, a Kalashnikov, magazines, ammunition and three fragmentation grenades (JDN). In Nazareth, a 62-year-old private investigator was found with an M16 and magazines; HaKol HaYehudi says more than 780 weapons have been seized in the Northern District this year (its figure) (HaKol HaYehudi). Separately, i24NEWS reports that a guard in his 20s at a moshav in the south is suspected of stealing hundreds of rounds and magazines from the standby squad's armory, caught on hidden cameras after a Border Police officer noticed gear missing; police are checking whether it was meant for criminals (i24NEWS). Ayelet Lash names the moshav as Netta and says the guard is Arab; neither detail is in the i24 report (Ayelet Lash).
items.source: Channel 14 / JDN / HaKol HaYehudi / i24NEWS / Ayelet Lash

places.name: Musmus
places.note: Nominatim; cache site in open ground nearby (approximate)

items.headline: From the right: Ra'am's Walid Taha and Ahmad Tibi slated as Knesset deputy speakers; Meir Ettinger reposts Taha's visit to Hamas's Aziz Dweik; Moran Tal on Islamic Movement chants in Kafr Qasim
items.summary: The Knesset arrangements committee was set on Monday to name nine deputy speakers, among them Ahmad Tibi (Joint List) and Walid Taha (Ra'am), reporter Amiel Yarchi wrote (Amiel Yarchi). Smotrich had offered to back Matan Kahana for speaker if he promised not to name deputies from parties that do not call Hamas a terror group; Kahana refused and called the demand "anti-statesmanlike" (Netanel Frankel, JNS Hebrew). Writer Meir Ettinger reposted an older post showing Taha on a visit of support to Hamas leader Aziz Dweik after his release from prison, and other posts on Ra'am's roots in the Muslim Brotherhood (Meir Ettinger). Moran Tal wrote that at conferences and marches of the Islamic Movement's southern branch, youths in Kafr Qasim chant Muslim Brotherhood slogans such as "In the path of Allah we walk... and our blood will be spilled" (Moran Tal). Elchanan Groner reported that the Mossawa center, linked to Hadash, wrote to the heads of the Arab parties proposing joint demands for "leadership roles, centers of influence, policy-making and decision-making" in a government (Elchanan Groner). These are the writers' claims and views.
items.source: Amiel Yarchi / Netanel Frankel / Meir Ettinger / Moran Tal / Elchanan Groner

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian media report a large incursion into Yarmouk Basin villages with house searches and families leaving Kuwaya; tanks at Jubata al-Khashab; Knesset event marks two years on the Hermon
items.summary: Al Arabiya's correspondent reported an Israeli incursion of about 23 military vehicles into villages of the Yarmouk Basin in western Daraa on Monday night, with house raids and heavy fire (Al Arabiya). Local outlet Daraa 24 says troops searched homes in eastern Ma'ariya with 11 vehicles and two troop carriers, and fired machine guns from the edge of Ma'ariya toward Kuwaya, setting a room on fire; Aksalser and others say families left Kuwaya (Daraa 24; Daraa 24; Aksalser). Al Jazeera's Syria Now reported two Merkava tanks at the edge of Jubata al-Khashab in northern Quneitra early Tuesday (Syria Now). No IDF statement on these moves was found. Earlier Monday the IDF confirmed a predawn strike on a weapons shipment meant for Hezbollah on the Syria-Lebanon border, and a Kan report said Syria admits it cannot fully seal the border (retweeted by Itay Blumental, Kan). MK Limor Son Har-Melech (Otzma Yehudit) is holding a Knesset event on Tuesday to give thanks for "the liberation of the Hermon crown and parts of the Bashan," marking two years since the IDF took the Syrian Hermon summit (Netanel Frankel). Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new on X or Telegram since the last edition.
items.source: Al Arabiya / Daraa 24 / Aksalser / Syria Now / Kan / Netanel Frankel

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: High Court orders the army to keep Emek Tirtza farmer Moshe Sharvit off Wadi al-Far'a land; WAFA says a settler rammed eight people in Tuqu'; Israeli rights groups back Al-Haq's director
items.summary: The High Court this week (ACRI dates the ruling 15 November) unanimously accepted a petition by the Association for Civil Rights in Israel and Bimkom for Palestinian residents of Wadi al-Far'a in the Jordan Valley, and ordered the state to take real steps to keep Moshe Sharvit of the Emek Tirtza farm off their land and ensure their access to it; ACRI says the court rejected the state's claim that its actions were enough (ACRI; Takdin). No response from Sharvit was found. WAFA says a settler drove into eight Palestinians gathered near a road accident at Khirbet al-Deir in Tuqu' on Monday evening, then hit them again; no Israeli statement on the incident was found (WAFA). A PA official in Jenin says settlers took over two homes near Mevo Dotan, on Arraba land, and began clearing about 16 dunams (Raya). B'Tselem and other Israeli rights groups called for lifting the travel ban on Al-Haq director Shawan Jabarin (B'Tselem). Elisha Yered says left-wing activists spread an AI-made video of "settlers destroying a Palestinian banana plantation" as proof of Jewish terror (Elisha Yered).
items.source: ACRI / Takdin / WAFA / Raya / B'Tselem / Elisha Yered

items.headline: Security cabinet meets for the first time in six weeks and discusses "reversing the barrels", the scenario in which PA security forces turn their weapons on IDF troops and Israeli communities
items.summary: The security cabinet discussed the plan known as "reversing the barrels" (hipuch kanim), meaning a scenario in which Palestinian Authority security forces turn their guns on IDF troops and on Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria, together with the chief of staff's plans for a possible escalation there, Israel Hayom reports (Israel Hayom). Kan News reports that the cabinet met on Sunday for more than three hours, its first meeting since 5 October, and that Mossad chief Roman Gofman took part and was to update ministers on his talks in the United States (Kan News). Neither outlet reported any decisions. Background: in August, Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir told ministers that the Judea and Samaria Division had trained for this scenario, and reports at the time put the number of armed men in the PA forces at about 60,000 (Behadrei Haredim, 27 Aug; the 60,000 figure is an estimate, not an official count).
items.source: Israel Hayom / Kan News / Behadrei Haredim

items.headline: Despite new orders, the army still told PA forces before two raids, and both came up empty: in a Jericho camp, cameras showed the wanted men leaving 10 minutes before troops arrived
items.summary: Olam Katan reports that two weapons searches carried out over the weekend were coordinated in advance with the Palestinian Authority's security forces, a practice that critics say tips off the targets. In a camp in Jericho on Saturday, security cameras showed the adult men leaving the house about 10 minutes before the soldiers arrived, and the troops found only sleeping children. In Samu'a in the South Hebron Hills the force set out at 12:30 a.m. for two targets and found nothing. Olam Katan says it has no direct proof that the warning caused the failures. The IDF spokesperson's answer: "the procedures were sharpened; it may be that this has not yet reached everyone" (Olam Katan). Settlement activist Elisha Yered, who has campaigned against the coordination, posted the report (Elisha Yered; second post), and Olam Katan's Simcha Raz added comment (Simcha Raz). See the desk items of 7 to 9 November on the order to stop warning PA forces.
items.source: Olam Katan / Elisha Yered / Simcha Raz

items.headline: Standby squads are back in northern Samaria: first two-day training at Sa-Nur, with Samaria council head Yossi Dagan, a reserve captain, among the members
items.summary: The IDF has re-established the standby squads (local armed first-response teams) in the communities of northern Samaria, and the first two-day training was held at Sa-Nur, Olam Katan reports. Members include Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan, a captain in the reserves, along with Akiva Smotrich, Ze'ev Wasserteil, David Padida and the local committee head, Yehoshua Levanon. The weapons come from the IDF; extra equipment was paid for by donors, among them One Israel Fund. A squad also works at Har Eival under security coordinator Binyamin Klein, with committee head Avi Kashi (Olam Katan; Netanel Frankel; Simcha Raz; Olam Katan on X). This comes days after reports that Central Command had halted standby-squad training (desk item of 12 November); the sources do not say whether that order was changed.
items.source: Olam Katan / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) / Simcha Raz

items.headline: Otzma Yehudit MKs Limor Son Har-Melech and Hanamel Dorfman visit the eight Jewish-owned homes in Jericho
items.summary: The two Otzma Yehudit Knesset members toured the eight homes near the Hasmonean palaces site on the edge of Jericho, guided by Nachala chairman Tzvi Elimelech Sharabaf (Olam Katan; Netanel Frankel). See the desk items of 5 to 15 November.

places.name: Jericho
places.note: Nominatim, approximate: city point, homes not mapped

items.headline: JSR, Sunday: windshield cracked near Neve Daniel Junction, about 10 masked men stone a Nekuda BaEmek shepherd, Ein Duma spring vandalized with a knife and PLO flag left behind; 14 incidents over the weekend
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) reported on Sunday, 15 November: Arabs threw an object at an Israeli car about 200 meters north of Neve Daniel Junction in Gush Etzion, cracking the windshield, with no injuries; about 10 masked Arabs threw stones at a shepherd from the Nekuda BaEmek farm in Binyamin, with no injuries; the Ein Duma spring in Binyamin was vandalized, and a knife and a PLO flag were left there; stones were thrown at a car near the Malachei Avraham farm in the Hebron Hills, with no damage; and Arabs blocked an access road in the grazing area of the Giborei David farm (JSR on Telegram, Hebrew; Nekuda BaEmek; Ein Duma; Malachei Avraham; Giborei David). Netanel Frankel listed the same events (Netanel Frankel). JSR's weekend count for 13 and 14 November: 14 incidents, namely 7 attacks on shepherds and residents, 4 stone-throwing attacks, 2 roads blocked with rocks and spikes and 1 fake explosive device, with 2 Israelis hurt (JSR summary). JSR also posted a video of former British Army colonel Richard Kemp saying that European sanctions would mainly cost Arab workers their jobs (JSR).
items.source: JSR (Yesha Council Situation Room) / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel)

places.name: Neve Daniel (junction about 200 m south of the incident)

items.headline: Jordan border: eight handguns caught in one bag and hashish, GPS units and SIM cards in another; six people in rubber boats caught crossing the Dead Sea near Avnat
items.summary: Over the weekend the Jordan border police unit, Battalion 47 and the Judea and Samaria Border Police special unit stopped two smuggling attempts: one bag held eight handguns (FN, Glock and Taurus models), and the other held hashish, GPS devices and SIM cards (Olam Katan; JNS). Separately, six people who crossed the Dead Sea in rubber boats were caught near Avnat (Hallel Bitton Rosen). HaKol HaYehudi says they were Turkish nationals, one a woman, taken for Shin Bet questioning, and says earlier crossings of this kind were not caught; it also says Bedouin smugglers use helium balloons (HaKol HaYehudi; Elchanan Groner). JNS, citing Ynet, describes them instead as Turkish and Sri Lankan migrant workers (JNS; Yotam Deshe); the reports disagree, so who they were is unconfirmed.
items.source: Olam Katan / JNS / HaKol HaYehudi / Hallel Bitton Rosen / Elchanan Groner

items.headline: Eight Palestinians without permits found hiding in a fuel tanker at the Tunnels Checkpoint; two drivers who carry Hadassah nurses suspended after filming Binyamin roads and communities
items.summary: Crossing staff at the Tunnels Checkpoint south of Jerusalem found eight Palestinians without entry permits hiding inside a fuel tanker; the driver is a resident of east Jerusalem (Channel 14; JNS). Separately, Olam Katan reports that two drivers who take nurses to Hadassah Mount Scopus were suspended, and a Shin Bet security check was opened, after its report that shuttle drivers filmed roads and communities in Binyamin on their trips and posted the videos online (Olam Katan; single source so far, unconfirmed).

items.headline: Galilee: Mazraa man indicted for spying for Iran on his own initiative; he photographed army bases and police stations out of support for Hezbollah
items.summary: The Shin Bet and police said on Sunday that Wissam Ghaleb Saleh Awad, an Israeli citizen from the village of Mazraa near Nahariya, contacted Iranian agents on Telegram on his own, offered to work for free out of support for Hezbollah and a wish for revenge, and photographed IDF bases and police stations; a serious indictment was to be filed (Besheva; Elchanan Groner). Makor Rishon, Kan, Haaretz and HaKol HaYehudi carried the same report.
items.source: Besheva / Elchanan Groner / Shin Bet and police statement

items.headline: Bnei Sakhnin announcer Said Hassanein of Shefa-Amr convicted of contact with a foreign agent and identifying with a terror group over an interview with Hamas's TV channel
items.summary: The Haifa District Court convicted Said Hassanein, the stadium announcer of the Bnei Sakhnin soccer club, of contact with a foreign agent, identifying with a terror organization and destroying evidence; the case arose from an interview he gave to Hamas's Al-Aqsa TV that Channel 14 exposed about two years ago, and Joint List MKs expressed solidarity with him (Channel 14 reporter Omri Haim). The pro-Palestinian outlet Ultra Palestine reported the conviction as well (Ultra Palestine). No sentence has been reported yet.

items.headline: Route 6 near Baqa al-Gharbiya: a 5-kilogram rock smashes a windshield and injures a father driving to work with his son, a combat veteran who believes it was thrown on purpose
items.summary: A rock weighing about 5 kilograms smashed the windshield of a car on Route 6 near Baqa al-Gharbiya, hitting the father, from the Ramla area, in the head as he and his son drove to work at Big Nazareth. The son, Paz, who fought on 7 October and in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, says he believes the rock was thrown on purpose (Channel 14; Ayelet Lash). The reports do not give the date of the incident or say whether police have identified a suspect; that it was deliberate is the family's view, not a police finding.

items.headline: North and center: six Tamra men held for a murder, guns found on a horse farm near I'billin, a weapons store and coin-forging lab in Gan Yavne, and the al-Batuf council head held in a protection-money case
items.summary: Six residents of Tamra were arrested after an undercover investigation into the murder of Mohammed Yassin (Channel 14). Border Police raided a horse farm near I'billin, found two pistols and arrested four people; police say more than 780 weapons have been seized in the Northern District this year (Channel 14). In Gan Yavne, police found a weapons store with an M16, a Glock and ammunition, plus a lab for forging coins, and arrested three (Channel 14). Channel 14 says 192 people have been killed in Arab communities this year, 74 of them in the Northern District, and criticizes the district's top officers for flying to Poland this week (Channel 14; Channel 14's figures, not checked against police data). The Haifa Magistrate's Court extended by three days the detention of al-Batuf Regional Council head Ahed Rahal of Arab al-Heib, suspected of collecting protection money (khawa) from contractors through a guard company that provided no real guarding, along with extortion and money laundering; he was one of about 50 suspects arrested last Monday (Arab48, in Arabic). See the 15 November item on the Kafr Manda grenade murder.

items.headline: From the right: Moran Tal warns Ra'am is the Islamic Movement's political arm and "we will lose the Negev and Galilee"; bereaved families urge Matan Kahana not to become speaker with Arab votes
items.summary: Researcher Moran Tal wrote that Ra'am is the political arm of the southern branch of the Islamic Movement and warned that relying on it means "we will lose the Negev and the Galilee forever"; she also wrote that Ra'am and the Joint List are enemies of the state (Moran Tal). Elchanan Groner reported that bereaved families wrote to MK Matan Kahana asking him not to become Knesset speaker with the votes of Arab parties (Elchanan Groner); the speaker vote is set for 17 November. Minister Orit Strock said "a red line has already been crossed" over plans to rely on Arab parties (Olam Katan). These are opinions and political statements.
items.source: Moran Tal / Elchanan Groner / Olam Katan

items.headline: Around the communities: American donors honored for buying tractors for Judea and Samaria farms; Sde Yonatan hill puts up solar panels; Ben Arli remembered at Karmei Binyamin
items.summary: American Friends of Judea and Samaria (AFJS) held an evening in Brooklyn honoring the donors who paid for tractors for farms in Judea and Samaria (JNS; Makor Rishon). Elisha Yered posted that the Sde Yonatan hilltop is installing solar panels and that the Tel Talpiot hill (Jabal Ein Aina) is drawing water from a spring, and marked three years since the death of Ben Arli with a memorial at Karmei Binyamin (Elisha Yered; second post; single source).

items.headline: Southern Syria: Haaretz quotes soldiers describing boredom and raids on homes with no clear enemy; Haaretz also reports Damascus waiting for a security deal while Netanyahu insists on holding the area
items.summary: A Haaretz magazine report quotes soldiers in the Syria sector saying that, with no real enemy and no clear policy, the army "dreams up" home searches and other operations, and one officer warns "they'll eventually turn their anger on us" (Haaretz, feed summary; the article itself is paywalled and was not read in full). Haaretz also ran a report that Damascus is waiting for a security agreement while Prime Minister Netanyahu insists on keeping the territory, and an editorial urging the next government to seek a deal with Syria. Ultra Palestine cites Israeli security sources warning that local armed resistance groups could form in southern Syria (single source). Halutzei HaBashan, which wants Israelis to settle the area, is urging the public to mark Tuesday, 17 November, the second anniversary of the move into the Hermon and the Bashan area (Halutzei HaBashan); it has posted nothing new since 14 November.

items.headline: Otzma Yehudit director general questioned over the Mitzpe Yericho clash with police; the party calls it political persecution
items.summary: Police's Lahav 433 unit questioned Otzma Yehudit's director general, Itiel Neiman, over the assault on police at Mitzpe Yericho about a month ago, in which three officers were hurt; Haaretz says the suspicions include extortion by threats, assault, obstructing a police officer and obstruction of justice (Israel Hayom; Haaretz). Srugim quotes the party calling the questioning "political persecution." No charges have been filed.

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: army notice to demolish two Hebron buildings housing 65 families in Area A; Palestinians report a home attacked and car burned in Masafer Yatta and attacks in Turmus Ayya
items.summary: Hebron city council member Muammar al-Uweiwi said the army had issued demolition notices, on security grounds, for two apartment buildings with 65 flats and one house in Area A of Hebron, which he says hold Palestinian permits (Arab48, in Arabic); no army statement was found. Raya and WAFA report that settlers attacked a home in Masafer Yatta and burned a car, that a home was attacked in Turmus Ayya, and that property was damaged at Ras al-Ahmar near Tubas (Raya; WAFA headlines). Raya's Jenin correspondent says the army is putting up watchtowers at a new post overlooking the Jenin camp and pressing about 100 residents to leave Khirbet al-Sarouj (Raya, 12 Nov). These are Palestinian claims with no Israeli confirmation. The PA security forces' spokesman issued no statement in the window, and png.plo.ps again showed no news.

items.headline: Push to settle Areas A and B: HaBayta Forum calls for ending the Oslo division and taking farms into open land, as young families hold the Or Binyamin hilltop in Area B's Wadi Zarqa
items.summary: The HaBayta Forum, a group led by bereaved families, released a new video on Saturday calling for the Oslo accords to be canceled, for the division of Judea and Samaria into Areas A, B and C to be ended, and for the farm model now used in Area C to be extended to the open land in Areas A and B, Arutz 7 reports. Settlement activist Azri Tobi, who leads the video, says Judea and Samaria is 15 times the size of the Gaza Strip, with about two million Arabs, a hostile ideological base like Gaza's, large amounts of weapons and tens of thousands of Palestinian police trained by foreign armies. He says there are about 1.28 million dunams of open land there and that whoever settles it first will decide the future of the area. The video lists driving times from the ridge: about five minutes to Afula and Kfar Saba, ten to Netanya, Kiryat Gat and Ben Gurion Airport, and a quarter of an hour to Tel Aviv. Bereaved parents Yehoshua Sherman and Eliav Libi, who joined the forum's recent call not to form a government that relies on Arab parties, said settling the open land is "the most moral, Zionist, security-minded and just demand" (Arutz 7; JNS Hebrew's Netanel Frankel; Elchanan Groner, sharing Tobi's explanation). One hilltop is already trying this on the ground. Or Binyamin, named for Staff Sgt. Binyamin Meir Arli, who fell in Gaza, was set up about half a year ago by a young couple, Yiftach and Efrat Kevin, and a group of young people in Wadi Zarqa, along the Talmonim bloc in western Binyamin; the whole wadi was defined as Area B under Oslo. Residents told Arutz 7 that Jews who tried to come near the area for years were attacked from nearby villages, that springs had been built over and pumped dry, and that after they cleaned and repaired the springs thousands of Jewish hikers came over the summer and the fall holidays. They say the daily flock and their presence have made the road between Neve Tzuf and Nahliel safer, that Arabs threw a dead wild boar into a spring they were repairing, and that the security forces have evacuated them, torn down structures, seized equipment and tried to seize the flock. The site has no water or power lines and is reached only by four-wheel-drive vehicles; Efrat Kevin calls it "a first step to canceling the Oslo accords" (Arutz 7, 9 Nov; Arutz 7, 12 Nov). Both Arutz 7 pieces carry a fundraising link for the hilltop. On Saturday the anti-settlement account Settlers From Within posted video of a resident celebrating the outpost and speaking of "returning the wadi to Jewish hands" (Settlers From Within). The residents' account of attacks and of the springs has not been checked against a second source.
items.source: Arutz 7 / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) / Elchanan Groner / Settlers From Within

places.name: Or Binyamin (Wadi Zarqa)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Wadi a-Zarqa; the hilltop is not mapped

items.headline: Plans for about 895 new homes move forward in Kedumim, Beit Hagai, Talmon, Ariel and Elon Moreh, plus a Kiryat Arba industrial zone, the PA's settlement tracker reports
items.summary: The Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, which tracks Israeli land orders and building plans, said on Saturday that it had found 11 new plans for Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria that together add 895 homes and expand industrial and commercial land. By its count: a 288-home expansion of a neighborhood in Kedumim over more than 158 dunams; 225 homes on about 190 dunams in Beit Hagai, south of Hebron; 200 homes on 65 dunams in Talmon, with new roads and infrastructure; two plans in Ariel, one adding 98 homes in the north of the city; 83 homes in Elon Moreh; changes to building rights in the Karnei Shomron industrial area, a small housing addition in Oranit and new building lines in Peduel; a crafts and light-industry zone of more than 165 dunams in Kiryat Arba; and rules allowing commercial and service buildings on public-use plots in the Gush Etzion communities (Al-Quds, in Arabic; Ultra Palestine). The commission did not say which planning stage each plan has reached. These are the PA body's figures: no Israeli announcement of these plans by the Civil Administration or the regional councils was found this morning, so the numbers are unconfirmed. Ultra Palestine separately wrote on Saturday that there are plans for 35 more industrial zones in Judea and Samaria, most along the Green Line or the security barrier, without naming a source (Ultra Palestine).
items.source: PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission (via Al-Quds, Ultra Palestine)

items.headline: Weekend attacks: stones smash a windshield near the Beit Ummar gas station and hurt a Gush Etzion farm resident; "harvesters" attack hikers near the Emmanuel industrial zone; four minors held for stoning a Jerusalem bus
items.summary: On Saturday evening stones were thrown at an Israeli car on Route 60 near the Ya'ar al-Qarn farm in Gush Etzion, breaking the windshield; the driver was lightly hurt by shards, an army force came to the spot and he did not need to be taken to the hospital, Ynet reports (Ynet). Olam Katan reporter Simcha Raz and Elisha Yered place the attack on old Route 60 next to the Beit Ummar gas station and say the victim, a resident of the farm, was hit in the eye; Yered says one stone almost broke through the windshield and that no arrests had been reported (Simcha Raz; Elisha Yered). Activist Ayelet Lash complained that the public broadcaster did not report it (Ayelet Lash). Earlier this month Arutz 7 reported that rioters from Beit Ummar set fire to a Jewish family's car at nearby Gefen Ami. On Friday afternoon, Arab men who came as olive "harvesters" attacked Israeli residents who were walking near the Emmanuel industrial zone in Samaria, according to Elisha Yered and Olam Katan, which both posted video (Elisha Yered; Olam Katan); no police or army statement and no injury figures were found, so the details are unconfirmed. Olam Katan also posted video of what it called an attempted car-ramming that was stopped at the last moment on Saturday, without giving the place (Olam Katan); no other report was found. In Jerusalem, police from the Oz station arrested four minors on Saturday evening on suspicion of throwing stones at a bus driving through Har Homa, which damaged its rear window (Maariv). The Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) did not post its usual daily incident count for Friday and Saturday.
items.source: Ynet / Olam Katan (Simcha Raz) / Elisha Yered / Ayelet Lash / Maariv

items.headline: JSR: Bedouins who left a site near Natuf burned what they left behind and then blamed Jews; Palestinian outlets report "settlers burned a tent" at Deir Qaddis
items.summary: Palestinian news sites reported on Saturday evening that settlers set fire to a tent of a Bedouin community near Deir Qaddis, west of Ramallah. Al-Quds (Hebrew edition) placed it in the al-Mughayyir area northeast of the village, reported no injuries, and blamed residents of an outpost there, which it says want to push the community out (Al-Quds). The Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) gives a different account: it says Bedouins who left the site during the weekend, next to the Jewish community of Natuf now being built in western Binyamin, set fire to the remains themselves and then accused the Israeli residents (JSR in Hebrew; JSR in English). JSR did not publish its evidence with the post, and no police or army statement was found, so neither version has been confirmed. JSR has published an earlier analysis on what it calls a pattern of Arabs setting fires and then blaming settlers. JSR also reported on Saturday that Laila Ghannam, the PA governor of Ramallah and al-Bireh, who JSR says attended a terrorist's funeral where Hamas flags were flown, keeps regular ties with many European officials, and that in April she met Rear Adm. Edward Ahlgren, the British Defense Ministry's senior adviser for the Middle East and North Africa (JSR). The April meeting is JSR's account and was not checked independently. No new JSR report or weekly situation report appeared on its website since the last edition.

items.headline: Elisha Yered's Front Hills Administration hands out drones to hilltop communities and trains them to film attacks; a Hamas-aligned outlet takes note
items.summary: The Front Hills Administration, a group run by Elisha Yered that supports the hilltop communities, says it held another handout of drones on Friday to a number of settlement points in Judea and Samaria, paid for by private donors. Each representative was trained to fly the drone and to film security incidents accurately. Yered says the drones help spot attacks and infiltrations as they happen and help document incidents "and refute blood libels," and that dozens of front-line settlement points "have no government backing" (Elisha Yered). The Hamas-aligned Quds News Network reported the handout in Arabic, noting the support of "Jewish donors"; Yered answered that "the Hamas channels did not much like" it (Elisha Yered). Channel 18 Israel also aired a sit-down interview with Yered by Sam Schubert on daily Arab attacks and the "settler violence" claims; asked whether his biggest problem is the Palestinians or the Israeli security forces, he said both, because it would be far easier to deal with Arab terror if the state did not stop Jews from defending themselves (Channel 18 Israel; Channel 18 Israel).
items.source: Elisha Yered / Quds News Network / Channel 18 Israel

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian and Arab media report Israeli shells east of al-Asbah and new incursions in central Quneitra; Halutzei HaBashan marks the second anniversary of the move into the area
items.summary: Al-Quds, citing local sources, reported on Saturday that two Israeli artillery shells fell east of al-Asbah in southern Quneitra province, and that Israeli ground forces moved into al-Mushayrifa and al-Ajraf in central Quneitra and into al-Hafayer, north of Khan Arnabeh. It cites rights groups as counting about 70 Israeli ground incursions and moves in southern Syria in the first half of November, mainly in Quneitra but also in western Daraa and near Mount Hermon, and local sources as saying at least 11 people, including a child, were detained in two weeks, some later released (Al-Quds, in Arabic). Anadolu, citing Syria's state Al-Ikhbariya channel, also reported an incursion into a Quneitra village and shelling of land in the south (Anadolu, in Arabic). The army did not comment. These are Syrian and Arab media accounts. Halutzei HaBashan, the group pushing for Israeli settlement in southern Syria, posted that Tuesday, 17 November, marks by the Hebrew calendar two years since Israeli forces took "part of the Bashan" (Halutzei HaBashan); the army moved into the buffer zone on the Syrian side of the Golan on 8 December 2024, the day the Assad government fell. Its Telegram channel has had no new posts since July.
items.source: Al-Quds / Anadolu (citing Syrian state TV) / Halutzei HaBashan

items.headline: Makor Rishon's Yehuda Yifrach: the High Court asks about enforcement in the Judean Desert "agreed reserve" while a near-city of PA building grows there; analyst warns a Democratic Congress may target settlement banks
items.summary: Writing about this week's conditional order by Justices Yitzhak Amit, Daphna Barak-Erez and Ofer Grosskopf (reported on this page), Makor Rishon legal affairs writer Yehuda Yifrach says the court ignored "almost a whole city" built without permits in the reserve. Under the 1998 Wye memorandum, about 166,000 dunams in the Judean Desert were set aside as green land and nature reserves under PA civil control, with a PA pledge not to change their status or build there. Yifrach cites a Settlement Ministry study of aerial photos that counted 268 buildings in the reserve in 1998 and 3,048 by June 2023, 598 of them added in 2021 alone, and more than 630 km of roads. He points to the al-Malaha project east of Za'tara, near Tekoa and Nokdim, where plots were marketed online under a fictitious "al-Malaha municipality" for tens of dinars a square meter. He writes that the Civil Administration carried out only 11 enforcement actions there in 2018 to 2020; that the cabinet decided in June 2024 to begin enforcement, Central Command signed a building-restriction order in July 2024 and seven buildings were razed that December; and that the petitioners are the Za'tara municipality and the "al-Malaha village council" (Makor Rishon). The building counts are from the ministry study as quoted in the column and were not checked independently. Separately, Dr. Kobi Barda of the JPTI institute told Arutz 7 that the settlers will be "the first to take the hardest blow" from the Democrats' gains in the U.S. midterm elections. He expects Congress, from 3 January, to push personal and area sanctions, and fears steps against Israeli banks that finance building and mortgages in Judea and Samaria; he says President Trump may not be able or willing to block all of them (Arutz 7). This is his forecast.

items.headline: Lod: "The Arab threat has grown on our streets since the elections," a longtime resident writes, listing harassment of Jews after election night
items.summary: Ofra Lax, a Lod resident for 23 years, writes in Makor Rishon that Arab residents celebrated the election results with shouts of "Allahu akbar" near Likud activists, convoys of cars with green flags in the north of the city, fireworks and gunfire. Since then, she says, Arab girls shouted "barra" ("get out") at a Jewish woman; a car cut off a Jewish driver and forced him onto a traffic island; on Friday night Arabs did dangerous car spins next to students of a pre-army academy gathered in the empty market square, threatened to run them over and shouted "barra"; and a boy was punched in the stomach by passing children. She ties this to the May 2021 riots, when Lod resident Yigal Yehoshua was killed and synagogues, schools, homes and cars were set on fire, and says police then worked to separate the sides rather than arrest rioters. She also writes that heavy gunfire was heard near a public meeting with Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich in the city a few days before the elections (Makor Rishon). The recent incidents are her account and were not checked against police reports; the 2021 events are well documented.

items.headline: North and Triangle: woman killed by a grenade thrown into a Kafr Manda pastry shop, three suspects held; man shot dead in Taibe; off-duty Border Police officer shoots a driver in Acre
items.summary: Lina Qassem Zidan, 51, of Daliyat al-Karmel, was killed on Saturday when a grenade was thrown into a pastry shop in Kafr Manda; four others were hurt, including her husband, whom the attackers ran over. Police arrested three suspects and found the car they used hidden; residents said a second grenade was thrown elsewhere in the village and that there had been shootings and grenade attacks in recent days. Police Commissioner Danny Levy came to the scene (Ynet). On Saturday evening a man of about 50 was shot dead in Taibe (Maariv; Haaretz). Counts of Arab murder victims this year differ by outlet: Ynet called Zidan the 200th, Haaretz counted 197 after the Taibe killing and Maariv 189. In Acre, an off-duty Border Police officer opened fire on Route 85 at a driver who, police say, was driving in a way that endangered pedestrians and the officer; the driver fled and was later taken to the hospital seriously hurt, and police opened an investigation (Ynet). Ayelet Lash asked why there is "a murder in this sector every day" (Ayelet Lash). No weekend security incidents were found in the Negev.

items.headline: From the right: Moran Tal on an Al Jazeera commentator's view of the Arab vote as "revenge"; Meir Ettinger on Ra'am's founder and a Hadash MK; Elchanan Groner on Israeli Arabs shopping in Jenin
items.summary: Moran Tal posted a clip of Ehab Jabareen, whom she describes as an Al Jazeera commentator from Umm al-Fahm, explaining the jump in Arab party seats as the first chance since 7 October for Arab citizens to speak politically "without paying a price," in order to take revenge on Netanyahu, Smotrich and Ben-Gvir for the past three years. She reads this as proof that their motive was to punish the government, not to take part, and says the problem is that "Israel's enemies" can act through the ballot box (Moran Tal). She also reposted a 2014 clip of a woman from Sakhnin backing Hamas, which she calls a common view in Arab society (Moran Tal). Meir Ettinger pointed to the Hebrew Wikipedia entry on the Muslim Brotherhood that lists Ra'am founder Abdullah Nimr Darwish, against those who deny the link (Meir Ettinger), and wrote that Hadash MK Atauna is repeating the "conspiracy" that the government works with crime groups (Meir Ettinger). Elchanan Groner posted a photo he says shows traffic jams of Israeli Arab citizens going shopping in Jenin on Saturday, objecting that Defense Minister Israel Katz still allows thousands of them to go there and send money into the city (Elchanan Groner). These are their own claims and readings; the photo's date and place were not checked.
items.source: Moran Tal / Meir Ettinger / Elchanan Groner

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: army says masked Israelis fled to an outpost near Sa'ir after a clash with harvesters in Wadi Saif; Palestinians report a man shot near Deir Jarir; Kerem Navot flags a new seizure order
items.summary: On Saturday a clash broke out when Israelis came to disrupt a Palestinian olive harvest in Wadi Saif, east of Beit Fajjar; Palestinians reported five people hurt. The army said a Palestinian car was smashed, that troops pushed the rioters away and closed the area, and that when masked Israelis in vehicles were reported later, they had fled before the troops arrived. On the way, troops fired in the air at two suspect vehicles that fled to an unauthorized outpost near Sa'ir; one, with Palestinian plates, appears to have been stolen and was returned to its owner. No one was arrested, and the army condemned "Israeli rioters who take the law into their own hands" (Ynet; Kan's Itay Blumental). Palestinian outlets reported that settlers shot and wounded a Palestinian man in his car at the entrance to Deir Jarir, east of Ramallah, on Saturday afternoon, and that the army closed the iron gates at Deir Jarir and Yabrud (Al-Quds, in Arabic); no Israeli statement or account of the circumstances was found. Dror Etkes of Kerem Navot posted a seizure order, 132/26, that he says Central Command chief Avi Bluth signed eight days after the elections to open a new road, which he expects will lead to a new farm, as with orders for the Bazak and Tamun outposts in the same area (Dror Etkes). Ultra Palestine said soldiers turned a home in Balata al-Balad into a field interrogation center during a pre-dawn raid on Saturday that also reached the Balata, Askar and Ein camps in Nablus (Ultra Palestine). The PFLP-aligned site Al-Hadaf ran a video headlined that PA security services stopped a march in support of prisoner Bilal Kayed from heading toward Beit El (Al-Hadaf, in Arabic); only the headline was readable. A Haaretz editorial objects to the renewed arrest of Palestinian journalist Samer Khuwaira, brought before the Samaria military court on Thursday a year after nine months in administrative detention (Haaretz). These are single-side claims unless noted.
items.source: Ynet / Kan (Itay Blumental) / Al-Quds / Kerem Navot (Dror Etkes) / Ultra Palestine / Al-Hadaf / Haaretz

items.headline: Court freezes the tender for the survey meant to restart land registration in Judea and Samaria, a quiet 2025 cabinet decision that settlement backers call the government's biggest land move
items.summary: Besheva columnist Yoni Roten has made public a step that he says the outgoing government kept out of the news on purpose: in May 2025 the security cabinet decided to end the 1968 military order that froze the registration of land ownership in Judea and Samaria, and to set up a large survey to register who owns each plot. In his account, land with no serious ownership claim would be declared state land, and disputed claims would go to a dedicated committee instead of the High Court, which he blames for the evacuation of Migron, Amona, nine homes in Ofra and Netiv HaAvot over Palestinian private-land claims. He calls the decision "the closest thing to an official declaration" of sovereignty (Besheva; Yoni Roten on X). The Justice Ministry's land registration authority put out a tender to hire a private firm to run the survey, and the firm Geoda, of Ramat HaHayal, won it, Roten writes. The step stalled at the next stage: the Central Command order that gives the survey its legal footing never took effect, held up for a year and a half in the Justice Ministry. Yesh Din, Bimkom and the Association for Civil Rights in Israel then petitioned the Jerusalem District Court against the tender on 25 June 2026. On 28 October 2026 Judge Shirley Renner froze the tender in Judea and Samaria, ruling that the Justice Ministry and its tenders committee have no authority to act there without an order from the military commander. She did not rule on the groups' other claims (that the step breaks international law, illegally privatizes state powers and discriminates against Palestinians) (Yesh Din case page, in Hebrew). Yesh Din's own page says an earlier High Court petition against the cabinet decision was rejected in January 2026 as premature, and that cabinet members described the aim as strengthening settlement. Roten notes that the ruling leaves room for a future general's order to make the tender valid again, but says that with no one yet named to the justice and defense ministries, the halt may last a long time. Shiloh Valley farmer Amishav Melet shared the column: "There is no decision in Judea and Samaria without smashing the lie of 'the private lands of the local Palestinians'" (Amishav Melet). Note: Roten's post on X dates the cabinet decision to May 2026, but his column and Yesh Din both say May 2025.
items.source: Besheva (Yoni Roten) / Yesh Din / Amishav Melet

items.headline: Inside the eight Jericho homes: Nachala says there is room for 15 families, a nearby community for 12 families is next, and it wants an access road down from Mitzpe Yericho
items.summary: Makor Rishon visited the homes on the edge of Jericho that Jewish families moved into last week. It reports eight houses in Area C, in one neighborhood, in three clusters a few minutes' walk apart, bought by the Nachala settlement movement with support from the Binyamin Regional Council. The houses have names drawn from the Bible's Jericho stories ("Beit HaShani," "Beit Salomon"); yeshiva students from Kiryat Arba have turned one living room into a study hall, and most of the first families came from Marom Yehuda, the community north of Hebron that Nachala founded about two years ago. Nachala chairman Tzvi Elimelech Sharabaf, a grandson of Rabbi Moshe Levinger, has moved there with his family. He compares the move to the first Jewish settlers' arrival in Hebron in 1968, says a group called "Harhivi" bought five homes in Hebron about a year ago and showed it could be done, and says Nachala moved in quickly because it feared the PA would discover the purchases. The bought homes have room for 15 families living there permanently; for now "reserve" families are staying for the first weeks while Nachala looks for permanent ones. The nearby community of Diya, which Nachala expects to set up soon, would start with 12 families. The main obstacle is access: Nachala wants to open a road down from Mitzpe Yericho and says it has drawn up plans for the government ministries (Makor Rishon). Sharabaf's broader claims, that many Arabs want to sell and emigrate and that half the Arab population of Judea and Samaria would leave within a few years if the state set up a fund and protected sellers from the PA, are his own and cannot be checked. The Palestinian side's account: Haaretz, from residents of the Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta neighborhood, reports demolitions, looting and the violent removal of Palestinian residents, and a teenage settler at the neighborhood entrance who said he had "blocking authority" (Haaretz); these are residents' claims that no police or army statement in the sources confirms. See the desk items of 5 to 12 November, including the army's decision to keep the residents in place and reinforce the nearby post.

items.headline: Two Islamic State-linked terrorists among four arrested near Jenin; army says it arrested more than 55 wanted men in Judea and Samaria this week and razed memorials to Hamas and Islamic Jihad founders
items.summary: Paratroopers under the Menashe Brigade, guided by the Shin Bet, arrested four terrorists overnight from Thursday to Friday who the army says were advancing attacks on Israeli civilians and security forces; two of them are identified with the Islamic State (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Times of Israel's Emanuel Fabian). Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe called the arrests unusual for the Menashe sector, where arrests are routine but most of those held belong to local groups such as Hamas and Islamic Jihad (Yotam Deshe). In its weekly summary the army said dozens of battalions and special units arrested more than 55 wanted men across Judea and Samaria, among them Hamas and Islamic Jihad members, men planning an attack, inciters and a suspect in firebomb throwing, and that in the Etzion area troops destroyed memorials glorifying terror that belonged to two founders of Hamas and Islamic Jihad and to other terrorists (Ynet; Simcha Raz). Separately, the Judea and Samaria Division commander, Brig. Gen. Kobi Heller, presented the security assessment and plans for 2027 to council heads at a conference in Ariel run by the division's civilian security office and the Yesha Council; it focused on strengthening the defense of the communities, the infrastructure effort, and coordination with the Defense Ministry's settlement division, Home Front Command, the Civil Administration, police, fire service and Magen David Adom (Arutz 7).
items.source: Arutz 7 / Channel 14 / IDF / Israel Hayom (Yotam Deshe) / Ynet

items.headline: JSR: ten terror incidents on Thursday and five Israelis hurt; stones hit a car near Tmara on Friday; JSR video shows Hamas flags beside Fatah flags at the Silwad funeral
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) counted ten incidents across Judea and Samaria on Thursday, 12 November: four attacks on Jewish shepherds and residents, four stone-throwing attacks and two roads blocked with rocks and burning tires, with five Israeli residents hurt (JSR, Hebrew; JSR on Telegram). JNS Hebrew's Netanel Frankel, citing JSR, listed the main ones: two shepherds hurt at Ateret, a shepherd attacked at Yehonatan farm in Gush Etzion with no injuries, the access road to Shir LeDavid in Samaria blocked with stones, and burning tires south of Ir HaTmarim in Binyamin (Netanel Frankel); the Ateret and Yehonatan attacks were in the 13 November edition. On Friday, 13 November, Arabs threw stones at an Israeli car south of Tmara, damaging its body with no injuries, JSR said; Olam Katan's Simcha Raz reported the same attack (JSR, English; Simcha Raz). JSR places Tmara in Binyamin, while Raz writes the Jordan Valley, so the spot is not mapped here. JSR also posted video of Hamas flags flown alongside Fatah flags at Wednesday's funeral of a terrorist in Silwad, noting that Fatah is the movement that controls the Palestinian Authority, headed by Mahmoud Abbas (JSR; see the 13 November item on the funeral). No new reports appeared on JSR's website (news, analysis and English briefings pages) since the last run.
items.source: JSR (Yesha Council Situation Room) / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) / Olam Katan (Simcha Raz)

items.headline: Jordan Valley: man from al-Jiftlik held after police find a classified army map of the Gaza border area, military gear and knives in his home
items.summary: Police from the Judea and Samaria District and Border Police officers on a routine patrol in the al-Jiftlik area noticed a Palestinian man in his 20s wearing army boots on Thursday, 12 November. He said they belonged to his son and admitted he had more military equipment at home. A search turned up an airsoft pistol, knives, other military gear and a military map of the Gaza border communities marked "secret." He was taken to the Bik'a police station, held after questioning, and police are investigating what he meant to do with the gear and how he got the map (Channel 14; Olam Katan; Simcha Raz). Arutz 7 and Israel Hayom carried the same police statement.
items.source: Israel Police (via Channel 14 and Olam Katan)

items.headline: Naqura spring near Mount Ebal flows again under a project begun by the late Benayahu Melet; Ma'on Farm, demolished 27 years ago, now has dozens of families
items.summary: The Naqura spring, a natural pool on the way to Mount Ebal in northern Samaria, is filling again after years in which, according to area residents, its flow was diverted by nearby Arab residents while there was little Jewish presence there, Olam Katan reports (Olam Katan). Its settlement reporter Simcha Raz says the project was begun by Benayahu Melet, killed on 24 July 2026, and posted photos credited to the Hilltop Fund (Simcha Raz). This is single-source; no council or water-authority statement was found. Elchanan Groner marked 27 years since the army and police destroyed Ma'on Farm in the South Hebron Hills, then one of a few lone hilltops; today it has dozens of families, and hundreds of hilltops and farms have gone up since (Elchanan Groner). Elisha Yered posted that Givat Tidhar in Wadi a-Zarqa, named for the late Tidhar Gozlan, hosted a group of young men who came to strengthen the hilltop this weekend; it has no power or running water, and the nearest grocery is 40 minutes away over dirt roads (Elisha Yered).
items.source: Olam Katan (Simcha Raz) / Elchanan Groner / Elisha Yered

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian state media say Israeli forces cut a new road from the Sihan post toward Wadi al-Raqqad and held three men in a Jubata al-Khashab raid
items.summary: Syria's state news agency SANA reported that on Friday, 13 November, Israeli engineering vehicles and bulldozers began cutting a new road and track from the Sihan observation post on the Golan toward Wadi al-Raqqad, near the village of Abidin in the Yarmouk basin of western Daraa province (SANA, Arabic). It also said a force of more than nine military vehicles entered Jubata al-Khashab in northern Quneitra province that day, searched homes, broke the doors and fronts of several shops, and detained three men, later freeing one (SANA, Arabic). Families of Syrians held by Israel protested outside the UN observer force (UNDOF) base at Nabe' al-Fawwar (SANA, Arabic). These are Syrian government claims; headlines from Enab Baladi and the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights report the same raids and road, but their pages blocked automated reading, and no Israeli army statement was found. Halutzei HaBashan, the movement pushing for Israeli settlement in the Bashan, has posted nothing on X since 10 November, when it called for standing "like a fortified wall" against pressure to withdraw from the Bashan (Halutzei HaBashan); its Telegram channel has not posted since July.

places.name: Abidin (Wadi al-Raqqad area, Daraa)
