items.headline: Negev: police put snipers on Rahat rooftops with orders that "fire will be met with fire"; loaded pistol hidden on a woman and 315,000 shekels seized in the Azazme area
items.summary: Police confirmed on Friday that snipers and marksmen are posted on rooftops in Rahat as part of an operation against armed men behind shootings in the city, after photos of armed men on the roofs spread on social media. Southern District commander Maj. Gen. Haim Bublil ordered special units into the city after a situation assessment, and officers were told to identify armed suspects who open fire and "neutralize" them; the message, police said, is that "fire will be met with fire." Police say more than 600 weapons and tens of thousands of rounds of stolen military ammunition have been found in the south since the start of the year (Arutz 7; Kan; Haaretz carried the same report). On Thursday, Border Police's National Guard and Segev Shalom detectives searching a compound in the Azazme area found a loaded pistol hidden on a 20-year-old woman, a box of 9 mm rounds, and 315,000 shekels in cash hidden in the bedroom, closets and ceiling; she and her 21-year-old husband were arrested (Arutz 7). See the 3 and 7 November items on Rahat shootings and seized M-16s.

places.name: Azazme area
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for the Azazme area; the compound is not mapped

items.headline: North: Yafa an-Naseriyye man indicted for online posts praising Sinwar and Yassin and calling for "fighting and jihad"
items.summary: The Northern District prosecution was due to indict a resident of Yafa an-Naseriyye, near Nazareth, on Friday for serious incitement on social media, Channel 14 reports. The charge sheet says he posted tributes to terror leaders including Yahya Sinwar and Ahmed Yassin with explicit calls to continue "fighting and jihad" against Israel, praised terrorists who attacked civilians and security forces, and reshared a Hamas post celebrating the deaths of Maj. Yaniv Kula and 2nd Lt. Itay Yaavetz. Prosecutors are asking that he be held until the end of proceedings (Channel 14). Single-source; the court file was not checked.

items.headline: From the right: Ayelet Lash posts an Arab wedding chant of "we are the masters of the land"; Meir Ettinger says Haaretz left out a doctor's Islamic Movement role; Moran Tal on Mansour Abbas
items.summary: Activist Ayelet Lash posted video she says was filmed at an Arab wedding on Thursday in which guests chant "we are the masters of the land," asking "what definition is there for this other than enemies?" (Ayelet Lash); the place of the wedding is not given and the video was not checked. Meir Ettinger wrote that a Haaretz feature about a doctor hid from readers that he is a very senior Islamic Movement activist, a former head of the movement's national youth department and the son of a former head of the movement in Rahat (Meir Ettinger); the Haaretz piece and his claims about the doctor were not checked. Moran Tal posted a clip she says shows Mansour Abbas speaking while already a Knesset member, and wrote that "for Mansour Abbas, Erdogan represents a democratic model" (Moran Tal; Moran Tal). These are their own posts and claims.
items.source: Ayelet Lash / Meir Ettinger / Moran Tal

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: Ynet says youths from the Te'ena outpost wrecked a new Susya security system; PA governor protests Bustanei Hefetz; tent reported on the al-Mughayyir plain
items.summary: Ynet reports that last week youths from the Te'ena outpost in Wadi Rahim, next to Susya, damaged power boxes and tore cables of a new security system worth hundreds of thousands of shekels that was about to start protecting Susya; police are investigating and have collected camera footage, including from Palestinian homes nearby. The outpost has been cleared several times recently, most recently on Thursday evening (Ynet); no suspect has been named. The PA's Tulkarm governor, Abdullah Kamil, said the Bustanei Hefetz industrial zone (see the 13 November item) continues "settlement projects" against Palestinians, and Ultra Palestine claims its 800 dunams were taken by a Central Command military order (Ultra Palestine). Ultra Palestine also reports that settlers pitched a tent on the eastern al-Mughayyir plain, northeast of Ramallah, in an area the army has declared a closed military zone, and that two brothers in Sur Baher, in Jerusalem, were made to tear down their own homes, built without permits (Ultra Palestine; Ultra Palestine). These are Palestinian claims not confirmed by an Israeli source. B'Tselem's website blocked automated reading again, and its X account and Basel Adra's had no new posts.
items.source: Ynet / Ultra Palestine / PA Tulkarm governor

places.name: Susya (Te'ena outpost nearby)
places.note: Nominatim point for Susya; the outpost is not mapped

places.name: al-Mughayyir
places.note: Approximate: village point (Nominatim); the tent site on the plain is not mapped

items.headline: Border Police and Civil Administration tear down Kfar Tarfon homes near Ateret at 3 AM, after a High Court petition by Palestinians the residents say had squatted on an ancient site
items.summary: At about 3 AM on Thursday, 12 Nov, about 100 Border Police officers and Civil Administration inspectors with heavy equipment demolished three homes, a sheep pen, a chicken coop and a dining hall at Kfar Tarfon, a Jewish hilltop community next to Ateret in Binyamin, and seized two of the residents' vehicles and much equipment. Residents say two families were ordered to stay inside their homes while the other buildings were bulldozed (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Elisha Yered; Elchanan Groner). The residents' account of the background: Palestinians had for years occupied Khirbet Tarfin, a nearby archaeological site from the Second Temple period, damaging remains and looting antiquities; the Civil Administration removed them, they came back and built two houses on the site, and the damage stopped only when the hilltop was set up. Those same Palestinians then petitioned the High Court to have the hilltop cleared and the army ordered to secure their return; the residents say the justices did not throw the petition out, and that the Defense Ministry and Civil Administration did not fight it in court. "The squatters became the petitioners," they said (residents' claims as carried by Arutz 7 and Channel 14; the court file was not checked here). See the 6 Nov desk item on the petition. The army's statement, as reported by Maariv, said troops and Border Police carried out repeat enforcement over the past day at two "illegal outposts" near the villages of Atara and Wadi Rahim, from which it says "violent and illegal activity" repeatedly came; near Atara, it said Israeli "rioters" barricaded themselves on the buildings and others tried to reach the area, and troops used riot-dispersal means (Maariv; Times of Israel's Emanuel Fabian). Residents protested by blocking Route 465 between Ateret and the British Police junction, causing heavy traffic, Olam Katan's Simcha Raz reported (Simcha Raz). The Situation Room (JSR) reported that Jewish shepherds were stoned by Arabs on the access road to Kfar Tarfon that morning and two were hurt (JSR). The Palestinian side: Palestinian outlets say that after the demolition, hundreds of settlers attacked Atara, damaging four homes and three cars, and the Red Crescent says it treated a 67-year-old man who was beaten (Raya, Arabic); Haaretz, citing Yesh Din and WAFA, put the number hurt at five, one seriously (Haaretz). These are the Palestinian and NGO accounts; no police or army figure for injuries in Atara was found. Reactions: Zehut leader Moshe Feiglin said the state "surrendered" to the petitioners and that Kfar Tarfon drives a wedge into the Area A and B bloc around Ateret, holding thousands of dunams of grazing land; "the houses will be destroyed, but the hill will rise again" (Feiglin, via Yered's Telegram). Elchanan Groner told Central Command chief Avi Bluth and Judea and Samaria Division commander Kobi Heller to "get your heads out of Kfar Tarfon and deal with the enemy" (Groner).
items.source: Arutz 7 / Channel 14 / Kfar Tarfon residents / IDF (via Maariv) / JSR

places.name: Kfar Tarfon (near Ateret)
places.note: Approximate: point is the village of Atara (Nominatim); the hilltop itself is not mapped

items.headline: Cornerstone laid for "Bustanei Hefetz," a 800-dunam industrial zone in northern Samaria, the largest in Judea and Samaria in decades
items.summary: Housing Minister Haim Katz, Economy Minister Nir Barkat, MK Boaz Bismuth and Samaria council head Yossi Dagan laid the cornerstone on Thursday, 12 Nov, for the Bustanei Hefetz industrial zone next to Avnei Hefetz, on the road toward Einav and Shavei Shomron. It covers about 800 dunams (about 200 acres) with 96 lots for industry, commerce and offices, about a quarter hour from Route 6 and 25 minutes from Netanya; the Israel Land Authority tender for the lots is open to developers until the end of November (Ynet; Arutz 7). Arutz 7 says it comes after 10 years of planning (Dagan said 15), is being developed by the Samaria council's economic company with the Israel Land Authority, and is close in size to Barkan, the largest existing zone; Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe called it the largest industrial zone in Judea and Samaria since Barkan (Deshe). Olam Katan's Simcha Raz gives the breakdown: 789.65 dunams, of which more than 445 are lots for sale, 93 lots for industry and crafts, two commercial lots and a 30.75-dunam lot for a gas station and electric-car charging (Simcha Raz). Quotes: Dagan: "After 21 years since the expulsion, northern Samaria is coming back to life in every field... We are not only founding communities; we are building a whole region." Barkat: the next big goal "is dismantling the Palestinian Authority" (Arutz 7). A dissent from the right: activist Meir Ettinger warned that unless policy changes, new industrial zones reported as good news for settlement will be "a lifeline for the Palestinian Authority," since factories have been moving work into PA areas and Judea and Samaria zones since Palestinian workers were barred from entering Israel, and more zones could employ tens of thousands more Arabs (Ettinger).
items.source: Ynet / Arutz 7 / Samaria Regional Council / Israel Hayom (Yotam Deshe) / Olam Katan (Simcha Raz)

places.name: Bustanei Hefetz industrial zone (next to Avnei Hefetz)
places.note: Approximate: point is Avnei Hefetz (Nominatim); the zone's boundaries are not mapped

items.headline: Olam Katan count: 21 new communities went up in Judea and Samaria in ten months, out of 104 approved under the outgoing government
items.summary: Olam Katan's settlement reporter Simcha Raz tallied the outgoing government's settlement record: 104 communities approved in Judea and Samaria over four years, of which 34 were existing communities approved after the fact (among them Sde Boaz, Evyatar, Migron, Brosh HaBika and Avigayil), six were neighborhoods made into separate communities, 11 are farms to become communities and one (Har Bazak) is an army base to become a community. That leaves 52 new communities, of which 21 went up in the last ten months: 11 in Samaria, three each in Binyamin and Gush Etzion, and two each in the Jordan Valley and the Hebron Hills. In Samaria the list includes the four northern Samaria communities rebuilt after the 2005 evacuation (Homesh, Sa-Nur, Ganim, Kadim) and Noa, Har Eival, Emek Dotan, Rehavam, Geva Shomron, Shalem and Rom Gilboa (Olam Katan; Simcha Raz). Raz says about 160 farms were set up under Minister Smotrich in the early years of the term, holding more than a million dunams. Activist Ayelet Lash shared the figures ("nothing like it since the 1980s") (Ayelet Lash). The 104 figure matches what Smotrich gave at the Metzukei Eretz ceremony in September as reported by Makor Rishon; the count of 21 is Olam Katan's own and was not checked against a second source.

items.headline: Stone attacks hurt four Israelis on Thursday morning, JSR and rescue volunteers say; shepherds attacked near Ateret and at Yehonatan farm
items.summary: Incidents logged on Thursday, 12 Nov: at about 6:00 AM, Arabs from Sa'ir threw stones at residents of Ma'ale Tidhar riding a Ranger utility vehicle in Gush Etzion, lightly hurting one; at about 6:15 AM, stones on Route 60 south of the Halhul junction, no injuries; at about 7:20 AM, two Kfar Tarfon residents lightly hurt by stones (Olam Katan's Simcha Raz; JSR's report described them as Jewish shepherds attacked on the access road near Ateret, JSR). Overnight, an Israeli car's window was smashed and a driver lightly hurt near Einav, apparently by a thrown object, according to activist Ayelet Lash citing a Judea and Samaria rescue volunteer group (Ayelet Lash; unconfirmed). Channel 14 headlined four Israelis lightly hurt in a string of stone attacks since the night (Channel 14 headline seen in Google News; article not opened). Later: six Arabs attacked a shepherd with stones at Yehonatan farm in Gush Etzion, no injuries (JSR); the access road to Shir LeDavid farm in Samaria was blocked with stones and cleared by the farm's residents (JSR); and burning tires were set overnight south of Ir HaTmarim in Binyamin, no damage (JSR). JNS Hebrew's Netanel Frankel counted four terror incidents in the day, two of them stone attacks on shepherds, citing JSR (Netanel Frankel). JSR's summary for Wednesday, 11 Nov: eight incidents, namely four attacks on shepherds and residents, two stone attacks on vehicles and two roads blocked with stones (JSR).
items.source: JSR / Olam Katan (Simcha Raz) / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) / Ayelet Lash

places.name: Kfar Tarfon (near Ateret)
places.note: Approximate: point is the village of Atara (Nominatim); the hilltop itself is not mapped

items.headline: Hundreds march with Hamas, Fatah and PFLP flags at a Silwad funeral, near Ofra and Route 60; army enters to disperse it, Elisha Yered reports
items.summary: Israel on Thursday, 12 Nov, handed over the body of Walid Khaled Ahmad, 17, of Silwad, who died in Megiddo Prison in March 2025 about six months after his arrest; the PA's prisoners' commission says the release followed legal action by its lawyer (WAFA). He was arrested in September 2024 on suspicion of throwing stones at Israeli soldiers and had not been charged, according to the Guardian and AP at the time (Guardian); Palestinian sources blame starvation and denial of care, which Israel's prison service did not confirm; WAFA says an Israeli court closed the inquiry into his death in December 2025. The funeral went from Ramallah to Silwad, attended by thousands according to a Palestinian outlet, which also says Brazil's envoy to the PA took part (Palestine Today, Arabic; the envoy's presence is unconfirmed). Elisha Yered posted video of hundreds marching with Hamas, Fatah and Popular Front flags in Silwad, a short distance from Ofra and Route 60, and later wrote that Binyamin Brigade troops were entering to break up the march (Yered; Yered, second video); no army statement on the dispersal was found. Elchanan Groner said Central Command and the Judea and Samaria Division "failed utterly" by allowing a pre-announced Hamas procession that brought back "scenes from before 7 October" (Groner). Yered and Groner call the dead teen a terrorist; the public record shows only the stone-throwing suspicion.
items.source: Elisha Yered / Elchanan Groner / WAFA / Guardian

items.headline: Army destroys a memorial in Turmus Ayya to a terrorist killed during attacks, a week after a similar demolition in Burqa
items.summary: Israeli forces on Thursday, 12 Nov, destroyed a monument in Turmus Ayya, in Binyamin, built in memory of a terrorist who was killed after carrying out attacks, Olam Katan and Elisha Yered reported; Yered said the army last week also took down a terrorist's memorial in Burqa and displays glorifying terror in other villages (Olam Katan; Yered). The Palestinian news site Ultra Palestine confirmed that Israeli forces demolished a "memorial to the martyrs" in Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah (Ultra Palestine, Arabic). Neither report names the man commemorated.
items.source: Olam Katan / Elisha Yered / Ultra Palestine

items.headline: Civil Administration demolishes five illegal Palestinian buildings in the Gush Etzion area and clears farming encroachment at Wadi Artas
items.summary: Civil Administration forces, secured by the Etzion Brigade, demolished five illegal Palestinian structures built on farmland at al-Walaja, Khirbet a-Deir and Umm Salamuna in the Gush Etzion area: three houses, a car wash and a garage. They also cleared an illegal agricultural encroachment at Wadi Artas on the edge of Bethlehem, according to posts by Olam Katan's Simcha Raz and JNS Hebrew's Netanel Frankel citing the Etzion Brigade spokesperson's photos (Simcha Raz; Netanel Frankel). Gush Etzion council head Yaron Rosenthal: "We will keep acting with full force against illegal building in the area" (Frankel).
items.source: Olam Katan (Simcha Raz) / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) / Gush Etzion council

items.headline: Palestinian from Rammun to be charged with attempted murder over last month's arson and knife attack at Hanina farm: "I planned to stab a settler"
items.summary: Police and the Shin Bet filed a prosecutor's statement on Wednesday, 11 Nov, ahead of an indictment against a man in his 30s from the Palestinian village of Rammun over the attempted attack at Hanina farm in Binyamin last month. Two men reached the farm's grazing land and set fire to a farm vehicle; one drew a knife (about 10 centimeters long) and was overpowered by residents, and the other fled. In questioning he said: "I set fire to a car near a tent of Jewish settlers and at the same time I planned to stab a settler." He is to be charged with attempted murder and planning military activity (Ynet; Arutz 7). The desk reported the attack and the arrest of the second suspect on 6 Oct.

places.name: Hanina farm (near Rammun)
places.note: Approximate: point is Rammun village (Nominatim); the farm is not mapped

items.headline: Army's no-questions-asked weapons return drive collects 210 guns and 3,800 grenades and launchers; extended to Monday
items.summary: The army said more than 300,000 items of military equipment have been returned since it opened 62 collection points at bases on 1 Nov, with legal immunity for those returning gear. Over two weeks it collected about 210 firearms; 3,800 stun and fragmentation grenades, mortars and launchers; 8,700 uniform and textile items; 3,000 weapon accessories; 1,600 items of combat gear including vests and helmets; and 430 medical items. Because of the response the drive was extended by two days, to Monday; after that, immunity ends and enforcement against holding military equipment resumes (Times of Israel's Emanuel Fabian; JNS). Stolen army weapons reaching criminal and terror groups are a recurring desk topic.
items.source: IDF (via Times of Israel and JNS)

items.headline: Settlement camp braces for a government that relies on Arab parties: bereaved parents' forum vows to defend the farms; Strock answers Liberman
items.summary: With the change bloc weighing a government backed by Arab parties, the "HaBayta" forum of bereaved families held an emergency meeting and declared a campaign to protect the farms and open land in Judea and Samaria; bereaved fathers warned of severe security consequences: "We will not sit quietly while the lives of Israel's citizens are sold" (Olam Katan). Makor Rishon reported that Galilee Jews fear the momentum of Jewish settlement there will be hurt under the next government (Makor Rishon headline via Google News; the site blocks automated readers, so the article was not read). Settlement Minister Orit Strock answered Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman, who had questioned a transitional government's authority on security, by listing what she said the last transitional government he sat in did: handing Israeli sovereign territory to Lebanon without a Knesset vote, "confidence-building measures" for the PA, a U.S. presidential visit to east Jerusalem without Israeli escort, and Operation Breaking Dawn in Gaza; she called the attacks on the security forces' loyalty "toxic and fake" (Netanel Frankel; Olam Katan).
items.source: Olam Katan / JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) / Makor Rishon

items.headline: HonestReporting: big outlets now call Judea and Samaria the "occupied West Bank" in nearly half their stories, up from 39% a year earlier
items.summary: The media watchdog HonestReporting analyzed 5,370 articles from 17 major outlets between May 2025 and October 2026 and found that 46.3% used "occupied West Bank" and 62.3% used related terms such as "occupation"; the share using "occupied" rose from 38.9% (May to October 2025) to 52.2% (May to October 2026). By outlet: BBC 71%, CNN 68%, NBC 64%, Los Angeles Times 61%, Reuters 60%, Fox News 12%. In a sample of 60 articles, 50 used the term in the outlet's own voice rather than in a quote (JNS). Figures are HonestReporting's, shared with JNS; the study itself was not opened.

items.headline: Rain uncovers a century-old British shell near Route 437 by a rehabilitation farm for wounded soldiers; bomb squad destroys it
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council said on Thursday, 12 Nov, that rain exposed British unexploded ordnance about 100 years old near Route 437, close to Yinon Farm and the "Island of Tranquility" farm at Nofei Prat near Ma'ale Adumim, which serves as a rehabilitation center for dozens of wounded soldiers and security personnel; a bomb disposal expert destroyed it in a controlled blast (JNS; Makor Rishon carried the same story, headline seen via Google News).

places.name: Nofei Prat (Route 437 area)
places.note: Approximate: Nofei Prat community point (Nominatim); the find site is not mapped

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: a father and son hurt in Burqa; a new outpost reported in al-Jiftlik; 165 more dunams seized, says the PA
items.summary: Short items from Palestinian, PA and activist sources, not confirmed by Israeli authorities. An Israeli activist account posted that a family returning from the olive harvest in Burqa, east of Ramallah, was attacked by about 10 Israelis and came home with broken limbs (Mistaclim); Palestinian outlets reported a child and his father hurt there (Al-Quds and Yafa headlines via Google News; not opened). No Israeli-side account was found. A Palestinian outlet says settlers set up a new outpost with tents, water and power on a hill above the al-Shuna community in al-Jiftlik in the Jordan Valley, and that masked men surrounded about 80 families' homes (Noon Post, Arabic). The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission says Israel issued military orders seizing a further 165 dunams in the Qalqilya, Nablus and Tubas districts (Al-Shaab radio, Arabic), and counts 1,182 arson incidents by the army and settlers since October 2023 (Anadolu Arabic); these are PA figures. Local Call's Oren Ziv quotes Palestinian families who say they fled their Jericho homes after Israelis moved in (see the 12 Nov item on the army's decision there) (Local Call). Peace Now and Rabbis for Human Rights plan a joint olive-picking day with Palestinian farmers on 20 Nov (Peace Now).
items.source: Activists / Palestinian media / PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission / Local Call / Peace Now

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian media say Israeli troops set up a checkpoint at Jubata al-Khashab, held two young men for hours, and shelled near Bariqa
items.summary: Syrian outlets reported on Thursday, 12 Nov, that Israeli forces set up a checkpoint and searched passersby on the Ein al-Baida to Jubata al-Khashab road in northern Quneitra (Syria Now), then detained a young man and later a second one after searching homes in Jubata al-Khashab (Al-Ikhbariya, Syrian state TV), and released both hours later (Al-Ikhbariya). Al-Ikhbariya also reported four artillery shells on woodland at Bariqa in central Quneitra (Al-Ikhbariya). On Wednesday, Al Jazeera reported a patrol west of al-Rafid that searched olive pickers and sent them off their land, and Syria's UN envoy said Israel keeps setting up new positions inside the UNDOF zone (Al Jazeera, Arabic). These are Syrian-side reports; no IDF statement was found. Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new on X since the last run, and its Telegram channel's last post dates from July.
items.source: Syrian media (Al-Ikhbariya, Syria Now, Al Jazeera)

items.headline: Police, Shin Bet and National Security Ministry hold a national drill day for mass riots, with a session on terror groups' influence inside Israel
items.summary: The National Security Ministry and Israel Police held a national, multi-agency study day on Thursday, 12 Nov, as part of the "Eretz Ra'asha 3" exercise, to prepare for widespread violent riots across the country. Speakers from academia and the security services lectured on terror organizations' influence on the home front, and the riots in France a few weeks ago were analyzed for lessons; the Shin Bet, the National Security Council, the Home Front Command, Fire and Rescue and local authorities took part (Channel 14; Kipa). Channel 14 framed it as preparation for a possible repeat of the May 2021 riots in mixed cities ("Guardian of the Walls 2"); the official statements do not name a population or a trigger.

items.headline: North: lawyer among four held in Nahf and Majd al-Krum with an armored jeep, 380,000 shekels in cash and army observation gear; crime group's camera network found in Ka'abiyye
items.summary: Northern District police, Yasam Galil and a canine unit searched compounds in Nahf and Majd al-Krum and held four suspects, among them a lawyer and his relatives, on suspicion of shooting in a residential area, other crimes and money laundering. They found a jeep illegally armored against gunfire, an ATV with a mismatched license plate, airsoft pistols, suspected stolen army observation equipment and more than 380,000 shekels in foreign currency (about $70,000 and over 17,000 euros). Police say more than 770 weapons have been seized in the district since the start of the year (JDN; Ayelet Lash, who called it "a drop in the ocean"). In Ka'abiyye, police took down a hidden surveillance center that they say a crime organization used to watch its rivals and police movements, with cameras hidden in treetops on the village's access road, in a communications cabinet and behind a slot cut in a sheet-metal fence (Channel 14). In Kafr Qasim on Thursday, three men in what looked like security-force uniforms blocked a car in daylight, robbed its occupants at gunpoint and fled (Ynet). In the Negev, a 16-year-old from Tarabin was arrested on suspicion of stealing an ATV from a home in Netivot, according to activist Ayelet Lash, who called such thefts "economic terror" (Ayelet Lash; police statement not found, unconfirmed). Lash also posted a video she says shows Arabs wearing skullcaps filming themselves entering the yellow gate of an unnamed Jewish community, asking whether it was a test run (Ayelet Lash; location and identities unverified).
items.source: JDN / Channel 14 / Ynet / Israel Police / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: New Interior Minister Sa'ar moves to strip citizenship from an Umm al-Fahm man who drove a suicide bomber in 2002 and gets PA payments
items.summary: A day after his appointment as interior minister, Gideon Sa'ar (also foreign minister) told Ziad Mahmoud Aref Jabarin of Umm al-Fahm that he will ask the administrative court to revoke his Israeli citizenship under Section 11 of the Citizenship Law, which covers people convicted of terror offenses who served prison time and receive terror-linked payments. According to the case, in 2001 Jabarin bought a weapon and bullets from a West Bank resident and sold them to Fatah-affiliated PA police officers, and in 2002 he drove two men from the Jenin area knowing they were on their way to a suicide attack, one carrying a 10-kilogram explosive belt, and guided one of them toward Karkur; he was sentenced in 2004 to 20 years. Sa'ar acted, the report says, because Jabarin also receives payments from the PA (Ynet).

items.headline: Moran Tal and Meir Ettinger on Ra'am's roots in the Islamic Movement; Channel 14 says Jabareen backed a convicted arms dealer; state asked platforms to remove 186,000 Arabic posts
items.summary: Regavim OSINT researcher Moran Tal argued in a long X thread that Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas, who told President Herzog last week that he follows the path of Islamic Movement founder Abdullah Nimr Darwish, comes from a Muslim Brotherhood movement that seeks a caliphate in one state; she says that in a speech he boasted of entering politics in coordination with Hamas leaders in prison, and posted video clips she says support this (Moran Tal; Moran Tal; her reading of the clips, not independently checked). She also discussed the Arab leadership and governance in the Negev on Regavim's behalf on the "Al HaMashma'ut" podcast (Regavim). Channel 14 reported that Hadash chairman Youssef Jabareen voiced support for Nasser Badran, convicted of aiding Islamic Jihad and selling weapons to terror groups (quoted by Moran Tal, Moran Tal quoting Channel 14; Channel 14 article not opened). Meir Ettinger described how a Hebrew University-based institute's poll was, in his view, used to press Liberman toward a government backed by Ra'am (Ettinger). Elchanan Groner promoted the second part of a HaKol HaYehudi magazine feature on internal state debates about the threat from Arab citizens (Groner). From the other side: Haaretz reported that since 2024 the state prosecution's cyber unit asked platforms to remove 186,000 Arabic posts and five in Hebrew, 99% of them on suspicion of incitement to terror, and that 73% of the requests were granted (Haaretz, feed summary; paywalled).
items.source: Moran Tal / Regavim / Meir Ettinger / Channel 14 / HaKol HaYehudi / Haaretz

items.headline: France bars Samaria council head Yossi Dagan from entering the country over his role in building communities; Israel calls it "completely unacceptable"
items.summary: Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan said on Wednesday, 11 Nov, that French border officials at Charles de Gaulle airport in Paris refused him entry last week, where he was due to meet elected officials before flying on to the Czech Republic. He said an officer showed him documents saying he was barred as head of the Samaria council, for building communities in Judea and Samaria and for working toward a return to Gush Katif; the officer spoke of 35 communities and Dagan says he corrected him to 50. He also said the officer told him the decision had been taken in May or June, and that he had been asked by the Foreign Ministry not to make the incident public (Ynet does not say which country's ministry). The French Foreign Ministry told Ynet that Dagan is under an administrative entry ban "because of his active part in carrying out settlement policy in the West Bank." Israel's Foreign Ministry said it views the decision "with gravity," called it a "completely unacceptable" step against a law-abiding elected official on clearly political grounds, and said Israel will demand an explanation from France and "consider its steps" (Ynet; Olam Katan). Dagan's reply, as he told it: "I am proud to be a Jew and a Zionist and to build the historic homeland of the Jewish people"; he went on to meetings with government ministers and lawmakers in Prague (Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe). Reactions: former U.S. ambassador David Friedman wrote "France is nuts" (Friedman). Yotam Deshe argued that people who demand a diplomatic agreement should respect the one already signed: the Oslo accords left Area C under Israeli administration and made Israel responsible for the security of the Israeli communities there, so the Samaria council operates under that agreement (Deshe). On the other side, Kerem Navot's Dror Etkes said he hoped other countries would bar more council heads, officials and officers (Etkes).
items.source: Ynet / Samaria Regional Council / Foreign Ministry / Israel Hayom (Yotam Deshe)

items.headline: Central Command chief Avi Bluth asks the attorney general to set rules for making Judea and Samaria's farms legal
items.summary: Israel Hayom's settlements correspondent Yotam Deshe reported first on Wednesday, 11 Nov, that Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, head of Central Command, has asked the government's legal adviser to advance the regularization of the agricultural farms in Judea and Samaria. Deshe's account: even farms that work in coordination with the security forces and the government have no legal status for their buildings, so anyone who sets up an unauthorized outpost can also call it a "farm," and the public cannot tell the two apart. Most security officials, he wrote, back the coordinated farms and see them as part of the defense of open areas. Bluth wants rules for when a farm may operate lawfully, so the authorities can regularize the farms that meet them and enforce the law against outposts set up without approval (Yotam Deshe). Arab48 relayed the Israel Hayom report, describing it as an army move to make the farms an official security arm (Arab48). The Israel Hayom article itself blocks automated readers, so this item rests on Deshe's post and the Arab48 relay.

items.headline: Army decides not to remove the Israelis living in the eight homes on Jericho's edge, and reinforces the nearby post from a squad to a platoon
items.summary: A week after a group of Israelis moved into eight homes on the outskirts of Jericho, in Area C, without coordinating with the army, Central Command under Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth finished a security review and found no real security reason, for now, to keep them out, Channel 13 reported. The army will not evict them right away, but it will not give them the protection it gives other Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria; instead the nearby army post will grow from a squad to a platoon. The Civil Administration is still examining the purchase of the land, and the army says the houses were built without permits and have demolition orders, like thousands of other structures, but no demolition is expected soon because a legal process has to be completed first (Kipa, citing Channel 13). Walla's military correspondent Amir Bohbot wrote that Bluth should take a clear public position on settlement in Area C opposite Jericho rather than vague wording, and said the IDF spokesman had not answered his questions (Amir Bohbot). Background: the families entered the homes, bought through the Nachala movement, last week (see the Desk's 5 Nov edition).

places.name: Jericho
places.note: Nominatim (city point); the eight homes are not plotted, approximate

items.headline: Education minister and Samaria council agree on the first school in the rebuilt northern Samaria communities, for children of Ganim, Kadim and Noa
items.summary: Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan told the community committee heads of Ganim, Kadim and Noa on Wednesday, 11 Nov, that a regional elementary school (grades 1 to 6) will be built for the new communities in northern Samaria, after a tour with Education Minister Yoav Kish more than a month ago. It is the first school to be built in the communities that were removed in the 2005 disengagement and have now been re-established. Kish called it "a holiday for settlement and a historic step." According to the council, the school is part of a plan, run with government ministries, Amana and the Settlement Division, to build 19 new communities in northern Samaria in place of the four removed in 2005; it says 11 new communities were set up in the council in the past eight months, among them Eival, Rehavam, Rom Gilboa, Shalem, Emek Dotan, Noa and Geva Shomron, plus the four disengagement communities Homesh, Sa-Nur, Ganim and Kadim (Srugim; Olam Katan). The list of 11 communities is the council's own count.
items.source: Srugim / Olam Katan (Samaria Regional Council announcement)

items.headline: High Court issues an order against the state over enforcement in the Judean Desert "agreed reserve"; Regavim says the timing raises hard questions
items.summary: A High Court panel led by Court President Yitzhak Amit, with Justices Ofer Grosskopf and Daphne Barak-Erez, on Tuesday, 10 Nov, issued an order nisi (an order requiring the state to explain itself) on petitions by the Palestinian Authority against Israeli enforcement in the "agreed reserve" east of Gush Etzion. In June 2024 the security cabinet decided Israel would take over enforcement powers there, which the Oslo accords had given to the PA, citing large-scale PA takeover of the area and thousands of illegal structures; the PA petitioned in November 2024. The court merged four petitions, two on the principle and two on a school building in the reserve, and gave the state until 3 Jan 2027 to explain why it should not refrain from enforcement, and why the 2024 order limiting building there should not be canceled. It also asked the state to address whether it should avoid acting against people holding PA building permits, and whether to separate "natural growth" of existing villages from new building. Interim orders stay in force (Olam Katan). Regavim, which led the legal fight, said issuing the order on the day the new Knesset was sworn in "raises hard questions" and called it a "cynical use of the political momentum" (Simcha Raz, quoting Regavim).

places.name: Agreed reserve, Judean Desert (east of Gush Etzion)
places.note: Approximate: marker at Nokdim; the reserve lies to the east

items.headline: Central Command to stop army-supported training for community standby squads across Judea and Samaria next week, citing budget cuts
items.summary: Central Command has decided to halt, from next week, all army-supported training of the standby squads (the armed resident teams that are the first line of defense in each community) across Judea and Samaria, Channel 14's Elya Aviv reported on Wednesday, 11 Nov. The reason given is cuts across IDF units' budgets and resources. A security source in Judea and Samaria told Channel 14 that "the standby squads are the shield of the communities, and their readiness must not be touched even for one day." A senior Central Command officer said: "This is something we don't like at all either. There are cuts in all IDF units and the wave has reached us too," adding that the army is working to restore the training as soon as possible and "will not abandon the security of the residents" (Olam Katan, citing Channel 14; Simcha Raz). The decision comes a few days after the Defense Ministry's eastern-border plan called for arming and training local standby squads (see the 11 Nov lead).

items.headline: Shepherds attacked at three farms, one hurt in the leg at Yoyo farm; stones hit cars on Route 60 near Ma'ale Levona
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) logged, on Wednesday, 11 Nov: a Jewish shepherd attacked by two Arabs at Magen Yehuda in Samaria, with no injuries (JSR; Olam Katan's Simcha Raz placed it near the Sela army post, Simcha Raz); a shepherd from Yoyo farm (also called Sfat HaMidbar farm) in the Hebron Hills hurt in the leg in an attack (JSR; Simcha Raz); stones thrown at a shepherd from Tomer Liani farm in the Hebron Hills, no injuries (JSR); two Arab "olive harvesters" throwing stones at Israelis in the grazing land of Maoz Shaul farm in Samaria (JSR); and, at about 6:50 PM Israel time, stones at several Israeli cars on Route 60 south of the Ma'ale Levona South junction, with a windshield damaged and no injuries (JSR). Activist Ayelet Lash said the stone throwers came from the Sinjil area and also threw a bottle of paint at another car (Ayelet Lash). JSR's morning summary counted three attacks on shepherds and residents, one stone attack and two roadblocks set by Arabs between Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday morning (JSR), and JNS Hebrew reporter Netanel Frankel listed the day's incidents the same way (Netanel Frankel). These are JSR's reports; no second outlet carried most of them.
items.source: JSR Situation Room / Olam Katan (Simcha Raz) / Netanel Frankel / Ayelet Lash

places.name: Route 60 south of Ma'ale Levona South junction
places.note: Nominatim point for Ma'ale Levona; the junction is not plotted, approximate

items.headline: Farm owner near Mikhmas films masked men from Mukhmas setting a stone roadblock at night, with activist Arik Ascherman filming beside them
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that shortly before midnight on Tuesday, 10 Nov, the owner of a farm near Mikhmas in Binyamin saw on a security camera Arabs from the village of Mukhmas setting up a roadblock of stones on one of the access roads. When he and a few residents reached the spot, he found left-wing activist Arik Ascherman there with a camera, standing in front of dozens of masked men; Yered posted video and said Ascherman had not been arrested (Elisha Yered, with video; Olam Katan). Background: Ascherman was recently indicted over an assault on a 16-year-old Jewish shepherd near Rimonim in June (Besheva). The account of the roadblock is the farm owner's and Yered's; Ascherman's side was not published.

places.name: Mikhmas
places.note: Nominatim (community point; the farm road is nearby, approximate)

items.headline: Residents of Givat Beit Anot spot pirate taps on the main water line in the Hebron Hills; an army water-theft team cuts them
items.summary: Residents of the Givat Beit Anot hilltop in the Hebron Hills noticed signs of water theft from the main water line during a routine patrol and called in the army's "Nahshol" team, a unit dedicated to water theft in Judea and Samaria. The soldiers found a network of long-standing illegal connections, hidden under soil and plants, carrying water to nearby Arab villages, and cut and destroyed them (Olam Katan; JSR; Elchanan Groner). Damage figures differ: JSR and Olam Katan say hundreds of thousands of shekels so far; Elisha Yered put it at over a million (Yered); resident Yedidya Amsali said an official told them the loss would have exceeded a million shekels a month had it not been found. Amsali: "There is no substitute for daily Jewish presence on the ground" (Netanel Frankel). Olam Katan notes that the State Comptroller called water theft in Judea and Samaria a serious governance failure as early as 2013. No army statement was found.
items.source: Olam Katan / JSR / Elchanan Groner / Netanel Frankel

places.name: Givat Beit Anot (near Beit Einun)
places.note: Approximate: hilltop not mapped; marker at the Sa'ir–Beit Einun road (Nominatim), assuming Beit Anot is the Beit Einun area

items.headline: Undercover Border Police arrest three wanted men in Urif and Qabalan, two of them Hamas operatives
items.summary: Undercover Border Police officers acting on Shin Bet intelligence raided three locations in the villages of Urif and Qabalan, south of Nablus, overnight into Wednesday, 11 Nov, surrounding the buildings and breaking in, and arrested three wanted men, two of them Hamas operatives. Police said they are suspected of advancing attacks and of activity against the security forces (Israel Police; JNS; Times of Israel's Emanuel Fabian).

items.headline: Civil Administration orders tools returned to Palestinians caught paving a road through a firing zone, a reporter says; Elisha Yered calls it the third such release
items.summary: Reporter Ayana Ben Aderet reported on Tuesday evening, 10 Nov, that the army seized work tools last Saturday from Palestinians paving a road illegally inside a firing zone, but the Civil Administration ordered them returned because enforcement in that case had low priority. She said the road was being built to get around routes the army closed for security reasons after an attack at a checkpoint about six weeks ago (Ayana Ben Aderet). Elisha Yered said this follows the release of a tractor seized at an illegal dump in al-Mughayyir and another at a dump in Burqa, and accused the Civil Administration of a policy that helps the other side take over open land (Elisha Yered). The location of the firing zone was not published, and the Civil Administration's response was not found.

items.headline: Police correct their statement on vehicles taken from Mevaser Shalom: they were seized because the hill is a closed military zone, not because they were unsafe
items.summary: HaKol HaYehudi reported that police had announced they seized "mashtuvot" (unsafe, unlicensed vehicles) at a hilltop in Samaria; residents said the vehicles were legal, and after the site asked, police said the statement was wrong and the vehicles were taken because they were inside a closed military zone. The hill is Mevaser Shalom, where several families have lived for more than a year and a half, on a stretch of the Allon Road between Evyatar and Migdalim; Central Command chief Avi Bluth recently declared it a closed military zone. HaKol says similar seizures of a buggy, a Ranger and other vehicles took place in recent days at Gefen Ami (HaKol HaYehudi). Mevaser Shalom is the site where Israeli cars were set on fire on 9 Nov (see the 10 Nov lead). The police correction is as HaKol reports it.

places.name: Evyatar (near Mevaser Shalom)
places.note: Nominatim point for Evyatar; Mevaser Shalom itself is not mapped, approximate

items.headline: New prayer hall dedicated in Ofra in memory of Dvir Sorek, in the synagogue where his circumcision and funeral took place
items.summary: A new prayer hall named for Dvir Sorek, murdered in a stabbing attack in Gush Etzion in August 2019 shortly before he turned 19, was dedicated this week in a new building of Ofra's old synagogue, where his circumcision was held and from where his funeral left. The new synagogue, "Mizmor LeAsaf," is named for Asaf Hershkovitz, an Ofra resident killed in a shooting attack on Route 60 in May 2001. His father, Yoav Sorek: "Dvir is probably the only person who closed the circle of his life inside the old synagogue building" (Netanel Frankel, photos from the Binyamin council). Makor Rishon carried the story under the headline "From the circumcision to the funeral: a new synagogue in Ofra commemorates two murder victims" (headline seen in a Google News feed; the article blocks automated readers).
items.source: Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew) / Binyamin Regional Council / Makor Rishon

items.headline: Chief of Staff Zamir at the Jordan border: the army must be ready for "rapid change and surprise" even without intelligence warning
items.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir toured the eastern border on Wednesday, 11 Nov, in the sector of the new 96th "Gilad" Division, and said: "Alongside the demand for intelligence warning, the basic state of IDF forces must be readiness for rapid change and surprise." He presented the division, set up during Operation Rising Lion, as a lesson of 7 Oct put into practice, deployed in a forward line of posts in front of the communities, and called the eastern border "of the highest strategic importance"; he also told commanders to keep law and order and to ensure the safety of all populations in the sector (Arutz 7; Emanuel Fabian). The visit came two days after the Defense Ministry's eastern-border settlement plan was reported (see the 11 Nov lead).

items.headline: On the anniversary of Arafat's death, the PA's Ramallah governor writes that "the dream is drawing closer" of a Palestinian flag over Jerusalem's walls; Marda schools hold student rallies, JSR says
items.summary: JSR reported that Laila Ghannam, the PA's governor of Ramallah and al-Bireh, marked 22 years since Yasser Arafat's death with a Facebook post hoping a child would one day raise "the flag of Palestine above the walls of Jerusalem the capital, its minarets and its mosques," ending: "The memory grows distant, the idea remains, and the dream is drawing closer" (JSR). JSR also reported that schools in the village of Marda in Samaria held student rallies stressing Arafat's legacy of struggle against Israel (JSR). Ghannam's post was not checked directly; this is JSR's account.

items.headline: Activist and PA claims: groups ask the attorney general to keep the E1 tender sealed; a new road and a planned caravan site near Kharbatha; work on a road at al-Mughayyir
items.summary: Peace Now, Bimkom and Ir Amim, through lawyer Michael Sfard, wrote to Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara asking her to order that the bids for the 1,234-home E1 tender stay sealed until a new government is formed (Peace Now; Peace Now site). Kerem Navot's Dror Etkes said Israelis are opening a road north of the villages of Kharbatha and Deir Qaddis, through a Bedouin community, that a new outpost is operating nearby and that preparations have begun for a new caravan community called "Netof"; this is his claim, with photos, and no settlement-side source has confirmed the name or plan (Dror Etkes). The PA-side outlet Ultra Palestine reported bulldozing in the al-Rafid plain at al-Mughayyir to open a settler road (Ultra Palestine), and relayed the PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission's claim of 1,182 burnings by the army and settlers in the West Bank between 7 Oct 2023 and 30 Sep 2026, a PA figure that could not be checked (Ultra Palestine).
items.source: Peace Now / Dror Etkes (Kerem Navot) / Ultra Palestine (PA commission)

places.name: Kharbatha Bani Harith
places.note: Nominatim village point; the new road is north of it, approximate

items.headline: Israel's ambassador to the Netherlands is called home after telling a Dutch paper there are "thousands of extremists, thugs and Jewish terrorists" among the settlers
items.summary: Israel's ambassador to the Netherlands, Zvi Aviner Vapni, was summoned home by the Foreign Ministry on Wednesday, 11 Nov, for clarification after an interview with the Dutch daily Algemeen Dagblad. Asked about the ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir, he said they had said things he finds "terrible and unacceptable" and that he feels no need to defend them. Asked about settlers using violence, he said: "Not all of them. 300,000 people live in the settlements, and among them a few thousand extremists. They are hooligans and Jewish terrorists, and they should all go to prison," adding that he thinks 80 percent of Israelis agree (Ynet). His figure of "a few thousand" violent settlers was not sourced in the interview.

items.headline: Channel 18 launches on YouTube with a long interview with Elisha Yered on the "settler violence" campaign; David Friedman promotes it
items.summary: Channel 18 Israel, founded by former U.S. ambassador David Friedman and run by Sam Schubert, launched on YouTube on Wednesday evening, 11 Nov, with a full interview of Elisha Yered, described as a leader of the Hilltop Youth, in Hebrew with English subtitles. Yered said he discussed Arab terror on the ground against the "settler violence" campaign, work on the ground to undo the Oslo accords, and growing up on a hilltop 350 meters from an Arab village with no fence (Elisha Yered). In a clip, Yered calls the Palestinian state plan the "Fayyad Plan": "They create Arab settlement sequences to control the open areas and establish a de facto Palestinian state. We do the opposite" (Channel 18). Friedman wrote: "Here's the other side of the 'settler violence' myth that you won't find anywhere else!" (David Friedman).
items.source: Channel 18 Israel / Elisha Yered / David Friedman

items.headline: Neria Leiter, gravely hurt in the Route 443 ramming attack, leaves Shaare Zedek for rehabilitation, still unconscious
items.summary: Reserve soldier Neria Leiter, son of Israel's ambassador to the United States Yechiel Leiter, who was gravely hurt in a ramming attack on Route 443 more than a month ago, was discharged from Shaare Zedek hospital on Wednesday, 11 Nov, and moved to Sheba hospital for neurological rehabilitation. He is breathing on his own but still unconscious, and is out of danger to his life; the family asks for prayers and privacy (Olam Katan; Netanel Frankel). Ynet's headline gave the transfer to Sheba.

items.headline: Galilee: 40 drones, some able to drop explosives, seized at a Daburiya home; police say 49 armed squads were caught in the act in the north this year
items.summary: Police and the Tax Authority said a 30-year-old Daburiya man was arrested on suspicion of selling drones smuggled into Israel to criminals and of repairing and upgrading them in a home workshop; a raid on his house on Wednesday, 11 Nov, found about 40 drones of various kinds with tactical abilities, some with dual-use technology that allows dropping explosives from the air (HaKol HaYehudi, citing the police and Tax Authority statement; Ayelet Lash). Northern District police data show that since the start of the year officers and Border Police caught at least 49 armed squads or gunmen "red-handed," just before or during a crime, sometimes under fire. The same day: a pistol, a loaded magazine, loose ammunition and two working stun grenades found in a search in Jdeideh-Makr, with the suspect and four relatives arrested; an indictment in Tamra against a 25-year-old caught with a loaded FN pistol; and a remand hearing in Kabul for suspects caught with ready explosive charges (HaKol HaYehudi; Ayelet Lash). The drone details are from the police statement as HaKol quotes it; the original statement was not found.
items.source: Israel Police and Tax Authority via HaKol HaYehudi / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: Tibi tells an Umm al-Fahm wedding "we are the owners of the land"; Ra'am's Yoav Segalovitz joins the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee and says Hamas's status is not a yes-or-no question
items.summary: Activist Ayelet Lash posted video of MK Ahmad Tibi telling a wedding in Umm al-Fahm, "We are the owners of the land" (Ayelet Lash, with video). Islam researcher Moran Tal (Regavim) said the line comes from a Knesset speech Tibi gave in November 2025, which has been widely reused since the election in clips with Palestinian flags and maps of Israel "from the river to the sea," and that at the wedding he joined that trend (Moran Tal). In the new Knesset, Ra'am's number two, former police major general and deputy minister Yoav Segalovitz, was named to the temporary Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee (Olam Katan); Minister Amichai Chikli posted a clip in which Segalovitz says whether Hamas is defined as a terror group "is not a yes-or-no question," and Channel 14's Arab-affairs editor Omri Haim wrote that the former deputy minister is defending the head of the Islamic Movement's political arm, who will not call the terrorists who killed his fellow police officers a terror group (Omri Haim). Moran Tal also posted video of Mansour Abbas in Tiberias, with Yousef Jabareen beside him, warning that if Israel turns an abandoned mosque into a museum the conflict could reach "Jewish places of worship around the world"; the date of that event was not given (Moran Tal). The claims and readings here are those of the people quoted.
items.source: Ayelet Lash / Moran Tal / Olam Katan / Omri Haim (Channel 14)

items.headline: Negev: Times of Israel reports the state demolished the family homes of Youssef Ziadna, the Bedouin driver who rescued about 30 people on 7 Oct
items.summary: The Times of Israel reported that Israel demolished the homes of the family of Youssef Ziadna, the Bedouin minibus driver credited with saving about 30 people on 7 Oct and whose cousins were kidnapped. It quotes him saying he had hoped his community's efforts would change its status, but "in the end, you're still an Arab" (Times of Israel, headline and summary from its feed). The article itself was blocked to automated readers, so the location, the legal status of the homes and the authorities' response could not be checked; the Khamaisi Plan backgrounder covers the Negev planning dispute (Desk backgrounder).

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian media report an Israeli incursion into Samdaniya al-Sharqiya, a man detained at Mazraat al-Fityan and shelling in Quneitra's countryside
items.summary: Syrian state TV Al-Ikhbariya reported on Wednesday evening, 11 Nov, that Israeli forces entered the village of Samdaniya al-Sharqiya in central Quneitra countryside with military vehicles (Al-Ikhbariya), and Syrian outlets reported that Israeli troops detained a man from Mazraat al-Fityan in southern Quneitra (Syrian news account). The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported Israeli artillery fire on central Quneitra countryside and a shepherd held on a farm in the south (SOHR), and another outlet reported an incursion at Sariyat Jamla in the Yarmouk basin of western Daraa (local report). These are Syrian-side reports; no IDF statement was found. Haaretz reported that, according to the Syrian government and the UN, Israel has detained 49 Syrian civilians since taking over the buffer zone at the end of 2024, most still held, with released detainees alleging abuse (Haaretz headline and summary from its feed; the article is behind a paywall). Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new on X or Telegram since the last run.

items.headline: Defense Ministry plan for the eastern border: a 500-kilometer barrier along Jordan, about 40 new settlement and presence points, a wider Route 90 and a goal of doubling the population in ten years
items.summary: Walla's military correspondent Amir Bohbot reported on Monday afternoon, 9 Nov, a Defense Ministry plan for the whole eastern border, and especially the Jordan Valley, that ties security to more civilian settlement. Its main element is a new barrier of about 500 kilometers along the Jordan border, at an estimated cost of 5.5 billion shekels; the first few dozen kilometers have already been built by the Seam Line Administration under Maj. Gen. Eran Ofir, and the ministry is examining moving the barrier's route east to the line of the Jordan River, at about 2 billion shekels more, which would free land to widen Route 90 and for new farming and infrastructure. On the civilian side, the ministry is advancing about 40 settlement and presence points along the eastern region, including pre-army academies, service-year programs and leadership groups, plus new communities such as the farming moshav Batron in the Jordan Valley; local standby squads are to be armed and trained and linked to the new 96th Division, which holds the eastern sector. The stated goal is to double the eastern region's population within a decade; the Transportation Ministry has set aside 35 million shekels to plan a multi-lane Route 90. The plan is run by the ministry's Eastern Region Directorate under Brig. Gen. (res.) Mordechai Benita(Walla). Benita laid out the same plan to Arutz 7 in September, describing 40 new settlement points across seven regional councils plus Beit She'an (Arutz 7, 15 Sep). The two reports give different figures for the population on the Jordanian side of the border (about a quarter million in Walla, about four million in Benita's Arutz 7 interview). The PA-side outlet Ultra Palestine relayed the Walla report as a settlement plan (Ultra Palestine).

items.headline: Four stone attacks on Israelis in one day, and a Palestinian page posts video boasting that stone throwers "drove away" the residents of Kornit farm
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) logged these attacks on Tuesday, 10 Nov: overnight, stones hit an Israeli car on Route 60 about one kilometer north of the British Police junction in Binyamin, damaging the bodywork, with no injuries (JSR); in the morning, stones were thrown at an Israeli car at the old Bik'ot checkpoint in the Jordan Valley (near Hamra, according to Olam Katan's Simcha Raz), with no injuries (JSR); and at about 3:30 PM Israel time stones damaged an Israeli car on the road down from Ariel toward Marda junction, with no injuries (JSR). JSR also reported that Arab channels posted video of stone throwers attacking Israeli residents near Kornit farm in Binyamin, boasting that they had managed to "drive away" the residents; the footage came from the Facebook page "Shabakat al-Irsal" (JSR; Simcha Raz, with the video). JNS Hebrew's Netanel Frankel counted the same four incidents, no injuries, and called it "a normal day in Judea and Samaria" (Netanel Frankel). Simcha Raz said he is preparing a long Olam Katan report on stone attacks in Judea and Samaria (Simcha Raz). The attacks are JSR's reports; no other outlet reported the Route 60 and Bik'ot incidents in what we read.
items.source: JSR Situation Room / Netanel Frankel / Olam Katan (Simcha Raz)

items.headline: Army and Border Police tear down four hilltop sites near Burqa, Wadi Rahim and Jalud; three Israelis detained after clashes, and the settlers dispute the army's account
items.summary: The IDF spokesman said that over two days soldiers and Border Police carried out enforcement against four illegal outposts near the villages of Burqa (Binyamin), Wadi Rahim (southern Hebron Hills) and Jalud, from which, the army says, "violent and illegal acts" were repeatedly carried out. Vehicles, tents and temporary structures "without infrastructure and without adequate living conditions" were removed. During the night operation near Burqa, the army says, forces met barricades of burning tires, rocks and spikes placed by "Israeli rioters"; two security vehicles were damaged, stones were thrown at the forces and fires were set in the village area; three Israeli civilians were detained and taken to the Binyamin police station (Maariv; Emanuel Fabian, Times of Israel). Simcha Raz added that at the site near Burqa the residents say no violence was used against the forces and no stones were thrown (Simcha Raz). Activist Elisha Yered called it a "destruction spree" overnight at two settlement points in Binyamin, carried out by more than 15 Border Police teams, and wrote that it was missed among the day's political headlines (Elisha Yered). The army did not name the four sites.
items.source: IDF via Maariv / Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian) / Olam Katan / Elisha Yered

places.name: Burqa (Ramallah area, Binyamin)
places.note: Nominatim village point; the outpost itself is not mapped, approximate

places.note: Nominatim village point; outpost not mapped, approximate

items.headline: Fifteen settlers under administrative orders ask the Shin Bet chief to cancel them, citing a former police commander's claim that the agency forges intelligence
items.summary: Fifteen people from Judea and Samaria who are under administrative orders (restrictions imposed without trial), represented by the legal aid group Honenu, wrote to Shin Bet head David Zini on Tuesday demanding that the orders be canceled. The letter followed an appearance on Channel 14's "HaPatriotim" by Ch. Supt. (ret.) Avishai Mualem, former head of the police central unit in the Judea and Samaria District, who said the Shin Bet's Jewish Division uses forged "paraphrases" (summaries of secret intelligence) and material against Jewish residents. The letter says that about two years ago Defense Minister Israel Katz ordered an end to administrative detention for settlers, but that Central Command keeps issuing administrative orders with severe restrictions "without trial, without evidence" and without a way to defend themselves. Honenu attorney Moshe Polsky is quoted in the reports (Elchanan Groner, full letter text; Olam Katan). Mualem's forgery claim is his own and has not been tested; we found no Shin Bet response.
items.source: Honenu via Elchanan Groner / Olam Katan

items.headline: A new neighborhood, "Kfaror," goes up at Havat Gilad in memory of Benayahu Melet, farmer Eliav Libi reports
items.summary: Eliav Libi, a farmer and Farms Association board member, posted photos on Tuesday of "the new Kfaror neighborhood of Havat Gilad," which he said was set up in memory of Benayahu Melet, near the place where he was killed (Eliav Libi). In a separate post Libi wrote that the Harashash farm he founded in memory of two friends became a community in the government's latest decision (Eliav Libi). The Kfaror neighborhood is single-source and unconfirmed; we found no council or press report on it.

places.name: Havat Gilad
places.note: OpenStreetMap point; the new neighborhood is not mapped, approximate

items.headline: Thirteen U.S. state attorneys general press Britain and the Netherlands to drop sanctions on Judea and Samaria communities, while J Street and a French bill push the other way
items.summary: Thirteen U.S. state attorneys general, led by Iowa's Brenna Bird and including those of Florida, Georgia, Kansas, South Carolina and Ohio, wrote last week to the British and Dutch ambassadors in Washington asking them to rescind sanctions on Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria. They warned that state laws against boycotts of Israel could bar British and Dutch companies from state contracts or force states to divest from them (JNS). On the other side, the lobby J Street published a policy plan presented by its policy chief Ilan Goldenberg, calling for targeted economic sanctions so that people must choose between the settlements and access to the financial system; it also calls for pausing offensive arms supplies and recognizing a Palestinian state (Makor Rishon). Arab48 reported that a French parliamentary committee on Monday approved a bill by Socialist Party leader Olivier Faure to ban imports of settlement goods and services, including financial services and tourist rentals, with a plenary vote set for 19 Nov; it says President Macron's party and the National Rally oppose it (Arab48). The French bill details are single-source (unconfirmed).

items.headline: PA commission says Israel approved a plan allowing shooting ranges at 31 settlement sites
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said on Tuesday that Israeli authorities approved a plan that adds shooting ranges, for firearms training and qualifying gun holders, to the permitted uses of land set aside for public buildings, commerce, industry and sport at 31 sites: 29 communities and neighborhoods and two industrial zones, among them Sha'ar Binyamin, from south of Nablus to the Jerusalem area and east toward Jericho and the Jordan Valley. The commission cites a 2022 list of nine licensed ranges in communities including Ariel, Karnei Shomron, Ma'on and Alon Shvut, and a 2024 Mateh Binyamin economic company plan for a range in Psagot (Ultra Palestine). These are the PA's claims; we found no Israeli report or Civil Administration notice confirming the plan.
items.source: PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission via Ultra Palestine

items.headline: Jericho's PA governor hosts Archbishop Atallah Hanna, who has called the intifada a "legitimate right," JSR says
items.summary: JSR reported that on Monday, 9 Nov, the PA governor of Jericho, Hussein Hamayel, met Archbishop Atallah Hanna. According to JSR, Hanna has repeatedly backed Palestinian terror: in a television interview he called the intifada a "legitimate right," urged all Arabs to take part and praised "the shahids for their various actions," and in 2016 he took part in a project to fund rebuilding the homes of terrorists demolished by the IDF (JSR; JSR English). This is JSR's account; we did not find the meeting in Palestinian media we read.

items.headline: Police tell the attorney general the Shin Bet's evidence that Ayman Odeh took PA money is too thin to question him; Channel 14's Yinon Magal says the Shin Bet has strong intelligence but is not allowed to investigate
items.summary: Haaretz reported that police, in an official opinion, found the evidence the Shin Bet presented that former Joint List leader Ayman Odeh received money from the Palestinian Authority insufficient to question him under caution; a senior source said that once the material was shown it raised "more question marks than exclamation marks" (Haaretz). Ynet reported that the police opinion sent to the attorney general found no election-financing offense (Ynet), and Olam Katan reported that police found no security offenses. Channel 14's Yinon Magal said that from what he understands from the Shin Bet "there is very significant intelligence, but they are not being allowed to investigate" (Channel 14). This follows Channel 14's report on Monday that intelligence material suggests a senior Arab-party MK received money from the PA over a long period.

items.headline: Channel 14: security officials link a sharp drop in terror warnings since the election to terror groups waiting to see whether an Arab-backed government forms
items.summary: Channel 14's military correspondent Hallel Bitton Rosen reported Tuesday evening that senior security officials see a direct link between the talks on a government backed by Arab parties and the moves of terror groups in the region. A senior source told her that "on the eve of the election the level of warnings was very high," and that its sharp drop, according to intelligence, is because "the red side" is waiting to see how Israeli politics develop (Hallel Bitton Rosen). This is a single-outlet report from an unnamed source.

items.headline: Arab MKs walk out before "Hatikvah" at the swearing-in; a new Joint List MK had shared a post calling Israel's Arabs the vanguard ahead of Hamas rockets; Tibi tells a wedding crowd "we are the owners of the land"
items.summary: Members of the Arab parties left the Knesset plenary before "Hatikvah" was sung at Tuesday's swearing-in of the 26th Knesset; Avigdor Liberman asked: "With them you want to form a government?" (Srugim; Hillel Fuld). Gadi Taub pointed to a post shared by new MK Hassan al-Nasasra (No. 10 on the Joint List), written after the May 2021 riots by Rahat deputy mayor Amer al-Huzail (Gadi Taub). The Telegram channel Abu Ali Express posted video of MK Ahmad Tibi telling guests at a wedding in Umm al-Fahm, in Arabic, "We are the owners of the land" (Abu Ali Express). Channel 14 reported that Mansour Abbas and the Democrats were negotiating over recognizing Hamas as a terror group; Omri Haim, head of Channel 14's Arab-affairs desk, quoted a report that Yair Golan confirmed Abbas would accept that wording in exchange for "real partnership," and called it Muslim Brotherhood pragmatism (Hallel Bitton Rosen; Omri Haim). Researcher Moran Tal wrote that Abbas's own past words about one Islamic state under a caliphate were finally thrown back at him, by Netanyahu himself (Moran Tal). The Tibi video and the Golan quote are each single-source.
items.source: Srugim / Gadi Taub / Abu Ali Express / Channel 14 / Moran Tal

items.headline: Three young Nazareth men from the Bakri crime group charged with shooting at a Kafr Manda gas station owner's home after he refused to pay up to a million shekels
items.summary: Israel Police said that a businessman in the north reported that a man was demanding 400,000 shekels in protection money from him under threats; soon after, a cell of the Samir Bakri crime organization shot at his home, police gave chase, and two suspects were hit by police fire (Israel Police). On Monday prosecutors indicted three Nazareth residents aged 17, 18 and 23 for shooting, extortion under threats, carrying weapons and other offenses; according to the reports the demand later rose to one million shekels and shots were also fired at the gas station he owns.(Elchanan Groner). Separately, Regavim welcomed the police "Shadow Guardians" operation against protection rackets (which led to the arrest of al-Battuf council head Ahed Rahal, reported here yesterday) and said its work in the Galilee shows governance gaps in some northern local authorities, including land, planning committees and the laundering of illegal building (Regavim).
items.source: Israel Police / Elchanan Groner / Channel 14 / Regavim

items.headline: At least ten arrested, including active-duty soldiers, on suspicion of smuggling weapons from Syria into Israel and selling them
items.summary: A joint Shin Bet, police and IDF investigation exposed a network of at least ten suspects, among them soldiers in active service, suspected of using their operational access and closeness to the border to bring weapons from Syria into Israel on several occasions and then selling and distributing them inside Israel. How the weapons were moved, and who was meant to receive them, has not been published; the suspects were sent for further criminal and security questioning (JDN; Olam Katan). Where the weapons ended up (criminal or terror use) is not yet known.

items.headline: Nachala sets up its temporary "Halutzei Aza" settlement site near Sderot, aiming for a new Sderot neighborhood on Beit Hanoun land
items.summary: The Nachala settlement movement put up its temporary "Halutzei Aza" (Pioneers of Gaza) site near Sderot overnight Monday to Tuesday, after its families left the Simhoni forest at the Jewish National Fund's request. Their next goal is to move into Nisanit and to promote a new Sderot neighborhood on Beit Hanoun land, in line with the vision of Sderot mayor Alon Davidi. Nachala chair Daniella Weiss said: "A true oath of allegiance means a practical return and settlement in the Gaza region" (Olam Katan). The report is based on Nachala's own announcement.

places.name: Sderot
places.note: Nominatim city point; the temporary site is nearby, approximate

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian media report Israeli checkpoints at Jubata al-Khashab and Rasm al-Halabi; Halutzei HaBashan urges standing firm against pressure to withdraw
items.summary: Syrian state TV (al-Ikhbariya), cited by Arab48, said Israeli forces set up a checkpoint at the entrance to Jubata al-Khashab in Quneitra province on Tuesday and searched passersby, a day after a similar checkpoint at the Rasm al-Halabi junction in central Quneitra; Syria's SANA news agency said Israeli troops fired toward journalists documenting in the Quneitra countryside on Monday (Arab48). The IDF has not commented in what we read. The Bashan settlement movement Halutzei HaBashan posted a video on Tuesday night saying Israel "must stand like a fortified wall against all the pressure to withdraw from the Bashan and from all parts of our land" (Halutzei HaBashan); it did not say what pressure it meant, and its Telegram channel had no new posts.
items.source: Syrian media via Arab48 / Halutzei HaBashan

items.headline: Beita industrial zone and a Lubban al-Sharqiya scrapyard set on fire; a JNS Hebrew reporter says the Beita fires came after Arabs burned Jewish cars at Mevaser Shalom
items.summary: Beita mayor Mahmoud Barham told Ultra Palestine that about 70 masked men in matching black clothes attacked the village's industrial zone at about 4 PM on Monday, 9 Nov, burning bulldozers, trucks, cars and electrical equipment, with initial losses of about 5 million shekels and no workers hurt; Arab48, citing Anadolu, gave about 200 attackers and 10 million shekels (Ultra Palestine). The zone lies near Jabal Sabih, the site of Evyatar. Earlier the same afternoon, JSR reported that Arabs set Israeli vehicles on fire at nearby Mevaser Shalom (reported here yesterday). JNS Hebrew's Netanel Frankel wrote that "yesterday they torched Jews' cars and Jews torched Arabs' cars in response" (Netanel Frankel). Overnight Tuesday to Wednesday, the IDF said forces were rushed to Lubban al-Sharqiya after reports and footage of vehicles burning (Arutz 7); Kan posted footage of cars burning in a scrapyard there (Kan), and Ultra Palestine blamed settlers. No arrests or official findings on who set either fire have been reported; the damage figures are Palestinian claims.
items.source: Ultra Palestine / Arab48 / Netanel Frankel / IDF via Arutz 7 / Kan
