items.headline: Harvest clash near Jalud and Qusra with activists and foreign photographers; army says dozens of Israelis threw stones, police report two lightly hurt
items.summary: Olam Katan's Simcha Raz reported a clash near Jalud during an olive-harvest event with anarchists, foreign photographers and left-wing groups, with two people hurt (Simcha Raz); police said two people were lightly hurt and taken to the hospital (Walla). The IDF said forces were called to Jalud over friction that began before they arrived, and then to Qusra, where dozens of "Israeli rioters" threw stones when the forces got there; troops used riot-control means, and the army said attempts to stir friction "harm the security of the area." Rabbis for Human Rights says about 20 settlers attacked with clubs and stones and six people were hurt, including a journalist (Walla). Separately, Haaretz reported (article blocked; feed summary only) that Palestinian professor Dirar Aliyan, a university president and British citizen, says troops beat him during a night raid while looking for a wanted nephew; this is his account.
items.source: Olam Katan (Simcha Raz) / Walla / IDF / Haaretz

items.headline: Activist Ayelet Lash posts photos of a Ramallah-area man she says shows off stolen Israeli luxury cars
items.summary: Ayelet Lash posted images on Tuesday of a man she named as Bashir Jadir from the Ramallah area, who she says posts photos of many luxury cars, some of them stolen from Jews, (Ayelet Lash). This is her claim; we could not confirm the man's identity or that the cars are stolen.

items.headline: Stones hit Jewish children playing in a garden near Arraba, and Arabs set Israeli cars on fire at Mevaser Shalom, on a day of more than ten attacks logged by the Situation Room
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) reported that on Monday evening, 9 Nov (about 7:50 PM Israel time), stones were thrown at Jewish children playing in a garden near the Arab village of Arraba in the Dotan Valley, northern Samaria, and that several people were hurt (JSR). Earlier in the afternoon JSR reported that Arabs set Israeli vehicles on fire at Mevaser Shalom in Samaria, with no injuries (JSR, with photo); Olam Katan's Simcha Raz and activist Ayelet Lash said the arsonists came from the village of Awsarin and that the site is near Evyatar (Simcha Raz; Ayelet Lash). The rest of JSR's day: at about 9:30 AM stones hit a car on Route 60 about 100 meters south of Sha'ar Binyamin junction, damaging the windshield; the rescue group Hatzalah Judea and Samaria told JNS one person was lightly hurt and drove on to get treatment (JSR; JNS). At about 10:40 AM some 20 Arabs got out of a garbage truck and attacked a Jewish shepherd with stones and clubs in pasture near Kfar Tapuach; no one was hurt (Ayelet Lash says they came from Yasuf) (JSR). Stones were also thrown at the gas station of Burqa in Samaria (JSR), at a shepherd of the Hesed LeAvraham farm northwest of Deir Jarir in Binyamin (JSR), by two Arab children at an Israeli car near Deir Samit in the Hebron Hills (JSR), at a car on the Lamaked (Doran) road in the southern Hebron Hills (Olam Katan), at an Israeli woman's car at western Marda junction, cracking the windshield (JSR), and at an Israeli car on Route 60 near Ofra (JSR). JSR also said eight Arabs attacked two Israeli residents on what JSR calls the Ga'ava road in Binyamin, with no injuries reported (JSR), and that in the morning an Arab who tried to throw a firebomb at soldiers near Zababdeh was shot by them (JSR). JNS Hebrew reporter Netanel Frankel summed up the day as stones at children near Arraba, an attempted firebomb, cars set on fire and stone attacks in ten other places (Netanel Frankel). These are JSR's own reports. Apart from the Sha'ar Binyamin stoning (JNS, Hatzalah) and the Zababdeh shooting, no police or army statement was found, so the number and condition of the hurt children, and the details of the other incidents, are unconfirmed.
items.source: JSR Situation Room / JNS / Olam Katan / Netanel Frankel

items.headline: Ten Islamic Jihad suspects arrested in Arraba over a planned attack on Israelis in northern Samaria, the third such operation there in two months
items.summary: The army said soldiers of the Paratroopers reconnaissance unit and the Duvdevan unit, with Border Police and on Shin Bet intelligence, raided several sites in Arraba, southwest of Jenin, early Monday, 9 Nov, and arrested ten men who were organizing a terror network to carry out an attack on Israeli civilians in northern Samaria (Olam Katan, IDF statement; JNS). Ynet reports that the forces hit ten buildings at once and found all ten wanted men within about half an hour, that the suspects are linked to Islamic Jihad, and that this is the third major operation in two months under the Menashe Brigade: an earlier ten-man cell, a cell from Qabatiya (five arrested) and a Hamas network in Aqaba, where a rocket without a launcher and an M-16 rifle were seized (Ynet). Times of Israel military reporter Emanuel Fabian and Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe carried the same army account (Emanuel Fabian; Yotam Deshe). A Makor Rishon headline names Mevo Dotan as the suspected target (headline only; unconfirmed).
items.source: IDF via Olam Katan / JNS / Ynet

items.headline: Noa in northern Samaria receives its official community code, the 40th new community recognized this way in under a year
items.summary: The Interior Ministry on Monday, 9 Nov, gave Noa in northern Samaria an official community code (semel yishuv), the last step in making it a full community in the state's records. The code lets it get a security coordinator post, Israel Post service and a direct water hookup from Mekorot. Noa was approved as a new community by the security cabinet in March 2026, and Central Command head Avi Bluth signed its jurisdiction area; it sits in a bloc with Ganim and Kadim (Olam Katan). Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said 40 community codes have been issued in less than a year for the new communities and for regularizing young settlements: "Against those who want to set up a government with terror supporters, destroy the settlements and set up a Palestinian state, we are building, regularizing and strengthening our hold." JNS Hebrew reporter Netanel Frankel gave the same figure, and Olam Katan's X account posted the Samaria Council's photo (Netanel Frankel; Olam Katan on X). The figure of 40 comes from Smotrich's office (not independently counted).

items.headline: Central Command signs the jurisdiction for "Mevo'ot Lachish," a 3,039-dunam Gush Etzion industrial zone north of the Tarqumiya crossing
items.summary: Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe first reported that the head of Central Command signed the jurisdiction area for Mevo'ot Lachish, a planned industrial zone of 3,039 dunams (about 750 acres) just north of the Tarqumiya crossing. The Settlement Administration and the Civil Administration are leading the plan with the Gush Etzion Regional Council; Deshe notes a Palestinian industrial zone had earlier been promoted for the same area (Yotam Deshe). Council head Yaron Rosenthal told Olam Katan the zone will lie between the villages of Tarqumiya, Beit Ula and Nuba and the Adullam area, is meant to strengthen Israel's hold on the seam line and the Route 6 and Kiryat Gat area, and should bring the council more than 100 million shekels a year; he thanked Smotrich for "stopping Arab building." Smotrich linked it to more than 60,000 homes being advanced across Judea and Samaria and said: "We are building, regularizing and developing, not in words but in deeds" (Olam Katan; Simcha Raz; Netanel Frankel). Signing the jurisdiction is a procedural step; planning and building approvals are still ahead. The revenue figure is the council head's estimate.

items.headline: Tenders published for 732 homes in Givaot and 91 in Oranit
items.summary: The Housing Ministry and the Civil Administration's custodian of government property published a tender for 732 housing units in Givaot, west of Bethlehem in Gush Etzion, on Sunday, 8 Nov, and tenders for 91 units in Oranit two days earlier, according to Peace Now, which opposes them. It says Givaot now has about 60 families and the tender would turn it into a town of thousands, that tenders were also issued for commercial and employment areas in Givaot and Modi'in Illit, and that between the Knesset's dissolution on 18 Jul 2026 and the election the government issued tenders for 2,944 units, including 1,234 in E1, for a 2026 total of 5,225 units in Judea and Samaria (Peace Now; Peace Now on X). The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission also reported the Givaot tender (Ultra Palestine, citing the commission). Peace Now notes the tender text does not warn bidders about European sanctions threats. The counts are Peace Now's; the tenders themselves were not opened on the Israel Land Authority site.
items.source: Peace Now / PA Colonization Commission via Ultra Palestine

items.headline: Grazing licenses on about 5,500 dunams of state land in the Tubas area and near Abud and al-Lubban al-Gharbi, according to the PA commission
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said it found two notices from the Civil Administration's custodian of government and abandoned property announcing the intent to grant temporary grazing licenses on land Israel classes as state land: license 203033143 for about 4,037.6 dunams in the Tubas district, and license 203037588 for about 1,460.14 dunams of the lands of Abud and al-Lubban al-Gharbi, northwest of Ramallah, for a total of 5,497.74 dunams (about 1,360 acres). The notices are dated 9 Sep 2026 and allowed 30 days for objections. The commission says this is a step before allocation, not proof that final licenses were issued, and calls grazing allocations a tool for taking control of open land (WAFA). Grazing licenses of this kind are usually granted to Israeli farms. This is the PA body's account; no Israeli report or the notices themselves were found, so the figures are unconfirmed.
items.source: PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission via WAFA

items.headline: Artillery trains again in Firing Zone 918 in the southern Hebron Hills, for the first time in years, Regavim says
items.summary: Regavim said that over the weekend the army trained in Firing Zone 918 (the Masafer Yatta area) for the first time in years, with guns of the 405th Battalion firing there. Regavim says Palestinians had moved into the zone and built illegally, which kept the army from using it, and recalls that the High Court ruled in 2022 that the building was illegal and could be removed; it says the work is not done until all illegal structures are cleared (Regavim). Activist Ayelet Lash also cited the May 2022 ruling, which found no permanent residence there before 1980 (Ayelet Lash). From the Palestinian side, WAFA reported that troops trained with tracked vehicles and armored personnel carriers at Khirbet al-Fakhit in Masafer Yatta on Monday, declared the area a closed military zone and kept residents out (WAFA). No army statement on the training was found.

places.name: Yatta (Firing Zone 918 lies to the south)
places.note: Nominatim town point; the firing zone is not mapped, approximate

items.headline: Two men from al-Shuyukh arrested over last week's attack that hurt two Ma'ale Tidhar shepherds
items.summary: Etzion police detectives and Border Police arrested two residents of al-Shuyukh, aged 28 and 45, overnight into Monday, 9 Nov, about a week after an attack that hurt two shepherds from the Ma'ale Tidhar hilltop. Police said a search of their homes found the distinctive clothing they wore during the attack, and that they were taken for questioning (Elisha Yered, quoting the police; Yotam Deshe; Simcha Raz, with police photo).
items.source: Israel Police via Elisha Yered / Israel Hayom (Yotam Deshe) / Olam Katan

items.headline: Army fires at stone throwers it says were about to target a highway near Burqa; Palestinian health ministry says a 14-year-old was killed
items.summary: The army said forces on an operation on the edge of Burqa, northwest of Nablus, on Monday night spotted several terrorists who meant to throw stones at a highway used by Israeli cars, in an area of recent stone attacks, and fired at them to remove the threat; hits were identified (Arutz 7; Olam Katan). The Palestinian health ministry said Israel told it through the PA's civil affairs authority that Mu'taz Iyad Daghlas, 14, was killed and that Israel is holding the body. WAFA and Arab48 also report that a 17-year-old was shot in the abdomen and a 19-year-old in the hand earlier that evening, that three Red Crescent volunteers were detained, and that the boy's father was arrested (WAFA; Arab48). Stones were thrown at the Burqa gas station earlier the same day, and Olam Katan reported stones between Homesh and Shavei Shomron near Burqa (Olam Katan). The army has not said whether the boy was among those it fired at; the Palestinian details are unconfirmed.
items.source: IDF via Arutz 7 / Olam Katan; WAFA / Arab48

items.headline: PA security says more than ten people are held over the sale of the Jericho homes to Jews, some with Israeli citizenship; the PA land authority resumes deals for Israeli Arabs under tighter checks
items.summary: PA security forces spokesman Maj. Gen. Anwar Rajab told Raya radio that more than ten people have been arrested over what he called the "leak" of about eight homes in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, to settlers, that they come from several districts, and that some hold Israeli citizenship or are from Jerusalem. He called it an organized network tied to other land and organized-crime cases, said the sales were "illegal, unofficial and unpatriotic," and said those involved should be treated as traitors (Raya, 8 Nov). Euronews Arabic reports that the PA land authority has now resumed land purchases and registrations for Arab citizens of Israel and Jerusalem residents, after suspending them last week, with stricter document checks; the PA land authority denies there were any valid sale papers and says one of the two plots is state land (Euronews Arabic). HaKol HaYehudi notes that about 20 Jewish families moved into the eight homes last week in an operation led by the Nachala movement, that they say the homes were bought in full with ownership papers, and that PA law treats land sales to Jews as treason, punishable since 2014 by life with hard labor (HaKol HaYehudi). The Times of Israel also reported the arrests (its page was blocked to this desk).
items.source: PA security spokesman via Raya / Euronews Arabic / HaKol HaYehudi

items.headline: Channel 14: intelligence material suggests a senior Arab-party MK received tens of thousands of shekels from the PA over a long period
items.summary: Channel 14 military and security reporter Hallel Bitton Rosen reported on Monday, 9 Nov, that material received by the security establishment raises the suspicion that a senior MK from an Arab party received tens of thousands of shekels from the Palestinian Authority every month for a long period. The material is with investigators and security bodies, who are checking it quietly, including why he got the money and what he provided in return (Hallel Bitton Rosen). Olam Katan carried the report and stressed that these are unproven suspicions; the MK was not named (Olam Katan). Single-outlet report; unconfirmed.

items.headline: JCFA study: the PA still pays more than 20 million shekels a month to prisoners, and Israel has seized only about 15 percent of the money it ordered taken
items.summary: A study by Lt. Col. (res.) Maurice Hirsch, a former chief military prosecutor in Judea and Samaria, at the Jerusalem Center for Foreign Affairs and Security (JCFA), finds the PA and PLO still pay more than 20 million shekels a month to terrorists held in Israel and their families, despite Israeli law and Mahmoud Abbas's pledge to Washington to stop. Payments rise with time served, from 1,400 shekels a month in the first three years to 12,000 shekels after 30 years. Since 2019 defense ministers have issued seizure orders worth 50 million shekels, but Hirsch estimates no more than 15 percent was actually seized. After banks were warned in 2020, about 35,000 accounts were closed and the PA moved to cash at post offices and then to special ATMs outside the banking system, which he says Israel should map and target (Ynet). The figures are the study's.

items.headline: Hebron news channel posts a memorial poster for Hamas commander Marwan Issa, JSR says
items.summary: JSR said the Hebron Telegram channel "Hebron News Network" published a memorial poster for Marwan Issa, deputy to Hamas military chief Mohammed Deif and one of the planners of the 7 October massacre, who was killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza in March 2024. The poster calls him "the great martyred commander" next to a eulogy from the Hamas military wing's website (JSR). JSR's report; the channel itself was not checked.

items.headline: Property seized in Judea and Samaria reached almost 18 million shekels in 2025, up from 1.9 million in 2019, army data show
items.summary: Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe reports, from army data released under a freedom-of-information request, that property worth almost 18 million shekels was seized in Judea and Samaria in 2025, against about 1.9 million in 2019. The jump began in 2024, when about 10.8 million shekels' worth was seized, more than in the five years before combined (Yotam Deshe). The post does not say what kinds of property or whose; single source.
items.source: Israel Hayom (Yotam Deshe), army FOI data

items.headline: Al-Battuf council head Ahed Rahal among about 50 arrested in a nationwide protection-racket sweep; his son is charged in a case involving a Mekorot water site
items.summary: About 500 police and Border Police officers arrested some 50 suspects on Monday, 9 Nov, in 15 separate protection-racket cases, at the end of a 10-month covert investigation named "Shadow Guardians." Among them is Ahed Rahal, 55, head of the al-Battuf council in the Lower Galilee, whose detention was extended to 15 Nov (Ynet). HaKol HaYehudi reports that his son, Rida Rahal, is charged with extorting protection money for a guard company he ran with Odai Idrib, a criminal from Tamra, after a contractor running a Mekorot (national water company) facility stopped paying (HaKol HaYehudi, via Meir Ettinger). Activist Meir Ettinger says Rahal met Gadi Eisenkot to ask that Ra'am be in the government (Meir Ettinger); that meeting is his claim and was not confirmed elsewhere.

items.headline: Mansour Abbas praises Khaled Meshaal's "positive" speech to the Fatah conference; Balad MK Nasasra hopes "all the prisoners" go free; Tibi wants Eisenkot to be "like Rabin"
items.summary: Moran Tal posted video of Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas, in an interview she says was conducted by actor Hisham Suliman, saying Hamas's participation in the Fatah conference and the speech by its political bureau head Khaled Meshaal was "detailed and positive and gave a new spirit" to Palestinian national action and unity, that Fatah and Hamas are the two most important Palestinian factions, and that a Palestinian state "will be a reality" despite "racist, fascist Israeli obstacles" (Moran Tal, with video). She also posted video from Jaffa, at the release of Balad activist Abed Abu Shehadeh on Sunday, in which incoming Balad MK Hassan al-Nasasra expressed hope that "all the prisoners" would be freed; Ayelet Lash quoted him as greeting "all the prisoners inside the jails" (Moran Tal; Ayelet Lash). Channel 14's Arab-affairs editor Omri Haim quoted Ahmad Tibi saying overnight: "We want Eisenkot to be like Rabin... Rabin in the 1990s relied for four years in a minority government on two Arab parties," and linked it to a senior PA official hoping the next Israeli government has the "courage" to overcome obstacles with them (Omri Haim; Omri Haim). The quotes come from the videos these accounts posted; the full interviews were not checked.
items.source: Moran Tal / Ayelet Lash / Channel 14 (Omri Haim)

items.headline: A Dan bus driver in Tel Aviv played "Fida'i," the PA anthem, over the bus speaker, a passenger told Elchanan Groner
items.summary: Elchanan Groner of HaKol HaYehudi posted a passenger's video and account from Monday morning, 9 Nov: "Bus in Tel Aviv this morning. The driver played 'Fida'i', the anthem of the Palestinian Authority, on the bus speaker" (Elchanan Groner). Channel 14 and Olam Katan carried it; Olam Katan noted it rests on one passenger's account, the line and driver are not known, and Dan had not responded (Channel 14; Olam Katan). Unconfirmed beyond the video.

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian media say an Israeli patrol shot a shepherd near Bir Ajam in Quneitra
items.summary: Syria's SANA and the Quneitra media office said an Israeli army patrol entered the Bir Ajam woods in southern Quneitra on Monday, 9 Nov, and shot a shepherd, who was taken to Golan National Hospital, and that a SANA reporter and local media crew in the village came under fire without injury. Arab48, which carried the report, also cites Anadolu interviews with farmers in Daraa and Quneitra who say Israeli posts and checkpoints have kept them from their land since 2024 (Arab48). Syrian official media's account; no IDF statement found. Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new on Quneitra this run.

items.headline: Binyamin Council puts one million shekels into "HaZe'evim," a program for 11 local nightlife and culture businesses
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council, through its community center arm Binyamin Plus, launched "HaZe'evim" ("the wolves"), a one-million-shekel program to develop nightlife, culture and food venues. Eleven entrepreneurs were picked for two months of mentoring by five local business heads, including the Psagot winery owner, with grants at the end; only after the selection did the council learn the 11 had served 3,160 reserve days in the war. Council head and Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz said: "We are making Binyamin the best place to live" (Olam Katan; Simcha Raz).

items.headline: Army clears olive trees beside Route 60 near the Lubban schools after repeated stonings, Ayelet Lash says
items.summary: Activist Ayelet Lash posted a photo and wrote that, after many stone attacks on Route 60, soldiers began clearing the ground near the schools of Lubban (al-Sharqiya) and cutting olive trees close to the road. She argues the army should act against the places the stones are thrown from rather than the trees, and predicts the stoning will go on (Ayelet Lash). Her report; no army statement or second source was found.

items.headline: Palestinian reports: equipment burned at the Beita stone works; olives taken in Yatta; a new road near Asael
items.summary: WAFA, citing Palestinian security sources, and Arab48 say dozens of settlers burned three excavators and other vehicles and equipment at stone-cutting works in the Beita industrial area south of Nablus on Monday evening, 9 Nov (Arab48). WAFA also says settlers took olives from a grove at Khallet al-Hummus in Yatta (WAFA). Kerem Navot's Dror Etkes posted a photo of work on a road north of Asael in the southern Hebron Hills that he says will link it to a new outpost south of Samu' (Dror Etkes). Beita has long been a flashpoint near Evyatar, where Israelis were attacked the same day (see the lead item). These are Palestinian and activist claims; no police, army or Israeli-side account was found.

items.headline: Five attacks on Israelis in one day, by the Situation Room's count: stones at Karnei Shomron, Barta'a junction twice and Allenby Bridge, and a truck runs over a farm's flock
items.summary: The Yesha Council's Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) logged five incidents on Sunday, 8 Nov. At about 9:40 AM stones hit a car near the Karnei Shomron roundabout, cracking the windshield. Minutes later a car was stoned at Barta'a junction on the seam line in northern Samaria, again with windshield damage and no one hurt. JSR called these the 103rd and 104th stone attacks in Judea and Samaria in the past 30 days. At about 11:15 AM JSR reported that an Arab truck ran over sheep and a dog belonging to HaMakoch farm in Binyamin, and later posted a photo of the dog. In the evening, stones were thrown from a passing car at an Israeli car at the Allenby Bridge junction in the Jordan Valley (windshield damaged; JSR's 22nd stoning in seven days), and at an Israeli motorcyclist between Harish and Barta'a junction (no injuries or damage) (JSR, Karnei Shomron; JSR, Barta'a; JSR, HaMakoch farm; JSR, Allenby; JSR, motorcyclist). JNS Hebrew reporter Netanel Frankel republished the day's list and noted that none of the morning stonings were reported by the news media; Olam Katan's Simcha Raz carried the Barta'a report (Netanel Frankel; Simcha Raz). These are JSR's own reports. No police or IDF statement on them was found, and the 30-day count is JSR's figure (unconfirmed). The farm incident gives no details on whether the truck hit the animals on purpose.
items.source: JSR Situation Room / Netanel Frankel (JNS Hebrew)

places.name: Karnei Shomron
places.note: Nominatim (town point; the roundabout itself is not plotted)

places.name: Barta'a junction
places.note: OSM point named Barta'a junction; OSM has several, so approximate

places.name: Allenby Bridge
places.note: Nominatim (bridge point; the junction is nearby, approximate)

items.headline: Elisha Yered: men from Abu Falah beat a Jewish shepherd with clubs; a resident's finger likely broken by stones
items.summary: Settlement activist Elisha Yered reported that on Sunday afternoon men from the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, drove up in a Ford pickup, hit a Jewish shepherd from a nearby hilltop community with clubs and tried to grab his phone. Residents who ran down from the hill drove them back to the edge of the village. He says the attackers then called others and threw stones, likely breaking one resident's finger, and fled into the village when the army arrived. No arrests were reported (Elisha Yered, with video). The Hadashot Israel news channel relayed the same account (Newsrael), but that is not an independent source. No IDF or police statement was found, so the details are Yered's account (unconfirmed).

places.name: Abu Falah
places.note: Nominatim (village point; the hilltop community is not named)

items.headline: PA's Nablus governor joins a campus event for Zakaria Zubeidi and, per JSR, calls him "the national leader"
items.summary: On Sunday, Fatah's student wing hosted Zakaria Zubeidi at An-Najah National University in Nablus for a talk titled "A nation's story, told by the memory of the struggle." Zubeidi, the former head of the al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades in Jenin, was freed in the January 2025 prisoner exchange and now sits on Fatah's Central Committee. Fatah's own commission confirms that the PA governor of Nablus attended, along with former PA prime minister Rami Hamdallah (vice chairman of the university's board of trustees) and the university president. The event opened with a short film on Zubeidi's "struggle" (Fatah National Relations Commission, Arabic). JSR reports that governor Ghassan Daghlas then posted that Zubeidi is "the national leader," praising his "path of struggle full of sacrifice" and saying such meetings pass "national memory" to the young. JSR describes Zubeidi as convicted of murdering five Israelis (JSR). Daghlas's post itself was not found, so the quotes are JSR's account (unconfirmed). The Fatah page gives the governor's first name as Bassam; the governor appointed in 2024 is Ghassan Daghlas.

items.headline: Jerusalem couple and their baby enter Bethlehem by mistake; PA police find them and hand them over
items.summary: On Thursday evening a father from Jerusalem called the police emergency line to say he had entered Area A by mistake with his wife and their one-year-old son. Through coordination between Israeli forces and the Palestinian police, Palestinian officers found the three near a hotel in Bethlehem and handed them, unharmed, to Israeli forces, Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe reported. They were taken to the Etzion police station. The parents, 41 and 34, were questioned for entering a closed area (Israeli law bars Israelis from Area A) and released under restrictions (Yotam Deshe, Israel Hayom). Olam Katan's Simcha Raz, citing the police spokesman, adds that they entered together with tourists (Simcha Raz).

places.name: Bethlehem
places.note: Nominatim (city point; the hotel is not named)

items.headline: Yered: PA forces will still be told of routine patrols, which he calls a danger to troops; IDF says weapons seizures are up since the change
items.summary: Following up on Central Command's order to stop warning PA security forces before raids, Elisha Yered says the IDF is now claiming there was never a formal procedure, only units on the ground who over the years began telling the PA even about sensitive operations, and that orders were merely "sharpened." He calls that "a gross lie." Central Command says there will be no advance notice before arrests and weapons searches, but the PA will still be told about patrols in villages that are not based on precise intelligence. Yered says this rules out stumbling on terror activity by chance and exposes troops to ambushes by crowds (Elisha Yered). In an interview with HaKol HaYehudi, Yered says the PA forces used to pass the warnings straight to terrorists, who spread them on Arab Telegram channels. HaKol HaYehudi reports that the IDF says the amount of weapons seized has risen since the decision (HaKol HaYehudi). The IDF figure was not published elsewhere (unconfirmed). Background: the IDF's account to Olam Katan was in the 8 Nov edition.

items.headline: 98th Division hands Judea and Etzion brigades back after six weeks: 1,500 operations, more than 140 arrests, about 35 weapons
items.summary: The headquarters of the 98th Division finished its command of the Judea and Etzion regional brigades on Sunday and returns to General Staff reserve. It took over on 25 Sept to strengthen command in the southern part of Judea and Samaria, without bringing its own combat units. The IDF says the brigades under it carried out more than 1,500 counterterror operations, arrested more than 140 suspects and found about 35 weapons. During this period Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roitman and Sgt. Yuval Shai Soilam were killed in a shootout with terrorists; the IDF says they prevented a serious attack. The division also secured the hundreds of thousands who visited the Cave of the Patriarchs over Sukkot and the Chayei Sarah weekend (Olam Katan; Maariv; Emanuel Fabian, Times of Israel). For contrast, a 7 Nov Haaretz English headline said the Hebron raid forced 3,300 Palestinians from their homes and found four guns; the IDF's 35 weapons cover the whole six-week period across both brigades (the Haaretz article itself was not read).
items.source: IDF via Olam Katan / Maariv / Times of Israel

items.headline: Troops shoot a man about to throw a firebomb at Zababdeh; stone-throwers shot in Qalqilya; M16 and stun grenade seized in Nablus
items.summary: On Sunday evening, troops of the Menashe Brigade working in Zababdeh, near Jenin, spotted a man holding a firebomb who was about to throw it at them. They opened fire and the IDF reported a hit; no soldiers were hurt (Ynet; Arutz 7). On Saturday night, troops in Qalqilya fired at several Palestinians who threw stones at them, also reporting a hit (JNS). Over the weekend the Israel Prison Service's Yamar unit, with Samaria Brigade troops and the Shin Bet, acted on intelligence about arms trading and smuggling in Nablus. With a sniffer dog they found an M16 rifle, a pistol, an IDF stun grenade, weapon parts and about 9,000 shekels, and arrested two suspects (Olam Katan). The Nablus seizure has one source so far.

places.name: Nablus
places.note: Nominatim (city point; the site is not named)

items.headline: Driver speeds at Ma'ale Adumim detectives at an East Jerusalem roadblock; police fire in the air and arrest him
items.summary: On Sunday evening, detectives from the Ma'ale Adumim police station set up a roadblock in a-Tur in East Jerusalem and signaled a suspicious car to stop. Police say the driver ignored them and sped toward them. Feeling their lives were in danger, they fired in the air. No one was hurt, and the driver was arrested and taken for questioning (Srugim; Maariv). An early report by Channel 14's Hallel Bitton Rosen said police hit several suspects, and a follow-up said the car carried illegal entrants from Issawiya and the driver probably got away (Bitton Rosen; follow-up). The police statement, issued later, says there were no injuries and the driver was caught.

items.headline: Samaria council head Yossi Dagan recruits Czech allies against new EU sanctions; a ruling-party leader backs sovereignty
items.summary: Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan finished several days of meetings in Prague with Czech government and parliament figures, aimed at blocking further EU sanctions on Judea and Samaria, Israel Hayom's Yotam Deshe reported first. EU foreign-policy sanctions need a unanimous vote, so one government's objection can stop a new decision (Yotam Deshe, Israel Hayom). Dagan met Health and Sports Minister Boris Šťastný and Ondřej Knotek, head of the Czech ruling party's delegation in the European Parliament. Both voiced support for Israeli sovereignty in the area, according to the Samaria council. Knotek said in a joint video that "Europe needs to support and strengthen Judea and Samaria." Dagan told them the country is about 70 km wide from the sea to the Jordan, about 55 km of it in Samaria. The trip follows his three visits to Slovenia in the past half year, after Prime Minister Janez Janša's government dropped its ban on goods from Judea and Samaria (Olam Katan). The officials' support comes from the council's account and the joint video; no Czech government statement was found.

items.headline: Binyamin to build a memorial to the 85 killed in the 1994 AMIA bombing in Buenos Aires
items.summary: Binyamin Regional Council head and Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz visited the AMIA Jewish community center in Buenos Aires and agreed with its president, Osvaldo Armoza, to build a memorial in Binyamin to the 85 people killed in the 18 July 1994 bombing, which is blamed on Hezbollah and Iran. Two stones from the original building are kept at the new center, and planners are looking at working an element linked to them into the memorial. "Iran, Hezbollah and Israel's enemies keep trying to harm Jews... our answer has not changed: we will keep building and settling," Ganz said. The trip also included a meeting with President Javier Milei (Olam Katan). Single source so far; no site or date for the memorial was given.

items.headline: 14 foreign activists held at Ras Karkar face deportation; police say they came to provoke clashes
items.summary: Police said on Sunday that 14 foreigners arrested with three Palestinians near Ras Karkar, west of Ramallah, during an olive-harvest confrontation on Friday were handed to the Population and Immigration Authority for deportation hearings. Police say the questioning raised suspicion that they came to stir up provocations and clashes for anti-Israel media campaigns, and that some support the BDS boycott movement. The three Palestinians are still under investigation (JNS, citing Israel Police; Elisha Yered). Ultra Palestine says the group holds Italian, German, Canadian and U.S. passports and includes two journalists, and counts 28 foreign activists deported in a week, after 14 picked up at al-Lubban al-Gharbiya (Ultra Palestine, Arabic). The nationalities and the 28 figure are Palestinian-side details (unconfirmed).
items.source: Israel Police via JNS / Ultra Palestine

items.headline: Abu Ali Express: Beita terrorists' homes back up a week and a half after the IDF blew them up
items.summary: The Abu Ali Express Telegram channel reported on Sunday that in Beita, near Nablus, the homes of terrorists Ibrahim and Zakaria Daoud have been rebuilt since the IDF blew them up about a week and a half ago, and said this undercuts the point of the demolitions (Abu Ali Express). Al Jazeera's Arabic site reported on 5 Nov that about 1,000 people from Beita and nearby villages, bringing sand, cement and steel, finished repairing four neighboring homes damaged in the 28 Oct demolition "within a few days." One resident told it, "In Beita, building is faster than demolition" (Al Jazeera, Arabic). The two accounts differ: Al Jazeera speaks of the neighbors' homes, and says Israel bars rebuilding the demolished homes themselves. No IDF response was found.

items.headline: Brawl between Jewish and Arab residents in Lod after a right-wing "governance tour"; 11 arrested, police deny a stabbing
items.summary: On Sunday evening right-wing activist Mordechai David, who campaigned for Itamar Ben-Gvir, brought a group to Arab neighborhoods of Lod, saying in an Instagram video that "after the Arabs regularly attack Jews in Lod, we came to do a governance tour." Mayor Yair Revivo says the outside group drew about 20 local teens. After police broke it up, the teens shouted insults outside Arab homes, Arab residents came out, and a brawl left several hurt. Police arrested 11 people, Jews and Arabs, including minors and a woman, and said that, contrary to rumors, no stabbing took place (Ynet; Israel Hayom; Ynetnews). Revivo, who has kept the city relatively calm since the May 2021 riots, said he had asked the Shin Bet chief to prepare for possible escalation, and condemned provocation, threats with knives and taking the law into one's own hands "not by Jews and not by Arabs." The claim of regular attacks on Jews in Lod is David's; the reports give no figures.

items.headline: Ad Kan report: cash envelopes, fuel cards and ballot tracking at Arab and Bedouin polling stations; Attorney General sees no effect on the result
items.summary: The anti-racket group Ad Kan published a 32-page preliminary report based on 488 statements from observers and polling-station staff and 20 interviews in Arab and Bedouin society and the Islamic Movement. It describes cash envelopes, fuel cards, demands that voters photograph their ballots, threats against staff, and unauthorized desks recording voters' ID numbers. Among its examples: at al-Hikma school in Rahat a committee member says he was offered 400 shekels in fuel cards, then 600 in cash, to vote for the Joint List. Others are from al-Atawna school in Hura, Kafr Qara, Tamra and Abu Ghosh. The report cites the Shin Bet telling the Central Elections Committee of a phenomenon "exceeding thousands of people" (Olam Katan). Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said on Sunday she knows of no evidence that comes "even close" to affecting the election result (Srugim). Ad Kan's findings are its own claims; the Shin Bet quote comes through its report.

items.headline: Balad activist Abd Abu Shehadeh freed after five days; Shin Bet chief sought to question all Arab party heads
items.summary: Media figure and Balad activist Abd Abu Shehadeh, a relative of Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, was released Sunday without restrictions after five days in custody, since police and the Shin Bet did not ask to extend it. He was held on suspicion of contact with a foreign agent and of involvement in the election-bribery affair; the background is an interview he did in Qatar with former MK Azmi Bishara for Al Jazeera (Olam Katan). Kan and Haaretz report, citing a source, that his questioning focused on his political views (headlines only; articles not read). i24News reports that Shin Bet chief David Zini also asked to question Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen, so that he has sought warning-status questioning of all Arab party heads. The Attorney General agreed there is reasonable suspicion only against Ayman Odeh (Srugim). Writer Meir Ettinger mocked reporters who cover the "Qatargate" affair all day and then present the Qatar trip as just a press interview with Bishara (Meir Ettinger).

items.headline: Joint List's number 3 on Hamas: "international law allows resistance"; Abbas cites Darwish as his model
items.summary: Channel 14 aired Fatan Ratas, number 3 on the Joint List and, it says, a member of a Health Ministry council, saying "there was never an occupation in the world without resistance; international law allows an occupied people to resist the occupier." Channel 14's Arab-affairs head Omri Haim asked whether Gadi Eisenkot would form a government with help from such a figure (Omri Haim, Channel 14). Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas told Al-Arabiya that his list holds both "our Israeli citizenship and our Palestinian nationalism" and presented his "Bridges of Reconciliation and Peace" plan for two states based on the Arab Peace Initiative (Olam Katan). Researcher Moran Tal points out that Abbas told President Herzog he follows Islamic Movement founder Abdullah Nimr Darwish, and posts material from Darwish's last movement conference (Moran Tal). Activist Ayelet Lash argues that since about 99 percent of Arab voters chose lists that will not call Hamas a terror group, Jews should not be expected to trust Arab medical staff the state will not draft into the army (Ayelet Lash). These are statements and opinions; the Ratas quote is from Channel 14's clip, and the 99 percent figure is hers.
items.source: Channel 14 (Omri Haim) / Olam Katan / Moran Tal / Ayelet Lash

items.headline: David Friedman launches a Channel 18 series challenging "settler violence" claims
items.summary: Former U.S. ambassador David Friedman says his Channel 18 Israel will put out a lot of content over the coming weeks "exploring, and ultimately exposing the myth, of 'settler violence,'" starting with his own introduction and what he took away from reporting in Judea and Samaria. He calls it "something that almost never gets reported accurately or fairly" (David Friedman). Friedman founded Channel 18; this is his own framing of the series.

items.headline: Jericho homes stay manned under army-escorted convoys; IDF calls Haaretz report on Blot false
items.summary: The Jewish families who moved into eight homes on the edge of Jericho on Wednesday are staying. They say the homes were bought lawfully through the Nachala movement, with the Binyamin Regional Council's help. The homes are in Area C, next to the Hasmonean palaces archaeological site. Nachala says army-escorted convoys run every two hours from 6:00 AM to midnight. Residents Emanuel Weiss and Shmuel Gazit told Ynet the army is with them between the houses, and that they made the purchase on their own (Ynet). On Saturday night Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Blot ordered that, until further notice, people can enter and leave the neighborhood several times a day under military escort. Commanders toured the site, and the army says it will keep checking the purchase claims this week. A security official said it is not yet known whether the Civil Administration approved the deals (Jerusalem Post). Haaretz reported Friday that before the move, Blot talked with the Binyamin council, Nachala and the regional defense officer, Lt. Col. Elitzur Trabelsi, and kept his usual subordinates out of the loop. On the record, the IDF called the whole report false. IDF sources told the Jerusalem Post that Blot did meet Trabelsi, but about routine matters, and that Haaretz misread answers to "convoluted questions." Haaretz's Sunday editorial calls Blot a "coordinator of settler activities" and asks the chief of staff for an independent probe. It also attacks his closed-area order at Burin, which canceled a harvest visit led by Ehud Olmert (Haaretz editorial). The army says three platoons meant for stopping smuggling on the Jordan border were moved to guard the site. It also says two Bedouin families living nearby left their homes "in unclear circumstances" despite its attempts to talk them out of it, and that it will stop Jews from taking over the empty homes (Ynet).

places.name: Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta, Jericho
places.note: Nominatim (neighborhood point; the exact homes are not mapped)

items.headline: IDF: no warning to PA forces before arrests and weapons searches, but routine patrols are still coordinated
items.summary: The IDF Spokesperson told Olam Katan there was no formal change of procedure, only a "sharpening" of existing orders. Some units had not known when they were allowed to tell the PA security services about an operation and when they were not. The rule now spelled out: arrests, weapons searches and any raid that depends on surprise get no advance notice. Routine patrols, and moves where coordination can prevent PA forces and the IDF from firing on each other by mistake, are still reported. The army says the clarification began about six weeks ago, after media questions and leaked photos and WhatsApp messages from operations rooms (Olam Katan; Simcha Raz). This follows Friday's Makor Rishon report that Blot had stopped the tip-offs (lead story, 7 Nov). Elisha Yered then posted a letter from a reservist. The reservist says that in a June 2025 division operation in northern Samaria, a wealthy Arab homeowner told the troops he knew in advance they were coming for a week, and boasted that a Coordination and Liaison Office (DCO) officer had recently been his guest at a barbecue. According to the reservist, the division's information-security branch replied that "there is nothing to do with it" (Elisha Yered). The reservist's account is unconfirmed.

places.name: Deir Dibwan
places.note: Nominatim (site of the original leak report)

items.headline: Suspected car ramming at the Rimonim junction guard post; Kalashnikov magazine found at the nearby Abu Faza Bedouin camp
items.summary: Late Saturday night an Arab car sped toward IDF troops at the guard post (pillbox) at Rimonim junction in Binyamin, Olam Katan reported. The troops fired at the car and arrested the driver, and no soldiers were hurt (Olam Katan; Olam Katan on X). No IDF statement was found by the time of this edition, so the details are unconfirmed. Hours earlier, Elisha Yered reported that Paratroopers Battalion 202 had searched the illegal Bedouin camp of the Abu Faza clan near Rimonim square, beside the Allon Road. In a parked car the troops found a hidden Kalashnikov magazine. Yered says the camp has been a base for attacks and water theft for years with little enforcement. One clan member, he says, served 18 months for throwing a firebomb at a shepherd. He also posted a video showing that clan member Ahmad Abu Faza had added a poem urging more attacks to an Arabic report of an earlier shooting near the square. Yered says far-left activists, Arik Ascherman among them, protect the camp (Yered; the post). The magazine find is confirmed only by Yered.

places.name: Rimonim junction (Allon Road)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Rimonim; the junction and the Abu Faza camp are nearby

items.headline: Six Palestinians arrested over stone-throwing near Metzudat David farm
items.summary: After a report of stones thrown near Metzudat David farm in Binyamin on Saturday evening, IDF troops arrested six suspects. They were handed to Binyamin police station of the Judea and Samaria District for questioning (Maariv; Ynet; Simcha Raz). Police gave no more details. Background: on 5 Nov, JSR counted the 57th attack this month on Jewish shepherds, when about ten Arabs threw stones at Metzudat David's flock east of al-Mughayyir (JSR).

places.name: Metzudat David farm (east of al-Mughayyir)
places.note: Approximate: farm not mapped; marker at al-Mughayyir (Nominatim)

items.headline: Paratroopers seize an al-Mughayyir garbage tractor in Area C; the DCO hands it back hours later
items.summary: Elisha Yered reports that on Saturday, a tractor from al-Mughayyir was filmed for the sixth time this week dumping a trailer of garbage at an illegal dump in open Area C land west of the village. This time troops of Paratroopers Battalion 202 caught it. The driver claimed it would not start, but a Jewish civilian operator started it easily and drove it to the impound lot at the Mevo Shilo base. A few hours later, Yered says, Coordination and Liaison Office (DCO) officers brought the driver to Malakhei HaShalom and gave him back the keys, with no fine. Villagers credited pressure from the PA's coordination offices. Yered says a tractor from Burqa that dumped waste into Nahal Mikhmas was also released after two days, about three months ago (Yered; follow-up). Palestinian outlets and activists tell a different story: settlers, guarded by soldiers, "seized" the tractor of Amin Salih Abu Aliya and dumped its load of garbage at the entrance of the al-Mughayyir boys' secondary school (al-Quds; Ultra Palestine). Neither side's account of where the load ended up has been confirmed independently, and the IDF has not commented.

places.name: Mevo Shilo base (near Shiloh)
places.note: Approximate: marker at Shiloh (Nominatim); base and Malakhei HaShalom not mapped

items.headline: Tens of thousands fill Hebron and Kiryat Arba despite heavy rain; Machpela closes an hour early Saturday night
items.summary: Tens of thousands of visitors from Israel and abroad came to Kiryat Arba and the Cave of the Patriarchs for the Chayei Sarah weekend. They stayed in residents' homes, in tent camps and in a caravan park, with meals, lectures and a business fair. Council head Israel Bramson said Hebron "is the capital of Judea" (Olam Katan; Srugim; Makor Rishon). JNS Hebrew reporter Netanel Frankel wrote that every hall of the cave was open and full around the clock, and that no unusual incident was recorded (Frankel). On Saturday night the cave was locked at 8:50 PM instead of the agreed 10:00 PM, and dozens who came to pray in the Isaac Hall were left outside. The IDF Spokesperson said the matter is being checked (Olam Katan). In a fundraising post, Ayelet Lash wrote that 15 new families, with more than 60 children, moved into Hebron in the past year, and that the Harchivi association has so far recovered 40,000 square meters for Jewish use in the city. These are her figures and are unconfirmed here (Ayelet Lash).

items.headline: Six homes burgled in Neria during the weekend; a pistol and 20,000 shekels taken
items.summary: According to Eliya Aviv, relayed by Olam Katan's Simcha Raz, six homes in Neria in western Binyamin were broken into over the weekend. Much property was stolen, including electrical goods, a pistol and 20,000 shekels (Simcha Raz). No police statement or second report was found by the time of this edition, and the suspects are not identified.

items.headline: Ayelet Lash: about 240 smuggling vehicles into the Arad area in a week, and stones at cars at the Deir al-Asad interchange
items.summary: Ayelet Lash posted that in the past week alone, about 240 vehicles smuggled illegal entrants from Judea and Samaria to the Arad area through the Judean Desert. She says about 8 stolen off-road vehicles went the other way, from the Negev to the south Hebron Hills, "only what we know of," and that any of these vehicles could carry weapons. She posted 220 vehicles a week earlier (1 Nov edition). She does not name her source, and the figures are unconfirmed (Ayelet Lash). She also posted a video she says was filmed Friday at the Deir al-Asad bridge in the Galilee, showing a child throwing stones at cars at the interchange (Ayelet Lash). No police report of the incident was found.

places.name: Deir al-Asad
places.note: Nominatim (town point; the interchange is nearby on Route 85, approximate)

items.headline: In Nof HaGalil, the city renamed to stress its Jewish identity, the Joint List came first
items.summary: In the 27 Oct Knesset election, the Joint List won 8,216 votes in Nof HaGalil (formerly Upper Nazareth), 31.65 percent of valid votes. Likud, which led the city for years, got 21.31 percent. Makor Rishon notes that the Joint List alone beat Likud, Otzma Yehudit, Religious Zionism, United Torah Judaism and Shas combined (8,197 votes). With Ra'am (941 votes, per Local Call), the Arab lists took 35.27 percent. Turnout was about 62 percent, fourth-lowest among towns with 10,000 or more voters (Makor Rishon; Local Call). Mayor Ronen Plot, who led the 2019 renaming, says Likud lost only about 300 votes. In his view the result reflects high Arab turnout, and successive governments that did not build enough housing in Arab towns, so Arab families moved into the city. According to Local Call, Chabad council member Menachem Gendel has called on the next government to make Judaizing the Galilee "national mission number 1." For the planning side of the Galilee contest, see the Khamaisi Plan backgrounder.

items.headline: PA commission claims 674 "attacks" on the olive harvest from 1 Oct to 6 Nov
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission says 674 "attacks" on olive trees and pickers took place in Judea and Samaria, including Jerusalem, from 1 Oct to 6 Nov. It attributes 520 to settlers and 154 to the army, and says the Nablus, Ramallah and Salfit districts account for about 73 percent. These are PA figures, relayed by Ultra Palestine, and the commission does not say what it counts as an attack (Ultra Palestine). For comparison, over the same harvest JSR has counted 58 attacks on Jewish shepherds by 6 Nov, many by Arabs arriving as "olive pickers" (7 Nov edition).

items.headline: Central Command stops tipping the PA before raids; weapons seizures rise
items.summary: Central Command Maj. Gen. Avi Blot ordered the IDF to stop giving the Palestinian Authority security services advance notice before arrest, weapons and village search raids in Judea and Samaria, Makor Rishon's Yishai Elmakyes reported. The old "fold the PA forces" practice (קיפול שו"פים) had become a tip-off channel: PA officers were passing the planned routes to local Arabs, who then hid weapons and fled. Since Blot tightened the order, the army says the volume of weapons seized on operations has gone up. Senior Central Command officers told Makor Rishon the trigger was a report by settler activist Elisha Yered: while driving Route 60 near Deir Dibwan he saw IDF vehicles staging for a village patrol, then minutes later saw a local Arabic Telegram channel publish the exact planned route about ten minutes before the troops entered. Yered had first published the leak pattern about a month earlier; he wrote that Central Command admitted his report was the background to the change, and that weapons seizures rose afterward (Makor Rishon; Elisha Yered; tip relayed by Aleph). Former prime minister Ehud Olmert separately attacked Blot as "aiding Jewish terror," a political charge Kan headlined the same day.

items.headline: PA freezes land registration for Israeli Arabs after Jericho house sales to Jews
items.summary: In response to the sale of houses in Jericho to Jews, the Palestinian Authority Land Authority ordered a freeze on land-registration transactions for Palestinians who hold Israeli citizenship or an Israeli Jerusalem identity card, including Arab Israelis and East Jerusalem residents, until further notice. Olam Katan's Simcha Raz reported the official PA notice; the Hebrew outlet Emess published the same order, quoting the Arabic circular that tells registration and land-settlement offices to stop processing those deals. The freeze follows the Jewish families' entry into eight houses in Jericho covered in earlier editions. Raz also noted a separate security incident at the new Jewish site in Jericho in which, according to Eliya Aviv, an Israeli in a security role arrived dressed as an anarchist, drew a pistol and pointed it at settlers — a claim labeled as Aviv's report and not independently confirmed here (Olam Katan; Emess; Simcha Raz).

items.headline: Duvdevan and Shin Bet grab three suspects planning attacks near Ramallah
items.summary: In a joint IDF–Shin Bet announcement, Duvdevan commandos arrested three Arabs this week in al-Am'ari, a-Ram and al-Bireh in the Binyamin brigade sector who, the military said, planned terror attacks and military activity against Israeli civilians and IDF troops. The three were handed to the Shin Bet for questioning. Times of Israel military correspondent Emanuel Fabian and Channel 14 both carried the IDF/Shin Bet statement; Israel Hayom and Maariv reported the same raids (Channel 14; Emanuel Fabian; Israel Hayom; Maariv).

places.name: al-Am'ari
places.note: Approximate (Nominatim street point near Beitunia / Amari area)

items.headline: Hebron man dressed as a Haredi, with six illegal entrants, stopped at a-Za'im
items.summary: Border Police stopped a car that raised suspicion at the a-Za'im crossing. Behind the wheel was a Palestinian from Hebron who, police say, had grown sidelocks, put on a kippah and dressed as an ultra-Orthodox Jew, apparently to slip the check. Six other illegal entrants were in the vehicle; the car had already been taken off the road and its plates swapped. All seven were arrested. Israel Hayom settlements correspondent Yotam Deshe and Arutz 7 both reported the case (Yotam Deshe; Arutz 7).

items.headline: Foreign activists stage unauthorized olive harvest at Sde Efraim; 58th shepherd attack of the month
items.summary: JSR reported that dozens of foreign far-left activists arrived for an unauthorized olive harvest near Sde Efraim Farm in Binyamin, aiming to provoke; only three Arab pickers were actually at the grove (JSR; JSR on X). Separately, JSR and Olam Katan's Simcha Raz counted the 58th attack this month on Jewish shepherds in Judea and Samaria: about 15 Arabs who arrived under the cover of the olive harvest threw stones at a shepherd from Nahal Avraham Farm (Avraham and Orit Pofer) in Gush Etzion; no injuries reported (JSR; Simcha Raz).

places.name: Nahal Avraham / Pofer Farm
places.note: Approximate (Gush Etzion; nearest Nominatim point Ma'ale Tidhar used as sector anchor)

items.headline: Stone attack from Sa'ir wounds shepherds at Ma'ale Tidhar; father of a prior attacker among those held
items.summary: Arabs from Sa'ir threw stones at Jewish shepherds from Ma'ale Tidhar, east of Gush Etzion near Metzad. Elisha Yered reported one shepherd wounded in the hand; Simcha Raz wrote that two shepherds were lightly hurt and did not need treatment. IDF troops called to the scene arrested several suspects. Among them, Yered named Sand Shalaldeh, father of a terrorist killed after taking part in a lynching attempt on a group of Haredi hikers in the area months earlier. Ayelet Lash also flagged the attack and asked whether Rabbi Benny Lau — who had praised Beit Ummar's leadership the day of the Gefen Ami arson — would condemn it (Elisha Yered; Simcha Raz; Ayelet Lash).

items.headline: Arab "olive pickers" from Deir Ammar attack residents of Ramatayim Tzofim farm
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that on 5 Nov, Arab "olive pickers" from Deir Ammar attacked residents of Ramatayim Tzofim Farm in Gush Talmonim who had gone out looking for a lost cow. He warned that the olive-harvest terror wave would last at least another two weeks and that the security establishment should not treat it as fate (Elisha Yered). Details beyond his report are unconfirmed here.

places.name: Talmon (Gush Talmonim)
places.note: Nominatim (farm itself not found; sector point)

items.headline: Four Judea and Samaria suspects caught after night ambush over farm-tool thefts near Lachish
items.summary: Detectives from Magav South's central unit, with Magav fighters and Yoav volunteers, arrested four Judea and Samaria residents overnight Wednesday–Thursday on suspicion of a string of break-ins and thefts of farm tools and property in the Lachish area. The raid was part of case "Night Club." Intelligence put the cell entering Israel that evening; forces found them riding two farm machines without lights, arrested two on the spot as they tried to start a machine left in the field, and caught the other two after a chase. Police say the four are known to the unit. Walla and Israel Hayom both carried the police account (Walla; Israel Hayom).

items.headline: Five M-16s, a fragmentation grenade and stolen IDF ammo seized in Rahat
items.summary: In two separate police and Magav operations in Rahat, officers seized five M-16 assault rifles, a fragmentation grenade, stolen IDF ammunition (including MAG 7.62 belt rounds), magazines and, according to the police headline, two pistols; five suspects were arrested. In the first raid, Yoav unit fighters with police air support found two M-16s, magazines, a grenade wrapped in cling film and ammo hidden in a toilet shaft, plus two matching license plates suspected forged. In the second, Rahat station officers with Sahar and Magav South found three more M-16s and dozens of rounds. Police also released video of a Rahat suspect shooting toward family members, after which minors collected casings to spoil the scene; a prosecutor's statement was filed ahead of a serious indictment. HaKol HaYehudi tied the seizures to remarks days earlier by Dr. Awad Abu Freih, head of Rahat's popular committee, who told Radio a-Shams that "there is no family in the Negev without weapons" and that Negev Arabs are "all armed" with heavy automatic weapons and grenades (HaKol HaYehudi).

items.headline: Beit Anat greets Chayei Sarah crowds on Route 60 with hill wine; foreign Jews join the flock
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that residents of Beit Anat, on Route 60 between Jerusalem and Kiryat Arba, welcomed the throngs heading to Hebron for Shabbat Chayei Sarah with grape juice and wine from the hill. A year ago, he wrote, the bypass junction was crowded with hostile Arab stalls; now any resident can stop there safely. Separately he posted that a group of Jews from abroad visiting Judea chose Beit Anat, joined the sheep pasture and drew water from the cistern to water the flock. He also photographed a rainbow over Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal from Mitzpe Yehoshua Farm, founded months ago to guard the altar from further Arab attacks (Yered on Beit Anat; foreign visitors; Mount Ebal). Hebron itself saw a heavy police deployment for the Shabbat visitors (Arutz 7). Yishai Fleisher posted from Hebron for Chayei Sarah (Yishai Fleisher).

places.name: Beit Anat
places.note: Approximate (Route 60 hill between Jerusalem and Kiryat Arba; exact point not in Nominatim)

items.headline: First daycare budgets since the expulsion approved for Ganim and Kadim
items.summary: The Samaria Regional Council received a government budget and approval to put up large, upgraded portable daycare buildings in Ganim and Kadim in northern Samaria, the first such government daycare funding for those renewed communities in 21 years. The money comes from the Ministry for the Development of the Negev, Galilee and National Resilience under Minister Yitzhak Wasserlauf. About 30 families have moved into each of Ganim and Kadim; kindergartens already opened with the school year, and a hesder yeshiva opened in Ganim. With the return to Kadim, Jewish settlement was restored in all four northern Samaria communities emptied in the 2005 expulsion: Homesh, Sa-Nur, Ganim and Kadim. Seven more new communities have gone up in the area under the council's "connection plan" toward 19 communities and its "million in Samaria" goal. Wasserlauf said returning to northern Samaria corrects a historic wrong but "our mission does not end with returning to the ground," and that the budget creates conditions for young families to put down roots. Council head Yossi Dagan called it a "historic correction" that will "greatly speed" growth in Ganim and Kadim (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Olam Katan; 0404). Olam Katan's report also quotes Wasserlauf as naming Sa-Nur among the daycare sites; Arutz 7 and Channel 14 name Ganim and Kadim.

items.headline: Rioters from Beit Ummar set fire to a Jewish family's car at Gefen Ami
items.summary: On the evening of 5 Nov, Arab rioters from Beit Ummar set fire to a Jewish family's car on the peripheral path of Gefen Ami in Gush Etzion, about a day after the stone ambush on the access road reported in yesterday's edition. About 15 families live at Gefen Ami. Residents say they are coordinating with IDF forces in the sector and mean to keep building. Netanel Bleicher, a resident, said the attack showed "the enemy's death throes" and that the place is flourishing (Arutz 7; Elchanan Groner on Telegram). Groner wrote that 24 hours had passed since the earlier attack with "zero response" from the army in the village, and that the Etzion brigade commander needed to wake up. Elisha Yered shared the same report and attacked Rabbi Benny Lau for praising Beit Ummar's leadership hours before the arson (Yered on Telegram).

places.name: Beit Ummar
places.note: Nominatim (Beit Ummar village point; Gefen Ami hill itself was not found)

items.headline: Paint bottle on Route 463, dummy bomb at Qalandiya, and the 57th shepherd attack this month
items.summary: JSR reported these incidents on 5 Nov: Arabs threw an object, apparently a paint bottle, at an Israeli car on Route 463 a few meters east of the Na'ale junction in Binyamin; the car was damaged and no one was hurt (JSR; JSR English). IDF troops found a suspicious bag near the Qalandiya crossing the day before; inside was a gas cylinder with wires attached to look like a bomb. Inspection found no explosives. JSR called it the third dummy-bomb incident this month in Judea and Samaria (JSR). About ten Arabs threw stones at shepherds from the Metzudat David farm east of the Arab village of al-Mughayyir; no injuries or damage. JSR counted that as the 57th attack on Jewish shepherds this month (JSR).

places.name: al-Mughayyir
places.note: Prior Nominatim village point used on this desk

items.headline: Arab squatters who wrecked Second Temple ruins petition High Court to clear Kfar Tarfon
items.summary: Elisha Yered, writing for Olam Katan and carried by Arutz 7, reports that Arab squatters who built on Khirbet Tarfin, a Second Temple-period site east of Ateret in Binyamin, then rebuilt after Civil Administration enforcement, petitioned the High Court to order the state to secure their return and clear the nearby Jewish hilltop Kfar Tarfon. Yered writes the court pressed the state for a hurried reply and a report within two weeks on securing the squatters and removing the hilltop, instead of throwing out the petition. He says the state answer was weak, Magav later declared a closed military zone and photographed the Jewish homes, and Central Command signaled it meant to demolish soon; a local protest delayed the demolition for now (Arutz 7 / Olam Katan via Elisha Yered; Yered on Telegram). Yered also says Channel 13's Yossi Eli ran a long sympathetic piece on the Arab complainants without saying they had invaded and damaged the antiquities site. An earlier desk item on 30 Oct flagged an unconfirmed demolition move at Kfar Tarfon; this report is Yered's fuller account of the court fight. Single-source detail from Yered is marked as his claim where not independently confirmed here.

places.name: Kfar Tarfon (near Ateret)
places.note: Approximate: prior desk point at Atara/Ateret (Nominatim)

items.headline: Yesha Council chair meets Argentina's Milei to push recognition and fight sanctions
items.summary: Israel Ganz, head of the Binyamin Regional Council and chair of the Yesha Council, met Argentine President Javier Milei for about an hour at the Argentine government residence during a South America trip aimed at widening foreign support for Judea and Samaria settlement. Ganz asked Milei to act against boycotts and sanctions on the settlements and called for recognition of Judea and Samaria as part of the Land of Israel. The meeting was arranged by Rabbi Richard Kaufman, a personal friend of Milei, and was their third encounter. Ganz invited Milei on an official visit to Binyamin. Ganz's circle called the talk warm and fruitful (Arutz 7).

items.headline: Heritage minister: cabinet ministers should live in Jericho, as in Hebron
items.summary: On 5 Nov Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu toured the eight homes Jewish families entered on the edge of Jericho and said ministers should live in Jericho the way some live in Hebron. "I should have come here with my wife to pick a house to live in," he said. Israel Ganz repeated that Jericho was Israel's gateway and that Oslo had abandoned it, and that the settlers were dismantling the accords "house after house" (Channel 14; Arutz 7 on the mezuzah ceremony with rabbis). On the Palestinian side, Ultra Palestine quotes Jericho governor Hussein Hamayel saying an emergency cell is gathering facts, that three homes were taken not eight, and that the land is government land once held by the Jordanian treasury; an unnamed source told the outlet the Israeli sale story for eight homes is false, while one property sale may have happened (Ultra Palestine). JNS Hebrew (Netanel Frankel) also covered the Jericho return (JNS Hebrew author page).

places.name: Jericho
places.note: Nominatim (city point; homes are on the outskirts)

items.headline: Hebron gears up for Shabbat Chayei Sarah with tens of thousands expected
items.summary: The Harchevi Makom Ohalcha movement said preparations are finished for Shabbat Chayei Sarah in Hebron, when tens of thousands of visitors from Israel and abroad usually fill the city for the Torah reading of Abraham's purchase of the Cave of the Patriarchs. The group says homes redeemed from Arab owners over the past year open new areas for tours and hosting, and it is inviting the public to the "neighborhood of heroism" and the settlement spirit in Hebron (Arutz 7).

items.headline: Peace Now: demolitions begin in a Bedouin community inside the E1 plan area
items.summary: Peace Now's settlements page, dated 6 Nov, says Israel has begun demolishing homes of a Bedouin community inside the E1 plan area, the first such move since E1 planning was renewed (Peace Now). The Jerusalem Post, citing NGOs, says nearly half the structures at Bir al-Maskub near al-Eizariya have already been demolished under orders dating to 2008, including homes, kitchens and sanitation, displacing about 20 residents, with the rest of the community facing the same fate; NGOs argue the site is more than a kilometer from Ma'ale Adumim homes (Jerusalem Post). WAFA says the PA Foreign Ministry condemned the demolitions of about half the community's structures, including four residential clusters, and warned the remaining buildings had received new demolition notices (WAFA). Report Peace Now's and WAFA's framing as their claims; the state treats the buildings as illegal.

items.headline: Three dead and nine wounded in hours of Arab-sector shootings from the Galilee to the Negev
items.summary: On the evening of 5 Nov a wave of shootings and suspected killings hit Arab towns inside Israel. In Baqa al-Gharbiyye a man about 25 was shot dead and three others, ages 30, 25 and 22, were taken to Hillel Yaffe in serious condition with penetrating wounds; a 27-year-old went to Laniado in moderate condition. In Tamra a 22-year-old was killed and two men were badly hurt. A man about 45 was shot and badly wounded in Nazareth. Separate shooting wounded people in Qalansawe and Kafr Qasim. In the Nevatim Bedouin diaspora a woman in her 20s was found dead at home with signs of injury; police had not yet ruled it a murder, and her brother had died in a Negev road accident hours earlier. Police called the shootings criminal in nature and opened separate investigations; a helicopter joined the Baqa search (Channel 14; Maariv and Ynet headlines via Google News). This sits in the desk's wider Negev, Galilee and Triangle crime-and-security track.

items.headline: Ayelet Lash: stone-thrower caught on the way into Jerusalem; Jericho man selling a stolen Mazda arrested
items.summary: Ayelet Lash (Rachelim, Samaria) wrote on Telegram that for several days people had reported stones thrown at cars on the approach into Jerusalem, and that on the evening of 5 Nov police chased and arrested a young man from Ein Nakuba who was carrying more stones meant for throwing (Ayelet Lash). A Makor Rishon headline listed the same day on Google News said an Arab who threw stones at cars in Jerusalem was arrested after a chase in the alleys (article page itself blocked to automated readers; headline only). Separately she posted a listing she said showed Ahmad Ali of Jericho openly selling a Mazda with face, phone and plate visible, asking how he reaches Jewish cars from Jericho; a follow-up post said he had been arrested (Ayelet Lash; Ayelet Lash). She also posted that Arabs in the Negev were monitoring security-force radio traffic; that claim is hers alone here (Ayelet Lash).

items.headline: Taybeh: the assault was not filmed, the main witness is an unnamed diplomat, and JSR documents the French mayor's record
items.summary: The case against the attackers at Taybeh still rests mainly on the delegation's own word. Ynet, which interviewed one of the diplomats overnight without naming him, notes that the attack itself was not filmed. What was filmed is Bernard Baudoux, the French mayor, on the ground afterward, and a silver SUV with a broken rear side window. Belgium's foreign ministry spokesman says a window of the consul general's vehicle was broken, while a Guardian photo caption calls the damaged car the mayor's; no Belgian official called it armored (corrected Oct. 18). The diplomat says seven grown men, aged 20 and over, ran at the cars with clubs and iron bars, kicked Baudoux in the head and shouted 'Viva la France' after beating him. He also says the men 'probably' did not come from a nearby farm but from far away and were 'called in especially,' and that the delegation is 'convinced' it was an organized action aimed at Europeans. He gave no evidence for these points. Baudoux told AFP he was kicked and hit with iron bars. The delegation calls the claim that the visit needed coordination 'misleading,' since Taybeh is in Area B. The IDF did not say the diplomats needed a permit. It said the visit was not coordinated, so no troops were there to protect it, and Taybeh has been a closed military zone for non-resident Israelis since 9 August, which applies to the Israeli activists who came with the delegation. Haaretz, citing the army's preliminary inquiry, reports that warnings of settler threats reached the Binyamin Brigade operations room by 1 p.m., and activists sent more at 1:30 p.m. The room did not recognize the number and ignored the reports. Forces heard of the attack only around 3 p.m., when it was over, and the army has set up a special team to examine its handling. Overnight the Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) published a report on Baudoux, and its main points hold up against the original sources. On 26 April 2025 he gave one of the official speeches at a pro-Palestinian day in Maubeuge, where a representative of AFPS (France Palestine Solidarity Association) also spoke. More than 11,000 euros were collected there: 1,500 euros went to a group in Grande-Synthe and the rest to the association's regional branch, according to the branch's own website. On 7 October 2023 AFPS called the Hamas attack 'a military operation of the weak against the strong' and warned against using the word 'terrorist,' according to its own statement. JSR itself says this does not show that Baudoux is a member or shares all of the group's views. No arrests had been reported by early Sunday.
items.source: Ynet; AFP; Haaretz; IDF; JSR (Yesha Council Situation Room); AFPS statement of 7 Oct 2023; AFPS Nord-Pas-de-Calais website

items.headline: Netanyahu calls Jewish violence a 'plague' but urges caution; Eli Cohen wants far-left activists kept out; Rubio asks Israel to act
items.summary: In an interview with i24NEWS on Saturday night, Prime Minister Netanyahu called violence by Jews in Judea and Samaria a 'plague' and said he had brought in the Shin Bet to 'uproot' it. He also said the cases are being checked, because 'many times we were told things and then it turned out that is not exactly what happened' (Arutz 7). Minister Eli Cohen (Likud) blamed 'extreme left-wing elements' for provocations and said he would ask the head of Central Command to keep them out of the area (Kan). Likud MK Boaz Bismuth said there is no Jewish terror in Judea and Samaria and that he opposes administrative detention orders for Israelis (Kan radio). Kan also quoted an unnamed senior IDF officer as saying that 45 percent of the forces' activity in the area now goes to Jewish nationalist crime; the figure was not explained. From Washington, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States is 'very disturbed by those images' and has asked Israel 'to crack down on that stuff' (RTÉ; Kan). Ambassador Mike Huckabee called the beating of Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine a despicable act of terror by masked cowards, and said the attackers should spend years in prison (Arutz 7; Jerusalem Post). Amit Segal, a right-leaning analyst, wrote that Huckabee's words show how much damage the rioters have done to Israel's standing with its best friends.
items.source: Arutz 7 (Netanyahu on i24NEWS); Kan; RTÉ; Jerusalem Post; Amit Segal on X

items.headline: Abu Falah: a clip from a Hamas-aligned network shows masked village youths slinging stones as they advance on the hill, with press beside them
items.summary: Elisha Yered posted a 52-second clip published by the Quds News Network, which he describes as identified with Hamas, from Friday's clash near Abu Falah, and said it shows clearly how the event began. The desk reviewed the whole clip. It is marked 'Exclusive to Quds Network' and opens with the Arabic caption 'With their bare chests, the youths of Abu Falah confront the settlers.' It is an edited series of at least six shots set to music, not one continuous recording. It shows a group of roughly 20 to 30 people moving up a rocky olive grove toward a large white structure on a hillside. Several masked young men swing and release slings at three points in the clip, and another man throws an object by hand. Four to six people in blue helmets and vests marked PRESS move with the group, and others film on phones. Smoke rises near the white structure in the last shot. No Israelis or soldiers can be identified, and nothing is seen being thrown toward the group; no fireworks appear. This supports the settler account that village youths advanced on the hill slinging stones, with press moving among them. The clip starts in the middle of the event, with a man already swinging a sling, so it does not show who threw first, and it does not show the beating of Heidi Levine.
items.source: Elisha Yered on X; Quds News Network clip (reviewed by the desk)

items.headline: Beit Lid: the shepherd says he was stoned and then hit by a car; the army's first finding was that settlers crashed a stolen car
items.summary: The Saturday incident near Beit Lid, described here last night on the strength of the army's preliminary inquiry, is disputed. Arutz 7 published the account of a Jewish shepherd who says a group of Arabs from Beit Lid threw stones at him. He says he moved away, called his friends and the regional security center, and that the attackers then got into a car and followed him; while he stood a few meters off the path, the car swerved toward him and threw him through the air. Two other residents were hurt, and all three were taken for treatment.
