Arutz 7 also reports that troops arrested three Arab citizens of Israel from the town of Taibe, in central Israel, on suspicion of involvement, and seized their vehicles. No other outlet has reported these arrests, and the IDF has not confirmed them. The Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log, as posted by its volunteer Elad Huminer, records stones thrown at youths from Shirat Tzion at 11:50 a.m. during the harvest near Beit Lid, a clash in which three people were lightly hurt, one with a head cut treated by Magen David Adom, and a report by the youths that an Arab tried to run them over. Against this, Kan and Ynet reported on Saturday that the army's preliminary inquiry found no ramming, and that Jewish rioters were hurt crashing a Palestinian car they had stolen. Whose car was involved, and whether there was one car or two, has not been explained. The army has not published a final finding.
items.source: Arutz 7; Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log (Elad Huminer on X); Kan; Ynet

items.headline: Incidents the wire services did not carry: suspected booby-trapped flags near al-Mughayyir and Silwad, stones and an attempted weapon grab
items.summary: On Saturday evening Elisha Yered reported that men from al-Mughayyir had placed flags suspected of being booby-trapped on a road used by Jews west of the village, and that soon afterward men from Silwad placed another flag attached to a suspicious object next to an army post near Route 60. Army sappers were sent. The Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log for the Sabbath also records a stone roadblock with a suspicious object placed by Arabs from al-Mughayyir at 8:20 p.m. Whether the objects were real explosives or dummies has not been reported. On 12 October police said two dummy bombs with PLO flags had been found in Binyamin, and Elchanan Groner has written that several real ones have also been found. The same Hatzalah log lists other incidents. On Friday: harvesters shouted at a jogger on the Silat bypass road near Sanur and then tried to hit him with their car, and a firebomb was thrown at the fence of Kochav Yaakov at 11:30 p.m. On Saturday: stones and an attempted club attack on security men west of Tapuah; an attack on residents south of the place the log calls Bar Kochba, in which one Arab tried to grab a security man's weapon; stones at shepherds of the Metzudat David farm near al-Mughayyir; and stones at residents of Bat Ayin near Surif. The log puts the theft from the farm near Susya at 15 sheep, of which five were found, fewer than the 'dozens' in earlier settler reports. Elchanan Groner also posted a photo that he says shows men from Salem, during a harvest approved by the army and the Civil Administration, photographing buildings in the new settlement of Shalem near Elon Moreh. These are the organizations' and reporters' own accounts and were not confirmed by the IDF or a second outlet.
items.source: Elisha Yered on X; Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log (Elad Huminer on X); Elchanan Groner on X

items.headline: Nachala sets up 'Pioneers of Gaza' beside the border fence and demands that it be moved into the Strip
items.summary: Overnight Thursday the Nachala settlement movement set up an encampment it calls Halutzei Aza (Pioneers of Gaza) in the Simhoni Forest near Kfar Aza, facing the Gaza border fence, with portable homes and temporary structures. Nachala says more than 700 people took part, including bereaved families, wounded soldiers, rabbis and Knesset members. The site is inside Israel, not in the Strip. Nachala calls it temporary and demands that the government order it moved to the 'northern perimeter,' which the Times of Israel describes as the northern section of the settlement bloc Israel evacuated in 2005. Communications Minister Shlomo Karhi (Likud) joined the activists and spoke in support, and MKs Ohad Tal (Religious Zionism) and Limor Son Har-Melech (Otzma Yehudit) backed it on X. Police said they were watching the site in case the settlers tried to cross the fence. Netanyahu has denied that Israel seeks to resettle Gaza (Times of Israel).
items.source: Times of Israel; Nachala on X; Natanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

items.headline: Taybeh: masked Israelis confront an uncoordinated European delegation in a closed zone; the French mayor on the ground is the pro-Palestinian twin-town mayor
items.summary: The IDF says the European visit to the olive harvest at Taybeh on Saturday afternoon was not coordinated with the army, and that the alert was sent to a brigade operations account meant only for security personnel; by its preliminary inquiry no troops were there at the time. Since 9 August the army has kept Taybeh a closed military zone for non-resident Israelis (Reuters; Straits Times). After the Sabbath, the Prime Minister's Office issued a statement headed 'Serious accusations require serious evidence.' It said the delegation entered a sensitive area 'without prior coordination with the IDF, as officially confirmed by the military'; that the visit included Bernard Baudoux, 'a French Communist Party mayor' who had raised the Palestinian flag over his city hall until French authorities had it removed; that the published images 'do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility'; and that the reports come amid 'a coordinated campaign to smear Israel' during the harvest. What it says about Baudoux is correct: AFP and L'Humanité, the Communist daily, call him a Communist mayor, and L'Observateur reported in September 2025 that the sub-prefecture had the flag taken down the same afternoon. In May 2018 he also demanded 'strong sanctions' by France against Israel (L'Observateur), as Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner pointed out. The office's doubt about who attacked goes further than the army and Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, who both blamed 'Israeli rioters'; Sa'ar added that it was 'unfortunate' the visit was not coordinated (Ynet; Arutz 7). The office offered no evidence of a coordinated campaign. Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz said that 'provocateurs and terrorists' use the harvest to create clashes and that 'in many cases they are the ones attacking,' but also that 'Israelis who resort to violence play into their hands'; he demanded that police arrest stone throwers and organizers on every side at events known in advance, instead of opening an investigation afterward (JSR). Baudoux told AFP the attack shows Israel's 'tolerance' of settler violence. According to L'Humanité, he had come with a Catholic bishop from Cambrai and the parish priest of Aulnoye-Aymeries for the official signing of the twinning; the Belgian foreign minister also mentions 'catholic representatives.' Israeli activists nonetheless accompanied the delegation: Amit Orfali told Haaretz he came with another activist after Palestinians reported that settlers were taking sacks of olives. The man filmed on the ground was not a consul, as Army Radio and WAFA first said. He is Bernard Baudoux, 78, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France (Haaretz; the Belgian foreign minister speaks only of 'a French mayor'). In July his council voted to twin the town with Taybeh and he announced an autumn delegation; last year he flew the Palestinian flag on his city hall and called West Bank settlement 'a spoliation of Palestinian lands,' while also saying Hamas must free the Israeli hostages (Canal FM; L'Observateur). Moran T called him a known Israel-hater; that overstates it, but she was right that this was a politically organized visit and not a chance encounter. The first reports also did not hold up in other details. Army Radio said a car was pelted with stones; the three clips it published show masked young men with sticks at a car window, ATVs following the cars, and the mayor on the ground, but no stone-throwing, no broken window and no blow. AFP, citing witnesses and diplomats, says the men kicked Baudoux; two people who spoke to him said he did not need hospital care. The kicks are not in the clips examined. Ynet placed the mayor in Olonne-sur-Mer, which is wrong. At least one pro-Palestinian account said American and British diplomats were attacked; the delegations were French, Belgian and Polish. What is established: about seven masked Israelis on ATVs surrounded the cars, demanded IDs and broke a car window; Belgium's foreign ministry spokesman says it was the consul general's vehicle, the minister said only that 'a Belgian vehicle was damaged,' and a Guardian photo caption calls it the mayor's car (Army Radio; Haaretz; WAFA; Belga; corrected Oct. 18). The IDF condemned 'Israeli rioters,' and police opened an investigation and asked the Foreign Ministry to help find the victims. No arrests had been reported by Saturday night. What came before: Taybeh has been a flashpoint since 2025. Last July, international outlets reported that settlers set fire to the ancient St. George church; police found the fire was in open ground nearby and the church was not damaged, and U.S. Ambassador Huckabee, who had called it terror, said he had attributed it to no one (Ynet; Channel 14). JDN, reporting the Binyamin Council's case, says the images used as proof show Jewish herders trying to put the fire out. The fire's cause was never determined. The village priest, Bashar Fawadleh, who sits on the board of Kairos Palestine, is the Taybeh organizer of the twinning with Aulnoye-Aymeries (Canal FM). Residents and church leaders report repeated grazing, arson and harassment by settlers from nearby outposts (Times of Israel; OSV News). Whether the spot of Saturday's confrontation lies inside the closed zone, and in Area B or C, is not confirmed.
items.source: IDF spokesperson; Israel Police; Army Radio (Doron Kadosh); Haaretz (Rozovsky and Golan); Belgian Foreign Minister; Reuters via Straits Times; Canal FM; L'Observateur; Ynet; Channel 14; JDN; WAFA; Prime Minister's Office (after the Sabbath); Foreign Minister Sa'ar via Ynet and Arutz 7; Israel Ganz via JSR; AFP via BFM TV; L'Humanité; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X

items.headline: Ma'in: settlers say their flock was stolen first, and the army says both sides took sheep; near Beit Lid, a reported ramming turns out to be a stolen car
items.summary: In Ma'in in the South Hebron Hills, settlers say Palestinians stole a flock from them near Ma'on, and that they went to the village to get it back; stones were thrown and troops fired in the air to break it up (Ynet). After the Sabbath, Elisha Yered gave the settlers' account in detail: at about 5 a.m. Arabs broke into a farm near Susya and took dozens of sheep; the trail led to Khirbet Ma'on (the Hebrew name for the hamlet), and part of the flock was found there after hours of searches by farmers, volunteers, soldiers and police. He posted a night security-camera clip, filmed off a screen, of sheep in a lit lane; no face can be seen, and the place cannot be confirmed from it. The IDF said the confrontation began 'amid reports of livestock belonging to Israeli civilians being stolen,' and a military official told the Times of Israel the army knows of livestock theft 'by both sides.' The same official said armed Israelis on ATVs also took Palestinian sheep, which will be returned, and that their identities are unknown. Army Radio's Doron Kadosh posted a daytime security-camera clip of that raid. He says it shows masked Israelis taking the Palestinians' sheep while soldiers pass them without stopping them, and the soldiers then firing in the air to keep Palestinians back; he says the army confirmed the sheep were Palestinian. The clip does show a flock driven down a village street, armed men in uniform arriving and men running, but at its resolution faces cannot be made out. If both accounts are accurate, the theft from the farm in the night came first and the armed raid in the morning followed it. The Palestinian figures do not agree with each other: the Red Crescent says six people were hurt, WAFA says three were hurt and 380 sheep taken. Neither count has been checked independently. Elsewhere on Saturday the reports are thin and come mostly from Palestinian or activist sources. At Deir Jarir, Haaretz published photographs of masked men throwing stones at harvesters, with soldiers near them; when the soldiers arrived is not clear. The Israeli side reports the reverse. Elisha Yered, Elchanan Groner, Amit Segal and Srugim say Palestinian harvesters from Deir Jarir, with left-wing activists filming beside them, threw stones at a shepherd from the Ma'ale Ahuvia farm and then at the soldiers he called. Their clips show masked young men slinging and throwing stones in an olive grove, and a man swinging a sling a few meters from a group holding cameras; Yered says a stone hits the shepherd. The clips carry captions but no time stamps, and they do not show how the clash began. Whether Haaretz and Yered describe the same clash from opposite sides is not established, and the IDF has not commented. What came before: Ma'ale Ahuvia was set up in memory of Ahuvia Sandak, who died in a police chase in 2020, and the state cleared it in April 2021 and again in February 2022 (Honenu; Jerusalem Post); it is now described as a farm. Near Beit Lid in Samaria, the IDF first reported an Israeli civilian hurt after 'a confrontation between several Israeli civilians and several Palestinians,' and early reports spoke of a ramming attack. The army's preliminary inquiry found there was no ramming: Jewish rioters had stolen a Palestinian car, and one of them was hurt in a crash while driving it (Kan). Ynet adds that the settlers had come to stop the harvest and that several Palestinians were hurt by stones; Army Radio, as cited by Anadolu, said they came from the Shirat Tzion outpost. Some right-wing summaries after the Sabbath still repeated only the first IDF statement. Olive theft was reported at Burqa and Umm Safa. At Jalud, the American Substack reporter Jasper Nathaniel says soldiers watched an attack and tear-gassed him; that is his account alone. Yesh Din counts 487 incidents since 27 September, 234 tied to the harvest; that is its own tally. On the Israeli side, JSR on Friday reported stones thrown near Tzon Aviezer, twelve Arabs attacking two hikers near Shilo and stones thrown at a Ma'ale Ahuvia shepherd, and Elisha Yered reported two arrests near Karnei Shomron. None of these reached the wire services.
items.source: Ynet (Idan Blumhof); Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian); IDF spokesperson; Red Crescent; WAFA; Haaretz; JSR; Elisha Yered; Yesh Din; Elisha Yered, Elchanan Groner and Amit Segal on X; Srugim; Army Radio (Doron Kadosh); Kan; Honenu; Jerusalem Post; Anadolu

items.headline: Abu Falah: the village's history with the outpost, the activists on the ground, and what the inquiry still has to settle
items.summary: The Binyamin Council says the Palestinian Authority brought hundreds of activists and rioters to the hill under cover of the harvest to drag its residents into a clash, and the Prime Minister's Office says about 200 Arabs and far-left activists faced about 40 Israeli youths. The record gives that account some support. Among those on the ground was Jonathan Pollak, a veteran Israeli anti-occupation activist who has been convicted four times and was indicted in 2023 on charges of assaulting police and throwing stones at a Border Police jeep at a Beita protest (+972; Haaretz); the outcome of that case was not found. Jasper Nathaniel, the main witness quoted abroad, is a Substack writer who began reporting in the West Bank in 2024. He told the Columbia Journalism Review in January that he feels 'unshackled, unburdened, by some of the ethics,' that he is 'compromised,' and that he advises his sources; to those who call him an activist, he said, 'I don't care.' His video of a settler clubbing a woman at Turmus Ayya last year did lead to an indictment, so his footage is not to be dismissed, but his commentary is advocacy. The one Palestinian shot, council member Abduljaber Hassan, was hit by soldiers, not settlers; the IDF says he ran at troops with a sharp object. What came before: the hill is contested. On 8 March, Israelis who went up to found a new hill in Area B near the village clashed with villagers, with stones thrown both ways (Srugim; Ynet, which names the nearby outpost as Or Nachman). The army's first call was about Israelis attacking Palestinians near homes; two villagers were shot dead by gunfire whose source was never established, and a third died after inhaling gas. A criminal investigation was opened, and no charges have been reported. Kan has also reported a clash near the village in which, by the settlers' account, a Jewish shepherd was beaten with clubs and stones by dozens of Palestinians and his flock went missing; troops found him bleeding. Palestinians said settlers entered the village and burned a car. On 6 October Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner reported that villagers spread poison on Israeli pastures (their account). The injuries are not in dispute: Levine's daughter told AP that she has a broken rib, several broken vertebrae and a finger cut to the bone, and she had surgery on Saturday at Beilinson Hospital, which describes her condition as moderate, with injuries to the limbs (Ynet). After the Sabbath, President Isaac Herzog phoned her and apologized; he called the attackers 'criminals' and urged that they be found and prosecuted (his post on X; Times of Israel). Her children told Kan they want a real investigation and arrests. A letter of apology was also sent in the name of Commanders for Israel's Security, a group of about 600 former officials that calls for a basic change in government policy, and a forum of about 200 former police officers; Moshe Ya'alon and Tamir Pardo are among the signers (i24NEWS). Posts that speak of '800 senior officials' count the groups' members; how many signed in person is not clear. Still open: who threw the first stone, whether fireworks were used, who beat Levine, and where her cameras are. The Prime Minister's Office has not released the footage it cited. No arrests had been reported by Saturday night.
items.source: Binyamin Regional Council; Prime Minister's Office; IDF; +972 Magazine; Haaretz; Columbia Journalism Review; Srugim; Ynet; Kan; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X; AP via Times of Israel; Beilinson Hospital via Ynet; President Herzog; Kan; i24NEWS

items.headline: Claims on each side: where the Israeli sources were right, and what the Palestinian side asserts
items.summary: Israeli sources' claims. Moran T and JSR said the Taybeh and Abu Falah stories were driven by activists and staged for the cameras. Activists were in fact present at both: Israeli activists accompanied the Taybeh delegation into a zone closed to Israelis, and convicted activist Jonathan Pollak was at Abu Falah. Moran T was also right that the last big Taybeh story, that settlers burned the ancient church in 2025, did not hold up: police found the church undamaged, though the cause of the nearby fire was never settled. Her suggestion that the Shin Bet staged Saturday's footage, and her claim that the Taybeh priest was filmed throwing stones, are not supported by anything found. JSR, silent over the Sabbath, had said the Abu Falah harvesters came with fireworks and stones; stones are in the footage, fireworks are not. After the Sabbath, the Prime Minister's Office spoke of 'a coordinated campaign to smear Israel' around the harvest and warned of 'further allegations in the coming days'; it gave no evidence of coordination, though the activist presence at Taybeh and Abu Falah is established. Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner said Baudoux 'led the provocation' with dozens of anarchists. He came for a twinning ceremony with clergy and diplomats, and reports name only two Israeli activists with the delegation; their point that he once demanded sanctions on Israel (in 2018) is correct. Moran T again suggested that the Shin Bet or the left was behind the footage and compared the story to the Muhammad al-Durrah affair; nothing found supports that. The Palestinian side's claims. WAFA calls the attackers 'colonists' and reported a consul knocked down; it was the French mayor. One account said American and British diplomats were attacked; others said a child and an elderly woman were hurt at Taybeh; none of that is confirmed. The Red Crescent's and WAFA's casualty counts at Ma'in disagree with each other. Press TV's Hebrew account called Baudoux 'a French diplomat'; he is a mayor. An X account quoted Levine's daughter as saying about fifteen masked men attacked her with clubs and nails; that is not in her interview with AP or in any news report checked.
items.source: Moran T on X; JSR; WAFA; Red Crescent; posts on X; Prime Minister's Office; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X; Press TV (Hebrew)

items.headline: Heavy, prolonged gunfire from Kafr Qadum heard in Kedumim
items.summary: On the evening of 8 October residents of Kedumim, in Samaria, heard prolonged heavy gunfire from the Arab village of Kafr Qadum, a few hundred metres away, and the security department called out the community’s forces and the IDF. The head of the Kedumim council, Uziel Vatik, said that so many weapons so close to a Jewish community cannot be accepted, whether the shooting was a clan quarrel or something else. He demanded that the army enter Kafr Qadum in force to collect the weapons and arrest terrorists.

items.headline: Authority security men sent to the olive harvest in civilian clothes
items.summary: Hakol Hayehudi reported that the Palestinian Authority regularly sends members of its security forces, often in civilian clothes, to olive harvests in Area C and next to Jewish communities, under the name of “protection from settlers”; the director-general of the Palestinian police, Major-General Alam al-Saqa, has ordered higher readiness for the season. The practice goes back to a decision of Prime Minister Salam Fayyad in 2011 and to a later framework called “harvest in the hot zones”, which sends officers and intelligence men to points of friction. The report followed the death at Burqa of Ali al-Bazari, an officer of the National Security Forces, in a clash with the IDF after a Jewish shepherd was attacked.

items.headline: Attacks on shepherds in Binyamin rise sharply; farmers receive body cameras
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council has begun to give body cameras to farmers after a sharp rise in incidents at the start of the olive harvest. By the council’s figures, reports of incidents near farms rose from about 23 to about 48 in the first week of the harvest, attacks on shepherds rose from three to eleven, and more than 140 attacks on shepherds have been recorded since the start of the year. The council head and Yesha Council chairman, Yisrael Gantz, said the cameras would let the world see what actually happens on the ground.

items.headline: New community of Goder in the northern Jordan Valley to be inaugurated on 14 October
items.summary: The new community of Goder, in the northern Jordan Valley, will be formally inaugurated on Wednesday, 14 October. Twelve families already live there, the first of whom arrived about two months ago, and 400 more housing units are planned. The cabinet approved the community on Jerusalem Day 2025; it stands on the site of a former paratrooper base at a junction on Route 5799 between Tubas and Maskiyot.

items.headline: First tent put up again at Netzach Shmuel after the demolition
items.summary: After the Civil Administration and the Border Police demolished the hilltop community of Netzach Shmuel, near Adei Ad in Binyamin, the young men who live there returned to the same hill. They have put up the first tent again.

items.letter: Added to the desk on 9 October from +972 Magazine
items.headline: Seventeen settlements approved in the Jenin district since early 2025
items.summary: According to figures from Peace Now cited by +972 Magazine, the government has approved 17 settlements in the Jenin district since the start of 2025, among them four evacuated in 2005; Ganim and Kadim have now been re-established, and Defence Minister Katz spoke at the ceremony for Ganim on 13 August. The army has set up six new camps across the district, one of them inside the city of Jenin, and another is planned. In July the commander of Central Command, Major General Avi Bluth, signed at least 15 orders taking about 200 dunams in Areas A and C for a road between the new settlements of Emek Dotan and Noa; Peace Now says this is the first use of such orders in Area A for the needs of settlement since the Oslo Accords.

items.headline: Katz: what was done in Gaza and Lebanon will come to Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz said this week that the IDF is preparing as never before for a “turning of the barrels”, in which the forces of the Palestinian Authority would turn their weapons on Israelis. “If anyone dares to turn weapons against us, what we did in Gaza and Lebanon will come to Judea and Samaria,” he said, adding that Israel would answer with an all-out campaign. Dr. Edy Cohen told Channel 14 that the threat is “not science fiction”, recalled that such forces turned on their hosts in Jordan, Lebanon and Kuwait, and criticised the security cabinet for not yet deciding on Minister Ben Gvir’s call to dismantle the Authority.

items.headline: Stones near Yitzhar and a firebomb at a bus from al-Fawwar
items.summary: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria reported that at 20:11 on 7 October Arabs threw stones at vehicles between the Yitzhar interchange and the small Yitzhar junction. At 20:42 Arabs from al-Fawwar, in the Hebron hills, threw a firebomb at a bus; it burned at the side of the road. No one was hurt in either attack.
items.source: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria, via Yisrael Medad (X)

items.headline: Nine Jews detained near Susya and Sinia; residents report police violence
items.summary: The police said that Border Police detained seven suspects near Susya, in the southern Hebron hills, over what they called extreme violence, and two residents of Samaria after a reported assault near the village of Sinia. The legal-aid group Honenu gave a different account: six people were detained during the evacuation of an outpost near Susya, and residents described severe violence by officers and heavy fire of rubber bullets. Several residents were hurt.

items.headline: Broad arrests for incitement and for support of the 7 October massacre
items.summary: Alongside the demolition of the house of the murderer of Netanel Shukron, forces of the IDF, the Shin Bet and the police opened broad brigade operations across Judea and Samaria. Dozens of wanted men who had publicly supported the massacre of 7 October were arrested, together with men identified with Hamas, and thorough searches for weapons were made. The IDF said that it will continue to act on its own initiative against terror infrastructure.

items.headline: Groner: the Authority is heavily armed, and its workers build Israel’s defences
items.summary: Marking three years since the massacre, the journalist Elchanan Groner wrote that the next great attack could come at any moment from armed Arab citizens of Israel and from the Palestinian Authority, which he described as armed to the neck, including with armoured vehicles. He wrote that IDF bases, community fences, armouries and security cameras are built by workers from the Authority, and that convoys of smugglers cross every day from the Hebron hills to Arad. He also noted that the IDF had not explained the release of the smuggler whose vehicle rammed an IDF Humvee on 5 October.

items.headline: Officer of the Authority’s forces killed in attack on a shepherd near Sebastia
items.summary: On 7 October Arabs from Ramin and Burqa attacked a shepherd of about twenty from the Brit Avraham farm near the old railway station at Sebastia; a stone or concrete block struck his head, and he now has a severe head injury, and four others who came to help were lightly hurt. The IDF said that a commander shot a man running at him with a suspicious object. Arab channels named the dead man as Ali Hussein of Bazariya, an officer of the Palestinian Authority security forces, whom Elchanan Groner described as a soldier of the National Security Forces.

items.headline: Shepherds attacked at Givat Tidhar and Anatot; explosive device found near Burqa
items.summary: A shepherd from Givat Tidhar was wounded by Arabs from Deir Abu Mash'al who had presented themselves as olive pickers, and about eight Arabs with clubs and stones attacked shepherds from a farm near Anatot, injuring one in the head. During the night Arabs from Burqa placed a flag of the PLO and an explosive device made of a gas cylinder and a battery on an access road; a sapper destroyed it in the morning. Attackers from al-Mughayyir again spread poisoned bait near the Allon Road, and a goat died.

items.headline: IDF demolishes monuments to terrorists and the house of the Ein Ria murderer
items.summary: IDF forces began a broad operation to demolish dozens of monuments glorifying terrorists, among them a central monument in Nablus and one in Ya'bad to a man convicted in the murder of Avner Maimon in 2003. Notices left for residents said that anyone who glorifies terror will be arrested for incitement. On the same day the IDF demolished the house of Qadri Samara, who murdered Netanel Shukron of Alei Zahav at the Ein Ria spring.

items.headline: Ben Gvir: the Palestinian Authority must be brought down
items.summary: Speaking beside the separation fence near Road 6, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said that hostile elements are training and arming themselves behind the fence, and that kidnapping, terror or a “turning of the barrels” could reach the centre of the country. He said that he is the only member of the security cabinet who votes to bring the Authority down, while decisions to strengthen it come before the cabinet month after month. He said that Israel must take the initiative against the Authority as it did in Gaza.

items.headline: American state legislators visit Eival and the new communities of northern Samaria
items.summary: A bipartisan delegation of state legislators from Florida, Illinois, Texas, Indiana, Missouri and Alabama visited northern Samaria as guests of Yossi Dagan, head of the Samaria Regional Council. They saw Peduel, the new community of Eival founded this summer, the altar of Joshua on Mount Eival and the lookout above Joseph’s Tomb. The members are expected to promote state laws requiring the name “Judea and Samaria” in official documents and laws against boycotts of its businesses.

items.headline: Arab crime organisations hold military weapons, warns head of government task force
items.summary: Roy Kahlon, head of the Prime Minister’s Office task force against crime in the Arab sector, said that Arab crime organisations inside Israel now hold LAW anti-tank rockets, MAG machine guns, Claymore-type charges and explosive drones. He described a wartime scenario in which armed groups in vehicles with Israeli plates block roads, strike infrastructure and fire in residential areas. He compared the present approach to the assumptions held about Hamas before 7 October.

items.headline: Katz sets out plan for war if the Authority’s forces turn on Israel
items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz told the cabinet that, beyond an attempt by terror groups to repeat 7 October, the security establishment is preparing for a complete reversal by the Palestinian Authority’s forces and the Tanzim militias. He said that this would mean an all-out war against the Authority, not another wave of terror. An operational plan approved by Prime Minister Netanyahu and Mr. Katz provides for a short and intense campaign with air and ground fire, the targeting of senior figures, the destruction of weapons caches and the large-scale evacuation of Arab residents from combat zones.

items.headline: Mass poisoning of a flock near the Allon Road
items.summary: Nine sheep and a sheepdog died, and more than forty sheep were harmed, after poison was poured into a water trough on a hilltop near the Allon Road in Binyamin. Residents said that the cell came from the direction of al-Mughayyir; the suspects have not been caught. Residents described it as the thirteenth poisoning of pastures along the Allon Road in the past year.

items.headline: Shin Bet chief warns of military-type organisation among the Negev Bedouin
items.summary: David Zini, head of the Shin Bet, told the security cabinet of “very worrying” organisation in the unrecognised Bedouin settlements of the Negev, including infrastructure of a military character. He said that attempts have been identified to set up frameworks resembling military battalions. He also warned of ties between residents and terror organisations, Hamas among them.

items.headline: Central Command adopts the doctrine of “the community as a fortress”
items.summary: The IDF stated that Central Command has adopted the doctrine of “the community as a fortress”, with more observation, intelligence, weapons and security components inside the communities, and that all army camps in Judea and Samaria are being turned into fortified posts. Its forces continue to hold the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps under Operation Iron Wall. On the eastern border, Division 96, “Gilad”, has been established with five territorial rapid-response “David brigades”.

items.headline: Orders signed to demolish monuments glorifying terrorists
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reported that the IDF appears to be changing its policy on monuments glorifying terrorists, which until now required separate legal and command approval for each demolition. Orders signed by Brigadier General Kobi Heller, commander of the Judea and Samaria Division, have been distributed, and IDF sources said that an orderly procedure now allows demolitions as part of brigade operations. Arab media published one such order, placed on a monument in the Jenin area.

items.headline: Smuggler whose vehicle rammed an IDF Humvee is released
items.summary: Mahmoud Daisat, a known smuggler of illegal residents, was released on 6 October and handed to the Red Crescent as a free man. He had driven the vehicle that rammed an IDF Humvee in the Hebron hills on 5 October. Security officials expressed strong anger at the release and described the daily convoys of smugglers between the Hebron hills and the Negev as a serious danger; the IDF Spokesperson said that an inquiry has been opened.

items.headline: A new community, Elisha, to be established near Jericho
items.summary: Residents of Beit Hogla, in the Jordan Valley, are moving on to establish a new community named Elisha on the outskirts of Jericho. Azriel Pikar, one of the four founding families of Beit Hogla almost eleven years ago, said that Beit Hogla now has about sixty families. He said that the cranes for Elisha are being raised in daylight, with the support of all the authorities and the approval of the government.

items.headline: Homes demolished at Ora Israel and Netzach Shmuel
items.summary: Border Police and Civil Administration inspectors in large numbers demolished four family homes at two settlement points, Ora Israel near Salfit and Netzach Shmuel near Adei Ad, and confiscated the flock of Ora Israel. Several teenagers were hurt by police and five were arrested. Residents describe Ora Israel as a barrier to Authority control of the Area A bloc between Salfit and Ramallah.

items.headline: Kfar Ana: drone footage shows Palestinians started the fire blamed on settlers
items.summary: Palestinians from Ein Yabrud set fire to a roadblock of tyres on the access road to Kfar Ana, between Beit El and Ofra, and the fire spread to a nearby Palestinian car lot. The village then said that settlers had set the lot alight. Drone footage shows the Palestinians beside the fire, and the IDF said that its trackers determined from the evidence that Palestinians had set it.

items.headline: Smotrich petitions the High Court to advance the E1 tender
items.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich filed an urgent petition against an instruction by Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to delay the opening of bids in the tender for 1,234 housing units in E1, at seven sites in the Mevaseret Adumim neighbourhood of Ma'ale Adumim. He said that political approval was given in October 2025, before the election period. He said that the building will connect Jerusalem and Ma'ale Adumim for the first time and decide whether there is continuous Israeli territory.

items.headline: Children’s bus stoned on the Gilad road; poison spread on two pastures
items.summary: Arabs stoned a bus carrying children on the Gilad road in Samaria, the second attack on that road in two days. Attackers from Abu Falah spread poison on pastures near the Allon Road, and five sheep fell severely ill. Near Ma'ale Amos, in Gush Etzion, residents found dates laced with poison spread on their pastures by attackers from Kisan.

items.headline: Shin Bet chief raises the return of administrative detention against Jews
items.summary: David Zini, head of the Shin Bet, told the security cabinet that he may demand the return of administrative detention, imprisonment without charge or trial, against Jews in Judea and Samaria. Defence Minister Katz ended the use of such orders against Jews in November 2024, and any return rests with him. Coalition members of Knesset criticised the remarks, and Tally Gottlieb called on Mr. Zini to resign.

items.headline: Second attacker in the Hanina Farm stabbing attempt arrested
items.summary: The IDF announced that, after a joint pursuit under Shin Bet guidance, it arrested the second terrorist in the attempted stabbing near Kafr Rammun, together with a further suspect. Residents of the farm said that the first attacker set a vehicle alight and ran at them with a knife. One resident stopped him with his vehicle, and no Israelis were hurt.

items.headline: Two attempted attacks in Binyamin and the Hebron hills
items.summary: A terrorist with a knife came to the grazing land of Hanina Farm near Rammun, set fire to an Israeli vehicle and tried to stab residents, who stopped him with their vehicle. Earlier, near Bani Na'im east of Hebron, a vehicle carrying three Palestinians struck an IDF vehicle, and the soldiers fired. One occupant was killed and two were wounded; no soldiers or civilians were hurt.

items.headline: Minister Strook confronts the Shin Bet chief in the security cabinet
items.summary: Minister Orit Strook told the security cabinet that the security services give a partial picture of violence in Judea and Samaria, and that Palestinians attack shepherds and endanger their lives. Shin Bet head David Zini replied that Palestinians do not burn Jewish homes. Member of Knesset Limor Son Har-Melech answered with a photograph of the fire at Havat Gilad and asked whether Mr. Zini had dealt with the threat from the Palestinian security services.

items.headline: Authority forces warned before IDF raids, and the targets appeared on Islamic Jihad channels
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that before an overnight operation in northern Samaria the IDF told the Palestinian Authority security services in advance, so that they would withdraw from the area. The targets of the operation then appeared on Telegram channels of Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Those channels later complained that the IDF had entered Meithalun without warning, unlike the fourteen other targets.

items.headline: Central Command presents plans for a “turning of the barrels” to the cabinet
items.summary: The defence establishment was to present to the security cabinet the plans of Central Command for a scenario in which the weapons of the Palestinian Authority security services are turned against IDF forces or Israeli communities. On 7 September Defence Minister Katz said that he and the Prime Minister had instructed the IDF to prepare for a full war against the Authority’s senior figures and security services if they opened an attack of the 7 October type.

items.headline: Border Police prepare to demolish settlement points
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that Border Police carried out preparatory patrols for demolitions at no fewer than four settlement points, some of which house families. He criticised Brigadier General Kobi Heller for turning his forces against the settlements instead of against the organisers of disturbances during the olive harvest.

items.headline: Feiglin rejects the claim that armed settlers enter Arab villages to kill
items.summary: Moshe Feiglin, chairman of Zehut, challenged Gadi Eisenkot to give one name of an Arab whom a settler had deliberately gone to his village and murdered in the last ten years. He said that the Arabs killed in such incidents were terrorists who infiltrated communities and were stopped by the security forces or the emergency squads. He called Mr. Eisenkot’s account a gross lie and incitement.

items.headline: Hilltop communities seek recognition by the state, including in Areas A and B
items.summary: Residents of the new hilltop communities are campaigning before the elections for recognition and regularisation, including for communities in Areas A and B and on land registered as private. Shalhevet Goldstein of Givat Maoz Esther proposed cancelling the Oslo Accords, a new registration of all land, and the definition of a hilltop community as a security component that may be placed in Area B.

items.headline: Overnight raids in fourteen towns, and a general closure for 5 and 7 October
items.summary: Israeli forces raided at least fourteen villages and towns, arrested dozens of wanted men, and broke up a cell in Araneh, near Nablus, that was in advanced planning for an attack. In Awarta forces secured worshippers at the tombs of Eleazar and Ithamar. Defence Minister Katz ordered a general closure on Judea and Samaria on 5 and 7 October.

items.headline: False report of settler violence at Sebastia
items.summary: The main Nablus Telegram channel reported that settlers were attacking residents in Iyarib, Sebastia. Elisha Yered wrote after watching the video that the claim is false, and that footage presented as such an attack shows Jewish youths practising self-defence at the edge of a community.

items.headline: Molotov attack on Eretz HaTzvi farm stopped by the owner
items.summary: Two attackers carrying Molotov cocktails came to Eretz HaTzvi farm near Nachliel, in western Binyamin, intending to set it on fire. The owner followed the arrest procedure, then fired and wounded one; no Israelis were hurt. The Palestinian Authority Health Ministry and WAFA presented the death of a 19-year-old from Kafr Aqab as a killing by settlers near Kobar.

items.headline: Four foreign activists face removal after olive-harvest provocations
items.summary: Four foreign activists who took part in a violent olive-harvest provocation in Gush Kana, in which Jewish youths were hurt, were detained by the IDF near Tapuah. They were questioned at the Ariel police station, and their file was sent to the Population and Immigration Authority for a hearing on removal from Israel. Yossi Dagan said that those who come to provoke must know that there is a price.

items.headline: Wave of attacks in Samaria under cover of the olive harvest
items.summary: Near Nahal Kane and Tzon Aviezer, Arabs from Asira al-Qibliya attacked Jews and a Jewish youth was wounded in the head by a stone. Near Avnei Elad about fifty Arabs attacked settlers with stones, and Nahal Battalion 50 arrested five. Rioters from al-Mughayyir threw stones at a shepherd from Givat Or Nachman, and the IDF arrested two.

items.headline: Fatah and the anti-settlement committee prepare harvest riots in Binyamin
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that Fatah and the Committee Against Settlements held a long preparatory meeting in the Ramallah district with village Fatah secretaries. The meeting was held ahead of planned olive-harvest riots in Binyamin.

items.headline: About fifty terror suspects arrested during Sukkot
items.summary: During Sukkot the IDF, with Battalion 931 and the Maglan unit under the Samaria Brigade, arrested about fifty terror suspects, among them a Hamas activist in Nablus. Forces seized weapons, drones and materials for explosive devices, and struck a terrorist who tried to throw a charge at them.

items.headline: Stone attack near Yasuf, and an attempt to drag a youth into the village
items.summary: Dozens of Palestinians threw stones at a group of Israelis at a water cistern by the Anton farm, between Tapuach and Rechelim; police said a boy of about fourteen was lightly wounded and are examining a claim that attackers tried to drag one of the group toward the village. An armed security man stopped the attempt, and troops fired to disperse the rioters. Palestinian officials and several foreign outlets later presented the same afternoon as a killing by settlers.

items.headline: Shepherd stoned by rioters from al-Mughayyir
items.summary: Dozens of rioters from al-Mughayyir, in Binyamin, attacked a Jewish shepherd from a nearby outpost with stones; he was not hurt. Witnesses said that the IDF response was weak, and that the village has grown more aggressive since the Paratroopers replaced the Duchifat Battalion in that sector.

items.headline: Olive pickers attack Beit Karnaim farm and try to seize the owner’s weapon
items.summary: Three Palestinians picking olives refused to leave the grazing land of Beit Karnaim farm near Maoz Tzur and threw stones at residents, wounding one in the head. They tried to seize the farm owner’s weapon, and he fired three shots into the air; one attacker was detained. The Binyamin Regional Council said that the harvest must not be used as cover for attacks.

items.headline: Dummy charge wrapped in a Hamas flag closes Route 463
items.summary: An object that looked like an explosive charge, wrapped in a Hamas flag, was placed on Route 463, the Wallerstein Road in Binyamin. The road was closed for about two hours until checks showed that it was a dummy.

items.headline: Warning that the Authority’s anti-settlement committee will use the olive harvest for attacks
items.summary: Elisha Yered wrote that the Arab olive harvest would open on 2 October and would be used for attacks near Jewish communities. He asked the commander of Central Command and the commander of the Judea and Samaria police district to arrest Mu'id Sha'aban and his group from the Palestinian Authority committee for fighting the settlements. This was a request, not a report of an arrest.

items.headline: Shepherd attacked near Maoz Tzur by about fifty masked men
items.summary: Four men attacked a Jewish shepherd at a farm near Maoz Tzur, and about fifty masked men from Beit Ur al-Tahta then joined them with clubs, stones and tear gas. Two Jews were hurt, and about one hundred metal spikes were found on an access road. About ninety minutes later some twenty men stoned a shepherd from the Metzudat David farm near al-Mughayyir.

items.headline: New settlement point, Golot, established near Otniel
items.summary: A new settlement point named Golot has been established in the Hebron hills, a few kilometres from Otniel, near the springs and Tel Devir. A road has been prepared, a metal structure placed, and a guard kept there day and night for two to three weeks. A group of families from Otniel and Tekoa is waiting to move in.

items.headline: Prayer at Beitunia square after the kidnapping of a reservist by Palestinian police
items.summary: Hundreds of residents of western Binyamin came in more than 80 vehicles to Beitunia square for morning prayers under IDF security. The organisers said it was a response to the kidnapping, about a month earlier and nearby, of an IDF reservist by terrorists from the Palestinian police. They called on the IDF and the government to restore control and security in the area.

items.headline: Thousands pray at Joseph’s Tomb with the Four Species
items.summary: Thousands entered Joseph’s Tomb in Nablus in two rounds with IDF approval, for the first mass morning prayer there with the Four Species in several decades. Senior commanders, members of Knesset and Yossi Dagan attended. Mr. Dagan and Zvi Sukkot called for the full return of the Od Yosef Chai yeshiva to the tomb.

items.headline: Attacks on Israelis under cover of the olive harvest in Samaria and Binyamin
items.summary: Olam Katan reported that on the morning of 9 October Arabs from Zeita waited in an olive grove in the Gush Kana area, between Yitzhar and Emanuel, and stoned the car of Israeli hikers; the windscreen was damaged and no one was hurt. The same morning a Samaria resident on an all-terrain vehicle was rammed and lightly injured near Tapuah, and a Jew was lightly injured in the face by stones near Jama'in, south of Nablus. In the afternoon Elisha Yered reported stone-throwing near Gilad Farm and a booby-trapped PLO flag on the grazing land of the Hesed L'Avraham farm on Mount Hazor, and he warned that dozens of attacks were to be expected over the Sabbath.

items.headline: Hikers remove a monument to the murderer of Rabbi Nehemia Lavi and Aharon Bennett
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that hikers of the Chargavim group, touring western Binyamin on 9 October, found a monument in Surda to Muhannad Halabi, who murdered Rabbi Nehemia Lavi and Aharon Bennett in Jerusalem in October 2015, and removed it. Ynet, citing local Palestinian sources, described the same events as an attack by armed settlers who threw stones, fired in the air and damaged a monument. The episode came in the same week that the IDF demolished dozens of monuments to terrorists in Nablus, Jenin and nearby villages.

items.headline: Katz orders removal of far-left activists; Jonathan Pollak detained near Tapuah
items.summary: Hityashvut Achshav reported on 8 October that Defence Minister Israel Katz had directed that administrative removal orders be issued against far-left activists, including foreign nationals, who come to Judea and Samaria to provoke clashes with Israeli residents. The directive followed a request by Yisrael Gantz, chairman of the Yesha Council, on behalf of all the local council heads. On the morning of 9 October soldiers detained the Israeli anarchist Jonathan Pollak and the activist Roman Levin near Kfar Tapuah for violating a closed military zone order, according to JFeed.

items.headline: Hundreds walk the Wallerstein Road and call for it to be reopened to Israelis
items.summary: Hityashvut Achshav reported that on the morning of 9 October hundreds of hikers and residents, organised by the Chargavim group, walked from Beit El to Dolev along the Wallerstein Road, which has been closed to Israeli traffic for about 26 years, and held what the report called the first prayer on the road in 30 years. They called for full security and civil control of the road and for it to be reopened, which would cut the journey from Beit El to western Binyamin from about an hour to ten minutes. The organisers said the walk was the first step of a wider campaign.

items.headline: A further seizure order in Area A inside the city of Jenin
items.summary: WAFA's Hebrew service reported on 6 October, citing the Palestinian Authority's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, that the IDF has issued seizure order No. 33/26 for 741 square metres in the al-Jabriyat neighbourhood of Jenin, in Area A. The order was signed on 5 October as immediate and urgent on grounds of military need, is valid for 60 days, and covers a narrow strip along a road route. It adjoins and partly overlaps an earlier order of 7 May 2026 for 7.247 dunams and extends the seized corridor eastward.

items.headline: Paving begins on the Homesh–Sa-Nur road in northern Samaria
items.summary: Arutz 7 reported on 6 October that, after six months of earthworks, paving had begun on the new road between Homesh and Sa-Nur, which bypasses the Palestinian village of Silat al-Dhahr. The road is meant to give safe, continuous travel between the re-established communities of northern Samaria. The head of the Samaria Regional Council, Yossi Dagan, said that eight communities have already been established in northern Samaria and that eleven more are to follow, nineteen in place of the four evacuated in 2005.

items.headline: First Sabbath of the olive harvest: a youth from Givat Tidhar is struck on the head
items.summary: On 10 October hundreds of Arabs from Deir Abu Mash'al, with foreign and far-left activists, some of them masked and carrying clubs, came up towards Givat Tidhar in Wadi Zarqa, western Binyamin, under the pretext of picking olives. Residents held back the crowd until the troops arrived; a youth from the hilltop was struck on the head and taken to Assaf Harofeh hospital, conscious. The Palestinian Red Crescent said nine Palestinians were injured at Deir Abu Mash'al, and four masked foreign activists taken to the Modi'in Illit police station elsewhere were later released without explanation.

items.headline: Twenty-three attacks on Israelis in two days, most under cover of the harvest
items.summary: The volunteer rescue network Hatzalah Judea and Samaria Without Borders listed 23 attacks on Israelis in Judea and Samaria on 9 and 10 October, which it said had largely gone unreported in the national media. They included stone-throwing near Or Yedidya that lightly injured a security officer, a vehicle set on fire by Arabs from Talfit, shepherds attacked or beaten near Ateret, Rachelim, al-Mughayyir and Osarin, and an attempt to seize a resident's weapon at the Kela David farm near Neve Tzuf. The booby-trapped PLO flag found on 9 October on Mount Hazor was destroyed in a controlled explosion on Saturday.
items.source: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria Without Borders

items.headline: Binyamin Brigade ends week-long operation; house of Netanel Shukron's murderer destroyed
items.summary: The IDF Binyamin Brigade and the Border Police of Judea and Samaria completed a week-long operation in five villages, searching more than 600 locations, seizing weapons and incitement material, and arresting wanted men, among them suspects in the transfer of terror funds. The forces destroyed the house of the Hamas operative from Biddu who murdered Netanel Shukron at the Ein Ria spring near Neve Tzuf before Yom Kippur. During the same week dozens of people who had expressed support for the massacre of 7 October were arrested across Judea and Samaria.

items.headline: Har Bracha widow asks the army to destroy the monument to her husband's murderer
items.summary: Lea Ziv-Parag, the widow of Yaakov Parag, who was murdered in December 1988 while guarding the lands of Har Bracha, has written to the head of Central Command, Major General Avi Bluth, asking the army to remove a monument to his murderer, Hamdan al-Najjar, which the family says stands near the place of the murder. The request follows the army's current campaign to remove monuments to terrorists in Judea and Samaria. MK Zvi Sukkot, chairman of the Knesset subcommittee on Judea and Samaria, joined the request and asked the IDF to act urgently.

items.headline: Eastern Binyamin: a sixteenth poisoning attack and two dummy bombs with PLO flags
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that infiltrators from al-Mughayyir again scattered poisoned dates on the grazing land of the Metzudat David farm during the night, and four goats died; he counted it as the sixteenth poisoning attack in the area of the Allon Road, and the Hatzalah volunteer network records 19 since the start of the year. On the same day the police announced that two dummy bombs with PLO flags attached had been found in Binyamin over the weekend, one near Mount Hazor and one near the Metzudat David farm. Elchanan Groner wrote that the placing of dummy bombs in eastern Binyamin has increased sharply in recent months, and that several real ones have already been found.

items.headline: Shin Bet arrests two settlement security officers in Samaria
items.summary: Arutz 7 reported that two security men living in Samaria, a community's military security coordinator and a security officer, were arrested at five in the morning on suspicion of involvement in violence against Palestinians near Aqraba about a month ago; they were barred from meeting a lawyer, and a gag order covers the case. The Petah Tikva Magistrate's Court extended their detention by four days, not the twelve days that the Shin Bet and the police had requested. The head of the Samaria Regional Council, Yossi Dagan, and the security coordinators of the Samaria Brigade protested against the manner of the arrests.

items.headline: Kafr Ana: the access road is blocked again, and no one is arrested
items.summary: Elisha Yered published video showing rioters from Ein Yabrud again blocking the access road to the Kafr Ana settlement point in Binyamin, under cover of the olive harvest, and reported that none of them was arrested. Kafr Ana stands on a hill between Ofra and Beit El and, according to Mr. Yered, connects the two communities. A public appeal raised 12,000 shekels within a day to pave a proper access road to the site before the winter.

items.headline: Kerem Binyamin farm: shepherd's finger broken; two attackers arrested in Burham
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported that one of the shepherds attacked on Saturday near the Kerem Binyamin farm by Ateret went to hospital that night, where examinations found a broken finger and a probable sprain in the leg. The farm said that dozens of rioters took part and that no army or police force came to the site for almost a day. Later on 11 October IDF forces arrested two of the attackers in the village of Burham.

items.headline: Regavim: long-dead people are counted in Palestinian population censuses
items.summary: Regavim published an interview given to Channel 14 by Roi Drucker, its coordinator for Judea and Samaria, on the contradictory and unclear figures for the Palestinian population there. Regavim summarised the finding by saying that in the Palestinian Authority people who died long ago are counted in the censuses. The interview also explains why the true size of that population matters to Israel.

items.headline: High Court asks the state for a timetable for residents' return to the northern Samaria camps
items.summary: Olam Katan reported that Supreme Court President Yitzhak Amit and Justices Alex Stein and Khaled Kabub ordered the state to set out a timetable for the steps that would let residents return to the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps, and to examine whether those steps can be accelerated. The petition was filed by the Association for Civil Rights in Israel and six Palestinian petitioners. The IDF continues to operate in all three camps, and Olam Katan described the decision as judicial interference in the campaign against the terror centres of northern Samaria.

items.headline: Harvest orders: more land under IDF coordination, less closed to Israelis
items.summary: Peace Now reported that the head of Central Command has signed the harvest orders for 2026: Palestinians may enter about 88,300 dunams of olive groves only with prior coordination with the IDF, about 30 percent more than the 68,800 dunams of 2025 (a dunam is 1,000 square metres). The area closed to Israelis during the harvest has fallen from about 10,700 dunams in 2025 to 6,890 dunams this year. According to Peace Now, the coordination zones are drawn to protect new farms and hilltop communities and cover close to 20 percent of the olive groves in Judea and Samaria.

items.headline: Katz answers the High Court: the IDF will remain in the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps
items.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz stated on 12 October, after the High Court asked for a timetable for the return of residents, that the IDF will stay in the three northern Samaria camps with a permanent hold. He said that the 40,000 residents were evacuated, the terrorists killed and the terror infrastructure destroyed, and that terror in Judea and Samaria has fallen by 80 percent. He said that the matter is operational and not legal, that it is not the business of the High Court, and that he would not compromise even if special legislation were required.

items.headline: Youth from the Michtam LeDavid farm beaten during a harvest action by left-wing activists
items.summary: On 12 October a group from the organisation Looking the Occupation in the Eye, with foreign activists and media crews, came to the Michtam LeDavid farm near Duma after the IDF sent it away from Burin. According to the police complaint, after an Arab woman pushed a youth from the farm in front of the cameras, about three activists beat him with fists, kicks and a stick and took his telephone, which was later found hidden in an activist's harvest sheet. The police detained two activists and opened an investigation; Commanders for Israel's Security claimed the reverse, that Jewish youths had attacked Palestinian women.

items.headline: Metzudat David farm owner: the shepherd was giving the goats an antidote, not poison
items.summary: After a video spread showing the farm's shepherd giving the goats liquid from a bottle, left-wing activists, among them MK Ofer Cassif, claimed that the farm was poisoning its own flock to blame the Arabs. The owner, Evyatar Caro, told Olam Katan that the bottle held an antidote, that about 25 of his roughly 100 goats have died of poisoning in the past year, and that a cell from al-Mughayyir has poisoned the flock about 15 times. Elisha Yered also reported that a WhatsApp channel in Deir Dibwan published a shepherd's location together with the red inverted triangle that Hamas used to mark targets.

items.headline: Shaare Zedek nurses were driven to the communities by a family with terror links
items.summary: Hakol Hayehudi found that Ibrahim Shalabi, a Beit Hanina taxi driver killed in a road accident at the Michmas junction on 9 October, had been driving Shaare Zedek nurses home to communities in Judea and Samaria. His twin brother, Muhammad, was recently indicted for planning suicide bombings, and another brother was arrested after aiming a weapon from his balcony; the drivers enter the communities without restriction, sometimes late at night. Shaare Zedek said that the drivers work for a transport company that is responsible for the checks, and the police said that they are not the body responsible for such approvals.

items.headline: IDF to allow Arab harvesters inside the fences of Neve Daniel and near Kiryat Arba homes
items.summary: Olam Katan reported that the IDF intends to let Arabs from the surrounding villages harvest olives on land inside the fences of Neve Daniel in Gush Etzion, and residents gathered at the gate and said that they would block the entry with their bodies. A resident of the Orot Netanel neighbourhood beside Kiryat Arba wrote that the IDF had approved a harvest about 30 metres from the houses, with notice given only the evening before. In the evening of 12 October dozens of Arabs threw stones during the harvest at Kafr Malik in Binyamin, and the army arrested two of them.

items.headline: Border Police evacuate and demolish Shirat Zion and Givat Tidhar
items.summary: During the night of 11 to 12 October hundreds of Border Police officers evacuated the hill of Shirat Zion in Samaria, founded about a year ago in memory of Shir Hajaj; the family there was given about fifteen minutes to pack, and six structures were destroyed. At Givat Tidhar in western Binyamin, where a youth was struck on the head on 10 October, the forces demolished the Gozlan family's home, the young men's house, the small synagogue, the sheep pen and the kitchen. Settlers criticised the timing in the middle of the harvest, saying that it weakens the Jewish presence on the ground.

items.headline: Appeal filed for the two Samaria security men held by the Shin Bet
items.summary: On the morning of 12 October lawyers Nati Rom and Asaf Gonen of Honenu filed an urgent appeal to cancel or shorten the detention of the military security coordinator and the security officer arrested on 11 October, and to lift the order barring them from meeting their lawyers. MK Zvi Sukkot wrote to the head of the Shin Bet that the two are held under conditions harsher than those applied to heads of crime families. No decision on the appeal had been reported when the letter was written.

items.headline: Arik Ascherman indicted for assaulting a minor to take his donkey
items.summary: Following an application by Honenu, the police have filed an indictment against the left-wing activist Arik Ascherman on three counts of assault for the purpose of theft. According to the indictment, in early June 2026 he came with activists to grazing land in eastern Binyamin and tried again and again to pull a donkey away from a minor by force. Arutz 7 reported in June that the boy was 12 years old and had filed a complaint with the police.

items.headline: David Friedman rejects the 60 Minutes report on Jewish farms in Judea and Samaria
items.summary: CBS's 60 Minutes broadcast on 11 October a report by Lesley Stahl that argued that Jewish sheep farms in Judea and Samaria are used to take land and drive Palestinians from it. The former United States ambassador David Friedman called it "an embarrassing joke" for anyone who lives the real challenges on the ground, and said that Palestinian terror is a far graver threat than isolated incidents attributed to residents. He concluded that the only solution is to install a true sovereign, and that Israel is the only candidate.

items.headline: Dozens of illegal Bedouin structures demolished near Rahat
items.summary: On 12 October the Land Enforcement Authority, with the Yoav police unit, demolished dozens of illegal structures in the Abu Wadi clan's Dahiya compound south of Beit Kama, near Rahat, one of the largest illegal clusters in the scattered Bedouin settlement area. The court had rejected the residents' claims and ruled that the compound was an invasion of state land. Yehuda Kapach of Regavim said that aerial photographs showed that the land was occupied only from the 1990s, and that the occupants have refused offers of developed plots and legal housing in Rahat.

items.headline: Wallerstein Road: the IDF has begun preparations to reopen Route 463
items.summary: In an exclusive interview with Olam Katan, published on 8 October, Israel Ganz, head of the Binyamin Regional Council and of the Yesha Council, said that Wallerstein Road (Route 463) is joining the Ma'ozim axis plan and that the IDF has begun work toward its official opening to Israeli traffic. The road runs from Nili Junction in the west to Road 466 near Al-Bireh in the east; it was closed to Israelis during the Second Intifada, and the drive between the Talmonim bloc and the Beit El area lengthened from about a quarter of an hour to about an hour. Mr. Ganz said that the army must shift bases and equipment, that the work is already budgeted, that legal preparations are under way, and that the process is a matter of several months; the principal decision has been taken, but the road is not yet open for routine Israeli travel.

items.headline: Northern Samaria: Islamic Jihad cell planning an attack is arrested
items.summary: Maariv reported on the morning of 13 October that IDF forces of the Manashe Brigade, directed by the Shin Bet, completed two arrests during the week in the villages of Qabatiya and Arraba, in which four operatives of Islamic Jihad who were planning an attack in northern Samaria were detained. In a separate operation in the Beit Rima area of the Binyamin Brigade, fighters of the Duvdevan unit arrested a wanted man suspected of trafficking in weapons. Channel 14, citing the IDF Spokesperson, reported that the detainees were transferred for further interrogation and that there were no casualties among Israeli forces.

items.headline: Samaria security coordinators block Tapuah Junction over the Shin Bet arrests
items.summary: Hakol Hayehudi reported on 13 October that military security coordinators from Samaria communities blocked Tapuah Junction with their security vehicles in protest at the detention of two Samaria security men arrested by the Shin Bet at the start of the week, under a gag order and initially barred from meeting their lawyers. The slogan of the protest was "A ravshatz is not a terrorist." Adv. Nati Rom of Honenu, who met the detainees after the court accepted the appeal against the meeting ban, said they were being held in harsh conditions in a Shin Bet facility, in a small crowded cell without sunlight and with their eyes covered.

items.headline: Chief of Staff: the potential for escalation has risen; Division 98 brought into Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir held a situation assessment and operational review at Central Command on 14 October and approved plans for continued operations in Judea and Samaria. He said that because of the many warnings in all arenas the potential for escalation has risen, that forces in all sectors have been reinforced and readiness raised, and that Division 98 has been brought into the area to strengthen security; the army is preparing for an attempt to surprise it. Present were Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, the commanders of the Judea and Samaria Division (Brig. Gen. Kobi Heller), Division 98 (Brig. Gen. Meni Liberty) and Division 96 (Brig. Gen. Oren Simcha), and Shin Bet and Border Police commanders; the same report appeared in Kipa and Olam Katan.

items.headline: Ariel: a vehicle fleeing a checkpoint hits a guard; suspects arrested
items.summary: IDF forces and Judea and Samaria District police operated near Ariel on 14 October after a vehicle whose driver did not obey a guard at a guard post struck him and fled; the guard fired at the vehicle. Security forces arrested several suspects and continued searches and roadblocks. Channel 14 reported that the vehicle had been seen circling Ariel Square several times over two days and was seen entering Salfit, and said at first that no injuries were known; the guard's condition was not published.

items.headline: Six attacks on Israelis in Samaria and Binyamin in one day
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria war room (JSR) listed six incidents on 14 October, four in Samaria and two in Binyamin, all without injuries. They included stones thrown by about 15 olive pickers at an Israeli car on the quarry road south of Deir Abu Mash'al (a window was damaged), stones at a car on Route 60 about 200 meters south of the Givat Assaf junction, stones thrown by dozens of Arabs north of Magen Yehuda and at three residents near Emmanuel, and two Arabs who attacked a shepherd with clubs south of Khirbet a-Tawil. The list also counted the suspected ramming near the Salfit junction; apart from that event, these details have not been confirmed by a second source.

items.headline: Attempt to set fire to Givat Gefen Ami, next to Karmei Tzur
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported on 14 October that Arabs from the village of Beit Ummar tried to set fire to Givat Gefen Ami, a hilltop community next to Karmei Tzur in Gush Etzion, and then fled. Residents put the fire out before it reached nearby trees. Arutz 7 reported a similar arson at the same hill from Beit Ummar in August 2025; no arrests have been reported this time.

items.headline: IDF and Shin Bet raid Addameer in Ramallah and a Hamas charity in Yatta; five arrested
items.summary: The IDF and the Shin Bet said they raided the Ramallah offices of Addameer, which Israel declared a terrorist organization in 2021, on Tuesday 13 October, and in recent weeks the offices of the Islamic Society for Orphan Care in Yatta, which they described as an economic and organizational arm of Hamas. Five activists of Hamas and the Popular Front were arrested, and computers, documents and checkbooks bearing marks of declared Hamas funds were seized. According to the statement, some of the terrorists employed by Addameer took part in the August 2019 bombing at Ein Bubin (Dani's Spring) in which Rina Shnerb was murdered.

items.headline: Foreign activist who supports Addameer is arrested near Mitzpe Yair and sent for deportation
items.summary: Judea and Samaria District police arrested a foreign activist on the night of 13 October after a friction incident some days earlier near Mitzpe Yair in the south Hebron hills. Police said she is a founder of the student group MAC, came to intern at Addameer, and had been photographed abroad in a shirt showing Prime Minister Netanyahu with a sniper's crosshairs on his head; she was sent to a Population Authority hearing before deportation. District commander Maj. Gen. Moshe Pinchi said that since the start of 2026, 160 foreign activists have been refused entry and more than 60 deported.

items.headline: IDF destroys the "martyrs" monument in the Jalazone camp near Beit El
items.summary: IDF forces destroyed the "martyrs" monument in the Jalazone refugee camp in the Ramallah district on 14 October; video of the demolition was published by Palestinian outlets. Elisha Yered posted a picture of children from the camp, which lies next to Beit El, standing on the ruins of the monument. The demolition follows the orders signed this month to remove monuments that glorify terrorists.

items.headline: One of the two Samaria security men held by the Shin Bet is released to house arrest
items.summary: One of the two Samaria security men arrested by the Shin Bet at the start of the week was released to house arrest on 13 October, his lawyer, Adv. Asaf Gonen of Honenu, confirmed. On 14 October the wife of the second detainee, whose name is under a gag order, wrote to Shin Bet chief David Zini asking that he be moved from the Shin Bet facility to a regular detention facility. Adv. Nati Rom of Honenu said the detainee is held in a cell of two meters by two meters without daylight.

items.headline: Council heads of Judea and Samaria call for official communities in Areas A and B
items.summary: In a video campaign led by the HaBayta Forum before the elections, Yesha Council chairman and Binyamin council head Israel Ganz, Samaria council head Yossi Dagan, Gush Etzion council head Yaron Rosenthal, Hebron Hills council head Eliram Azulai and Kedumim council head Uziel Vatik called on the government to establish communities and roads in the open land of Areas A and B. Rosenthal cited the government decision that transferred authority in the agreed nature reserve in eastern Gush Etzion from the Palestinian Authority to Israel. Elisha Yered wrote that close to thirty settlement points have been set up in Areas A and B in the last three years; that figure has not been confirmed by a second source.

items.headline: HaShomer HaChadash: a yeshiva north of Jericho within three weeks, and a Haredi city beside it
items.summary: Yoel Zilberman, founder and director of HaShomer HaChadash, told the Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth conference on 13 October that within three weeks a first yeshiva will be set up at a point called Mahane Sadeh, north of Jericho, next to which a new Haredi city named Ir HaTmarim is to be built. He said the organization set up the first new moshav in Israel in twenty years a month ago, and aims at 150 new communities along the borders. Behadrei Haredim reported that the planned city received a community code from the Interior Ministry in February 2026; that detail has not been checked further.

items.headline: Palestinian report: new outposts since 2023 control about 1.07 million dunams
items.summary: A joint statement by the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics and the Environment Quality Authority, issued on 14 October, said that 185 new outposts were set up in Judea and Samaria between 2023 and 2025, about 130 of them shepherding outposts and hilltop sites, holding about 1.07 million dunams, or about 18 percent of the area; about 300,000 dunams were added in 2025 alone. It counted 231 shepherding outposts among about 400 outposts, about 790,000 Israelis living in 170 communities and 400 outposts at the end of July 2026, and Israeli control of 42 percent of the area, 71 percent of Area C and about 91 percent of the Jordan Valley. It also said that 118 Palestinian herding communities left their areas between 2023 and 2025; these are Palestinian Authority figures and have not been checked against Israeli data.
items.source: PLO National Bureau for Defending the Land (citing PCBS)

items.headline: Planning council agenda: 168 homes at Mitzpe Shalem and 275 at Givat Zeev
items.summary: Peace Now's list of plans brought to the Higher Planning Council shows two plans on the agenda for 14 October: final approval (validation) of plan 607/8 for 168 housing units at Mitzpe Shalem, and deposit of plan 215/2/47 for 275 housing units at Givat Zeev. Peace Now counts 10,982 housing units advanced in 2026 including these plans. The result of the meeting has not yet been published.

items.headline: Court orders the second Samaria security man held by the Shin Bet moved to house arrest
items.summary: On 15 October, Magistrate's Court Judge Dan Baumann rejected the prosecution's request to extend by eight days the detention of the Samaria security coordinator held by the Shin Bet, and ordered him released to house arrest for seven days. The prosecution said it would ask to delay the order so it can appeal, so his release had not yet taken place when the reports were published. His lawyer, Adv. Nati Rom of Honenu, said he was held in harsh solitary conditions. Samaria council head Yossi Dagan welcomed the decision. Reported by Channel 14, Arutz 7 and Hadashot 04.

items.headline: Settlers begin earthworks at the former Sanur army camp, evacuated in 2005
items.summary: Palestinian outlets reported that on the morning of 15 October a group of Israelis with a bulldozer began leveling land inside the former Sanur military camp south of Jenin, beside the road between Jaba' and Sanur. Israel evacuated the camp in the 2005 disengagement. The report comes from WAFA and was repeated by Al-Ayyam's Raya and other Palestinian outlets. No Israeli source or official response has been found, so the details are unconfirmed by Israeli sources.

items.headline: New herding outpost reported in Wadi Yasuf, east of Salfit
items.summary: WAFA and Sada News reported that on 15 October Israelis set up tents for a new herding outpost in the Wadi Yasuf area, east of Salfit and west of the village of Yasuf. Local Palestinian officials said it would limit residents' access to their land. Only Palestinian outlets have reported it; the exact location and whether the outpost is still in place are unconfirmed.

items.headline: Yesha Council opens a situation room to record friction incidents in real time
items.summary: A new situation room will document clashes between Israelis and Arabs in Judea and Samaria as they happen during the olive harvest, and issue reports in Hebrew and English, according to i24NEWS and to journalist Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251). Its stated aim is to publicize Arab attacks on Jews while not hiding incidents in the other direction, and it will operate into the Sabbath. That the Yesha Council runs it is reported by i24NEWS only and is unconfirmed.

items.headline: PA commission counts 219 incidents by Israelis in the first 12 days of October
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said, in a count WAFA called preliminary, that it recorded 219 incidents by Israeli civilians from 1 to 12 October, 136 of them tied to the olive harvest: 92 attacks on pickers or denial of access to land, and 45 cases of stolen crops or damaged trees.
