The petition argues that the 'illegality' of many buildings is 'a temporary situation, dependent on government decisions,' and that demolitions now 'decide in advance what the next government may decide otherwise.' Ra'am accuses National Security Minister Ben Gvir of using demolitions for his campaign. According to al-Qabas, the petition follows the demolition of more than 70 homes and a mosque in Dhahiya, north of Rahat, and demolition orders served in az-Zayadna, and the court has asked the attorney general to respond by Tuesday. Ben Gvir told Channel 14 that the Israel Land Authority, the Green Patrol, the enforcement authority and police units 'demolish all year... 24/6. Whoever builds illegally will have his house demolished.' Background: the Khamaisi Plan backgrounder on this site explains the Arab and Bedouin planning program behind such claims.

items.headline: Triangle: Regavim finds that farmland west of Taybeh beside Moshav Azriel and Route 6 has become 17 illegal villa compounds, with gunfire reaching the moshav
items.summary: Regavim reports that farmland on the western edge of Taybeh, a few meters from the fence of Moshav Azriel and beside Route 6, has become a residential compound of 17 illegal plots, some with large villas, lawns and swimming pools. In 2016 it warned about one building there that far exceeded a permit for a 25-square-meter farm structure. The city of Taybeh replied then that enforcement had begun and the building would be demolished, and the mayor promised in writing to act. That building is now a villa with a pool. The city's representative, Walid Tibi, now says the building dates from 2016 and has been handled by district enforcement inspectors. Regavim says the area has also become a center of constant gunfire, and that bullets have reached homes and yards in Azriel. Its northern director, Neria Shapira, says there is 'a direct link between the loss of governance and control on the ground and violence and terror.' Regavim renewed the warning on X on Wednesday. The report appeared in Olam Katan on 15 October; the account of bullets reaching homes comes from Regavim and residents and has not been confirmed by police.

items.headline: Jerusalem: a plan for 122 homes in towers of up to 12 stories at the Shepherd Hotel site in Shimon HaTzaddik
items.summary: A plan called 'Beit Ramban' proposes 122 apartments, in buildings of up to 12 stories and 47 meters, on about 5.8 dunams at 16 Mount of Olives Road. This is the Shepherd Hotel compound, also known as the Mufti's house, in the Sheikh Jarrah–Shimon HaTzaddik neighborhood. The plan also includes commerce, education and religious space and an underground parking garage, and it preserves the original 1930s building (mynet Jerusalem, from the plan documents of August 2026). The house was built for Haj Amin al-Husseini, the Mufti who collaborated with Nazi Germany. It was bought in 1985 by a company owned by Irving Moskowitz, and building there caused a clash with the Obama administration in 2009 and 2011. The PA's Jerusalem governorate, quoted by WAFA, calls it a 'settlement plan.' The plan has not been approved; the date of its first hearing could not be confirmed.

items.headline: Halutzei HaBashan welcomes reports of an IDF post on Mount Bashan (Jabal al-Druze) in southern Syria; the IDF has not confirmed it, and a Druze source denies it
items.summary: On Wednesday morning the Halutzei HaBashan (Bashan Pioneers) movement posted on X that there are 'reports of an IDF post being set up on Mount Bashan, deep in the historic region.' It called this 'a welcome and significant step to strengthen Israel's hold on the Bashan,' and added that long-term security 'also requires civilian settlement.' Mount Bashan, in this usage, is Jabal al-Druze (also called Jabal al-Arab), the Druze-majority mountain in Syria's Sweida province, about 1,800 meters high. The reports the group refers to began with the Syrian site Syria 360 on Oct. 17. Citing an unnamed local source, it said dozens of Israeli military helicopters had carried weapons and advanced equipment to the summit over 72 hours, to prepare a base for intelligence, surveillance and early warning, possibly with radar, and that Israeli soldiers, most of them Israeli Druze, had surveyed the site. i24NEWS in Arabic repeated the report on Oct. 20 and noted that there is no official confirmation or independent evidence. Other accounts placed a planned base on Tal Qulaib in southeastern Sweida. On Oct. 22 Asharq Al-Awsat quoted a Druze source opposed to Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri, who said residents of al-Kafr, on the slopes of Tal Qulaib, see 'no signs of a base being established.' Syrian journalist Omar al-Hariri called the reports fake, though he said Israeli helicopter flights carrying supplies and aid to Sweida are not new. The IDF has made no statement, and the post is unconfirmed. What came before: the IDF moved into the buffer zone and parts of southern Syria in December 2024, after the Assad regime fell. Israel says it is there to keep Hezbollah, Iranian proxies and jihadist groups away from the Golan, and to protect the Druze; in July 2025 the IDF struck Syrian regime forces in Sweida to stop attacks on the Druze there. Halutzei HaBashan was founded in April 2025 by Prof. Amos Azaria of Ariel University. It calls for Jewish settlement in southern Syria, and its activists have crossed the border many times, with the IDF removing them and condemning the crossings as a danger to soldiers (Ynet).
items.source: Halutzei HaBashan on X; i24NEWS (Arabic), citing Syria 360; Asharq Al-Awsat; Ynet

items.headline: The PA claims 23 'harvest attacks'; none confirmed by the IDF or police
items.summary: The PA claims 23 'harvest attacks' on Wednesday. Its Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, quoted by WAFA, counted 23 incidents against farmers and harvesters between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m., ten of them in the Nablus district. Among its claims: a farmer was shot in the hand at Usarin, armed settlers fired at pickers at Birin east of Hebron, settlers attacked pickers near the school in Jalud before troops came and beat the farmers, olives were taken at Beit Furik, and land was set on fire at Burqa. The commission also counts the closures at Deir Jarir and Turmus Ayya and the detentions at Nahalin, among them Brad Lander, as attacks, and says farmers at Deir Abu Da'if east of Jenin were made to leave even though their harvest had been coordinated. None of these claims has been confirmed by the IDF or police, and the commission does not separate violence from closures and arrests.
items.source: WAFA (Hebrew), quoting the PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission

items.headline: Geva Shomron: families from the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva will found a new community on the old Paratroopers training base by Sa-Nur, a site emptied in the 2005 disengagement
items.summary: A founding group of graduates of the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva, led by Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira and Rabbi Ben Zion Algazi, is to move onto the ground and found a new community, Geva Shomron, on the site of the former Paratroopers Brigade training base next to Sa-Nur in northern Samaria (Arutz 7; Olam Katan). Sa-Nur was evacuated in the 2005 disengagement. Dozens of families toured the site with Samaria Council head Yossi Dagan and Rabbi Shapira (Arutz 7). The community is part of the 'Hitchabrut' (connection) plan of the Samaria Council, Amana and the Settlement Division for 19 new communities in northern Samaria, and follows cabinet and government decisions led by Defense Minister Israel Katz and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich (Arutz 7; Olam Katan). Olam Katan adds that a branch of the yeshiva will be set up at the site. Rabbi Shapira: 'For thousands of years we waited to get here... we have been given a second chance for northern Samaria, and we are not missing it.' Dagan: 'We want to fix the disengagement and the Oslo Accords,' naming Noa and the renewed Homesh as the other new communities that, with Geva Shomron, connect northern Samaria to the Jordan Valley. A move-in date and the number of families committed have not been published. Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) also reported it on X.
items.source: Arutz 7; Olam Katan; Hadashot 0404; Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

places.name: Geva Shomron
places.note: approximate: shown at the Sa-Nur point; the former base has no map entry of its own

items.headline: Gun licenses: residents of 11 Samaria communities, among them Homesh, Ganim and Kadim, can now apply for private firearms
items.summary: On Thursday the National Security Ministry added 11 communities in Samaria to the list of places whose residents may apply for a private gun license on the basis of where they live, subject to the usual criteria: Asif, Ganim, Har Bazak, Homesh, Kadim, Shira, Havat Yair (Lehi), Maoz Tzvi (Maoz), Havat Gilad (Nezer Shomron), Sahlav and Eival (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Hadashot 0404). Several are the new communities of northern Samaria. Minister Itamar Ben Gvir: 'We are extending this reform to the new communities we established in Samaria... A gun in the right hands saves lives.' Yossi Dagan called Samaria 'the line of defense of the whole State of Israel' and said many residents are combat veterans and reservists.

items.headline: Neot Harim: Dvir Shnerb, wounded in the 2019 Ein Dani spring attack that killed his sister Rina, is among the first 14 families
items.summary: Seven years after the bombing at the Ein Dani spring, where Rina Shnerb was murdered and her brother Dvir and father Rabbi Eitan Shnerb were wounded, Dvir and his wife, an IDF officer, have moved from south Tel Aviv to the new community of Neot Harim, between Neve Tzuf and Nahliel (Arutz 7). At the founding ceremony Rabbi Shnerb recalled asking Prime Minister Netanyahu, on his shiva visit, to found a new community near where his daughter was killed. Dvir: 'To come back here not from a place of pain, but to build a community, a family and a home, is hard to put into words.' Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) also reported it. Neot Harim's founding was the lead story on Thursday.

items.headline: JSR's Thursday: stones at shepherds near Kfar Tapuach and Orot farm, and at drivers on Route 458, near Yitzhar, on the Dakota road and by al-Mughayyir
items.summary: The JSR situation room reported on Thursday (JSR's own account): Arabs and far-left Israeli activists armed with clubs threw stones at Jewish shepherds about a kilometer west of Kfar Tapuach's western hill, with no injuries; stones from a passing car hit an Israeli vehicle on Route 458 at the Malachei HaShalom junction, damaging the windshield; an attempted attack on a Jewish shepherd at the Orot farm in Gush Etzion; about 20 Arabs stoned a resident between the Avnei Elad neighborhood and the village of Hajjah; stones at residents on the Dakota road from the direction of Khirbet Safa; 20 Arabs attacked an Israeli vehicle near al-Mughayyir; and stones about 100 meters west of the small Yitzhar junction, damaging a windshield. No injuries were reported in any of them. Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) repeated the list in his daily summary; none of the incidents was confirmed by the IDF or police by Friday morning. JSR posted no new report on its website, where the latest is from 17 October.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X); Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

items.headline: JSR: a video on PA social media shows dozens from Abu Falah stoning Jewish shepherds under cover of the harvest, with foreign journalists alongside
items.summary: JSR says a video circulating on Palestinian social media shows dozens of men from Abu Falah, in Binyamin, throwing stones at Jewish shepherds 'under cover of the olive harvest,' accompanied by foreign journalists and photographers. Abu Falah is where photographer Heidi Levine was assaulted; in Wednesday's hearing the judge said the one video of that assault showed it 'in the middle of a much larger event of massive stone-throwing,' and police told the court the stones were thrown by Palestinians. The desk has not seen the video itself, and its date is not confirmed.

items.headline: Homesh: the IDF says Thursday's shooting was not a terror attack
items.summary: On Thursday evening the IDF received a report of gunfire near Homesh and sent forces to search for gunmen; no one was hurt (Walla; Channel 14). A preliminary inquiry found that an Israeli civilian apparently spotted an armed suspect and heard shots, and fired toward the source; the IDF says it was not a terror attack (Srugim; Maariv). Army Radio reported that the shooting was apparently Palestinian, in a clan feud, with no Israelis involved (via Srugim).

items.headline: Duvdevan drills a day of simultaneous attacks around the new communities of northern Samaria and Ariel
items.summary: Troops of the Duvdevan unit finished a 24-hour drill around the new communities in northern Samaria and in Ariel, practicing several emergencies at once inside communities, along roads and in villages (Arutz 7, with IDF video). A company commander told Arutz 7 the aim was to make sure every soldier and commander can act under pressure when 'we have to deal with several events in parallel,' and that the unit is 'ready for any development.'

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian state TV says the IDF blew up an empty house in Hamidiyah and fired toward farmland at Kudna, in Quneitra
items.summary: Anadolu, citing Syria's state broadcaster Alikhbariah, reports that on Thursday Israeli forces demolished an abandoned house in Hamidiyah in northern Quneitra, and that troops at western Tal al-Ahmar fired machine guns toward farmland around Kudna, with no casualties reported. The IDF has not commented, and the reports are unconfirmed. Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new after Wednesday's Mount Bashan post.

items.headline: Police detain 11 foreign activists who stayed in a closed military zone during a harvest
items.summary: Police arrested 11 foreign activists on Thursday after they took part in a Palestinian olive harvest. Police say they were in a closed military zone and refused to leave despite warnings from IDF soldiers (Haaretz). The location was not given in the part of the report the desk could read.

items.headline: Two soldiers killed as Hebron gunmen open fire at Route 35 checkpoint
items.summary: Two Hamas-affiliated men from Hebron, both 27, drove up in a car with yellow Israeli plates (JPost says an off-road vehicle no longer licensed for the road) and opened fire at a temporary checkpoint at the Hebron exit near Yehuda Junction on Route 35, at about 7:15 Friday morning. Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, of Ashkelon, a squad commander, and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, of Hod Hasharon, both of the Home Front Command's new Ari Battalion on its first Judea and Samaria deployment, were killed; three soldiers were lightly hurt. After a gunbattle of more than 20 minutes, the battalion's deputy commander, a company commander and a 101st Paratroopers officer flanked and killed the two. They carried an M4, a handgun and a lot of ammunition, and the IDF believes they were heading for a larger attack on civilians on Route 35 or inside Israel. Roytman's funeral is Sunday at 11:00 at the Ashkelon military cemetery. Also reported by INN, Ynetnews, Times of Israel and AP; more detail in Arutz 7.

places.name: Attack site, Route 35 at the Hebron exit (Farsh al-Hawa road)

items.headline: Hebron closed; Netanyahu says the refugee-camp operation model will be applied to the attackers' neighborhood
items.summary: Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir approved a full closure of Hebron and surrounding villages and stepped-up arrests (Arutz 7). At the scene, Netanyahu said Hebron and Halhul are closed, a full closure of Judea and Samaria is being prepared, and the "camps model" will be applied to the neighborhood the gunmen came from: evacuating residents, going house to house, seizing weapons and destroying infrastructure, possibly in other cities too, with faster clearing of illegal building along roads (Arutz 7). Central Command chief Avi Bluth announced a "significant counterterror operation" (Arutz 7). Ben Gvir called at the scene for dismantling the PA and ending shared roads (Arutz 7); Smotrich called for a full campaign to dismantle the PA. The IDF says more than 70 wanted men were arrested in Judea and Samaria last week.

items.headline: Civil Administration razes dozens of illegal structures by the attack site; Smotrich announces four new farms in the south Hebron Hills
items.summary: On Smotrich's direct order, the Civil Administration's enforcement unit demolished dozens of illegal Arab structures next to the attack site before Shabbat. "This is only the beginning… Jewish blood is not cheap," he said. He also announced four new farms in the south Hebron Hills, with residents organizing to move onto them before Shabbat, and said it was agreed with the prime minister and defense minister to map more areas for enforcement. Abu Ali Express places the demolitions in the Farsh al-Hawa area. Also reported by Kikar HaShabbat, Ynet and News1. The exact farm sites were not given.

places.name: Attack site, Route 35 at the Hebron exit (Farsh al-Hawa road)

items.headline: Hikers on ATVs attacked with clubs and stones near Burin on the way to Ein Amsha spring
items.summary: Three hikers riding ATVs to the Ein Amsha spring between Yitzhar and Givat Ronen were attacked with clubs and stones and lightly hurt. A victim told Arutz 7 there were 30 to 40 attackers, Arabs and foreign activists; Elchanan Groner and JSR say dozens came from Burin on off-road vehicles with foreign women activists who filmed, and the ATVs were vandalized. Samaria Council head Yossi Dagan demanded arrests and the deportation of the foreigners. Groner adds that the Shai District commander said the off-road vehicles would be dealt with.

items.headline: About 100 left-wing activists stopped at Hizma on the way to the Mukhmas olive harvest
items.summary: Elisha Yered reports that Binyamin police stopped about 100 far-left activists at the Hizma checkpoint as they headed to Mukhmas, near Sha'ar Binyamin. Elchanan Groner reports the IDF let activists, including Roi Elani, stay in the Shiloh valley. Neither report has been confirmed elsewhere.

items.headline: Yered: soldiers say they may not chase smuggler convoys in the Hebron Hills (unconfirmed)
items.summary: Elisha Yered relays a soldier's message that troops in the Hebron Hills are not allowed to fire at or chase smugglers' vehicles, which Elchanan Groner says cross the Judean Desert in convoys weekly; two weeks ago a smuggler rammed an IDF Humvee and was released within a day (second post). There is no IDF response, and the claim is unverified.

items.headline: Southern Syria: IDF closes roads near al-Rafid; artillery on Hamidiyah outskirts
items.summary: North Press reports Israeli forces with three vehicles moved west of Saida al-Hanout in south Quneitra on Friday and closed roads west of the al-Za'rura farm near al-Rafid after entering with a bulldozer. Anadolu reports artillery fire on the outskirts of Hamidiyah and western Zubayda. No IDF comment.

places.name: Saida (Saida al-Hanout)
places.note: approximate: Nominatim match for Saida in Quneitra

items.headline: Police: AFP photographer at the attack scene is not a suspect
items.summary: Early reports, including from JSR and Elchanan Groner, said AFP photographer Hazem Bader was suspected of knowing about the attack in advance. Police later said he is not a suspect, the IDF told AFP no investigation was underway, and the Foreign Press Association called the reports false (AFP via Al-Monitor, Ynetnews).

places.name: Attack site, Route 35 at the Hebron exit (Farsh al-Hawa road)

items.headline: Itamar security coordinator indicted over shooting at a car in Aqraba
items.summary: Prosecutors indicted Pinchas Shem Tov Ran, the security coordinator of Itamar's Gid'onim ridge, alleging he entered Aqraba with a career soldier, checked IDs without authority and fired at a car, badly wounding an 18-year-old woman. He says a car with no plates sped at them and they had to jump aside. His brother, Maj. Or Yosef Ran, fell at Kfar Aza on 7 October; Honenu represents him. Shai District police apologized for issuing the announcement right after the attack (Elisha Yered).

items.headline: Army operation "Roar of Judah" in western Hebron: about 2,000 residents moved out, 10 arrested
items.summary: The army began an operation called "Roar of Judah" (Sha'agat Yehuda) in Hebron on Friday night, after Friday's Route 35 attack that killed two soldiers. Arutz 7 reports that Duvdevan, Maglan, the Paratroopers, Givati reconnaissance reservists, Border Police and the Judea Brigade are taking part, using Shin Bet intelligence. As of Saturday, about 200 buildings had been searched, no weapons had been found and 10 people had been arrested. The Civil Administration also carried out demolitions at the city's northern entrance. The two attackers, Hamouda and Firas al-Ja'aba, came from Ein Dir Bahha in west Hebron. Ynet says the operation is focused on Deir Bahha and al-Jaldeh, and the army believes about 2,000 residents there belong to the al-Ja'aba clan, which it links to Hamas. According to Channel 14's Hillel Bitton Rosen, Defense Minister Katz said the more than 2,000 people moved out will not return until Hamas's infrastructure there has been dealt with. Abu Ali Express says about 400 families were told to leave with one bag each and that the operation is expected to last several days. The Palestinian figures are similar. WAFA quotes Hebron governor Khaled Dudin saying about 1,500 people (more than 200 families) have been moved out so far and another 2,500 are expected to follow, and that at least 13 people were arrested. According to Ynet, the Hebron mayor said shops, factories and roads were destroyed. Hebron schools are closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Hebron (Ein Dir Bahha / al-Jaldeh)
places.note: City center; the operation is in the western neighborhoods (location approximate)

items.headline: Netanyahu: "a very big surprise" is waiting for the PA
items.summary: In a Friday evening interview with Neve Dromi on i24NEWS, Prime Minister Netanyahu said that "a very big surprise is also waiting for the Palestinian Authority" but did not say what it was. "I don't declare, I act and then say what we did," he said. He said the order in Hebron was to enter the neighborhood the attackers came from, move out its residents, go house to house to collect weapons and destroy "all the terror infrastructure," as was done in the refugee camps. He said a wider operation against what remains of terror in Judea and Samaria would follow, on a scale not seen since the Six-Day War. PA officials responded the next day. WAFA reported that Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh called for international pressure, and Ynet reported that Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa and intelligence chief Majed Faraj made similar calls. Also reported by Al-Quds (Hebrew edition).

items.headline: No Palestinian workers in settlements until Monday, and crossings closed on election day
items.summary: The army spokesman said that from Sunday until Monday, Palestinian workers will not be allowed into settlements in Judea, Samaria and the Jordan Valley, except in industrial zones and some approved places. On election day, Tuesday, the political leadership has approved barring all Palestinian workers across Judea and Samaria, including in industrial zones, and closing all land crossings. These steps add to measures Chief of Staff Zamir ordered earlier, including cancelling soldiers' leave from Thursday and sending reinforcements. The army also said that over the weekend the army, Border Police and Shin Bet went into about 40 villages and about 400 sites, arrested about 40 people suspected of links to Hamas or Islamic Jihad, incitement, rioting or stone-throwing, seized weapons and destroyed memorials to attackers. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society, quoted by WAFA, counted about 70 arrests across the West Bank from Friday to Saturday morning.

items.headline: Hebron Hills council announces 2 new communities and 6 farms after the attack
items.summary: On Saturday night the Hebron Hills Regional Council announced two new communities and six new farms in response to Friday's attack. It said it had the backing of the Defense Ministry's Settlement Administration, the Defense Ministry and Amana. The council named the communities as Meged (between Negohot and Eshkolot) and Nofei Golot (between Otniel and Afka). It named the farms as Mitzpe Tzur near Telem, close to the attack site; Noy, between Karmei Yehuda and Adora; Lev Amit, between Makeda and Adora; Eshel, near Meged; Lemaan Achai, between Otniel and Shima; and Mitzpe Or, between Carmel and the nature reserve in the Judean Desert. Council official Eliram Azoulay is quoted. The names and locations come from the council's own announcement; no government body or other outlet had confirmed them by Sunday morning. In a related story, Arutz 7 reports that more than 100 farm owners signed a letter backing Finance Minister Smotrich.

places.name: Negohot area (Meged and Eshel sites, approximate)

items.headline: Teen hurt as dozens from Sinjil throw stones at shepherds; flock poisoned near al-Mughayyir
items.summary: On Saturday, dozens of people from Sinjil threw stones at shepherds from the Tzur Levavi farm and at a security vehicle, according to the Yesha Council Situation Room (JSR) and Elisha Yered. A teenager was hit in the head. Hatzalah Yosh said the injury was light and he was treated at the scene. That afternoon, sheep in the Or Nachman flock near al-Mughayyir were poisoned. Hatzalah Yosh said at least three sheep were affected and one died. JSR called it the 17th poisoning this year and Hatzalah Yosh counted 20, so the totals do not match. Hatzalah Yosh's weekend list, posted by Elchanan Groner, also records three firebombs near the Psagot fence and a stone attack on a Ma'ale HaTamar farm resident near Adam on Friday night, and stone attacks on shepherds near Duma and west of Kafr Malik on Saturday. In the same area, WAFA says settlers grazed sheep among homes and fields in Yabrud and al-Mughayyir on Saturday.

items.headline: Suspected shooting at Shara farm from a car out of Beit Ur al-Tahta
items.summary: JSR reports suspected shots fired at Shara farm in western Binyamin from a car that came from Beit Ur al-Tahta. No one was hurt. Elchanan Groner notes that the attacker who critically wounded Neria Leiter came from the same village. The army had not commented by Sunday morning, and no other outlet had reported the incident.

items.headline: Arrests in Burin after the attack on hikers, including the man filmed with a tree trunk
items.summary: On Saturday the army arrested several people in Burin, including the man seen on video hitting people with a tree trunk during Friday's attack on hikers (reported in the 24 October edition). A memorial to attackers was also torn down. Later, stones were thrown at a bus on the Gilad road. Also reported by Abu Ali Express.

items.headline: Shiloh-area settlers accuse soldiers of burning a youth house; protest at Shiloh Junction
items.summary: Elisha Yered says soldiers under a company commander burned a youth house, with tefillin inside, on the Nahalat HaNavi hill near Esh Kodesh, and that Paratroopers Brigade headquarters (Col. Roi Zweig) was called in. Elchanan Groner posted video of a masked soldier holding a club at a protest at Shiloh Junction. According to Yered, Shiloh Junction was then declared a closed military zone and sponge rounds were fired. MK Limor Son Har-Melech demanded an investigation. All of this comes from settler sources. The army had not responded by Sunday morning.

items.headline: Palestinian reports: car smashed in Sinjil, families leave Khirbet Saruj, iron gates near Jenin
items.summary: Quds News Network says settlers smashed a Palestinian car in Sinjil overnight. It also says families in Khirbet Saruj, west of Jenin, are leaving their homes and animal pens because of threats. WAFA reports that the army put up iron gates at the entrance to Marka and on the Jenin-Nablus road near Arraba. These are Palestinian accounts. Israeli sources had not reported them by Sunday morning.

items.headline: After the Hebron attack, Smotrich orders demolitions of dozens of unpermitted structures near the site and approves four more farms in the southern Hebron Hills
items.summary: Hours after Friday's attack near Hebron that killed two soldiers, Civil Administration enforcement teams began demolishing structures near the scene that the state says were built illegally. Arutz 7 (English) reports that Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is in charge of settlement and civil matters in the Defense Ministry, came to the site and ordered the work. His office said dozens of structures would be demolished in coordination with the army and the Civil Administration. Smotrich said the aim was to "establish deterrence and exact a price," that the work would continue until Shabbat, and that he had agreed with the prime minister and defense minister to map the area and other locations in Judea and Samaria to widen the effort. He also announced approval of four more farms in the southern Hebron Hills and said he would work to approve four new Israeli communities. The same account is in a second Arutz 7 report, and Ynetnews carries the headline "Smotrich announces establishment of 4 outposts." The Palestinian news agency WAFA reported separately that on Friday Israeli forces demolished a three-apartment residential building belonging to Riyad Amrish in northern Hebron and sealed the city's entrances. This is the Palestinian account of the same events. On Saturday, Elisha Yered wrote on X that bulldozers worked in Hebron on both Friday and Saturday (his own report, not confirmed by a second source). At the scene, Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Blut said the soldiers' bravery prevented a severe attack on civilians and announced a significant operation with a closure of Hebron and Halhul (Arutz 7, Hebrew). The council's separate announcement of two communities and six farms in the Hebron Hills is in another item in this edition.

places.name: Hebron (northern outskirts, near the attack site)
places.note: City center from OpenStreetMap; the demolitions were on the northern edge near Judea Junction (approximate, no exact coordinates in the reports)

items.headline: Families from the Ramat Gan yeshiva will found "Geva Shomron" on the former Paratroopers training base next to Sa-Nur, the 19th new community in northern Samaria
items.summary: A group of families, graduates of the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva led by Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira and Rabbi Ben Zion Elgazi, is preparing to move onto the land and found a new community called Geva Shomron, Arutz 7 reports. The site is the former training base of the Paratroopers Brigade, next to Sa-Nur, which was evacuated before the 2005 disengagement. Dozens of families toured the site with Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan. The community is part of the "Reconnection Plan" run by the council, the Amana movement and the Settlement Division, which includes 19 new communities in northern Samaria as part of the council's "a million in Samaria" vision. Dagan said the new communities, together with Noa and a renewed Homesh, "take back the space" and connect northern Samaria to the Jordan Valley. "We received a second chance and we will not miss it," he said. Rabbi Shapira said: "For thousands of years we waited to arrive here." Background: in July the cabinet approved a 19th community in the plan, according to VINnews and Channel 14's English site (both dated 15 July). The Arutz 7 report does not give a date for the move or a permit status, so those are unconfirmed.

places.name: Sa-Nur (reference point for the new community)
places.note: OpenStreetMap point for Sa-Nur; Geva Shomron is planned on the former Paratroopers base next to it (approximate, new site)

items.headline: Netanyahu to Arutz 7: "I prefer to do rather than declare" on sovereignty; says his government advanced 104 new communities and there will be no Palestinian state while he is prime minister
items.summary: In a special interview with Channel 7 (Arutz 7), which also ran in English, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said building in Judea and Samaria is "at a record pace." He said "we recognized, organized or built 104 new communities." Asked whether applying sovereignty is the next step, he said, "Well, it was discussed with the President" (President Trump), without giving a date or a step. He added: "I prefer to do rather than declare, unlike some of my rivals on the right who declare instead of doing." On a Palestinian state he said: "As long as I am prime minister of Israel, there will be no Palestinian state. That is the formula for our destruction," and "we made it impossible." Israel votes on Tuesday, and the interview is aimed in part at voters to his right. The 104 figure is the prime minister's own count. Arutz 7 does not say which communities it includes.

items.headline: Smotrich on Channel 14: "There is no escape from dismantling the Palestinian Authority through a military campaign and cancelling the Oslo Accords"
items.summary: Three days before the election, Religious Zionism leader Bezalel Smotrich said on Channel 14's "HaPatriotim" on Saturday night that Israel must change its policy and act against the Palestinian Authority by military means as well: "There is no escape from dismantling the Palestinian Authority through a military campaign and from canceling the Oslo Accords," Channel 14 reports. On Thursday, Arutz 7 reported that former chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the Yashar party, told a rally in Modi'in that if he joins the next government he will work to abolish the additional minister post in the Defense Ministry that Smotrich holds, bring back administrative detention orders and allow about 60,000 to 70,000 Palestinian workers to enter Israel. He also listed demolition of illegal construction among his steps. Smotrich replied, in his own words, that this would "close the Settlement Directorate we built," return settlers to military rule, "evacuate the farms and communities," and end up with "a Palestinian terror state" (Arutz 7). These are campaign statements by the two politicians. Neither report describes a government plan.

items.headline: Hebron attack debrief: two gunmen from Hebron, first operational deployment for the Ari Battalion squad; police say there is no suspicion the AFP photographer knew in advance
items.summary: According to the IDF's preliminary debrief, reported by Walla and the Jerusalem Post, two gunmen from Hebron came to the Judea Junction area with a large amount of ammunition, an M4 rifle and a handgun. They arrived in a vehicle with Israeli plates to a scrapyard nearby and watched the soldiers first. A squad-level outpost of the Ari Battalion had been set up at the junction two months earlier, and this was the soldiers' first operational assignment. They went out to set up a checkpoint to stop attackers from reaching Routes 35 and 60. Early reports counted five wounded, two critically. Arutz 7 later reported that two soldiers were killed, and the army killed both attackers. Judea and Samaria District Police commander Maj. Gen. Moshe Pinchi ordered investigators to focus on the use of a "mashtuba," a vehicle taken off the road, and to step up checks and seizures of such vehicles on the main roads. On the photographer: the Yesha Council's Joint Situation Room (JSR) wrote on Telegram that security officials suspected the AFP photographer who published close-up pictures of the attackers knew in advance, and said he told reporters he was on his way to a protest in Beit Jala. Elchanan Groner wrote on X that the suspicion was being checked. Police told Walla that no such suspicion arises, and the IDF said "the entire incident is under investigation." Ynetnews ran a headline saying the IDF is investigating whether the photographer was informed in advance. The suspicion is unconfirmed and the police statement contradicts it.

places.name: Judea Junction (Route 35), near Hebron
places.note: Hebron city center used as the nearest sourced point; the junction has no exact coordinates in the reports (approximate)

items.headline: Ben Gvir tells the Attorney General he will keep attending Negev demolitions, says more than 19,000 illegal structures were demolished on his watch
items.summary: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir sent Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara a letter on Thursday saying he will keep taking an active part in enforcement and demolition of illegal structures in the Negev, despite her instruction not to. He called her instruction "illegal and without authority." He wrote that no law bars a minister from supervising, visiting and attending events carried out under his ministry, as his predecessors did, and that his presence does not include operational involvement. He said more than 19,000 illegal structures were demolished in the Negev during his term (his figure, not independently confirmed), and that he will keep leading the governance reform and the return of state land, JDN reports. The report does not include the Attorney General's side. Background: on 12 October the Land Enforcement Authority, with hundreds of police, demolished buildings in the Abu Wadi family's Dahiya compound north of Rahat, near Beit Kama. The Rahat municipality said 80 buildings were demolished and about 400 people, about 250 of them students, were left without housing. Police said it enforced court demolition orders, and the Regavim movement said a court had rejected the residents' land claims (Be'er Sheva 7). For the planning background on Bedouin communities and state land, see the Khamaisi backgrounder.

places.name: Beit Kama (Dahiya compound is north of Rahat, near Beit Kama)
places.note: OpenStreetMap point for Beit Kama; the compound itself has no coordinates in the report (approximate)

items.headline: Police regret the timing of a statement on the Itamar security coordinator case, issued the hour of the Hebron attack; Honenu says he fired in the air after a car tried to run him over
items.summary: On Friday morning, shortly after the Hebron attack, the Judea and Samaria police district and the Shin Bet issued a media statement about a case in which the security coordinator of the Itamar Gideonim ridge was arrested over gunfire near Akraba, Elisha Yered wrote on X. Later in the day police expressed regret over the timing of an earlier statement and said such releases require "sensitivity to what is happening on the ground" (Walla, Jerusalem Post; both do not name the case). Yered, quoting the legal-aid group Honenu, named the suspect as Pinchas (Hasi) Ran, a reservist commando whose brother Capt. Or Yosef Ran fell in the battle of Kfar Aza on 7 October 2023. According to Ran, as relayed by Honenu, he fired into the air after a car without license plates tried to run over him and an officer with him, and senior commanders sent letters of support to the court (Yered's X account). This is the suspect's account via his lawyers, and an indictment has been filed, according to Yered's post. The police statement does not describe the evidence.

items.headline: Unconfirmed weekend reports: stones and firebombs near Psagot and Duma, and a suspected ramming near Havat Gilad (single-source)
items.summary: Hatzala Yosh, a group that posts incident alerts, reported stone-throwing and firebomb incidents in several places in the past 24 hours, according to Elchanan Groner's summary on X, including near Psagot, near Duma and near Ma'ale HaTamar. Separately, Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) wrote on X that a vehicle tried to ram Israelis at the Havat Gilad area. No casualties are reported in either account, and no army, police or news report confirming the incidents was found. Both are the posters' own claims and are unconfirmed.

places.name: Havat Gilad
places.note: OpenStreetMap point; exact spot of the claimed ramming not given

items.headline: Activist Ayelet Lash posts an anonymous message from a Hadassah Ein Kerem employee about Arab nursing staff (unconfirmed)
items.summary: Ayelet Lash, a right-wing activist who lives in Rachelim in Samaria, posted at 6:58 AM Israel time a message she says was sent to her by an employee of Hadassah Ein Kerem hospital in Jerusalem. His name and job title are hidden, and she gives no way to check who he is. The writer says that in many departments most nurses are Arab; that during the 2021 "Guardian of the Walls" operation some nurses held a solidarity strike with Arab rioters; that about three and a half years ago his department took down Israeli flags hung for Independence Day and hung PLO flags; that the nurses come from Nablus, Bethlehem and East Jerusalem and some support Hamas; and that an Arab nurse caring for a Jewish patient has "the intent, the means and the ability to kill him." He says Jewish staff are afraid to speak and calls on the state to act on Arab citizens (about 20 percent of the population) holding sensitive hospital jobs. This is one anonymous account. No hospital, Health Ministry or police statement and no second source for the strike or the flag incident was found. The post had about 8,900 views and 91 reposts at the time of writing.

items.headline: Paving begins on a new road linking Alon Moreh with Mekhora in the Jordan Valley
items.summary: Arutz 7 reports that paving began on Sunday on a new road that links Alon Moreh, east of Nablus in Samaria, with Mekhora in the Jordan Valley. The work is expected to take about a week, and the road will then open to traffic. It is part of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's plan for roads and infrastructure in Judea and Samaria. Smotrich thanked the Settlement Administration and the head of Central Command, Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth. He used the occasion for an election message, warning that what he called "the Eisenkot-Liberman-Golan government" would evacuate farms, and asking people to vote for his list. The opening date is the ministry's own estimate.

places.name: Alon Moreh
places.note: Western end of the new road (OpenStreetMap point at the Alon Moreh cemetery, so approximate)

places.name: Mekhora
places.note: Eastern end of the new road, Jordan Valley

items.headline: KKL-JNF adds NIS 5 million for the first medical center in Judea and Samaria, in Binyamin
items.summary: The board of KKL-JNF (the Jewish National Fund) approved another NIS 5 million for a medical center being built in the Binyamin region, bringing its total grant to NIS 15 million, according to Channel 14. It is described as the first center of its kind in Judea and Samaria. The building's frame is finished, and it is expected to open in 2027. More than 80,000 people live in the Binyamin Regional Council area. Israel Ganz, head of the Binyamin council and chairman of the Yesha Council, thanked KKL. KKL chairman Eyal Ostrinsky said the money serves residents who until now had to travel far for medical care. Kipa also reported the grant.

places.name: Binyamin region (Psagot)
places.note: Exact building site not given in the report; marker placed at Psagot (approximate)

items.headline: Netanyahu and Katz overrule the chief of staff: the Hebron operation will continue "with greater force"
items.summary: According to Channel 14 reporter Hillel Bitton Rosen, Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir recommended ending operation "Roar of Judah" in Hebron. The army's view was that its immediate goals had been met and that going further would put soldiers at risk and could set off a wider escalation. Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz instead ordered the army to keep going "with greater force" until the Hamas network in the city is uprooted, on the model of the operation in the northern Samaria refugee camps: house-to-house searches, arrests and strikes on headquarters. The cordon around Hebron and the closure of Judea and Samaria stay in place at least until after Tuesday's election. On Sunday, according to Channel 14, the army dropped leaflets telling Hebron residents: "Hand over all weapons in your hands or you will endanger your lives." Ynet reports 12 more arrests overnight, about 50 in all, and more than 500 places searched. The attackers' homes were sealed and are to be demolished, and a large exercise involving several divisions has begun. Army Radio's Doron Kadosh, quoted by Arutz 7, wrote that if over 500 houses were searched and only a hunting rifle and a pistol were found, "something is strange here." The account of the Zamir recommendation is Channel 14's and was not confirmed by the army in the reports seen.

places.name: Hebron
places.note: City center; the operation is in the western neighborhoods (approximate)

items.headline: The two soldiers killed near Hebron are buried; Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem's father asks the state to deport the attackers' families
items.summary: Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, of Hod HaSharon, was buried on Sunday at the Hod HaSharon military cemetery, Arutz 7 reports. His sister Shira said: "I won't give the terrorists the pleasure of breaking my spirit." His father, Amnon, called on the state to deport the attackers' families and said that if the state does not do it, "we'll have to take the law into our hands." His father told Ynet that Yuval was killed while trying to save a friend, after his weapon jammed. According to the 0404 news site, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir spoke at the funeral and called for executing terrorists, deporting their families and dismantling the Palestinian Authority. Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman was buried at 11:00 the same day in Ashkelon, according to Elchanan Groner. Both were killed in Friday's Route 35 shooting at the Hebron exit.

places.name: Hod HaSharon
places.note: Funeral of Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem at the military cemetery (city center point, approximate)

places.name: Ashkelon
places.note: Funeral of Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman (city center point, approximate)

items.headline: Paratroopers stop a planned attack on cars on Route 60 in Binyamin
items.summary: Acting on a Shin Bet tip, soldiers of the Paratroopers' 202nd Battalion arrested a Palestinian suspect on Sunday before he could attack Israeli cars on Route 60 in the Binyamin region, Srugim reports. He was not armed when he was caught. Srugim's first report called it a near-disaster in the Binyamin council area. Ynet, Kan, Kipa, Arutz 7 and Channel 14 reported the same arrest. The exact spot on Route 60 was not published.

places.name: Route 60, Binyamin (Ofra)
places.note: Exact spot not published; marker at Ofra on Route 60 (approximate)

items.headline: JSR: a resident is hit in the head by stones from olive pickers near Havat Gilad, spikes damage two cars, and grazing land is set on fire in Binyamin
items.summary: The settler emergency room JSR (Judea and Samaria Situation Room) reported several attacks on Sunday, all in its own account. Palestinians it describes as "olive pickers" threw stones at an Israeli resident at Tzur Benayahu in Samaria, a spot near Havat Gilad and Or Yedidya, and hurt him in the head (JSR on Telegram; also posted by Ayelet Lash). Two Israeli cars were damaged by spikes laid on the road near the Emek Kedem farm in Samaria. Arab suspects set fire to the grazing land of the Magnazi farm in Binyamin, and residents put the fire out. In a separate incident, Elchanan Groner reported stones, glass and paint bottles thrown from Burin at the Yitzhar junction and at three cars on the road to Gilad. JSR also published a harvest-season count: from 23 September to 23 October it recorded 320 attacks on Jews in Judea and Samaria, including 123 stone attacks, 46 attacks on Jewish shepherds, one shooting, 7 car-ramming attacks and 21 roads blocked with rocks, which it says is about 69% more than before the harvest began on 20 September (English version). These are JSR's figures; the army has not published its own count.

places.name: Tzur Benayahu (near Havat Gilad)
places.note: Stone attack on a resident; marker at Havat Gilad, the nearest mapped point (approximate)

places.name: Yitzhar junction / Burin
places.note: Stones and paint bottles thrown from Burin (village point, approximate)

items.headline: HaKol HaYehudi maps the PA's National Security battalions: about 8,000 men, and a Salfit base 340 meters from Ariel's fence
items.summary: The settler news site HaKol HaYehudi published a map of the Palestinian Authority's National Security Forces, dated 22 October and promoted on 25 October by Meir Ettinger. It says the force has 10 battalions, 9 tied to regions plus a mobile unit called Battalion 101, with about 8,000 men in all, plus more than 60 police points whose stations hold 15 to 40 armed officers each. Training is at Camp Nuweimeh near Jericho, and most battalion commanders trained in Algeria. A new commander took over in 2026, Maj. Gen. al-Abd Ibrahim Abd al-Salam Khalil, replacing Nidal Abu Dukhan. The site says the Salfit base sits about 340 meters from the fence of Ariel, under district commander Col. Ahmad al-Baz, and that the Jenin battalion sits at the Horsh Saada camp, on the ruins of an abandoned Nahal army outpost. These figures are the site's own and have not been confirmed elsewhere.

items.headline: Registrar revokes the certificate of a Jerusalem association linked to a Hamas charity; its Shuafat school says it will close
items.summary: Israel's Registrar of Associations revoked the 2026 proper-management certificate of the Dar al-Huda al-Namudhajiya association because it did not cooperate with an inquiry, HaKol HaYehudi reports. The association runs the Nur al-Huda school in Shuafat, which says it will close on 31 October. The site describes the association as an offshoot of Lajnat Zakat al-Quds, which an Israeli court ruled is a Hamas body. The report followed earlier stories by the same site. This is HaKol HaYehudi's account; the registrar's decision has not been seen in a second source.

items.headline: Week of police raids in Negev Bedouin towns: pistols, M-16s, stolen army ammunition and about NIS 275,000 seized
items.summary: Police raided homes for a week in Rahat, Tarabin, Hura, Tel Sheva, Ar'ara BaNegev, Kuseife and the unrecognized communities along Route 80, Makor Rishon reports. They seized 6 pistols, 4 M-16 rifles, 10 sets of M-16 parts, ammunition stolen from the army and about NIS 275,000 in cash, about NIS 250,000 of it in one compound in Hura. Twelve people were arrested in Rahat and Tarabin and two in Hura, and a Tel Sheva man was caught with a loaded, cocked pistol. Ayelet Lash put the number arrested at 17.

items.headline: Poll of Arabs in the north: 63% say Israel has no right to encourage new Jewish towns in the Galilee
items.summary: A Direct Polls survey for the Lev BaGalil group, taken among Arab citizens in northern Israel and reported by Arutz 7, found that 63% say Israel has no right to encourage new Jewish towns in the Galilee, 15% say it does and 22% do not know. 51% accept Israeli sovereignty in the Galilee without reservation, while 49% accept it only "for lack of choice." 76% support working with the police against illegal weapons. If a Palestinian state were created, 54% want the Galilee to stay part of Israel and 6% want it to join the Palestinian state. The sample size and dates were not given in the report. On planning in Arab towns, see the Khamaisi planning backgrounder. Separately, Finance Minister Smotrich wrote on X, addressing "the Arabs of the north," that "the party's over" and that his camp would do it "five times over" in the Negev and Galilee.

items.headline: Reports on outside money and Islamist ties in Arab politics: Qatari funds via London, and Moran Tal on Ra'am
items.summary: i24NEWS Hebrew aired a special report by Baruch Yedid on what it calls the Qatari funding network behind associations in Israel's Arab community; Yedid wrote that the money passes through the Galilee Foundation in London to groups linked to the Balad party. Moran Tal of Regavim appeared on Gadi Taub's podcast "Shomer Saf" (Taub, Regavim) to discuss the Ra'am party's ties to the Muslim Brotherhood and the Islamic Movement's Southern Branch. These are the reporters' and guests' claims; the groups named have not responded in these reports.

items.headline: Halutzei HaBashan: Syrian army-linked pages spread a simulated video of a jihadist invasion of the Golan
items.summary: The Halutzei HaBashan (Bashan Pioneers) group, which pushes for Israeli settlement in southern Syria, posted that pages linked to the new Syrian army are spreading a computer-made video showing a jihadist invasion of the Golan Heights. Ayelet Lash shared it too. The link between the pages and the Syrian army is the group's claim.

places.note: Golan front line in general; no specific place (governorate point, approximate)

items.headline: Effi Eitam on Smotrich's podcast: the Netanyahu-Smotrich partnership "restored Israel's security stability"
items.summary: Retired Brig. Gen. and former minister Effi Eitam told Finance Minister Smotrich on a podcast, reported by Arutz 7 on Saturday night, that the partnership between Netanyahu and Smotrich restored Israel's "existential security stability" across several fronts. He said that 7 October happened "on Netanyahu's watch," but that great leaders such as Churchill, Roosevelt and Golda Meir also faced strategic crises and the real test is recovery. Unlike past wars, he said, the fall of the enemy regime was set as an explicit goal this time, calling it "wounded, vengeful and genocidal." He called for "strategic continuity" with Netanyahu and Smotrich in the cabinet after the election. His son, Itamar Eitam, is sixth on the Religious Zionism list, JNS reported in September.

items.headline: Former security chiefs ask to declare the hilltop youth a terror group; Groner and Yered push back
items.summary: A group of former security chiefs signed a letter asking the government to declare the "hilltop youth" a terrorist organization, according to Shlomi Heller. Elisha Yered mocked the letter, and Elchanan Groner wrote that reservists should stop being sent against the hilltops. Yered also replied to journalist Carmela Menashe, saying the group she had called "rioters" were older Jews from the Tel Aviv area, mostly from the left, on a calm tour of settlement points. On Telegram he accused Maariv's military reporter Avi Ashkenazi of repeating army briefings against settlers. In a talk at the Olam Katan conference, Yered said dozens of settlement points in Areas A and B are waiting to be legalized.

places.note: Hilltop communities east of Shiloh in general (approximate)

items.headline: Follow-up on the Nahalat HaNavi fire: a reporter says the house belongs to a Palestinian; the army says the cause is under investigation
items.summary: Settler leaders and MK Limor Son Har-Melech said on Saturday that soldiers burned a youth house at the Nahalat HaNavi outpost near Esh Kodesh. Journalist Sivan Tahel of HaMakom (also on X) says the house belongs to a Palestinian from East Jerusalem who has petitioned the High Court. She quotes the army spokesman as saying the building is Palestinian-owned, the outpost is illegal, the area is a closed military zone, and that "the circumstances of the fire are under investigation." She also quotes two local residents who say settlers set the fire. This is Tahel's report and her quote of the army; the army statement has not been seen directly.

items.headline: Palestinian and activist claims: Hebron deputy mayor says 2,231 people removed; B'Tselem and OIC statements
items.summary: Hebron deputy mayor Khaled Fahd al-Qawasmi told Haaretz that 2,231 people from 373 families had been removed from their homes, with about 30 more families threatened; the Association for Civil Rights in Israel says this breaks international law. The Organization of Islamic Cooperation, as quoted by the Hamas-aligned Palestinian Information Center, gave a figure of about 1,500. B'Tselem attacked the operation in a 24 October statement. The Palestinian Information Center also claimed a soldier assaulted an elderly man in al-Jaldeh in Hebron and that a man was hurt in a raid in al-Mughayyir. Peace Now posted video of a bride crossing a closed gate at Sinjil. None of these claims were confirmed by the army.

items.headline: Olam Katan describes Nofei Golot, the planned new community west of Otniel: 10 to 15 families, no entry date
items.summary: Olam Katan (a religious-sector outlet, non-mainstream) published a field report on Nofei Golot, one of the two communities the Hebron Hills Regional Council announced on 24 October (see the 25 October item and the 1 October item on the Golot site). The reporter, Simcha Raz, says the site is west of Otniel, beyond Route 60, in an area with no Jewish community today, near the historic site of Tel Devir. He writes that 10 to 15 families are preparing to move in, about 10 have signed on to the core group, and entry is expected "in the coming weeks" with no date set. He says the group had planned to enter on 1 September, but the date slipped because of delays in military and political approvals and petitions against the community, which he says are expected to be resolved soon. The community is to be officially a neighborhood of Otniel and later independent, backed by the Otniel secretariat and Amana. Abraham Fishman (30, a youth social worker) says development and guard work have begun. He also says Palestinians cut most of a British Mandate-era forest on the ridge over the past 10 to 15 years and filed private-ownership claims; that is his account, and no source in the report confirms it. The report also says a farm called "Lema'an HaChai" was set up last Friday south of Otniel by the daughter of Rabbi Dan Merzbach; the Hebrew spelling in the report appears to differ from the council's "Lemaan Achai" ("for my brothers"), so that may be the same farm or a typo. Verification: the council's announcement of Nofei Golot between Otniel and Afka, and of the six farms, is carried independently by Arutz 7 and Makor Rishon (both describe the sites as planned) and by Maariv (which says the six farms "went up on the land"). Everything else above, including the family numbers, the delay and its causes, the petitions, the forest claims and the farm's founding, rests on this single report and is unconfirmed.

places.name: Nofei Golot site, west of Otniel beyond Route 60 (approximate)
places.note: Approximate; exact site not published. Same area point as the 25 October item.

items.headline: Twelve families move into the new community of Shalem near Alon Moreh, the ninth new Samaria Regional Council community in under a year
items.summary: Arutz 7 reports that 12 families moved into the new community of Shalem, near Alon Moreh in Samaria, on Monday morning, at a ceremony attended by hundreds of people. Speakers included Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan, Samaria rabbi Elyakim Levanon, the chief rabbi of Ukraine, Moshe Azman, and Knesset Constitution Committee chair Simcha Rothman. Arutz 7 and Makor Rishon both say it is part of the council's "Hitchabrut" plan, run with Amana and the Settlement Division, for 19 new communities in northern Samaria, following a cabinet decision about a year ago led by Israel Katz and Bezalel Smotrich. Arutz 7 lists the earlier eight as Rehavam, Eival, Emek Dotan, Noa, and the four northern Samaria communities evacuated in the 2005 disengagement and re-established (Homesh, Sa-Nur, Ganim and Kadim). Dagan said: "There will be a million residents in Samaria." Israel Hayom's settlements correspondent, Yotam Deshe, wrote on X that the regional councils sped up moves onto the land in recent months out of concern that a new government after Tuesday's election would stop communities that were approved but not yet populated. That is his reading, not a sourced fact. Simcha Raz of Olam Katan, a non-mainstream outlet, reported the same day that the site is on the Kabir ridge by Route 555 between Alon Moreh and Itamar, next to a lookout named for Ben Yosef Livnat; the lookout is confirmed by other sources (see the Olam Katan item below). The number of families and the ceremony are confirmed by two independent outlets.

places.name: Shalem, near Alon Moreh (approximate)
places.note: Approximate; shown at the Alon Moreh OpenStreetMap point. The exact site was not published.

items.headline: Olam Katan: Shalem gives Alon Moreh a neighboring community for the first time, on the Kabir ridge next to the Ben Yosef Livnat lookout
items.summary: Olam Katan settlements reporter Simcha Raz, under the headline "Alon Moreh is no longer isolated," wrote on Monday that Shalem, the ninth community to go up in the Samaria Regional Council area in a year, will for the first time create a settlement bloc around Alon Moreh after years in which that community stood alone. He places Shalem on the Kabir ridge by Route 555, between Alon Moreh and Itamar, beside the lookout named for Ben Yosef Livnat. The lookout and its namesake are confirmed: Livnat, 24, a nephew of then-minister Limor Livnat, was shot dead on 24 April 2011 near Joseph's Tomb in Nablus while visiting the site, by Palestinian police fire (Ynet, Haaretz and The New York Times, 2011), and the Samaria tourism body says the lookout was opened in 2015 on the southern slope of the Kabir ridge near the road to Alon Moreh, with a view of Mount Ebal, Mount Gerizim and Nablus. Raz adds that the site was approved about a year ago, which matches the cabinet decision that Arutz 7 and Makor Rishon date to about a year ago. Only Raz reports that the site has ancient wine presses and water cisterns, that the lookout's west side faces Joseph's Tomb, Mount Berakha and Yitzhar, and that researchers identify the biblical city of Shalem with the nearby Arab village of Salem; these points are unconfirmed. His claim that this is the first bloc around Alon Moreh is his own characterization. Raz also notes that paving of a road from Alon Moreh to Mekhora in the Jordan Valley began on Sunday (a separate item on this page). Israel Hayom wrote in its report on the arrival of the first families that Shalem is the last community expected to go up before the election and that several other cabinet-approved communities will not be populated in time, because settlement leaders fear that a new government would stop them. That is the same worry Yotam Deshe described on X; Israel Hayom's page blocked automated reading, so this comes from the text returned by search. Photo posted by Raz (the council's photo): families holding an Israeli flag and a Samaria Regional Council flag in front of mobile homes. The 12 families and the ceremony are confirmed by Arutz 7, Makor Rishon, Channel 14 and Israel Hayom.

places.name: Shalem, near Alon Moreh (approximate)
places.note: Approximate; shown at the Alon Moreh OpenStreetMap point. The exact site was not published.

items.headline: Court releases Itamar-area security coordinator Pinchas Ran to house arrest in the Golan, saying there is no objective evidence of what happened at Aqraba
items.summary: On Sunday the Jerusalem District Court, Judge Elad Persky, ordered Pinchas (Hasi) Ran, 37, the security coordinator (rabshatz) of the Gidonim Ridge near Itamar, moved to house arrest in the Golan Heights; the release took effect Monday morning (Arutz 7; Ynet; Israel Hayom; Olam Katan; JDN). The prosecution had asked to hold him until the end of the proceedings. Ran is charged with aggravated assault with intent (up to 20 years) and obstruction of justice (up to 3 years) over 18 September, when, according to the indictment, he entered Aqraba outside his area with an armed career soldier, checked IDs without authority, and fired at least three shots at a car that sped away, badly wounding the 18-year-old woman inside; the indictment also says he later searched for the shell casings and denied being there (Times of Israel). He says he fired in the air after a car without plates tried to run over him and the soldier, and they jumped aside (Honenu). The judge wrote that "there is no objective evidence of what happened when the car and the Ranger passed each other" and noted the conflicting accounts. He found a "very low" chance that Ran would violate house arrest or repeat the act, found no concrete risk of obstructing proceedings now that an indictment is filed, and weighed that Ran has no criminal record, has served over 600 reserve days, returned to combat after his brother, Capt. Or Yosef Ran, fell at Kfar Aza on 7 October 2023, and has letters of support from the Samaria Brigade commander and others. He also noted that police waited about three weeks to arrest Ran although he was responsible for dozens of weapons. He ordered the release before the probation report, which he called exceptional. Supervisors are former Sayeret Matkal and Shin Bet men. Honenu attorneys Nati Rom and Moshe Polski represent Ran. Rom said the prosecution "adopted the narrative of those who tried to ram the security vehicle" and urged it to reconsider the case; MK Limor Son Har-Melech called Ran "a hero of Israel" and over 100 supporters came to the hearing (Honenu's statement as relayed by Arutz 7, JDN and Olam Katan). How he was arrested: on Sunday 11 October, at 5 a.m., Shin Bet and Shai District police, with military police, took him and a second security man from their homes in a joint investigation of violence against Palestinians near Aqraba, with a gag order and a bar on seeing a lawyer; the order was lifted on 23 October (Arutz 7). Honenu says the second man was released earlier to house arrest. Not confirmed: the victim's father told Kan that Ran fired 10 rounds (the indictment says at least three; relayed by Times of Israel). The Times of Israel calls the court a magistrate's court; Ynet, Arutz 7 and Olam Katan say district court. No Shin Bet or prosecution comment on the ruling was found, and no statement from Peace Now, Yesh Din or the victim's family. Simcha Raz's own post was not retrievable by search.
items.source: Arutz 7; Ynet; Israel Hayom; Olam Katan (okn.co.il); JDN; Times of Israel; Israel National News; Honenu via the outlets; Ayelet Lash on X (wife's statement)

items.headline: The security-patrol driver Huckabee filmed at Turmus Ayya was Amishav Melet, a farmer and bereaved brother, who answered the Ambassador in a long post on X
items.summary:
This is the man Huckabee filmed at Turmus Ayya on 5 September, in the Ambassador's own words and his. Amishav Melet, a farmer from the Shiloh Valley and a member of a local security patrol, wrote on X after the Sabbath that he drove the security Ranger the Ambassador filmed. What happened: On Saturday 5 September Huckabee visited the Palestinian-American town of Turmus Ayya and, as the Times of Israel, Ynet and INN report, held up his phone to film an ATV or Ranger passing near the house where he was meeting residents. He posted the clip on X: "Visited American citizens in Turmus Ayya to hear disturbing stories about criminal terror acts by a band of trespassers brazenly roaming the property of lawful owners. Despicable actions that do not reflect 99% of Israelis" (Ynet). Sources at the event told Channel 12 he said he would send the video to President Trump (Times of Israel via Israel.com; INN). WAFA quoted a town council member, Awad Abu Samra, saying two settlers on an ATV entered the eastern part of the town about 100 meters from the Ambassador. Who pointed the vehicle out to Huckabee is not reported; the reports say only that he filmed it himself.
Melet's message (X, 5 Sep, about 22:07 Israel time; roughly 320,000 views): "Dear Mike Huckabee ... Well, that was me. I was the driver of the Ranger you filmed." He says a shepherd reported dozens of vehicles gathering at the edge of the village, in an area with repeated attacks and arson against his community; he drove out and notified the army as required; when he saw "respectable people and media crews, we said hello and continued on our way," and the army then told him it was a coordinated visit. "That is the entire story. And yet, within minutes, we were portrayed in the media as 'dangerous settlers.'" He then lists what he says the Ambassador was not told, all as his claims: that the town's former mayor, Lafi Shalabi, helped in the murder of Yehuda Guetta; that council member Abu Samra, with whom Huckabee was photographed, is a released terrorist who posted incitement; that the town has monuments glorifying terrorists; that the girls' school principal Abla al-Kuk spread incitement; that there were hundreds of attacks on Jews and soldiers in the past year; and that ambulance drivers showed Huckabee edited video of an army jeep incident. He closes: "I am a bereaved brother." Arutz 7 (INN) and Hakol Hayehudi carried the message the next morning.
The bereavement: Melet's brother Benayahu Melet, 32, a member of the Havat Gilad alert squad, was shot dead on 24 July 2026 while going to help hikers near the village of Tell (Ynet; Jerusalem Post; INN). The brother who spoke to Channel 14 that day, Eliyahu Melet, was a different brother.
Reactions: Former U.S. Ambassador David Friedman met Melet on 10 September and wrote that he was "the guy who the residents of Turmus Ayya tried to portray as a terrorist when all he was doing was driving a security patrol," a "vegan, a pacifist and a farmer" (INN; VINnews). On 18 September he wrote that Huckabee is "maybe the best ever," but that he thought Huckabee's Palestinian Affairs Unit "withheld some key facts in arranging his trip," and linked a long interview with Melet (INN; Elisha Yered on X). Channel 18 Israel put the interview out and gave his age as 35 and said he has six children (its own description; not checked elsewhere). No reply from Huckabee or the embassy to Melet was found. Unconfirmed: Melet's account of the shepherd's report and the army's call; his claims about the town's officials; and the suggestion on X that the visit was arranged to put the patrol in view. The Hebrew sources call the visit coordinated; the vehicle's exact route and whether it entered the town are not established. Note: this took place seven weeks ago and was not on the desk.
items.source: X: Amishav Melet (@amishav_); Arutz 7 / Israel National News; Ynet; Times of Israel via Israel.com; WAFA; VINnews; Hakol Hayehudi and Elisha Yered on X; Channel 18 Israel on X

items.headline: Hebron operation: forces find an underground dig about 15 meters deep next to the home of one of the Judah junction attackers
items.summary: During the counterterror operation in Hebron, forces on Sunday found an underground dig next to the home of one of the terrorists behind Friday's Judah junction attack, the IDF Spokesperson said, as reported by Srugim. It is about 15 meters deep and about 75 centimeters wide, has no exit opening, and an electronic device was found inside. The army says it was found during searches of more than 500 sites, and that it is inside the city, far from any Israeli community. The find was also reported by Elisha Ben Kimon (Ynet) and Amir Bohbot (Walla). Earlier, Bohbot reported that the Shin Bet and military intelligence had warned that Hamas planned a major attack in Judea and Samaria within days, and that a temporary checkpoint set up after the warning surprised the attackers and prevented the larger massacre they had planned (his report; not confirmed by the army). The purpose of the dig is not yet known.

places.name: Hebron
places.note: City center point; the dig is next to an attacker's home in the city (exact spot not published)

items.headline: "We were a step from disaster": after three attacks in three days, Yitzhar asks the army to clear buildings and trees along its access road
items.summary: The Yitzhar secretariat sent an urgent letter to the Samaria Brigade commander, Col. David Cohen, after stones were thrown on Sunday night at families driving home on the community's access road, Arutz 7 reports. According to the secretariat, the attackers came from the village of Burin and struck a few dozen meters from an army post, using darkness and nearby buildings and orchards for cover. It says this followed an attack on Friday on hikers on an ATV trip and stones thrown at a bus on Saturday night. The community asks the army to demolish buildings and uproot trees next to the road, including a house at the junction and another across the road, to cancel all olive-harvest permits in the area, and to carry out demolition orders on illegal building in Area C outside Burin. Copies went to Defense Minister Israel Katz, Minister Bezalel Smotrich, Central Command chief Avi Bluth and Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan. "We were a step from disaster," the secretariat said. Also reported by Yotam Deshe on X.

items.headline: JSR: stones thrown at Israelis near the Nabi Elias roundabout and on Route 60 north of Ma'ale Levona
items.summary: The settler emergency room JSR reported two more stone attacks on Monday, in its own account. Stones were thrown at an Israeli resident about 100 meters east of the Nabi Elias roundabout, near Qalqilya, and a car windshield was damaged (JSR on X). Stones were also thrown on Route 60 about half a kilometer north of the northern Ma'ale Levona junction (JSR on X). No injuries were reported. Israel8251 (Netanel Frankel) posted the day's summary of incidents.

items.headline: Police find a passage through sewer pipes from a-Ram into Jerusalem; 36 arrested
items.summary: Police uncovered a passage that used sewer infrastructure to cross from near a-Ram into the Beit Hanina neighborhood of Jerusalem, JNS reports. Its entrance was hidden under a parked commercial vehicle. Police arrested 32 Palestinians who had entered illegally and four suspected helpers, 36 in all. The find was also posted by JSR and Simcha Raz; Makor Rishon called it "a warning light for Jerusalem."

items.headline: JSR answers a PA TV claim that a settler poisoned his own flock: it says the "poison" was charcoal powder used to treat poisoned animals
items.summary: Awda TV, the PA's official channel, claimed that a "settler" near al-Mughayyir was filmed poisoning his own flock in order to blame the village. JSR rejected the claim in its own account: it says Jewish farmers carry charcoal powder as a veterinary treatment for animals that have been poisoned, and that this is what was filmed (JSR Hebrew; JSR English). JSR also says that since January 2026 it has recorded 18 poisoning incidents against Jewish shepherds, with more than 23 goats and sheep killed (JSR English). These are JSR's figures; no army or police count has been published.

places.name: al-Mughayyir
places.note: Village named in the Awda TV claim (village point)

items.headline: A Jerusalem hiking guide's field report: "The farms do the work the army didn't do"
items.summary: Asi (@Asi_T360), a Jerusalem hiking blogger and guide who also manages Beitar Jerusalem basketball, wrote a long post from the field. He says the Allon Road, once full of stone throwing, is now mostly quiet; hikers stop at Ein Samia and go on to Rashash and Fasayil; and Nahal Kana, Wadi Zarqa and the edge of the desert are safer because of the farms. "The farms do the work the army didn't do," he wrote. He says "settler violence" exists but almost not at the regulated farms, and "what there is, is inflation." This is his first-hand account. Separately, Elisha Yered posted a video of a drone keeping watch from the air while a Ma'ale Tidhar shepherd grazes his flock in Gush Etzion.

items.headline: Channel 18: a founder of the Tel Talpiot farm next to Qusra describes attacks on him, including an attempted lynching in his fields
items.summary: In field videos for Channel 18, Sam Schub interviewed Roee, a founding member of the farm outpost on Tel Talpiot next to Qusra. Roee describes violence by Arabs against the farm, including what he calls an attempted lynching in his fields, and explains why young Israelis set up a tent near a Palestinian home, which became the "besieged house" story in the media (video 1, video 2, video 3). On the same day, the High Court heard a petition by three Palestinian families from Jalud and Qusra. Hagit Ofran of Peace Now, posting live from the hearing, said the state attorney spoke of a "sense of shame and failure" that the families' return failed and said three Border Police officers were hurt, and that the deputy commander of the Judea and Samaria Division, Col. Dvir Almi, said the Area B outposts there "should not exist" (Ofran; her account, not a court record).

places.name: Qusra
places.note: Village point; the farm is on Tel Talpiot nearby (approximate)

items.headline: Ministers, MKs and Judea and Samaria council heads sign a demand to cancel Oslo as a condition for the next government
items.summary: A day before the election, ministers, Knesset members, Judea and Samaria council heads and public figures signed a letter asking that cancelling the Oslo Accords be a basic condition in coalition talks, Olam Katan reports. Signers include Ministers Itamar Ben Gvir, Shlomo Karhi, Amichai Eliyahu and Yitzhak Wasserlauf, Deputy Minister Almog Cohen, and MKs including Limor Son Har-Melech, Tali Gottlieb, Zvi Sukkot and Avichai Boaron. They commit to work through a government decision, legislation and steps on the ground, along with dismantling the PA and full sovereignty and settlement in Judea, Samaria and the Gaza area. The letter thanks the current government for "the settlement revolution" and calls Oslo the source of "rivers of Jewish blood." The initiative came from Mor Asraf and Ruth Levy, graduates of the Hotam group's "Dor HaNitzahon" (Victory Generation) course. Also posted by Elchanan Groner and Yotam Deshe.

items.headline: Election day: Religious Zionism sends 5,000 activists and 65 buses, some to Judea and Samaria communities
items.summary: Ahead of today's vote, Religious Zionism said it recruited 5,000 activists and 65 buses, some sent to communities in Judea and Samaria, according to Amiel Yarchi. Ayelet Lash urged a vote for Smotrich, crediting him with 104 new communities in Judea and Samaria and 150 farms that she says guard a million dunams, along with the repeal of the disengagement law for northern Samaria and the return to Homesh and Sa-Nur. Her figures are unconfirmed.

items.headline: Kalansuwa: police find 12 weapons stolen from the army; in Jatt, a preacher urges Arabs to vote to change the government
items.summary: Central District police and Border Police found a large cache hidden in open ground in Kalansuwa on Sunday: a Kalashnikov, three M-16 rifles, eight pistols, six fragmentation grenades, two stun grenades, thousands of bullets and three vests, JDN reports, citing police. Police say the weapons were stolen from the army. Two family members who were at the site were arrested and taken to the Tayibe station. Also posted by Ayelet Lash. Separately, Moran Tal reported that Sheikh Ahmad Badran, the preacher at the al-Bayan mosque in Jatt, whom she links to Hizb ut-Tahrir, urged Arabs in a Friday sermon to vote to change the government (her report; unconfirmed).

items.headline: Paratroopers reconnaissance unit arrests five Hamas and Islamic Jihad men in Qabatiya
items.summary: Fighters of the Paratroopers reconnaissance unit finished an arrest operation in Qabatiya last week and detained five terrorists linked to Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad, the IDF Spokesperson said, as reported by Ynet.
