Separately, the 202nd Battalion raided more than 50 targets, searched for weapons and questioned more Hamas-linked suspects.

items.headline: Catch-up: the High Court backed delaying E1 tender bids until after the election
items.summary: On Thursday, 22 October, the High Court rejected Finance Minister Smotrich's petition against the attorney general's order to delay opening bids in the tenders for more than 1,000 homes in E1, near Ma'ale Adumim, until after the election, Ynet reports. Justices Daphne Barak-Erez, Ofer Grosskopf and Khaled Kabub said the timing could be used for election campaigning. The tender was delayed, not cancelled. Smotrich had accused the attorney general's staff of "becoming active players in the elections." This desk missed the ruling last week; Peace Now posted the text on Monday.

places.name: Ma'ale Adumim (E1)
places.note: Ma'ale Adumim point; E1 lies between it and Jerusalem (approximate)

items.headline: Palestinian and activist claims: a demolition in Qalqilya, differing Hebron displacement figures, and outpost claims
items.summary: Short notes, all in the claimants' own accounts. The Hamas-linked Palestinian Information Center says the home of Naim Abu Shehab was demolished in Qalqilya (PalInfo) and that a house near the Deir Sharaf checkpoint was taken as an army post (PalInfo). Figures for people leaving homes in the Hebron operation area differ: PalInfo, citing a Hebron relief committee, says 619 families and about 3,971 people, while the Hebron governor, quoted by Baruch Yedid, says 409 families; neither figure is confirmed. Dror Etkes (Kerem Navot) shared a HaMakom report that the chairman of the Knesset subcommittee on Judea and Samaria, MK Zvi Sukkot, runs a guesthouse at Yitzhar that, according to HaMakom, stands on land the community's plan zones as open space where building is banned; Sukkot, the Civil Administration and the Samaria Regional Council did not comment, and claimed more outposts went up on Monday (Etkes). A UN commission accused Israel of crimes against humanity in the West Bank; Israel rejected the report as a "misinformation campaign" (Times of Israel; page not opened).

items.headline: IDF demolishes the Madama monument to terrorists, which stood for decades, and others in villages near Nablus
items.summary: On Tuesday morning the army demolished a monument in Madama, in Samaria, that for decades had honored terrorists who murdered Jews, along with monuments in nearby villages, Arutz 7 reports. The IDF confirmed the demolitions to JNS. Arutz 7 says it followed demands by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and MK Zvi Sukkot, chair of the Knesset subcommittee on Judea and Samaria, who gave the army a list of dozens of monuments in Palestinian villages. "After decades, the monument that honored terrorists in Madama has been destroyed," Sukkot said, and he called on the army "to keep removing every monument that honors terrorists in Judea and Samaria." In August Sukkot was filmed smashing the same monument with a hammer; the army said at the time that his entry was coordinated but the damage was not, and Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned it (JNS). The army says this is part of a wider operation with the Border Police and the Shin Bet in the Nablus area that will go on for several days and will include arrests of wanted men, searches for weapons and more monument demolitions, Ynet reports. Palestinian reports cited by Ynet say about 10 monuments were destroyed, including in Rujeib, Azmut, Madama, Iraq Burin and Beit Furik. HaKol HaYehudi, which says it gave the army the locations two months ago, claims credit. Elchanan Groner also reported an arrest operation in Burin, which he links to several attacks this week, and JSR reported the Madama, Azmut and Rujeib demolitions.

places.name: Burin
places.note: Arrest operation reported by Groner (village point)

items.headline: A woman is hurt in the face by a stone near Rehelim; a Ma'ale Ahuvia shepherd is beaten with clubs
items.summary: On Tuesday morning Arabs threw stones at an Israeli car south of Rehelim junction, toward the village of Sawiya. A stone broke the windshield and hit the driver, a woman aged 20, in the face. She kept control of the car and was taken to Beilinson Hospital in light condition (Kipa, Channel 14, JSR). The rescue group Rescuers Without Borders reported more attacks the same morning, as told by JDN: at about 8:10 a.m. a shepherd from Ma'ale Ahuvia was beaten with clubs and lightly hurt; at about 7:30 a.m. Arabs from Qabalan attacked several Jews from Maoz Yehuda with stones during the olive harvest, causing light injuries; a shepherd from the Sha'ara farm was attacked near Beit Ur al-Tahta without injury; and near Tel Binyahu three men with sticks tried to attack a Jewish ATV rider, who got away. These details are the rescue group's account. Separately, Yotam Deshe wrote that a stone was thrown at his car from a passing Palestinian car near Ariel and missed (his account on X)).

places.name: Rehelim junction
places.note: OpenStreetMap point for the Rehelim transit stop; the attack was south of the junction (approximate)

items.headline: Election day: the Yesha Council warns of staged harvest clashes, and forces detain dozens of activists in western Binyamin
items.summary: The Yesha Council warned on Tuesday morning that dozens of foreign activists with cameras had arrived in the Shiloh bloc in Binyamin. It said it feared they would try to start clashes there and elsewhere to create a media storm on election day, and it called on police and the army to prevent this (Walla; Yesha Council on X). Elchanan Groner reported dozens of anarchists, some of them foreigners, at a harvest event with a large crowd of Arabs in the Shiloh valley. Later, Yotam Deshe reported that the army and police in western Binyamin detained dozens of activists and removed harvesters from places where the harvest was not coordinated or approved, after the Yesha Council's warning. The army has not published a number of detainees.

items.headline: The European Parliament Left group's communications director is refused entry and sent back after coming for the olive harvest
items.summary: Manus Carlisle, communications director of the Left group in the European Parliament, was held for about eight hours at Ben Gurion Airport and refused entry with a woman activist. They had come to take part in a campaign helping Palestinian farmers with the olive harvest (Behadrei Haredim; Yeshiva World News). Speaking to Turkey's Anadolu agency, Carlisle said officials knew of every protest he had attended and his social-media posts, even though the two had deleted Israel-related posts a month before the trip, and that they were told the reason was "because you hate Israel." He said two more Irish citizens who came for the harvest were also refused. These are his claims; no Israeli statement was published.

items.headline: For election day the army closes off PA towns, reinforces the seam line, and guards hiking sites
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria Division, under Brig. Gen. Kobi Heller, put "breathing closures" (temporary barriers that limit but do not fully stop traffic) around Palestinian towns and villages seen as likely to produce violence, to reduce friction with Israelis on election day, Amir Bohbot of Walla reports. Forces were added along the seam line out of concern that terrorists would try to enter Israel, and approved hiking sites were guarded because large numbers of Israelis were expected to hike on the day off. Arrest raids were held in the Qalqilya, Jenin and Nablus areas, with warning talks for inciters. A security official told Walla that engineering units were preparing to demolish illegal buildings, terrorists' homes and monuments. Walla also reports that the Paratroopers Brigade is working against nationalist crime in the Shiloh valley, but forces did not prevent the torching of Palestinian vehicles in Binyamin overnight. Overnight into Wednesday, Palestinian outlets reported more raids: 11 arrests in Qalqilya, most of them released prisoners, and entries into al-Mughayyir, Tubas, Yasid, Idhna and al-Fawwar camp (Palinfo; the list is from local sources cited by Quds News Network and is not confirmed by the army).

items.headline: Election day in Judea and Samaria: high turnout, voting by generator light in Kedumim, and longer hours in Hebron
items.summary: Turnout in Samaria and Binyamin was high on Tuesday. Figures posted at the close of voting by Simcha Raz put Alei Zahav first at 85%, followed by Har Bracha and Enav (84.4%), Elkana (84.3%), Ateret (83.9%) and Bruchin (83.8%); Ariel (67.1%), Ma'ale Efraim (64.6%) and Tzofim (58.7%) were lowest. These are his figures from the Central Elections Committee; Olam Katan printed the 9 p.m. list. National turnout was a record of about 77.7% when polls closed at 10 p.m., according to a JDN headline. A power cut of about three hours hit Kedumim; council head Uzael Vatik brought generators and lights to every polling station so voting could go on (JDN; Israel8251), and he asked the elections committee to extend voting hours there (Yotam Deshe). After power cuts in Hebron, voting there was extended by two hours, to 10 p.m., Olam Katan reports.

items.headline: Gantz's joint right-wing field campaign sends out 5,000 volunteers; Smotrich vows the "settlement revolution" will go on (results still partial)
items.summary: The joint Likud and Religious Zionism field headquarters "Yamin Menatzeach" ("The Right Wins"), led by Binyamin Regional Council head and Yesha Council chair Israel Gantz, sent more than 5,000 volunteers door to door in cities across the country despite heavy rain, the headquarters said, as reported by Arutz 7. "This national turnout is a huge achievement in itself," Gantz said. In his election-night speech, Bezalel Smotrich said: "They are celebrating because they think they will manage to reverse our settlement revolution in Judea and Samaria. I tell them, they will not succeed," and promised Jewish communities in Gaza and no withdrawal from Lebanon (Ynet). According to Ladaat, he also said he would keep working to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and that parties that will not condemn October 7 are not legitimate partners. The exit polls gave his party six or seven seats; Smotrich said it stood at seven (Yotam Deshe). Results were still partial at the time of writing; the exit polls showed Likud as the largest party and no clear majority for either bloc.

items.headline: Jeremy Sharon: the Ram Farm outpost builds a communal building before winter
items.summary: On election day, residents of the Ram Farm outpost in the central West Bank were building a new communal building before the winter, Jeremy Sharon of the Times of Israel reported. They have a flock of sheep and hope to plant a vineyard soon. He says the outpost was set up in coordination with the Binyamin Regional Council and the Amana settlement organization, but does not have cabinet approval. This is his report; the exact location was not published.

items.headline: Channel 18 follow-up: residents say empty, PA-funded houses near Qusra serve as bases for attacks
items.summary: In more field videos for Channel 18, Sam Schub went back to the area of Qusra. Roee, a founder of the Tel Talpiot farm, says completed but empty houses funded by the PA are used as bases for attacks on nearby Jewish residents, and that a villa near the village, built by a Palestinian who lives in Ohio and does not live there, is used by a group that launches attacks; he identifies one of his attackers (video 1, video 2, video 3). These are his claims; the owner's side was not given.

items.headline: Three Negev men are arrested with Ra'am envelopes and tens of thousands of shekels in cash; one is a senior Ra'am activist
items.summary: Police arrested three Negev residents overnight into Tuesday on suspicion of election bribery. Police say envelopes marked with Ra'am's symbol, Ra'am ballots and tens of thousands of shekels in cash, including one envelope with 12,000 shekels, were found in their homes, apparently to be handed out to voters. Two were held for six more days and the third, a doctor, was released to house arrest. The case was moved to the Lahav 433 national crime unit, which is checking whether there is a wider, organized network (Ynet). One suspect says the money was Islamic Movement charity for poor families. Ra'am filed a complaint with the elections committee saying it was "marked as a target." The Choosing Life Forum says one detainee, "S.A.R." of Rahat, is a senior Ra'am activist, a former head of the youth department of the southern branch of the Islamic Movement, and a central fundraiser for the charity "Siyua 48", against which the forum earlier filed a police complaint alleging terror financing (JDN). These are the forum's claims; police have not named the suspects.

places.name: Rahat
places.note: Home of the detainee named by the forum (city point)

items.headline: Arab and Bedouin turnout jumps; a brawl with gunfire at a Rahat polling station; celebratory shooting after the exit polls
items.summary: Turnout in Arab and Bedouin towns rose sharply. Figures for 6:40 p.m. posted by Daniel Gold showed Laqiya at 75%, Kafr Qasim 73.9%, Kuseife 73.3% and Rahat 72.2%. HaKol HaYehudi said the rise was about 13 points, after Hamas-linked Gazans and leaders of the northern Islamic Movement called on Arabs to vote. Regavim's director, Meir Deutsch, said the long lines in the Negev show that "Arab society understands that the revolution under way in the Negev can be stopped" (Regavim). Analyst Moran Tal said enforcement in the Negev pushed Arabs to vote, but so did large Ra'am and Joint List campaigns that drew in conservative voters who had stayed away. Video from a Rahat polling station shows several people fighting while bursts of gunfire are heard; the circumstances and any injuries were not yet known (Channel 14). Olam Katan posted video it says shows fireworks and gunfire as Arab citizens celebrated the exit polls. In Majd al-Krum, Ayelet Lash claimed Arabs were attacking a Jewish regional elections committee member and that police could not control them (her post); a video posted by another user is captioned with the words "tonight we kick you out" (video). The Majd al-Krum claims are unconfirmed; no police statement was found.

items.headline: An Egyptian crosses the border fence near Nitzana and is caught about two kilometers inside
items.summary: Army lookouts spotted a suspect crossing the Egyptian border fence in the Nitzana area at 1:45 a.m. on Tuesday and kept watching him. Forces chased him and caught him about two kilometers from the fence, far from communities and bases, and he was handed to the Shin Bet, the IDF Spokesperson said, as posted by Elisha Ben Kimon of Ynet. His purpose was not stated.

places.name: Nitzana
places.note: Community point; the crossing was in the Nitzana area (approximate)

items.headline: Palestinian claims on Tuesday: vehicles burned in Umm Safa
items.summary: Palestinians reported that settlers set vehicles on fire in Umm Safa, northwest of Ramallah, and said there had been repeated attacks in the village in recent days (Ynet). Walla's military reporter wrote that forces did not prevent the torching of Palestinian vehicles in Binyamin overnight (Walla). No arrests were reported, and the identity of those responsible was not confirmed.

items.headline: Geva Shomron goes up the morning after the election: 10 families from Ramat Gan move onto the old Paratroopers training base by Sa-Nur, the 10th new Samaria community in under a year
items.summary: On Wednesday, the morning after the election, Geva Shomron was founded in northern Samaria as its first 10 families moved into caravans (mobile homes) (Srugim, Arutz 7). The families are graduates of the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva (a yeshiva whose students combine Torah study with army service), led by Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira and Rabbi Ben Zion Algazi. The site is the former Paratroopers Brigade training base next to Sa-Nur. Samaria Council head Yossi Dagan called the base "the first place uprooted in northern Samaria, in 2002" (Channel 14); Sa-Nur itself was evacuated in the 2005 disengagement and has since been rebuilt. The Samaria Regional Council says Geva Shomron is the 10th community it has set up in less than a year, under a plan for 19 new communities in northern Samaria in place of the four destroyed in the disengagement and the "Million in Samaria" plan, carried out with Amana and the Settlement Division. Other new or rebuilt communities in the push include Shalem, Rehavam, Eival, Emek Dotan and Noa, and the rebuilt Homesh, Sa-Nur, Ganim and Kadim. Dagan said: "Geva Shomron is our answer to the expulsion... We promised not to miss the second chance we were given, and we are keeping that promise." Rabbi Shapira, on a tour of the site days earlier, said: "We waited thousands of years to get here" (Channel 14). Those attending included Rabbi Yaakov Ariel, Rabbi Berel Lazar, MK Boaz Bismuth and Ze'ev Hever (Zambish). Yotam Deshe, Simcha Raz and Ayelet Lash also posted on the founding; see also Olam Katan.

places.name: Geva Shomron (next to Sa-Nur)
places.note: Approximate: point is Sa-Nur (Nominatim); the new community is on the former Paratroopers base beside it

items.headline: Sister of freed hostage Avinatan Or suffers spinal fractures after Arabs stone her car near Rehelim junction
items.summary: Emuna Schreiber, the sister of freed hostage Avinatan Or, was moderately hurt on Monday when her car left the road near Rehelim junction in Samaria as she tried to escape Arabs throwing stones at it, Channel 14 reports. Her family says she has spinal fractures and severe bruising, is at Beilinson Hospital, is not in danger and does not need surgery. JSR reported the same account (JSR, English, Hebrew). Ayelet Lash, who lives nearby, says she was driving from Ariel to Eli and a rock hit her windshield at the village of Lubban (her post); the exact spot is given differently in the two accounts. Lash also says the woman hurt by a stone near Rehelim on Tuesday (reported here yesterday) had a broken jaw and three hours of surgery (her post); this detail is unconfirmed. Yotam Deshe says both cases are part of a wave of attempted attacks since last weekend's Hebron-area shooting, mostly stone-throwing because of the heavy army presence, and that a stone was thrown at his own car on Tuesday (his post). No arrests were reported.

places.name: Rehelim junction (area)
places.note: Approximate: point is Rehelim (Nominatim); Lash places it at Lubban

items.headline: Har Hevron council: foreign activists led by Andrey Khrzhanovskiy punch and kick residents near Carmel
items.summary: The Har Hevron Regional Council's spokesman says a group of foreign far-left activists led by the pro-Palestinian activist Andrey Khrzhanovskiy attacked Jewish residents near Carmel on Wednesday evening. According to that account, the activists pushed cameras into residents' faces, punched and kicked them, blocked their car and touched one resident's gun; one resident was hit in the face and treated by medics (council statement via Israel8251; JSR's account: Hebrew, English). Elchanan Groner notes that Khrzhanovskiy has repeatedly entered Area A in Jenin and Tulkarm to support Palestinians after IDF operations (his post). This is the council's and JSR's account only: no police statement or account from the activists was found, and the report is otherwise unconfirmed.

items.headline: IDF demolishes the Beita homes of two bombers who planned a kidnapping; 72-hour Samaria operation ends with 12 terror monuments destroyed and 8 arrests
items.summary: On Wednesday morning the Samaria Brigade and the Yahalom engineering unit demolished the homes in Beita of Zakaria Muhammad Abd Dawud and Ibrahim Abd al-Karim Abd Dawud, who the army says carried out three bombing attacks in 2024 and 2025 that wounded security forces (Srugim, citing the IDF). JSR says the two also planned a kidnapping attack, and that Beita's Telegram group wrote that "demolishing the homes will not break the spirit of the free," a term used for security prisoners (JSR). The demolitions closed a 72-hour operation in eight villages and Nablus: forces destroyed 12 monuments honoring terrorists, searched about 300 sites, arrested eight wanted men and seized a hunting rifle, a pistol and ammunition. In Yatzid, Duvdevan arrested a man the army says traded in bombs and weapons for a terror cell, and the Judea and Samaria police SWAT unit arrested a man suspected of making bombs and weapons (Srugim). Elchanan Groner posted that more monuments in Beita were destroyed this week (his post). This follows yesterday's lead on the Madama monument.

items.headline: Hebron operation goes on: Border Police undercover troops arrest six wanted men, including Hamas members; an M16 is seized
items.summary: In the operation that began after last weekend's shooting at Judah junction, in which Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem were killed, Border Police undercover troops guided by the Shin Bet arrested six wanted men, some of them Hamas members, overnight in several villages in the Judah Brigade area. Searches in Hebron turned up an M16 rifle, knives, a vest and a fake pistol (Srugim, citing the IDF). Simcha Raz named the places as Dura, al-Fawwar camp, Bani Na'im and Dhahiriya; the army statement did not name them, so the map points are from his report.

items.headline: Judea and Samaria turnout put at 78.2%, above the national rate; Religious Zionism is the largest party there
items.summary: Simcha Raz of Olam Katan reports that turnout in Judea and Samaria was 78.2%, above the national average, and that Religious Zionism was the largest party there with 24.8%, followed by United Torah Judaism and Likud. The highest turnout, by his figures: Beit Hogla (Megilot) 92.47%, Asael (Har Hevron) 90.24%, Rehelim 86.27%, then Avigail (his post). These figures are his and were not checked against official results. Raz also reported that Carmel in the Hebron Hills was without power on election day; the Israel Electric Corporation first blamed the election-day closure for keeping a contractor's tractor away, then told him that was a reporting error, blamed the weather and a harder repair than expected, and apologized to the council head (first post, follow-up).

items.headline: JSR: Hamas-linked Jenin channel spreads Osama al-Saadi's dedication of the Arab parties' "victory" to Gaza and to prisoners; PA foreign minister tells an MEP "settler terrorism" is rising
items.summary: JSR's monitoring: Akhbar Jenin, which JSR calls the largest Jenin channel (225,000 followers) and Hamas-affiliated, is spreading a speech by former MK Osama al-Saadi of the Joint List dedicating the "victory" to Arabs in Gaza and Judea and Samaria and to "prisoners" (convicted terrorists) in Israeli jails (JSR). JSR also reports that PA Foreign Minister Varsen Aghabekian Shahin met European Parliament member Hildegard Bentele in Ramallah, alleged "genocide" in Gaza and rising "settler terrorism," and asked the EU to keep funding UNRWA (JSR). Both are JSR's account; not confirmed elsewhere.

items.headline: Effi Eitam on Galei Israel radio: "I was one of the few beside the prime minister in the hard hours"
items.summary: Brig. Gen. (res.) Effi Eitam told Sharon Gal on Galei Israel radio that Israel needs leaders able "not only to recover but to lead us on to finish the campaign." He said he was among the few who sat with Netanyahu in the hard hours and saw him make decisions, and he said of the parties seeking to replace him that he saw them serve only "defeat, cowardice, despair." "There are no great leaders in the world who did not fail," he said; the point is the ability to recover (Galei Israel). The page gives no date; search results date it to around 27 Oct, which is unconfirmed. No new X posts from Eitam were found, and no new JNS or Arutz 7 appearance.

items.headline: Bedouin reservist from Tel Sheva caught in an IDF patrol vehicle in Gaza with about 10 kg of captagon
items.summary: An active-duty reservist in his 30s from Tel Sheva was arrested inside the Gaza Strip in an army patrol vehicle with about 10 kilograms of what police believe is captagon, a stimulant drug, a joint police, Shin Bet and IDF statement said. The arrest by the Negev central police unit was based on advance intelligence; a Beersheba court extended his detention to Thursday (Srugim, Kipa). HaKol HaYehudi gave his hometown as Segev Shalom (its post); police say Tel Sheva.

items.headline: Likud hands police and the Shin Bet hundreds of testimonies of alleged fraud at Arab polling stations; claim that bribe money came from enemy states
items.summary: Likud says it has given police, the Shin Bet and the Central Elections Committee hundreds of testimonies, including envelopes of cash with Ra'am ballots, threats and violence against polling staff, double voting and gaps between envelopes and voters. The committee said it is reviewing the complaint; these are Likud's claims, not findings (Kipa). MK Simcha Rothman wrote to committee chair Judge Noam Sohlberg and to the Shin Bet (Israel8251), and HaKol HaYehudi reports MKs calling on the Shin Bet to investigate (its post). Ayelet Lash cites reporter Noam Amir that the investigation material raises suspicion of millions of shekels from enemy states (her post); this is unconfirmed. A Beersheba local news site also ran the headline "Fuel cards for votes? Testimony from a gas station near Meitar" (seen in Google News only; not opened). This follows the arrest of three Negev men with Ra'am envelopes reported yesterday.

items.headline: HaKol HaYehudi: new Joint List MK Hassan al-Nasasra praised the 2021 Negev road riots
items.summary: HaKol HaYehudi reports that Hassan al-Nasasra, Balad's Negev representative, 10th on the Joint List, praised the rioting on Negev roads during the May 2021 riots and shared a post saying "Arabs of 48" are "more dangerous than Hamas rockets" (HaKol HaYehudi). The quotes are from HaKol HaYehudi's report and were not independently checked.

items.headline: Court cancels the removal from Judea and Samaria of Rabbis for Human Rights volunteers detained at Nahalin
items.summary: The Jerusalem Magistrate's Court canceled the 15- to 30-day removal from Judea and Samaria of Rabbis for Human Rights volunteers detained last week during the olive harvest at Nahalin. The group says the court found no reasonable suspicion that they broke the law and that they will return to the harvest (Yotam Deshe). Israel Hayom also reported the ruling (headline seen in search; the site blocks the desk).

items.headline: Rom Gilboa goes up in northern Samaria, the third new community this week and the 11th in under a year, with neighbors from the Gilboa kibbutzim at the ceremony
items.summary: On Thursday the first families moved onto the site of Rom Gilboa, a new community in the northeast corner of Samaria near Malkishua and Kibbutz Merav, east of Ganim and Kadim, on high ground over the Ma'ayanot valley (Srugim, Arutz 7). Residents say terrorists often fired at Merav from this area. The Samaria Regional Council says it is the 11th community it has set up in less than a year and the third this week, after Geva Shomron, under its plan for 19 new communities, carried out with Amana and the Settlement Division. Simcha Raz counted nine founding families and put the site less than 10 km from Beit She'an (his figures). Minister Amichai Chikli attended, along with representatives of Ein Harod, Tirat Zvi, Merav and Ma'ale Gilboa. Council head Yossi Dagan said "3,500 dunams can be built on now" and that "a huge city will connect Samaria, the Ma'ayanot valley, the Gilboa and the Galilee"; he added that "two weeks ago there was nothing here." Harel Ben Ari of Ein Harod and Col. Levi Givon of Merav also spoke (Srugim). Yotam Deshe and Olam Katan also posted on the founding.

places.name: Rom Gilboa (near Malkishua)
places.note: Approximate: point is Malkishua (Nominatim); the exact site has not been published

items.headline: Binyamin sets up the first student village on a farm: students will live at Hanina's farm on the Allon Road for token rent and give 140 hours of farm work and guard shifts
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council is setting up what it calls the country's first student village, at "Hanina's farm" on the Allon Road (Israel Hayom, Kipa). Students will pay token rent and get a stipend, and in return give 140 volunteer hours of farm work and guard shifts. The project belongs to the farm-villages association of Torah BaHava and is led by the council's Binyamin Plus youth department with the Settlement Ministry, the Yesha Council and the Orot Eliraz group. The council says it is a pilot, with more farms to follow and several nearby farms later to share one student community. Council head and Yesha chair Israel Gantz said the students "will be a force multiplier for the farm families." Minister Orit Strock also backed the plan (Israel Hayom). Simcha Raz also posted on it.

places.name: Allon Road, Binyamin
places.note: Approximate: a point on the Allon Road (Nominatim); the farm's exact location has not been published

items.headline: Tourism Ministry opens a hotel-building plan for Judea and Samaria, with grants raised to 33%; councils must submit sites by November
items.summary: The Tourism Ministry and the Yesha councils' cluster are launching a plan to build hotels in Judea and Samaria and to develop tourism around Bible sites, under Government Decision 4323 (Srugim). Local councils must submit proposed sites by November. Keren Gefen, CEO of the cluster, said grants for developers will rise to 33% of costs from 20%. No sites or numbers of rooms have been published yet. Simcha Raz and Olam Katan also reported it. For planning background, see the planning page.

items.headline: Residents on Mount Ebal stop an attempt to pave a Palestinian road from Nablus toward Joshua's Altar; one vehicle is seized
items.summary: Residents of the Mitzpe Yehoshua hilltop on Mount Ebal saw engineering vehicles paving a gravel road from Nablus in Area C, toward the site known as Joshua's Altar (Srugim, Arutz 7). They called the security coordinator and the army. The operators fled toward Nablus, and one vehicle was seized. In the residents' account, the effort was backed by the Palestinian Authority; they say the hilltop was set up after Benayahu Melet was killed near Havat Gilad three months ago. The army has not commented in these reports.

places.name: Mount Ebal
places.note: Nominatim; the hilltop's exact point is not published

items.headline: A new farm goes up at Jiftlik in the Jordan Valley
items.summary: Eliav Libi reported that a new farm, the Jiftlik farm, went up in the Jordan Valley this week. This is his report; no news site had confirmed it by this edition.

places.name: al-Jiftlik
places.note: Approximate: point is the Palestinian village of al-Jiftlik (Nominatim); the farm's site is not given

items.headline: Unconfirmed: activists say forces moved to demolish homes at Kfar Tarfon in Binyamin
items.summary: An activist account on X reported on Thursday morning that large forces were on their way to demolish homes at Kfar Tarfon, a settlement point in Binyamin near Atara, where it says two large families and a group of young shepherds live. No news site or army statement confirming a demolition was found by this edition, so this is unconfirmed. The same site was demolished once before, in October 2025 (JDN, a report of that earlier event).

places.name: Kfar Tarfon (near Atara)
places.note: Approximate: point is the village of Atara (Nominatim)

items.headline: High Court approves demolishing the apartment of a terrorist whose rocket attack on Modi'in Illit failed: "a failed attack deters no less"
items.summary: The High Court of Justice unanimously rejected a petition against the army's order to demolish the home of Abdallah Mahmoud Saud al-Khatib, who it says built rockets and set up a cell (BHOL, Newsrael). On 17 September 2025 two cell members aimed two rockets at Modi'in Illit; one fell over and broke the launcher of the second, so neither was fired. He is also charged over a drone bomb flown over Sde Ephraim on 9 October 2023. Justice Yael Willner, with Justices Yechiel Kasher and Ruth Ronen, wrote that for deterrence it makes no difference that the attack failed. The order is limited to his apartment. The reports do not name his village.

items.headline: JSR: stones on Route 446 and HaKerem Road, a shepherd hurt in the face near Tzon Aviezer, an attempted ramming on the Duma road, and a jeep damaged at Ma'ale Tidhar; three from Deir Dibwan held over a burning gas canister on Route 60
items.summary: The settler emergency room JSR (Judea and Samaria Situation Room) reported on Thursday, all in its own account: stones thrown at an Israeli car on Route 446 near Deir Qaddis (JSR); stones at several Israeli cars on HaKerem Road, about 50 meters north of HaDoar junction, with no damage (JSR); an attempted ramming of a shepherd from the Michtam LeDavid farm on the Duma access road by a car with Palestinian plates, with no injuries (JSR); Arabs it calls "harvesters" stoning three Jewish shepherds between the Tzon Aviezer farm and Kfar Ro'im, one hurt in the face (JSR); and stones at settlers at Ma'ale Tidhar in eastern Gush Etzion that damaged their jeep (JSR). JSR and Yotam Deshe also flagged a poster on the Hamas-linked Telegram channel "Fida'i Filastin" urging attacks in Judea and Samaria (JSR). Separately, the army and police arrested three men aged 16 to 25 in Deir Dibwan over a burning gas canister thrown on Route 60 between Givat Asaf and Ofra on 12 October; a court extended their remand by about a week (JDN; Simcha Raz gives 3 November). Israel8251 posted a full list of the day's events.

items.headline: Court bars activists Andrey Khrzhanovskiy and Jasper Nathaniel from Judea and Samaria after the Carmel incident; 15 foreigners arrested near Lubban al-Sharqiya
items.summary: After Tuesday's incident near Carmel in the south Hebron Hills, in which a Jewish resident was hurt, a court ordered activists Andrey Khrzhanovskiy and Jasper Nathaniel kept out of Judea and Samaria until 1 January 2027 (JFeed, Israel News Pulse). JSR and Elisha Yered put the ban at two months and say police had asked for six. Police are examining an attempted weapon grab and assault complaints from both sides. Activist groups and some foreign outlets say Khrzhanovskiy was beaten and lost consciousness; that is their account. Separately, police said 15 foreign nationals were arrested by the army near Lubban al-Sharqiya in Binyamin (JSR).

items.headline: Huckabee answers Tucker Carlson over a Palestinian-American from Turmus Ayya, posting the embassy's timeline
items.summary: Ambassador Mike Huckabee rejected Tucker Carlson's claim that the embassy ignored a U.S. citizen who says Israeli settlers beat him (VINnews, Townhall). Huckabee posted the embassy's timeline: the man's son, in Chicago, emailed on 19 October, never gave his father's contact details, did not want to go to local authorities, and later thanked the embassy. Huckabee called Carlson "deranged." The attack itself has not been independently confirmed.

items.headline: Groner: Rabbis for Human Rights helped the harvest of a Jannata family whose daughter praised 7 October
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reported in HaKol HaYehudi that Rabbis for Human Rights volunteers helped Ammar al-Harimi harvest olives in Jannata near Bethlehem, and that his daughter had posted support for the 7 October massacre. This is Groner's report; the group had not responded in what was found.

items.headline: Shin Bet investigates suspected Qatari funding for Arab parties; Qatar denies it and the Mossad joins the probe
items.summary: Central Elections Committee chair Justice Noam Solberg directed Shin Bet head David Zini to investigate suspected foreign funding and election bribery aimed at the Arab parties (Israel8251, HaKol HaYehudi). The Shin Bet said the information came from its own collection under its legal duty to detect foreign influence, not from any party, and that no one outside the service but Solberg had seen it (Amir Bohbot). Qatar denied any interference or funding (Elisha Ben Kimon). Olam Katan reported that the Mossad is joining to trace how the money reached Israel. In the separate Negev case of Ra'am activists caught with cash, Elchanan Groner named Siaf Abu Rayash, a Bedouin doctor held since election day, and HaKol HaYehudi reported envelopes of cash, Ra'am ballots and Islamic Movement material.

places.name: Rahat
places.note: Nominatim; a general point for the Negev case, not a specific scene

items.headline: Army razes the Hebron homes of the two gunmen who killed Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, one week after the attack
items.summary: Soldiers and engineers of the Yahalom unit demolished the homes of the two gunmen from last week's attack at Yehuda junction near Hebron, in which Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem were killed and three more soldiers were lightly hurt (Ynet, Times of Israel). The gunmen, named by the Times of Israel as Mohammad Jaaba and Firas Jaaba, were killed in an exchange of fire. The army spokesman said the demolition came "only one week after the clash, an unprecedented time frame" for razing attackers' homes. The army also said soldiers tore down three memorials to terrorists in Judea and Samaria on Thursday. Simcha Raz posted video of the demolition.

places.name: Hebron
places.note: Nominatim; the homes' exact location was not published

places.name: Yehuda junction (attack site)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for the junction named צומת יהודה (listed as Beit Anun junction)

items.headline: Duvdevan and paratroopers arrest four arms dealers from a Jenin network; Channel 14 says they planned attacks on the new northern Samaria communities
items.summary: Duvdevan and Paratroopers Brigade forces, acting on Shin Bet intelligence, arrested four members of a Jenin network that traded weapons, a network that the army says it broke up during Operation Iron Wall (Channel 14, Yotam Deshe). Channel 14 reports the assessment that they planned attacks on the new communities in northern Samaria, apparently including Rom Gilboa, which went up this week. That link to the new communities is Channel 14's assessment.

items.headline: Border Police find a weapons cache with more than 2,300 rounds in Habla near Qalqilya; two arrested
items.summary: Border Police fighters raided the village of Habla next to Qalqilya overnight and found three pistols (one an airsoft gun), an M4 rifle, M16 parts, more than 2,300 rounds of several calibers and 67 magazines for M16, Kalashnikov, Uzi and pistols, police said (Ynet, Maariv). Two suspects were arrested. Simcha Raz added that silencers were found; that detail is his report.

items.headline: Binyamin council demands the army remove left-wing activists after clashes at Ma'ale Ahuvia farm near Kafr Malik; Yonatan Pollak among those arrested
items.summary: In its own account, the settler emergency room JSR said dozens of activists attacked an Israeli shepherd near Kafr Malik, that an Arab man was filmed punching an Israeli, and that Arabs and activists threw stones at Jewish shepherds of the Ma'ale Ahuvia farm (JSR, JSR). JSR also said videos in Arab media showing "settler violence" there were false. Srugim reported that security forces arrested Israeli and Palestinian activists, among them Yonatan Pollak and Roi Alani, and declared the area a closed military zone (Srugim). The Binyamin Regional Council called on the army "to act quickly and remove the anarchists" (i24 News). The Palestinian news agency WAFA said settlers attacked olive pickers in Kafr Malik and al-Mughayyir, and that two villagers and a foreign activist were arrested (WAFA).

places.name: Ma'ale Ahuvia farm
places.note: Approximate: point is Kafr Malik (Nominatim); the farm's exact site is not published

items.headline: Stones at shepherds and farmers from Maoz Yehuda to the Jordan Valley; one hurt near Armonot HaHashmonaim, an armed man flees from Sha'agat Yehuda farm
items.summary: JSR reported on Friday, all in its own account: several Arabs drove to the grazing land of the Maoz Yehuda farm in Samaria and threw stones at a shepherd, with no injuries (JSR); several Arabs threw stones at Jewish residents near the Armonot HaHashmonaim farm west of Jericho and one person was hurt (JSR, also reported by Simcha Raz); stones hit an Israeli car about 1 km north of Shdema junction in Gush Etzion, damaging the windshield (JSR); about 10 Arabs threw stones at the owner of the Yehonatan farm (JSR); and a man carrying a knife and a club approached the Sha'agat Yehuda farm and fled toward Tayasir (JSR). Israel8251 repeated the day's list. No news site had confirmed these by this edition.

places.name: Shdema junction area
places.note: Approximate: point is Shdema (Nominatim); the stoning was about 1 km north of the junction

places.name: Tayasir
places.note: Nominatim; the farm is nearby, exact site not published

items.headline: Police investigate suspected arson of an empty building between Susya and Avigayil, sprayed with "In blood and fire Judea will rise"
items.summary: Police opened an investigation into the suspected overnight burning of an empty building in open ground between Susya and Avigayil in the south Hebron Hills (Ynet). Graffiti on it read: "Regards from the evacuation. In blood and fire Judea fell, in blood and fire Judea will rise." Officers from the Hebron police station collected evidence. No suspects have been named.

places.name: Susya area
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point in the Susya area; the building's exact site is not published

items.headline: PA pays half salaries and opens schools three days a week as more than $7 billion in tax revenue stays frozen
items.summary: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has not transferred the tax revenue Israel collects for the Palestinian Authority for 18 months, and more than $7 billion is now held, the Times of Israel reports (Times of Israel). The PA is paying about 50% of salaries, and its schools open three days a week. With no new Israeli government yet, nothing is expected to change soon. PA Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh called the Israeli election "an internal Israeli matter."

items.headline: High Court orders the army to allow repairs of three burned homes in Jalud and to present a protection plan
items.summary: In a case brought by the Tubasi family and two other families who left their homes in Jalud, the High Court ordered the state to allow assessors and contractors to reach the burned homes within two weeks and to provide protection for repair work within a month, and awarded the families legal costs of NIS 51,000 (Israelinfo). The army and police had told the court that an earlier attempt, reported on 29 September, to return the families failed when about 200 Jewish residents threw stones, hurt three soldiers and burned the homes. That account is from the court ruling as reported; the order was issued Thursday.

items.headline: Army Hummer stolen from the Julis base in the south; maintenance battalion confined to base as military police investigate
items.summary: A military Hummer went missing from the Julis base in southern Israel, and military police opened an investigation, Elisha Ben Kimon reports (Ynet). The loss came to light Monday, when a similar vehicle was brought into the base's storage depot; a later check found the Hummer gone. All of Battalion 652, which maintains engineering and armored vehicles, was barred from leaving the base, and the army ordered an inventory count across vehicle companies. Ayelet Lash also reported that a large amount of ammunition was stolen this week from the Border Police base at Atarot; no news site had confirmed that by this edition.

places.name: Julis base (near Beit Shikma)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point returned for Julis in the south

items.headline: Supreme Court keeps the doctor suspected of buying votes for Ra'am in custody
items.summary: Justice Yechiel Kasher rejected the appeal of the doctor arrested on suspicion of trying to bribe voters to vote for Ra'am, saying the custody rested on the weight of the evidence and the risk that he would interfere with the investigation (Ynet).

items.headline: Man shot dead in Tel Sheva, the 190th killing in Arab society this year and the sixth in three days
items.summary: A man was shot dead in Tel Sheva in the Negev; police say the background is a criminal feud between families (Ynet). Ynet counts it as the 190th killing in Arab society since January and the sixth in three days, after shootings in Reineh, Arraba, Taibe and a killing in Kafr Qara.

items.headline: Two Jewish shepherds from the Giborei David farm are attacked with sticks and stones near Duma; police arrest an Anata man
items.summary: On Saturday morning, two Jewish shepherds from the Giborei David farm east of Duma in Binyamin were attacked while grazing their flock. In JSR's account, dozens of Arabs with sticks and stones ambushed them, both shepherds were hurt and treated by rescue teams, the flock was attacked, and far-left activists at the scene shouted support for the attackers (JSR Telegram, JSR on X). JSR also posted video and the testimony of the teenage shepherd (video, testimony). Israel Hayom confirmed that two Jewish shepherds from the farm were hurt near Duma by Palestinians throwing stones and swinging sticks, and that a suspect was arrested (Israel Hayom). Police told Walla that an Anata resident in his 50s was arrested on suspicion of assault after a report of "friction"; Judea and Samaria District police and the army gathered evidence, and he was questioned at the Binyamin station and held in custody (Walla, Srugim). Elchanan Groner wrote that the teenager had bruises on his head (Groner Telegram), and Eliav Libi wrote that soldiers took 35 minutes to arrive because an access road has not been opened (Libi on X); both are their own accounts. Peace Now's listing says the farm was set up in 2025 beside Route 505 and is also called "Duma East" (Peace Now). Haaretz and the activists give a different version (three hurt, including a Palestinian); see the short item lower down.

places.name: Giborei David farm
places.note: Approximate: Amud Anan map point for the farm; exact attack spot not published

items.headline: Groner: Jonathan Pollak and far-left activists bring Palestinians to harvest near Ateret and Kerem Binyamin
items.summary: Elchanan Groner wrote that activist Jonathan Pollak and other far-left activists brought Arabs to an olive harvest near Ateret and the Kerem Binyamin farm, which he called a "harvest provocation" (Groner Telegram, Groner on X). This is Groner's account; no second source was found, so it is unconfirmed. Background on Pollak: Jonathan Pollak page.

places.name: Ateret
places.note: Nominatim; Kerem Binyamin farm location not confirmed

items.headline: Lod: young Arabs drifting cars threaten pre-army academy students holding Friday-evening prayers in the market
items.summary: Makor Rishon reports that on Friday evening, students of a pre-army academy (mechina) who were holding the Kabbalat Shabbat prayers in the Lod market were confronted by young Arabs who drifted cars nearby, threatened to run them over and shouted "barra, barra" (Arabic for "out, out"). Police and Border Police broke up the crowd, and some of the young Arabs were reportedly detained. Residents told the paper that police also blamed the Jewish students (Makor Rishon). Only one source was found for this incident.

places.name: Lod
places.note: Nominatim (city center); the market spot was not plotted exactly

items.headline: Thieves strike the farm of fallen Shin Bet fighter Yossi Tahar in Bitzaron for the second time
items.summary: Overnight Friday to Saturday, thieves broke into the Tahar family farm in moshav Bitzaron in the south and stole a golf cart, an ATV, an off-road motorcycle and riding gear. Yossi Tahar, a commander in the Shin Bet's operational unit, was killed defending Kibbutz Mefalsim on Oct. 7, 2023. Similar equipment was stolen from the yard about a year ago. His widow, Liat Shor, said there are thefts in the moshav "twice a week" (Ynet). Police have not said who is suspected.

items.headline: Ayelet Lash: about 220 smuggling vehicles into the Arad area in a week, and 11 stolen off-road vehicles taken to the south Hebron Hills
items.summary: Reporter Ayelet Lash wrote that in one week about 220 vehicles smuggled about 2,000 illegal entrants from Judea and Samaria into the Arad area, and that 11 off-road vehicles stolen in the Negev were taken to the south Hebron Hills (Lash on X). She also wrote that a judge released suspects in the smuggling of 32 illegal entrants through a sewer pipe (Lash on X). These are her figures; no police or army source was found for them, so they are unconfirmed.

items.headline: Unconfirmed: Groner says a TikTok video shows the stolen army Hummer in the hands of a Bedouin group in the Negev
items.summary: Following the theft of an army Hummer from the Julis base (see the 31 Oct edition), Elchanan Groner wrote that a TikTok video seems to show the vehicle held by a Bedouin "militia" in the Negev (Groner Telegram). The army and police have not confirmed this, and the video was not checked.

places.name: Negev
places.note: Approximate: no place was named; point set at Tel Sheva area

items.headline: Triangle: a man about 30 is badly hurt in a shooting in Zemer; police suspect a criminal motive
items.summary: A man about 30 years old was badly hurt in a shooting in Zemer on Saturday night. Taibe police opened a search for the shooters and suspect a criminal background (Channel 14). Srugim and Maariv reported the same; Maariv also reported a 24-year-old moderately hurt in Umm al-Fahm, a 44-year-old woman moderately hurt in Tel Sheva and an 18-year-old moderately hurt in Pardes Hanna over the weekend.

items.headline: Itamar Eitam, son of Effi Eitam, enters the Knesset in the last seat of Religious Zionism
items.summary: Israel Hayom's list of the MKs who got in on the last seat of their party includes Lt. Col. (res.) Itamar Eitam, last on the Religious Zionism slate, which won six seats. He commanded a reserve battalion, was badly wounded in Gaza during the war and returned to command it. He is the son of Brig. Gen. (res.) Effi Eitam, a former National Religious Party minister under Ariel Sharon (Israel Hayom). Final seat counts are still subject to the official results.

items.headline: Luxembourg prepares to ban imports of goods from Judea and Samaria, though the trade is worth only about 10,000 to 15,000 euros
items.summary: Ynet reports that Luxembourg, which recognized a Palestinian state last year, is preparing to ban imports of goods from Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria without waiting for an EU decision. About two weeks ago its government approved an amendment to its 2018 foreign trade law allowing national import limits, and a separate bill to ban settlement goods outright was filed in parliament; neither is final. Local estimates put the direct trade at only 10,000 to 15,000 euros (about 35,000 to 52,000 shekels), so the step is symbolic (Ynet). The Netherlands has already banned such trade, according to Ynet.

items.headline: Haaretz profiles Samaria council head Yossi Dagan as the man driving roads, funding and foreign support
items.summary: A long Haaretz feature by Hagai Amit calls Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan "King of Samaria" and describes how he gets ministers to listen, funding to flow and foreign politicians to back his cause. It opens at the new Paduel bus terminal, which it says cost 10 million shekels, and the larger Rehalim terminal, which Dagan says cost 40 million (Haaretz). The paper frames this as a drive toward annexation; the figures were not checked elsewhere.

places.name: Rehalim
places.note: Nominatim (community; the bus terminal itself was not plotted)

items.headline: Jordan says it stopped 14 armed men trying to cross from Syria
items.summary: Jordan's armed forces said on Saturday that border guards stopped a group of 14 armed men trying to cross into northern Jordan from Syria, under heavy fire, with many casualties among the group (Haaretz/Reuters). It matters for the eastern border and weapons smuggling toward Judea and Samaria; no link to smuggling into Israel was reported.

places.name: Jordan-Syria border (north Jordan)
places.note: Approximate: no crossing point was named

items.headline: Haaretz and activist claims: soldiers halt a south Hebron Hills harvest; another version of the Duma clash
items.summary: Haaretz (Matan Golan) reports that soldiers stopped a Palestinian olive harvest in the south Hebron Hills after consulting an armed settler and told activists to leave the olives behind; the paper says there was no closure order. The army had not commented (Haaretz). On the Duma clash, Haaretz and activists say three people were hurt, including a Palestinian, and that police first held the Palestinian and two shepherds. These are their accounts.

places.name: South Hebron Hills
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point near Susya; exact grove not named

items.headline: A day of stone attacks: a mass stoning at Ma'ale Tidhar, and cars hit at Giti junction, the Jamma'in quarries junction and on the Galon road
items.summary: On Sunday, 1 Nov, JSR, the settlers' Judea and Samaria situation room, reported a run of stone attacks on Israeli drivers and residents. At 12:45 it reported a "massive" stoning at Ma'ale Tidhar in eastern Gush Etzion and later posted video credited to the volunteer group Rescue Without Borders (JSR on X, video). Elisha Yered, a settler activist from the hilltop community, wrote that men who came as olive "harvesters" from Beit Fajjar attacked hilltop residents on the access road; he said their faces are visible on video and that no one had been arrested yet (Yered on X). Earlier, at 10:38, JSR reported stones thrown at cars at Giti (Giti Avishar) junction on the Trans-Samaria road (JSR), and at 10:49 at the Jamma'in quarries junction, which Simcha Raz, a settlement-side reporter, places west of Tapuach junction (JSR, Raz). At 20:46 JSR said a car was hit on the Galon road in Gush Etzion, about 170 meters west of Taxi junction, and its windshield was damaged (JSR). No injuries were reported. The incidents also appear in the evening summary of @Israel8251, a settler-side incident tracker (summary). Police and army statements on these incidents were not found, so the details rest on these settlement-side sources.
items.source: JSR (settlers' situation room) / Elisha Yered / Simcha Raz / @Israel8251

places.name: Jamma'in (quarries junction is nearby)
places.note: Nominatim point for the village; the junction itself was not plotted (approximate)

places.name: Galon road near Taxi junction, Gush Etzion
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Gush Etzion junction

items.headline: Army inquiry into the Yehuda junction attack: a chamber safety insert caused jams in two soldiers' rifles, and the attack was directed by Hamas from Turkey
items.summary: Channel 14's military reporter Hallel Bitton Rosen reported on Sunday evening the new findings of the army's inquiry into the 23 Oct shooting at Yehuda junction near Hebron, in which Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, of Ashkelon and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, of Hod Hasharon were killed. According to the report, two soldiers' rifles jammed because a "mak-poruk" (a plastic insert that shows the chamber is empty) was still in the chamber. One of them cleared it and fired three rounds at the gunmen before he was hit. The army has since changed its instructions: soldiers on operations in the area must remove the insert. The report also says the attack was directed by Hamas operatives in Turkey. The IDF spokesperson said the inquiry has not yet been presented to the bereaved families (Channel 14). Bitton Rosen also posted the same findings and, later, footage of a jam during the Kiryat Arba security officer's response (X, footage). The findings have not yet been confirmed by a second outlet.

places.name: Yehuda junction (attack site)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for the junction named צומת יהודה

items.headline: Katz approves ending Operation Roar of Judah in Hebron after nine days, with two conditions
items.summary: Defense Minister Israel Katz on Sunday evening approved the army's request to end Operation "Roar of Judah" in Hebron, after a security meeting that began at 19:00 without Prime Minister Netanyahu, Channel 14 reported. Katz set two conditions: the army must keep the ability to evacuate city neighborhoods ready for future use, and the Palestinian Authority and other Palestinian bodies must be told that after another attack the evacuations will be used much more widely. The army had asked on Friday to end the operation after the attackers' homes were blown up, and the political leaders refused at that time (Channel 14; also Bitton Rosen on X). On the Palestinian side, Srugim, a religious-Zionist news site, reported that Palestinians moved out of their homes in Hebron say they will protest every day at 14:00 until they can return (Srugim). Ayelet Lash, a settlement-side commentator, reported shooting in Hebron overnight into Sunday (Lash on X; unconfirmed).

places.name: Hebron
places.note: City center (Nominatim); the operation was in the western neighborhoods

items.headline: Residents of Beit Lid and Qaddum pave an unauthorized road linking Route 55 and Route 57; the army blocks it
items.summary: Simcha Raz, a settlement-side reporter, wrote on Sunday that Palestinians from Beit Lid and Kafr Qaddum paved an unauthorized "strategic" road between Route 55 and Route 57 in Samaria. Residents of the Givat Shirat Zion hilltop warned about the work, the Kedumim local council turned to the army, and the army blocked the road on Saturday (Raz on X). The army has not confirmed this publicly, so the report is unconfirmed. Background on Palestinian building and planning: Khamaisi backgrounder on Palestinian planning.

items.headline: A shepherd from Jackson's farm in the Jordan Valley is attacked near Khirbet Tawil; five goats reported missing
items.summary: JSR reported at 14:35 on Sunday that "anarchists" (the settlers' term for left-wing activists) attacked a shepherd from Jackson's farm near Khirbet Tawil in the Jordan Valley area. One person was hurt, and about five goats were missing from the flock (JSR on X). No police statement was found; unconfirmed beyond JSR.

places.name: Khirbet Tawil area (east of Aqraba)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Aqraba; Khirbet Tawil itself was not found in Nominatim

items.headline: After Al Jazeera's film on Mohammed Deif, a large Nablus news page posts a Hamas poster; a settlement-side analyst warns of copycat attackers
items.summary: JSR reported that after Al Jazeera aired its documentary on the late Hamas military chief Mohammed Deif ("What Is Hidden Is Greater," broadcast on 30 Oct), the "Nablus News" page, with about 181,000 followers, posted a Hamas poster praising him (JSR on X). Yotam Deshe, a settlement-side security commentator, warned that such material can push lone attackers to act (Deshe on X). The follower count and poster are as JSR reported them.

items.headline: Police: 14 foreign nationals detained near a farm at Lubban al-Sharqiya are sent to the Population Authority for possible deportation
items.summary: Police said 14 foreign nationals were detained over the weekend on suspicion of involvement in a clash near a farm in the Lubban al-Sharqiya area. They were questioned at the Modiin Illit station on suspicion of breaking a lawful order and being in a closed military zone, and their files were sent to the Population and Immigration Authority for a hearing on deportation (Srugim, Channel 14). Simcha Raz called them "anarchists" who rioted at the farm (Raz on X). Makor Rishon's headline gave the number as 16; the police figure is 14.

items.headline: Settlement-side outlets on the harvest: Rabbis for Human Rights at the Beitar Illit fence, and US Reform groups behind the activists
items.summary: Olam Katan, a religious-Zionist weekly, described dozens of activists from Rabbis for Human Rights, most of them Reform rabbis, who came last weekend to "help" an Arab olive harvest right next to the Beitar Illit fence in Gush Etzion, mostly to be photographed, in the paper's account (Olam Katan on X). Elchanan Groner, a settlement-side journalist, wrote that delegations from US progressive and Reform groups, including the rabbis' group T'ruah, are behind the harvest "provocations" (Groner on X). Both are opinion reporting.

items.headline: Former US ambassador David Friedman visits Esh Kodesh: "Those living here deserve to live in peace"
items.summary: David Friedman, the former US ambassador to Israel, posted on Sunday that he visited Esh Kodesh in Binyamin, "a quiet village very close to all the noise we've been hearing lately," and wrote that its residents "deserve to live in peace" (Friedman on X).

items.headline: Arad's mayor describes an alleged vote-buying system in the Negev; the court rules on the Ra'am cash-envelope suspects
items.summary: In an interview with Olam Katan, Arad mayor Yair Maayan, a former director-general of the Bedouin Authority, described what he calls the bribery system behind the jump in Negev Arab turnout: suitcases of cash, fuel cards, and education budgets that he says flowed to Gaza (Olam Katan on X; his claims are unconfirmed). In court on Sunday, one of the three suspects in the Ra'am cash-envelope case had his custody extended by three days, a second was released under conditions, and the third was sent to house arrest, though police asked to delay that (Srugim). Separately, Srugim reported a suspicion that a Joint List MK received hundreds of thousands of shekels in cash, with no evidence so far that the money reached voters (Srugim).

items.headline: Two reports link new Arab MKs to groups in Turkey: Ta'al's Ahmad Darawshe and Ra'am's Abd al-Karim Masri
items.summary: Channel 14 reported that Ahmad Darawshe of Ta'al, the former aide to Ahmad Tibi who was elected eighth on the Joint List, met in 2021 in southern Turkey with officials of a Palestinian charity whose people have praised terrorists, including a man presented as a Fatah representative (Channel 14). Elchanan Groner, citing an investigation by the right-wing site HaKol HaYehudi, wrote that new Ra'am MK Sheikh Abd al-Karim Masri headed the "Humanitarian Deeds" association, which was dissolved and had its bank account frozen over suspected terror financing, and that he signed a cooperation deal with the Turkish group Hayat Yolu (Groner on X). Groner gives Masri's list place as 6th on X and 8th on Telegram, so it is unconfirmed; the claims about Masri are unconfirmed by a second outlet.

items.headline: Police raids in Negev Bedouin towns turn up three M-16 rifles, pistols and hashish; an illegal camel race in a firing zone is stopped
items.summary: Be'er Sheva Net, a local news site, reported a broad police operation in recent days in the Negev's Bedouin communities, with the national guard of the Border Police and the Yoav unit. In Rahat police found three M-16 assault rifles, two Glock pistols, hundreds of rounds and about 25 kg of hashish; in Tel Sheva a police drone led to the arrest of a 15-year-old who fled after attacking his family and was found with ammunition and an improvised gun (Be'er Sheva Net, Srugim). Srugim adds that suspects were also arrested in Arara, Rahat and Tarabin with stolen army ammunition. Police also stopped an illegal camel race planned in a firing zone near Route 222 at Bir Hadaj and held a man and a minor from Rahat (Srugim, Channel 14).

items.headline: 74 Palestinians without permits found in one building in Kafr Qasim; 18 caught crossing south of Tarqumiya; smuggling convoys still pass Carmel
items.summary: Border Police detectives raided a residential building in Kafr Qasim with a court search warrant and found 74 Palestinians staying in Israel without permits; all were sent back to Judea and Samaria (Srugim). On Saturday night Border Police, soldiers and Kiryat Gat police caught 18 people who crossed the seam line south of the Tarqumiya crossing, 15 of them found by drone hiding on a wooded hill (Srugim). Elchanan Groner wrote that smuggling convoys from the Hebron Hills to the Negev keep passing the edge of the Barkai neighborhood of Carmel and that the security services are "waiting for a disaster" (Groner on X; his account).

places.name: Carmel (Barkai neighborhood)
places.note: Community point; the neighborhood was not plotted

items.headline: Arab teen, 15, charged with vandalizing holy books and setting a fire in an Afula synagogue out of hostility to Jews
items.summary: The Northern District prosecutor charged a 15-year-old Arab boy with breaking into a synagogue in Afula on 19 Oct, throwing holy books on the floor, pouring liquids on them, setting toilet paper alight and stealing the charity box. According to the investigation he acted out of hostility toward Jews, shortly after an argument with his family. The charges include damaging property with a racist motive (Channel 14). Makor Rishon's headline reports the same case.

items.headline: Four Arab minors from a-Tur are arrested for throwing firebombs at Jewish homes in East Jerusalem
items.summary: Police arrested four minors from the a-Tur neighborhood on Saturday on suspicion of throwing firebombs at Jewish homes in East Jerusalem. The acts were recorded as they happened, and the court extended their custody to Wednesday, 4 Nov (Channel 14). No second outlet was found; the details are as Channel 14 reported them from police.

items.headline: A young man is shot dead in Isfiya, adding to the year's record of killings in Arab communities
items.summary: A man was killed early Sunday (06:25) in Isfiya on Mount Carmel; Magen David Adom found him with penetrating wounds (Srugim). Haaretz named him as Amir Abu Hamda, 23, of Yarka, with a criminal background, and counted 228 people killed this year, 188 of them Arab citizens (Haaretz). Srugim gave his age as about 25; Haaretz says 23.

items.headline: A Christian prayer house in Nahariya is vandalized; police are investigating
items.summary: Nahariya police opened an investigation after damage was done to a city building used as a Christian house of prayer; police said all lines of inquiry are being checked (Maariv). Ynet's feed says the building serves the Christian community of former South Lebanon Army soldiers, and religious images were smashed; Kan's headline reports the same.

items.headline: Burglars at Tel Menashe break a safe and take only the weapon
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reported a first summary of a burglary at Tel Menashe in northern Samaria: the burglars lifted a shutter, broke open a safe with a hammer and screwdriver, and took only the gun. New instructions tell residents not to show their weapons to workers and tradesmen (Groner on Telegram). Unconfirmed by a second source.

items.headline: Settlement-side voices: Israeli Arabs move freely into Area A while Jews are barred, and Israelis still take cars there for repair
items.summary: Eliav Libi, a settlement-side writer, called it "a surreal reality" that Jews may not enter Area A while Israeli Arabs come and go freely, and said this is also dangerous (Libi on X). Ayelet Lash wrote that Israelis keep taking cars for repair in Judea and Samaria despite the ban (Lash on X). Opinion.

places.name: Nablus (Area A)
places.note: Approximate: no place named; marker at Nablus

items.headline: Palestinian reports: large army forces enter the old city market in Nablus
items.summary: Citing Palestinian reports, Srugim said large army forces entered the market in Nablus's old city on Sunday morning (Srugim). Ultra Palestine, a Palestinian news site, also reported the raid on X. The army did not comment.

items.headline: Complaint: Border Police raided Givat Shirat Zion and beat a sleeping teenager (Makor Rishon headline)
items.summary: Makor Rishon's headline and summary say Border Police raided a building on the Givat Shirat Zion hilltop before dawn, woke a minor with violence, arrested him and then accused him of attacking the officers; Honenu, a legal aid group for Jewish suspects, asked the police internal affairs unit to investigate (Makor Rishon). Not confirmed elsewhere.

places.name: Givat Shirat Zion (near Kedumim)
places.note: Approximate: the hilltop is not in Nominatim; marker at Kedumim

items.headline: Palestinian and left-wing claims: 19 attacks on olive pickers on Saturday; Haaretz urges Israelis to side with the harvesters
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, as reported by Ultra Palestine, claimed 19 attacks by settlers on olive pickers and their land in seven governorates on Saturday, 31 Oct (Ultra Palestine; PA figures, unconfirmed). A Haaretz editorial said Israelis must take the Palestinians' side in the harvest (Haaretz).
items.source: Ultra Palestine (citing the PA commission) / Haaretz

items.headline: Ganim is connected to the national power grid, the last of the four northern Samaria settlements uprooted in 2005
items.summary: On Monday, 2 Nov, Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan, Israel Electric Corporation staff and Ganim's local committee switched on the regular power supply to Ganim. Arutz 7 reports that this completes the reconnection to the national grid of all four northern Samaria settlements evacuated in the 2005 disengagement: Homesh, Sa-Nur, Kadim and now Ganim (Arutz 7, Olam Katan). Dagan recited the Shehecheyanu blessing (said on a first-time occasion) and said 11 communities have been set up in northern Samaria in place of the four that were uprooted. Energy Minister Eli Cohen said: "We are correcting the disengagement, erasing the Green Line and continuing to advance sovereignty in practice," adding that this is a step "on the way to a million residents in Judea and Samaria." Settler-side accounts also posted the news (@Israel8251, Simcha Raz).

items.headline: Givat Ora Yisrael: a bulldozer brings down a roof with youths on it; Honenu demands a criminal probe; the army says 18 were arrested for attacking forces
items.summary: On Monday morning, 2 Nov, more than 100 Border Police officers and Civil Administration staff came to demolish the homes of two families living on the Givat Ora Yisrael hilltop near Rehelim, Olam Katan reports (Olam Katan). Video posted by Elchanan Groner, a settlement-side reporter, shows the bulldozer bringing down a roof while residents stand on it, and they fall with it (Groner on Telegram, video on X). Honenu, a legal aid group for Jewish suspects, wrote to the police internal investigations unit asking for a criminal probe, and to the regional commander asking him to freeze all demolitions in the area and suspend the force commander; its lawyer Eladi Weisel called it a "shocking" event in which minors fell from a height (Honenu via Groner). Residents of nearby communities blocked roads with burning tires on the Emanuel–Yakir road and at Ariel junction, and the organizers apologized to stuck drivers (Simcha Raz, Elisha Yered). A Central Command source told Raz that officers begged the youths to come down and that the shovel tilted the low roof so they would slide down safely (Raz). The army said rioters burned tires and attacked forces; 18 were arrested, and one seized car held flammable materials, attack tools and pepper spray. Kan, which places the outpost near Salfit, says it has been removed 15 times (Kan, army statement via @Israel8251, Emanuel Fabian).
items.source: Olam Katan / Elchanan Groner / Honenu / Simcha Raz / Elisha Yered / Kan / IDF

places.name: Givat Ora Yisrael (near Rehelim)
places.note: Approximate: hilltop not in Nominatim; marker at Rehelim

items.headline: High Court hears petition against demolishing PA-built homes in the Judean Desert "agreed reserve"; Gush Etzion head: "It endangers residents"
items.summary: The High Court held another hearing on Monday on the Palestinian petition against demolishing homes built without permits in the "agreed reserve," an area of the Judean Desert handed to the Palestinians in the late 1990s under the Oslo accords on condition it stay an open nature reserve (Olam Katan). In August 2024 the security cabinet took planning powers in the area back from the PA; the court then issued an interim order that has frozen demolitions for two years. Gush Etzion Regional Council head Yaron Rosenthal said Bethlehem-area residents built thousands of homes there in the past seven years, that this is "a dramatic security threat" to eastern Gush Etzion and could cut Tekoa, Nokdim and Kfar Eldad off from the desert, and that the court should not intervene in a policy decision. The state's position is that only buildings put up after the cabinet decision should be demolished (Simcha Raz). See also the Khamaisi backgrounder on Palestinian planning.
items.source: Olam Katan / Gush Etzion Regional Council / Simcha Raz

places.name: Agreed reserve, Judean Desert (east of Gush Etzion)
places.note: Approximate: marker at Nokdim; the reserve lies to the east

items.headline: Ariel: developer chosen for urban renewal project of 558 apartments
items.summary: Israel Hayom reports that residents of 10 buildings (90 apartments) on Derech HaTzionut 55–73 in Ariel chose the B.S.R. group to tear them down and build 7 new buildings with 558 housing units, less than a year after they organized; the final size still needs approval from the authorities (Israel Hayom).

items.headline: Settlers' situation room: shepherds attacked at four farms, stones at a bus and a car, and arson near Zibda
items.summary: JSR, the settlers' Judea and Samaria situation room, reported a string of incidents on 2 Nov: Arabs attacked a Jewish shepherd with clubs in the grazing land of the Kela David farm in Binyamin; stones were thrown at a shepherd from the Bakar Amichai farm in the Jordan Valley; 15 Arabs attacked a shepherd west of Kafr Malik; about 30 Arabs threw stones at a shepherd south of the Armonot HaHashmonaim farm in Binyamin, damaging a Ranger vehicle; stones hit a car's windshield on Route 60 between the two schools of Lubban al-Sharqiya; stones were thrown at a bus in al-Auja; and several fires were set near Zibda in Binyamin and put out. No one was hurt in these (JSR on Telegram, JSR on X). Elisha Yered said a youth from the Tzur Levavi farm was hit in the hand by a stone thrown by Arab olive pickers (Yered). @Israel8251 counted 8 incidents for the day (summary). No army or police statements were found, so the details rest on settlement-side sources.

places.name: Kela David, Armonot HaHashmonaim and Zibda (Binyamin)
places.note: Approximate: farms not in Nominatim; marker at Ofra in Binyamin

items.headline: Stone through a car window near Funduq injures an Israeli driver
items.summary: JSR reported that at about 3:30 a.m. on 2 Nov, Arabs at the edge of the village of Funduq, on Route 55 in Samaria, threw a stone that broke the window of an Israeli car and hurt the driver (JSR on Telegram, JSR on X). The driver's condition was not reported.

items.headline: Delivery man from Tamra arrested after harming a girl in a South Hebron Hills settlement
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reports that a delivery man of about 50 from Tamra, an Arab town in the Galilee, harmed a minor girl while delivering an order in a South Hebron Hills settlement; after a report to the local security coordinator he was held and arrested by police, and an indictment is expected (Groner on Telegram, HaKol HaYehudi). The settlement was not named, and no police statement was found.

places.name: South Hebron Hills
places.note: Approximate: settlement not named; marker at Mitzpe Yair

items.headline: The army ends its Hebron operation after about 10 days: four weapons found, a tunnel sealed, 25 vehicles seized; the Hebron municipality celebrates
items.summary: The army spokesman said the operation in Hebron's Hamas-linked al-Hamoula neighborhood, launched after the Yehuda junction attack that killed two soldiers, is complete (Makor Rishon). Forces from Duvdevan, Maglan, the Paratroopers and other units searched hundreds of buildings, detained and questioned dozens of suspects, sealed an underground cavity near the home of a terrorist involved in the gunfight, and seized 25 illegal unregistered cars of the type the attackers used. Only four weapons were found; army sources said warning in advance of the entry may have given people time to hide weapons. The Hebron municipality, through the group Adalah, had petitioned the High Court to return evacuated residents and stop the demolitions. HaKol HaYehudi's headline says the municipality celebrated the end of the operation with Palestinian flags and armed PA security men (HaKol HaYehudi). See also Simcha Raz and Emanuel Fabian.
items.source: Makor Rishon / HaKol HaYehudi / Simcha Raz / Emanuel Fabian

items.headline: Police to pay 10,000 shekels to a settler whose beard an officer tore out at a 2023 protest near Ateret
items.summary: Honenu reports that under a settlement given the force of a court ruling, police will pay 10,000 shekels to Dvir Ilan; at a 2023 protest near Ateret an officer was filmed pulling out half of Ilan's beard. The officer faced a disciplinary trial and was acquitted on grounds of doubt (Honenu via Groner).

items.headline: Liberman: the PA is the "foreign entity" that meddled in the Arab-sector vote; Shin Bet reportedly probing PA money to the Joint List
items.summary: Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman said on 2 Nov that the foreign entity suspected of passing money to the Joint List is the Palestinian Authority, which he said guided both the Joint List and Ra'am in the election (Arutz 7). Israel Hayom reports that the Shin Bet probe is examining suspected transfers of money from the PA to the Joint List to encourage Arab turnout, with the money said to come from Qatar. Liberman added that the election was not stolen. A source familiar with the probe told Israel Hayom that even the worst suspicions would not change the results (Israel Hayom, @Israel8251).

items.headline: Hussein al-Sheikh asks France's envoy to help stop "Israeli actions"; Ramallah governor who meets freed terrorists attends
items.summary: JSR reports that Hussein al-Sheikh met André Parant, France's special envoy for "strengthening the State of Palestine," and urged France to act to stop "Israeli actions" and back a state on the 1967 lines with East Jerusalem as its capital. Ramallah and al-Bireh governor Laila Ghannam, a Fatah central committee member who JSR says meets weekly with freed terrorists and families of convicted terrorists, also took part (JSR on Telegram, JSR on X).

items.headline: Nablus governor at Balfour anniversary event: "We do not give up the right of return"
items.summary: JSR reports that Nablus governor Ghassan Daghlas, speaking at a PA event marking the Balfour Declaration anniversary, called it a turning point in Palestinian suffering and stressed the "right of return" and a state with Jerusalem as its capital (JSR on Telegram, JSR on X).

items.headline: Galilee: Shfar'am man, 21, indicted for swearing loyalty to ISIS
