items.summary: An indictment was filed on 2 Nov in Haifa against Mohammed Suwaitat, 21, of Shfar'am, Kan reports. Investigators say he swore loyalty to ISIS, posted its material online, corresponded with its supporters and tried to persuade friends to join (Kan, Ynet, JNS, Groner).

items.headline: Rahat: man shot dead, two hurt, after hours of gunfire; police mission headquarters seizes weapons
items.summary: A man was shot dead and two were hurt in Rahat on 2 Nov; Haaretz counts 230 people killed in the Arab community since the start of the year, and residents reported gunfire for hours (Haaretz). Be'er Sheva Net's headline says the police mission headquarters set up to answer the shootings seized weapons and arrested suspects in Rahat (Be'er Sheva Net).

items.headline: Regavim on Bedouin building in Negev firing zones; Ben-Gurion conference panel: "More sovereignty in Judea and Samaria than in the Negev"
items.summary: Regavim, a group that campaigns against illegal building, posted an i24 report on Bedouin homes inside Negev army firing zones and warned that Arab parties' first condition for backing any government is to stop enforcement in the Negev (Regavim). At Makor Rishon's Ben-Gurion conference, Uri Safir of HaShomer HaChadash said there are "at least tens of thousands" of illegal homes in the Negev and that "there is more sovereignty in Judea and Samaria than in the Negev," because the government carries out its will there but not in the Negev (Makor Rishon).

items.headline: Jerusalem: undercover agent exposes weapons and drug market; 18 charged
items.summary: Ynet reports that 18 people were charged with weapons and drug dealing after a police undercover agent operation in Jerusalem (Ynet). HaKol HaYehudi says one suspect offered the agent 40 pistols (HaKol HaYehudi). Separately, Jerusalem deputy mayor Aryeh King said work began on a police station between French Hill and Issawiya (King on X).

items.headline: Bones found in the Negev identified as Nivin al-Amrani, murdered by her brother in 2020
items.summary: Ynet reports that bones found in the Negev were identified as the remains of Nivin al-Amrani, who was murdered by her brother in 2020 (Ynet).

places.name: Negev
places.note: Approximate: find site not given; marker at Beersheba

items.headline: Palestinian claim: about 120 Shuafat camp families' bank accounts seized over property tax
items.summary: Ultra Palestine, a Palestinian news site, says about 120 families in the Shuafat refugee camp had bank accounts seized over unpaid Jerusalem property tax (Ultra Palestine on X). Unconfirmed.

items.headline: Left-wing +972 Magazine launches "The West Bank transformed" project
items.summary: +972 Magazine, a left-wing outlet, launched a project it calls "The West Bank transformed" on changes under the current government (+972 on X). Advocacy.

items.headline: Route 55: new traffic lights go up and the Funduq bypass is set to open in about two months
items.summary: During a tour by Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan, Karnei Shomron council head Yehonatan Kuznitz and the state roads company Netivei Israel, officials said the Funduq bypass section of the Route 55 widening project is expected to open to traffic in about two months, with one lane in each direction. The full widening to four lanes is planned for summer 2027, and the project now costs about a quarter of a billion shekels (Arutz 7). New traffic lights are already in place; work on the western section, from Jinsafut junction to Karnei Shomron, is to start soon, and a date has been set to switch on the light at Gilad junction. Route 55 links the Route 6 and Kfar Saba area with the hilltop communities and northern Samaria. Dagan called it a milestone toward "a million residents in Samaria" and "a safer drive, both for security and road safety." The bypass takes traffic around Funduq, where JSR reported a driver hurt by a stone on 2 Nov.

items.headline: Court bars Elazar's local association from cutting water and power to Netiv HaAvot homes
items.summary: The local affairs court in Kiryat Arba accepted a petition by families in the Netiv HaAvot neighborhood of Elazar in Gush Etzion and issued a permanent order barring the Elazar cooperative association, which runs the community's services, from cutting off their water and electricity (Arutz 7, Srugim). The association had told the families it would cut them off amid a dispute over their rights to the plots and the process of putting the neighborhood's land in order. Judge Bialin Elazar wrote that "a property dispute, however complex, must be settled in the proper courts and not by denying basic services needed for human life," and called the threat a misuse of governing power meant to force the families off the plots. The association was ordered to pay the families 5,000 shekels in costs. The families were represented by lawyers Aryeh Arbus and Emanuel Nahon.

items.headline: Northern Samaria: Groner tours new farms and Geva Shomron; a map of new communities circulates
items.summary: Elchanan Groner, a settlement-side reporter, posted from a day in northern Samaria that farms, communities and roads are opening, with photos of Geva Shomron, the new community at the former Paratroopers base, and praise for Menashe Brigade commander Col. Matan Feldman (Groner, Groner, second post). Simcha Raz shared a map by Ben Tzion Macales of the new communities in northern Samaria and the Jordan Valley (Raz). These are the posters' own accounts.

places.name: Geva Shomron (next to Sa-Nur)
places.note: Approximate: point is Sa-Nur (Nominatim); the new community is on the former Paratroopers base beside it

items.headline: Binyamin got 105 of the 1,391 portable shelters placed nationwide; Ganz answers a Haaretz report
items.summary: Figures published by Haaretz show that 105 portable shelters were placed in Binyamin communities since the start of the "Roaring Lion" operation, out of 1,391 nationwide, and 423 in Judea and Samaria overall; other councils include Kiryat Shmona (64), al-Kasum (55), Upper Galilee (40) and Mateh Asher (36) (Channel 14, Olam Katan). In Binyamin every caravan neighborhood got shelters. Yesha Council head Israel Ganz said the national plan, about 80 million shekels, grew out of his push with Defense Minister Israel Katz and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, and that "the days when residents of Judea and Samaria were second-class citizens are over." The Haaretz report itself was not opened.

places.name: Binyamin (area)
places.note: Approximate: marker at Ofra in Binyamin

items.headline: Kiryat Arba–Hebron council expects more than 50,000 visitors this weekend
items.summary: Srugim reports that the Kiryat Arba–Hebron local council is preparing to host more than 50,000 visitors in Hebron on 6–7 Nov for its large annual weekend event, with lodging, meals, lectures, tours and a large business fair; council head Israel Bramson has invited the public (Srugim).

items.headline: U.S. House Speaker Johnson praises naming Route 60 the "Biblical Highway"
items.summary: In a letter, U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson praised Israel's decision to give Route 60, the main north-south road through Judea and Samaria, the official name "Derech HaTanach" (the Biblical Highway), likening it to Route 66 (Jerusalem Post). The government plan, advanced by Prime Minister Netanyahu and Transportation Minister Miri Regev, funds new signs and the development of heritage and tourism sites along the road; a ceremony was held in June.

places.name: Route 60 (Shiloh area)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point for Shiloh, near Route 60

items.headline: Homesh yeshiva says it will set up a yeshiva at Ras Abu Nemel in Area A
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reports that the Homesh yeshiva has set its next goal: a yeshiva at "Ras Abu Nemel," deep in Area A (land under full PA control under the Oslo accords), as part of a call to cancel the Oslo accords (Groner on Telegram). No date, permit or army response was reported, and the exact spot was not given. Settlement-side source.

places.name: Homesh
places.note: Nominatim point for Homesh; Ras Abu Nemel itself was not located

items.headline: Samaria Brigade seizes two diggers and a loader at Area C quarries near Urif
items.summary: Elchanan Groner reports that the Samaria Brigade seized two diggers and a loader that were quarrying in Area C at the Urif quarries, on the side facing Yitzhar (Groner on Telegram). No army statement was found. Settlement-side source.

items.headline: Regavim video: illegal Palestinian building in Area C continues despite February enforcement powers
items.summary: Regavim, a right-wing group that tracks unlicensed Palestinian building, posted a video saying illegal construction in Area C goes on despite the enforcement powers granted in February (Regavim on X). Advocacy; no figures were given. See also the Khamaisi backgrounder on Palestinian planning.

items.headline: Former U.S. ambassador Friedman meets hilltop activists at the home of a man under house arrest
items.summary: Elisha Yered, a settler activist, says he hosted former U.S. ambassador David Friedman for a meeting with hilltop activists at the home of Roeh Ze'ev in Givat Tel Talpiot; Ze'ev is under an administrative house-arrest order signed by the Central Command head, Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth (Yered). A critic, @IhabHassane, noted that Yered is under EU sanctions (post). Friedman's own account was not found on X.

places.name: Givat Tel Talpiot (not located)
places.note: Approximate: hilltop not found on maps; general West Bank marker

items.headline: Jenin cell made a rocket body and ran three test launches; six charged
items.summary: Police and the Shin Bet said six Jenin-area residents in their 30s were arrested in recent months on suspicion of building rockets and explosive devices for use against Israel and its forces. Investigators say the cell made a rocket body and bombs and carried out three test launches; the main suspect got instructions on explosive materials from a person outside Israel over a messaging app. An M16 rifle, an RPG part and written instructions were seized (Arutz 7, Emanuel Fabian). The Jerusalem Post reports that one suspect said the tests showed gains in power and range and that the cell improved the rockets after each launch, and another admitted selling them weapons and getting explosives; it says six were indicted on Tuesday, while the police said indictments were expected in the coming days (Jerusalem Post, JNS). JSR, the settlers' situation room, also posted it (JSR).
items.source: Israel Police / Shin Bet via Arutz 7, Jerusalem Post, JNS, Emanuel Fabian

items.headline: JSR: several Israelis hurt by stones at Ma'ale Tidhar; shepherds stoned at Kornit and Tomer farms; flag vandalized near Kiryat Arba
items.summary: JSR, the settlers' situation room, reported on 3 Nov that about 15 Arabs threw stones at a group of Israelis at Ma'ale Tidhar, hurting several (JSR on Telegram, JSR on X); about 5 stoned a shepherd in the grazing land of the Kornit farm near Kafr Malik, and 4 stoned a shepherd at the Tomer farm in Gush Etzion, with no one hurt (Kornit, Tomer). JSR also says an Israeli flag was vandalized on a road near Kiryat Arba, with a note in Arabic naming a "Sa'ir battalion" (JSR). Ayelet Lash listed more incidents, including at Deir Nidham and Bardala and on Route 60 (Lash). No army or police statement was found; these are JSR's own accounts.

places.name: Tomer farm, Gush Etzion
places.note: Approximate: marker at Gush Etzion junction

items.headline: Army sources say resistance to outpost removals is growing; Army Radio says rioters get advance word of the operations
items.summary: Haaretz quotes army sources who say hilltop activists are increasingly blocking roads, burning tires, throwing stones and attacking soldiers and police during removals of unauthorized outposts, and link this to the tense political climate (Haaretz, left-leaning). Arutz 7, citing Army Radio, reports that before Monday's removal in Samaria the rioters knew in advance when the Border Police would leave and from which base, set up burning roadblocks at four spots, and gathered about 150 people; it says the army has not answered for over a month how many leak investigations it has opened (Arutz 7). After that removal, suspected Jewish extremists burned two cars in Majdal Bani Fadil, south of Nablus, per Palestinian reports cited by the Jerusalem Post; 18 Israelis had been arrested at the outpost (Jerusalem Post).

items.headline: Military Advocate General: soldiers who meet Jewish violence must step in
items.summary: Speaking at a conference of the International Association of Jewish Lawyers and Jurists, Military Advocate General Maj. Gen. Itai Ofir said of Jewish violence in Judea and Samaria: "We have not yet managed to stop the violence. Soldiers who encounter violence may not stand by. They must intervene." He also rejected a film that accuses the army of war crimes in Gaza (Ynet).

items.headline: Supreme Court lets young man convicted over the 2018 death of Aisha Rabi stay free until his appeal
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ruth Ronen delayed the 13-year prison term of a young Jewish man convicted of manslaughter in the 2018 death of Aisha Rabi, a Palestinian woman killed by a rock thrown at her family's car. She cited the circumstantial evidence, the split 2–1 verdict in the Lod District Court, eight years without new offenses, and his being a minor at the time (Arutz 7, Kan). His lawyers, Yarom Halevy and Adi Keidar, are from Honenu, a legal aid group for Jewish suspects.

items.headline: Soldiers report jams caused by the MAG machine gun safety insert; safety department refuses to act, reporter says
items.summary: Hallel Bitton Rosen reports that dozens of soldiers say the chamber safety insert (the "MAG fork") jams their guns during operations, and that the army's safety department refuses to act (Bitton Rosen). This follows the 2 Nov item on the probe into the insert after an incident at Yehuda junction. No army response was found.

items.headline: 33,150 eggs with forged stamps seized in Beit Jala
items.summary: Police, Border Police, the Gush Etzion Brigade and the Poultry Board raided a warehouse in Beit Jala and found 1,105 trays holding 33,150 eggs stamped with forged marks of two licensed Israeli marketers, plus the stamping machine; the eggs were destroyed and the machine seized (Israel Hayom).

items.headline: Shin Bet looks at suspected PA money to Arab party figures; attorney general sets conditions on questioning aides
items.summary: N12, as cited by the Jerusalem Post, reports that the Shin Bet is checking whether the Palestinian Authority sent money to Arab party figures to sway the 27 Oct election; the probe is at an early stage. It is part of a wider probe of suspected Qatari money to a Joint List figure. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara required that an evidence basis against the lawmaker be set before his parliamentary aides are questioned; Likud accused her of blocking the probe (Jerusalem Post, Ayelet Lash). HaKol HaYehudi reports that the Lavi group threatens to petition the court (HaKol HaYehudi).
items.source: Jerusalem Post (citing N12) / Ayelet Lash / HaKol HaYehudi

items.headline: Abbas opens the first Palestinian cement factory, in Jericho; an Israeli expert warns about tunnels
items.summary: PA President Mahmoud Abbas opened a cement factory in Jericho, in Area A, on 2 Nov; the Jericho Cement Industry Company says it can make 1.3 million tons a year and will start with 100 workers. Maurice Hirsch of the Jerusalem Center for Public Affairs warned that unmonitored cement could be used for tunnels; Prof. Arie Reich of Bar-Ilan said Israel has no say over the PA's permits in Area A under the Oslo II accord (Jerusalem Post).

items.headline: PA commission: military order takes 26.5 dunams for an "Ateret–Neve Tsuf emergency road"
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, via the PA news agency WAFA, says military order T/48/26, issued on 28 Oct and valid to the end of 2028, takes 26.473 dunams (about 6.5 acres) of land of Deir Nidham, Umm Safa and Atara for a road linking Ateret and Neve Tsuf (Halamish); it says 5.891 dunams are classed as state land (WAFA, Ultra Palestine). The order was not seen directly and the army has not commented. PA-side claim. See also the Khamaisi backgrounder on Palestinian planning.

items.headline: B'Tselem posts its account of the July 2025 deaths at al-Mazra'a ash-Sharqiya
items.summary: B'Tselem, a left-wing rights group, posted its account of 11 July 2025 at al-Mazra'a ash-Sharqiya near Ramallah, where it says settlers shot dead Muhammad Shalabi, 23, and Seif Allah Mislet, 21, died of heart failure after being beaten and fleeing (B'Tselem on X). Advocacy; B'Tselem's own account.

items.headline: Humvee stolen from the Julis base found hidden in a packing house in Amioz
items.summary: The army Humvee stolen last week from the Julis base was found hidden in a packing house in Moshav Amioz, near the Gaza border, after a tip; Segev Shalom police seized it and are looking for the thieves, and no arrests were reported (Maariv, Kan, Olam Katan, Emanuel Fabian). Arutz 7's headline says "in the Bedouin dispersal" (unrecognized Bedouin villages), but its text also names the Amioz packing house (Arutz 7). Kan says the base is in the north, while Maariv places Julis in the Lachish area in the south. This updates the unconfirmed 1 Nov item.
items.source: Maariv / Kan / Olam Katan / Arutz 7 / Emanuel Fabian

places.name: Julis base (near Beit Shikma)
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point returned for Julis in the south

items.headline: Police counterterror unit catches three suspects in an Arara murder after a year hiding in Judea and Samaria
items.summary: The Yamam, the police counterterror unit, arrested three men wanted over the October 2025 killing of Samih Talqat Abu Arar in Arara in the Negev, in a blood feud between families; they had fled to Judea and Samaria. One was caught at a bus terminal near Rehelim and two in a hideout in Funduq (Be'er Sheva Net, Olam Katan). Four others were already charged.

places.name: Arara BaNegev
places.note: Approximate: Nominatim point at the town's junction

items.headline: Rahat committee head: "No family in the Negev without weapons"; video of a youth firing an M16 at his family
items.summary: Dr. Awad Abu Freih, chair of Rahat's popular committee (an unofficial body of parties and clans), told Radio a-Shams that every family in the Negev is armed, including automatic weapons and grenades, that over 25 active or likely feuds were counted in Rahat, and blamed the state (HaKol HaYehudi). Channel 14 aired security video from about two and a half weeks ago of a youth of about 18 firing an M16 at his family's home and later at his uncle; he was arrested (Channel 14). Police figures cited there show a 153% rise in shooting indictments and 625 guns seized in the past year. Ayelet Lash asked why there was no response to more gunfire in Rahat (Lash).

items.headline: Jewish families move into eight homes bought in secret on the edge of Jericho
items.summary: On 4 Nov, Jewish families entered eight homes on the outskirts of Jericho, near the Hasmonean Palaces archaeological site. The Nachala movement led the purchase, with backing from the Binyamin Regional Council. According to the organizers, the homes are on state land in Area C, inside the Binyamin council's area. They say the homes were bought "in full cash" and that ownership documents back the deals. The plan was kept secret until the families entered (Arutz 7; Besheva; Binyamin council and Nachala statement via Elchanan Groner). Israel Ganz, head of the Binyamin council and chair of the Yesha Council, said he was 16 when he walked into Jericho with hundreds of teenagers on the night Israel handed it over under the Oslo Accords. He said: "We are taking apart the Oslo Accords through actions, house after house, family after family." Nachala chair Daniella Weiss called it "a new chapter" in Jewish settlement in Jericho (Arutz 7). Yotam Deshe of Israel Hayom reported that Ganz toured the area in secret on a dirt bike the Friday before, so he would not be recognized (Yotam Deshe on X). Simcha Raz wrote that Palestinians began building in this spot only in 2008, that the building damaged antiquities, and that a new community, Dia, went up nearby in the Hasmonean Palaces area (Raz on X; Raz on X). Elchanan Groner gave the number as nine homes and reported that a local Arab man welcomed the families, saying Bedouin used to steal from his father (Groner; Groner). Yahel Roth-Cohen pushed back on X that this is the outskirts of Jericho, not the city itself (X). The number of homes (eight or nine) differs between sources. Other sides: Haaretz names the neighborhood as Ad-Duyuk at-Tahta and says the IDF stated the entry was not coordinated with it. Haaretz argues that because the land is state land, the settlers could not have bought ownership from Palestinians (Haaretz). Peace Now says about 30 settlers, some armed, came with the settlement's security coordinator, and that two Israeli activists were attacked and robbed. It demands that the IDF evacuate the site (Peace Now). Arab48, citing the Palestinian Red Crescent, says a resident and a foreign activist were beaten and taken to the hospital (Arab48).

places.name: Ein ad-Duyuk at-Tahta, Jericho
places.note: Nominatim (neighborhood point; the exact homes are not mapped)

items.headline: 2,615 dunams declared state land to expand Kerem Re'im and Nahliel
items.summary: On 4 Nov, 2,615 dunams in western Binyamin were declared state land to expand Kerem Re'im and Nahliel. Israel Hayom reports that this will allow planning of thousands more homes in the two communities. The Settlement Administration led the work, with the Civil Administration taking part, after several years of staff work. Any building still has to go through planning and permits. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called it "a strategic move for settlement" that will answer the housing needs of thousands of young couples. Israel Ganz said it is part of a wider plan for western Binyamin, where two new communities were set up in the past year (Israel Hayom; Yotam Deshe on X). The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission gives a slightly different figure: 2,536.44 dunams from the lands of Beitillu, al-Mazra'a al-Qibliya and Deir Ammar, northwest of Ramallah, in declaration number הכ/08/26, dated 3 Nov. It says the move links the Talmonim bloc communities (Palestine TV, citing the commission). See the Khamaisi backgrounder on planning.

items.headline: Rioters from Beit Ummar block the road to Gefen Ami and stone a resident
items.summary: On the evening of 4 Nov, Arab rioters from Beit Ummar put a rock roadblock on the western access road to the Gefen Ami hill in Gush Etzion, coming from old Route 60. A resident who got out of his car was stoned from nearby orchards. Elchanan Groner reports that residents of the hill pushed the rioters back to the village before security forces arrived, and that the crowd grew to about 200. Video shows a stone from a sling hitting a resident in the stomach. The rioters then set burning tire roadblocks. The IDF began searches; no arrests had been reported (Groner; Elisha Yered on X; Simcha Raz on X). Arab48 gives a different account of the same evening: it says armed settlers attacked residents in the Zad al-Sheikh area of Beit Ummar, burned a vehicle and took a tractor (Arab48).

places.name: Beit Ummar
places.note: Nominatim (Beit Ummar village point; the Gefen Ami hill itself was not found)

items.headline: Tractor ramming attempt near Mikhmas and stone attacks across Judea and Samaria on 4 Nov
items.summary: JSR (the Judea and Samaria situation room) reported these incidents on 4 Nov: a tractor tried to run over three shepherds from Benayahu's farm northeast of Mikhmas in Binyamin, then fled back to the village (JSR); stones were thrown at an Israeli car at the Nabi Musa junction on Route 1 (JSR); stones were thrown at residents at the Ancient Susya farm in the south Hebron Hills (JSR on X); stones were thrown at a resident at a gas station near Karmei Tzur, at a car 100 meters north of Gad Natan, and at the Ma'ayan Adora junction (JSR; JSR; JSR). No injuries were reported in any of these. Elchanan Groner reported that olive "harvesters" from Yatta attacked Ancient Susya residents openly, and that no suspects had been arrested (Groner). Rescue J&S, as relayed by Groner, reported stones thrown at cars between Homesh and Shavei Shomron near Burqa, and a dummy bomb left on a road nearby the night before (Groner; Groner).

places.name: Mikhmas
places.note: Nominatim (village point; the farm is northeast of it)

places.name: Susya
places.note: Nominatim (a point in Susya, used for the Ancient Susya farm area)

items.headline: Bomb aimed at troops in Nur Shams blown up; four battalions finish raids in Samaria
items.summary: Simcha Raz reports that terrorists planted a bomb in Nur Shams on the night of 3 Nov to hit IDF forces, and troops blew it up in a controlled way; the IDF spokesman released video of the blast (Raz on X; Raz on X). Raz also reports that four battalions, working with the Duvdevan special forces unit, finished an operation in Nablus and the villages of Qaddum, Beit Furik, Yatma and Ein Beidan, finding among other things a weapon next to a children's book, a stun gun and a knife (Raz on X). Kan cites Palestinian reports that 45 people were arrested across Judea and Samaria in an "unusual arrest operation" (Kan). The arrest number comes only from Palestinian reports.

items.headline: Report: Division 98 to end its operations in Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Hallel Bitton Rosen of Channel 14 reported on 4 Nov that, after a situation assessment, the IDF decided to end Division 98's operational activity in Judea and Samaria for now. The division is expected to finish in the coming days and become an IDF reserve division (Bitton Rosen on X). Unconfirmed: no second outlet was found carrying this yet.

items.headline: Shin Bet and police foil a planned bomb and shooting attack at the Lions' Gate and Temple Mount
items.summary: It was released on 4 Nov that a 19-year-old from Beit Hanina in east Jerusalem was arrested. The Shin Bet and police say he planned to set off a bomb at the Lions' Gate, then enter the Temple Mount with a gun and shoot at Jewish civilians and police. Srugim reports he prepared for about two years, checked security cameras and forces on his way to Friday prayers, looked for a weapon on the dark web and trained in martial arts (Srugim).

items.headline: Kedumim head demands full bus service in Samaria
items.summary: Kedumim council head Uziel Vatik wrote to Transportation Ministry director-general Moshe Ben Zaken demanding that the ministry cancel an exemption that, he says, lets the Tnufa bus company run only 75% of its service in the area. "The residents of Kedumim and Samaria are not second-class citizens," he wrote. The letter comes as Dan signed a deal to buy Tnufa for about NIS 150 million (Israel Hayom).

items.headline: PA commission: grazing licenses planned on about 9,487 dunams in Salfit and Jenin
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission says two notices dated 1 Nov announce the intent to approve temporary grazing licenses on land classed as state land: about 8,336 dunams in az-Zawiya, Rafat and Deir Ballut (Salfit) and about 1,152 dunams in Arraba, Kafr Ra'i and Ya'bad (Jenin), with 30 days for objections. The notices do not name who would get the licenses (WAFA, 3 Nov). See the Khamaisi backgrounder on planning.
